**GN-0000 00 Gundam**

Serial number GN-0000, it is the titular [[mecha|mecha]] of the [[gundam 00|gundam 00]] series.

Uses two [[gn drive|gn drive]]s in tandem to produce much better unit performance, and combines with the [[0 raiser|0 raiser]] to produce the [[00 raiser|00 raiser]].

Like its predecessor, the [[gundam exia|gundam exia]], the 00 Gundam is also equipped with seven melee weapons. Three of them (the dual GN Sword IIs and the switchblade-like GN Sword III) can switch between Sword or Rifle Modes to handle both melee and ranged combat, respectively. The GN Sword IIs has a broadsword-like appearance and as mentioned beforehand, the GN Sword III has a switchblade-like appearance and mechanism, which it inherited from Exia's GN Sword.

Has a Mobile Suit Variation called the 00 Gundam Seven Swords/G.

The 2014 FIFA World Cup is the 20th FIFA [[world cup|world cup]], a tournament for the men's [[soccer|association football]] world championship, took place in [[brazil|brazil]] from June 12 to July 13, culminating with the final in Rio de Janeiro.

[[germany|germany]] won their fourth champion title after a victory against [[argentina|argentina]] 1-0 in extra time. This World Cup is also well known for Brazil's humiliating defeat to Germany 1-7 in the semi-final.

The 2018 FIFA World Cup is the 21st FIFA [[world cup|world cup]], a tournament for the men's [[soccer|association football]] world championship. It took place in [[russia|russia]] from June 14 to July 15, culminating with the final in Moscow. 

[[france|france]] defeated [[croatia|croatia]] 4-2 in the final to claim their second title.

The 2022 FIFA World Cup was the 22nd FIFA [[world cup|world cup]], a tournament for the men's [[soccer|soccer]] world championship, taking place in [[qatar|qatar]] from 20 November to 18 December 2022. It was the first World Cup to take place in the Middle East, the first to be held in autumn in the northern hemisphere, and the first to not be held in either May, June, or July, known to be extremely hot months in Qatar.

[[argentina|argentina]] won their third World Cup against [[france|france]] in a 4-2 penalty shootout, after a 3-3 draw in extra time.

Even before the tournament began, it became the focal point of numerous controversies, primarily revolving around allegations of bribery of FIFA officials for the rights to host the tournament, poor treatment of workers (mostly immigrants), and suppression of LGBT rights.

**2channel** (2ちゃんねる, *ni channeru*; 2ch for short) - also known as **5channel** (5ちゃんねる, *go channeru*; 5ch for short) since 2014 split.

A Japanese internet forum, often thought to be the largest in the world in its prime. It has over 600 boards covering a wide range of topics, as their slogan ('*From "hacking" to "side dishes for tonight's dinner"*') would suggest. 

2ch/5ch plays a large part in Japanese internet culture and has created a culture and language in and of itself. [[ascii art|ASCII]] and [[shift jis art|Shift-JIS]] art is popular there and many [[meme|meme]]/[[neta|neta]] and characters have been created based on it. In addition, several internet celebrities have been born there, as have many collaborative projects and pranks (ie: [[densha otoko|densha otoko]], [[buront|buront]], [[kasane teto|kasane teto]] and the [[vippaloid|vippaloid]]s). However, not unlike [[4chan|4chan]] of the west, 2ch/5ch is infamous for its near anarchic, non-existent moderation, which results into the site being a hotbed for political extremists and illegal activities.

In 2014, after the dispute about the domain ownership, the original 2ch.net domain was seized by a group of American shareholders led by Jim Watkins and renamed to 5ch.net, whereas the original founder of 2ch, [[nishimura hiroyuki (2ch)|nishimura hiroyuki (2ch)]] (who went on to purchase 4chan domain and renamed it "4channel") later opened a "successor" site based in Singapore with the registered domain of 2ch.sg. Both sites are still disputing over their claim of being the "legitimate" successor of 2ch.net to this day.

It is important to note that 2ch/5ch is *not* an image board - it is a text board. Do not confuse with "2chan", also known as the [[futaba channel|futaba channel]], or [[2ch.ru|2ch.ru]], a Russian imageboard of similar origin.

It began publication by ASCII Media Works under their [[dengeki bunko|dengeki bunko]] imprint in February 2017. The series is licensed in North America by Yen Press.

A manga adaptation illustrated by [[yoshihara motoki|yoshihara motoki]] has been serialized in [[square enix|square enix]]'s seinen manga magazine Young Gangan since 2018, with a spin-off manga series titled **86: Operation High School** by [[somemiya suzume|somemiya suzume]] being serialized in Media Factory's seinen manga magazine Monthly Comic Alive since June 27, 2020. An anime television series adaptation by A-1 Pictures premiered on April 2021.

A high fantasy novel series by American author [[george r.r. martin|george r.r. martin]], running since 1996 with five novels (out of a projected seven) as of 2012.

The saga revolves around three interconnected stories, set in a world where summer and winter can last decades: a seven-way war for the throne of Westeros, a looming threat of supernatural beings from beyond a massive wall of ice as a long winter approaches, and an exiled princess' quest to retake Westeros from the usurpers who killed her father.

A pose shaped like the capital letter "A", where the arms are held straight out and angled downwards from the sides of the body.

This is more relaxed than a [[t-pose|t-pose]] or [[outstretched arms|outstretched arms]], but less relaxed than [[arms at sides|arms at sides]] where the arms simply hang against the torso due to gravity.

You often see this pose in a few contexts, for example:

- A character showing off an outfit.
- A character posed similarly to a [[sailor moon|sailor moon]] magical-girl style [[transformation|transformation]] scene or the like where the character appears to be relaxed, but floating.

The name comes from 3D modelling as an alternative to the more common [[t-pose|t-pose]].  The A-pose allows for the shoulders to be modeled and textured in a more natural position, and the defined angle can aid in rigging.

The **Mitsubishi A6M** was the primary carrier-based fighter aircraft operated by the [[imperial japanese navy|imperial japanese navy]] during [[world war ii|world war ii]]. Its long designation was "Type 0 Carrier Fighter" (零式艦上戦闘機), and it was commonly called "Reisen" (零戦, zero fighter) by its pilots. This nickname was also popular among the Allies, more so than the official reporting name "Zeke". The plane was designed by [[horikoshi jirou|horikoshi jirou]]. 

When the **ZERO** was first introduced in 1940 it was considered the most capable carrier-based fighter, combining excellent maneuverability with a good climb rate and a very long operational range. These qualities combined with the excellent training of IJN pilots allowed the Japanese to win numerous early victories over their Allied adversaries. Because of its attributes the Zero was instrumental in the success of the attack at [[pearl harbor|pearl harbor]].

However, after the Americans introduced the [[f6f hellcat|f6f hellcat]] and [[f4u corsair|f4u corsair]] in 1942, both of which are much faster, have longer operational range, and are more resilient and have better armor than the Zero, it began to struggle to compete against both planes, particularly due to its weak airframe and being particularily vulnerable to boom-and-zoom tactics. In the later half of the war, with [[battle of midway|the loss of experienced IJN pilots]], the Zero were mostly assigned as suicidal *[[kamikaze pilot|kamikaze]]* aircraft in a desperate attempt to defend the country of [[japan|japan]].

**Aa! Megami-sama** (ああっ女神さまっ, *Oh My Goddess!* or *Ah! My Goddess!*) is a Japanese seinen manga series.

The series follows college sophomore [[morisato keiichi|morisato keiichi]] and the goddess [[belldandy|belldandy]] who moves in with him in a Buddhist temple; after Belldandy's sisters [[urd (aa megami-sama)|urd (aa megami-sama)]] and [[skuld (aa megami-sama)|skuld (aa megami-sama)]] move in with them, they encounter gods, demons and other supernatural entities as Keiichi develops his relationship with Belldandy.

The series is written and illustrated by [[fujishima kousuke|fujishima kousuke]] and has been serialized in *Monthly Afternoon* since September 1988; the individual chapters are being published in tankōbon by [[kodansha|kodansha]], with the first released on August 23, 1989; the final volume of the manga series, volume 48, was released on July 23, 2014, marking nearly 26 years of publication.

Aside from the manga, the series is also known for the two main anime adaptations: the 1993 OVA, and the later 2005 anime series that spanned two seasons. These are the most popular versions of the series, especially outside of Japan (where the manga remained the most popular iteration of the series). Other media include the 2000 movie, a series of short comedy episodes, a second OVA (consisting of three episodes), and a special called "Fighting Wings" that adapts the story arc of the same name from the manga.

**Abyssal ships** (深海棲艦, *shinkaisei-kan*) are monstrous enemy ships in the [[kantai collection|kantai collection]] universe.

Abyssals are characterized by their [[pale skin|pale skin]], black armor plates, [[glowing eyes|glowing]] [[aqua eyes|aqua eyes]], and many [[teeth|toothy]] mouths. Alternate [[glowing|glows]] include [[red eyes|red]], [[yellow eyes|yellow]], and [[blue eyes|blue]].

The weaker versions tend towards being all black armor plates with fish-like forms, while the more powerful, "evolved" forms tend towards being humans with large black metal guns attached. In-between ships tend to have a human part (like just the torso or just the head) leading into metal-skull-crab parts.

Just as player shipgirls take inspiration from real WWII Axis warships, many abyssal boss or event-type characters seem inspired by real-life bases or ships from the Axis or Allied sides. Earlier bosses notably were more Allied (including Port Darwin as [[seaport princess|seaport princess]] or [[isolated island oni|isolated island oni]] as Wake Island) while more recent bosses are clearly meant to reflect [[dark persona|dark versions]] of Japanese ships ([[aircraft carrier water oni|aircraft carrier water oni]] as "dark [[shoukaku (kancolle)|shoukaku (kancolle)]]" or [[destroyer princess|destroyer princess]] as "dark [[harusame (kancolle)|harusame (kancolle)]]").

Abyssal ships were designed and illustrated by [[oguchi|oguchi]] (regular enemies) and [[akira (kadokawa)|akira (kadokawa)]] (boss characters & submarines). Most of their model numbers are based on the "Iroha order":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iroha].

A popular series of arcade  style flight action games published by [[bandai namco|bandai namco]] and developed by in-house team Project Aces. Initially named Air Combat as it’s Namco System 21 arcade original.

From the very first Ace Combat console game, the setting of the games take place in a world similar to Earth but with a radically different history, countries, geography, and having mixed existence of both real and fictional aircraft, as well as exponentially advanced technology, superweapons, submarines, and airships that are larger than life. This world is known as "Strangereal". Two major events have shaped many of the events of the mainline Ace Combat games: The [[ace combat zero|Belkan War]], and the [[ace combat 04|Ulysses Impact]].

The typical Ace Combat plot follows a nameless/faceless fighter pilot's rise from a fledgling rookie to become a feared and respected ace in the war he is fighting, but told in narrative perspective of the people surrounding the pilot. The pilot in question will also typically face off against "rival" aces from the opposing nation. The music in the series has been composed by quite a few talented people within Bandai Namco sound team, with Tetsukazu Nakanishi, Hiroshi Okubo, and Keiki Kobayashi among them. Who also worked on other projects such as [[tekken|tekken]], [[ridge racer|ridge racer]], and [[soulcalibur|soulcalibur]].

There are two manga adaptions; a 3 volume 2013 one illustrated by **Mani**, which was serialized online via Square Enix's Gangan Online website, and the other, an ongoing adaptation that began in 2019 with illustrations by [[yuzuhara moke|yuzuhara moke]]. There is also a 12 episode anime adaption by *Tezuka Productions* which aired Fall of 2020.

During [[gundam zz|The First Neo Zeon War]] both the AEUG and Karaba fought against [[neo zeon|neo zeon]]. An image that was initially [[ai-generated|ai-generated]] but then painted over or retouched by an artist. This also includes posts where an artist uses an AI-generated image as a background or reference for a drawing.

###### Uploading fully AI-generated art to Danbooru is against the [[help:upload rules|upload rules]]; see forum #223144.

An image that, rather than being drawn by a human artist, was generated by an artificial intelligence program.

This tag applies to **fully AI-generated** images, that is, images that underwent no edits or extremely minor retouchings. For edited images, see [[ai-assisted|ai-assisted]].
Note that AI-assisted posts that are up to Danbooru's standards are exempt from the ban on AI-generated art.

#### Examples of common AI model outputs

#### Identification

Signs that something may be AI-generated:

- Anything in 512×768 or 768×512 resolution. This is a very common resolution for Stable Diffusion 1.5-based models, and it is rarely used by humans.
  - Anything in 832×1216 or 1216×832 resolution. This is a very common resolution for Stable Diffusion XL-based models.
- High quality art in low resolution, less than 1000×1000. Older AI generators are restricted to low resolutions, whereas skilled artists normally use much higher resolutions. AI art may be [[upscaled|upscaled]] to higher resolution, but this can produce artifacts. 
  - Newer models are capable of higher resolution, such as NovelAI starting at a free tier of 1024×1024.
- EXIF metadata in the file indicating it is AI-generated. For example, AI prompts or model names. On the upload page, you can click the filesize beneath the image to see the EXIF metadata. Danbooru will automatically tag [[ai-generated|ai-generated]] after upload if the metadata indicates it is AI-generated.
- A certain generic-looking art style with a generic background. This is typical of anime-styled images generated by NovelAI and Stable Diffusion. Browse AI-generated status:deleted to get a feel for this.
- Abnormal/unusual mistakes within the artwork, such as:
  - [[anatomical nonsense|anatomical nonsense]], such as extra legs (post #5732513), fused fingers (post #5742855), fused legs (post #5735212), etc.
  - Strangely drawn objects/environments such as a book with it's cover as another layer of pages (post #5738243), wooden floor conforming with the shape of a character's hair (post #5850417), poor line continuity/object permanence when an object is hidden or goes behind other objects (post #5779922), etc.
  - Note that [[bad hands|bad hands]] or other mistakes are not in themselves signs of AI-generation, as humans can make mistakes too. The errors made by AI tend to be completely illogical or physically impossible things that no human would draw.
- A brand new artist pumping out improbably large volumes of high quality-looking art in a short period of time. This isn't automatically a sign of AI-generation, as sometimes new artists may release a pre-prepared portfolio of artwork to establish their presence.
- An artist with an illogically drastic change in art style after early-October 2022 (around the time NovelAI became popular). This can easily be seen with artists with a low quality art style suddenly shifting into the generic-looking artstyle typical of NovelAI. Bear in mind that artstyles of skilled artists can evolve and improve over time.
- No [[signature|signature]], [[watermark|watermark]], or [[web address|web address]]. Human artists often (but not always) sign their work, while AI works are often unsigned, as the AI can't produce realistic signatures or written text. Do note however, that some AI artists may add a signature or watermark after the image is generated.
- Mentions of "AI" or common AI generators such as "Nijijourney," "Midjourney," "NovelAI," or "Stable Diffusion" in the tags or description of a post are a good place to start, but should not be used to automatically assume [[ai-generated|AI-generation]] (see below).
  - **Note:** Artists frequently use AI keywords when prohibiting their work for its use, so be careful when making assumptions based on them.
 

If you are unsure whether a post is AI-generated or not, ask in topic #22285.

E-3 Stage Boss of the Operation AL/MI Summer 2014 event.

She appears as a young woman wearing a [[short dress|short]] [[black dress|black]] [[sailor dress|sailor dress]] with [[armored boots|armored]] [[thigh boots|thigh boots]] and [[gauntlets|gauntlets]], [[very long hair|very long]] [[white hair|white hair]] with [[one side up|one side up]], sitting atop a monster-ship creature, typical for abyssal ship bosses.

She is assumed to represent the USS [[yorktown (azur lane)|yorktown (azur lane)]], the carrier sunk by the Japanese in the battle of Midway. An alternate theory, based on her ingame lines as well as her hairstyle, suggest that she may be a corrupted [[kaga (kancolle)|kaga (kancolle)]] or [[akagi (kancolle)|akagi (kancolle)]] or even a composite of both. This theory is also supported by the fact that she is voiced by [[fujita saki|fujita saki]], who also voices Akagi. Fans generally go for the abyssal Kaga theory due to the visual resemblance and that [[aircraft carrier princess|aircraft carrier princess]] sounds the closest to Akagi, especially when defeated.

E-5 Stage Boss of the Operation AL/MI Summer 2014 event.

Basically [[aircraft carrier oni|aircraft carrier oni]] with torn clothes and glowing red veins all over the monster-ship bits. It's easy to confuse the two.

As she sinks, she begins to talk normally instead of the usual reverberated voice of the abyssal bosses, a voice that is sometimes identified as [[akagi (kancolle)|akagi (kancolle)]], given how the event is essentially a re-enactment of the [[battle of midway|battle of midway]] where she was critically damaged and scuttled. Both even share the same seiyuu: [[fujita saki|fujita saki]].

She has [[very long hair|very long]] [[white hair|white hair]] and [[orange eyes|orange eyes]]. She wears a [[short dress|short]] [[ribbed dress|ribbed]] [[black dress|black]] [[sailor dress|sailor dress]] with long [[detached sleeves|detached sleeves]], black gloves, and [[black thighhighs|black thighhighs]]. Her most prominent feature is her giant black [[armored boots|armored]] [[knee boots|knee boots]].

Shoukaku was sunk during the [Battle of the Philippine Sea](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_Philippine_Sea,) which is what E-4 represents. Aircraft Carrier Water Oni also resembles Shoukaku visually (Similar facial structure and hair style, bulky footwear, hair ornaments across her head exactly where Shoukaku's hairband is). Though her high armor would make her a closer fit with [[taihou (kancolle)|Taihou]] who also sank in the same battle.

The **AK-47** (**А**втомат **К**алашникова образца 19**47** года) is a 7.62×39mm **[[assault rifle|assault rifle]]** of [[soviet|soviet]] origin, developed between 1944–1946 by [[mikhail kalashnikov|mikhail kalashnikov]]. The [[kalashnikov rifle|AK]] platform has a reputation for its ruggedness, reliability, simple mechanism and ease of manufacture. It can perform well with poor quality [[ammunition|ammunition]] and under harsh conditions.

Visual cues of the original AK-47 are its slanted fixed buttstock profile, a milled receiver with a large rectangular indentation as the [[magazine (weapon)|magazine]] guide and a smooth dust cover, (see post #4852784).

**Do not** simply tag any [[kalashnikov rifle|kalashnikov rifle]]s as AK-47 without even looking at their details.

The **AK-74** (**А**втомат **К**алашникова образца 19**74** года 'Kalashnikov assault rifle model 1974') is a 5.45×39mm **[[assault rifle|assault rifle]]**, developed in Izhevsk Mechanical Plant, 1974. It largely replaced the larger-caliber [[akm|akm]] in [[soviet|soviet]] service, and many of its parts are interchangeable with the earlier [[kalashnikov rifle|AKs]]. First used by Soviet [[military|forces]] during the [[war in afghanistan|Afghanistan conflict]] from 1979.

Use this tag solely if the [[weapon|weapon]] is depicted with full-bodied, fixed stock, and these characteristics: *(post #5952944 as an example)*
- Common presence of synthetic brown/orange furniture (pistol grip and handguard), as well as the magazines.
- Distinctive, longer, non-canted [[muzzle device|muzzle device]]/[[muzzle device|muzzle device]].
- Fixed stock has elongated indentations on both sides.
- Less-curved [[magazine (weapon)|magazine]] profile due to smaller [[rifle cartridge|cartridges]].
- Stamped receiver with visible rivets and smaller rectangular indentation on it.

赤松 健 (Akamatsu Ken) is a Japanese mangaka, born in Kanagawa prefecture, Japan, on July 5, 1968. Most of his works fall into the "harem" genre and feature ecchi material.

In his teenage years, Akamatsu failed the entrance exam to Tokyo University, and applied for Film Study instead (it is speculated that this is where he got the idea for Love Hina). Eventually, he became famous as an illustrator featured in Comiket (short for Comic Market, a comic convention bi-annually held in Japan). He used the pen name Awa Mizuno (水野 亜和, Mizuno Awa "[1]":[#dtext-external-links]). Akamatsu, still in college, then proceeded to win the Weekly Shonen Magazine award twice. His "A Kid's Game for One Summer" was awarded the coveted 50th Shonen Magazine Newcomer's Award soon after he graduated.

After a big hit with [[ai ga tomaranai!|A・I ga Tomaranai!]] (A.I. Love You), he finally made a grand success with his new manga, [[love hina|love hina]]. The series appeared in Weekly Shonen Magazine and has been collected in eleven volumes (with fourteen volumes in total), which have sold over 6 million copies in Japan, and received the Kodansha Manga Award for shōnen in 2001. Akamatsu had added elements of his own life experiences to the story, and this was said to have induced a unique feeling to the manga especially for Western readers, whose lack of familiarity with Japanese culture for the most part added to the effect. The series, published in America in 2002, was especially well received in many overseas countries - Akamatsu was surprised that even foreign readers found Love Hina to be "cute" and to their liking.

He is married to his wife 'Kanon' Akamatsu. Love Hina and the his manga after that, [[mahou sensei negima!|mahou sensei negima!]] (Negima!: Magister Negi Magi), were made into an anime series produced by XEBEC. A second independent retelling of Negima by SHAFT was made called **Negima!?** "[2]":[#dtext-external-links], but it never reached the popularity of the first series or [[love hina|love hina]]. It is has also been aired as a live action series. 

His current manga is [[uq holder!|uq holder!]], a story in the same universe as Negima. It received an anime adaptation by JC Staff that was based on a backup plot.

He later announced in December 2021 he would be running in the summer 2022 elections for a seat in the House of Councillors, the upper house of Japan's House of Representatives, through a nationwide proportional district with a platform "to protect freedom of expression, artistic freedom and creators' rights in Japan from foreign and domestic puritan and politically correct censorship, standards, regulations and influences" according to Wikipedia. His campaign was a success.

A Japanese facial gesture that consists of [[eyelid pull|pulling an eyelid]] down while sticking the [[tongue out|tongue out]]. It is sometimes accompanied by the sound べえだ (beeda, pronounced "behhh-dah"). This gesture is also done in France and Québec, where it is accompanied by saying "mon oeil" ("my eye").

The gist of the gesture is an infantile taunt - the Japanese equivalent of thumbing your nose at someone, or yelling "Nyah nyah nyah" or "Neener neener" or the like.

Akita Neru is a [[vocaloid|vocaloid]] Derivative. Her name (**亞北ネル** - *Akita. Neru*), in phonetic reading, sounds like "I quit. Going to sleep."

She started out as a meme on 2channel, where a troll user started threadcrapping all Vocaloid related threads. Some user commented that he wouldn't get angry only if the troll was a cute girl. Thus Akita Neru, a tsundere non-Vocaloid net-chara was born. Her image color is orange-ish yellow and her character item is a cell phone. Her design was created by [[smith hioka|Smith Hioka (スミス･ヒオカ)]] in 2007. Neru is sometimes written as a Miku wannabe, others as the anti-hero of the Vocaloid personage. She has been officially recognized as a [[hatsune miku|Miku]] derivative by Crypton since 2008.

In the West, she's largely remembered for her appearance in [[triple baka (vocaloid)|triple baka (vocaloid)]]. She would once more return to prominence in 2024 as a result of a meme relating to [[mesmerizer (vocaloid)|mesmerizer (vocaloid)]], due to a reply to a tweet reminiscing about Triple Baka, where Neru was called ""the yellow one that doesn't appear in Mesmerizer":[https://twitter.com/FailedDumbFuck/status/1800938120416010623]". The wave of Neru fanart that followed would culminate in [[swagamicchi|swagamicchi]]'s fan design for what Neru "could've looked like ":[/posts/7736166] in Mesmerizer.

The **AKM** (Russian: Автома́т Кала́шникова модернизи́рованный "[[kalashnikov rifle|Kalashnikov's]] Automatic [[rifle|rifle]] Modernized") is a [[soviet|soviet]] 7.62×39mm **[[assault rifle|assault rifle]]**, designed in 1950s as the major improvement from the earlier [[ak-47|ak-47]]. Main features of the AKM are its stamped receiver (visible rivets) instead of heavier milled one, slanted muzzle brake, and straighter fixed buttstock profile.

Its design was copied and manufactured by various Soviet satellite states, such as Hungarian [[amd-65|amd-65]] and East German [[mpi-km|mpi-km]].

The main antagonist of *[[resident evil|resident evil]]* franchise.

Power-hungry, knowledgeable and cunning, **Albert Wesker** was a man who sought power and domination over the entire human race, all for his own gain. To this end, he was affiliated with the Umbrella Corporation, as one of its most promising researchers, and at the same time participated in illicit activities by going undercover as an officer in the RPD and the leader of S.T.A.R.S. in Raccoon City. 

Through the course of much betrayal of his allies to further his own plans, Wesker faked his death, gained superhuman powers from an experimental virus, and worked alongside both the mysterious "Organization" and Tricell, Inc. He would eventually enact a plot, originally created by Ozwell E. Spencer, to transform the human race into powerful superhumans like himself, and be a god to rule over them and a new age.

He had a son named [[jake muller|jake muller]] who was raised by his mother in order to respect his late father.

Complete or partial absence of skin and hair pigment due to an absence or defect of an enzyme needed for the production of melanin. Due to this, people and animals appear very light-skinned and typically have red eyes because while there is no pigment in the irises, the blood vessels can still be seen. This does not disqualify blue eyes, however, as most people with ocular albinism have blue eyes that bear a slight red tint due to the blood vessel still present. 

Characters with albinism **must** have the following to qualify:

- Either [[white hair|white]] or [[grey hair|grey]] hair.
- [[red eyes|Red]], [[blue eyes|blue]], [[pink eyes|pink]] or [[purple eyes|purple]] eyes.
- [[pale skin|Pale]] or [[white skin|white]] skin.

**Aldnoah.Zero** (アルドノア・ゼロ *Arudonoa Zero*) is a [[science fiction|science fiction]] [[mecha|mecha]] anime series created by Olympus Knights and [[a-1 pictures|a-1 pictures]], that began July 2014. The director is Ei Aoki and the original creator is listed as Gen Urobuchi.

#### Synopsis

In 1972, an ancient alien hypergate was discovered on the surface of the moon. Using this technology, humanity began migrating to Mars and settling there. After settlers discovered additional advanced technology, the Vers Empire was founded, which claimed Mars and its secrets for themselves. Later, the Vers Empire declared war on Earth, and in 1999, a battle on the Moon's surface caused the hypergate to explode, shattering the Moon and scattering remnants into a debris belt around the planet. Cut off from Mars, the remnants of the Vers Empire established several massive orbital space stations within the debris belt and a ceasefire was established. 15 years later, in 2014, an attack on the Vers princess during a peace mission causes the Empire to launch a new attack on Earth, this time determined to conquer it once and for all.

Her familiar is a [[polar bear|polar bear]].

Aleksandra is structured and sometimes perfectionistic, often acting as foil to the hijinks of [[waltrud krupinski|Krupinski]] and the carelessness of [[nikka edvardine katajainen|Katajainen]]. With Nikka, Aleksandra is portrayed as especially close; despite the constant headache of having to repair Nikka's broken [[striker unit|units]], it has brought them together in a certain "care-taker" sort of way.

This character was inspired by Russian ace Alexander Ivanovich Pokryshkin, who was nicknamed "Engineer" when he was a teenager, to which Aleksandra's mechanical inclinations are a reference.

Aleksandra's family name seems to break the rules of real-world Russian, where this type of last name should absolutely have a feminine suffix ("Pokryshkin**a**").

The collective name of a book duology by English author Lewis Carroll as well as a large media franchise which resulted from them.

The first book, *Alice's Adventures in Wonderland* (1865), tells the story of a girl named Alice, who falls down a rabbit hole into a fantasy world populated by peculiar and anthropomorphic creatures. *Through the Looking-Glass, and What Alice Found There* (1871) is a continuation in which Alice goes through the titular looking glass and enters a world that works like a chess board. Once again, Alice finds various peculiar and anthropomorphic creatures and has to deal with their eccentricities.

From the [[persona|persona]] series starting with [[persona 3|persona 3]], a battle mechanic where when all enemies are in "Downed" status, the player is given an option for an "All-Out-Attack", triggering a graphic-cut in and a dust-clouded beat-up animation for high damage.

The sequence is often parodied by both Persona series and non-series alike. It is characterized by split facial profiles, along with often two red exclamation points, "!!".

[[persona 4|persona 4]] parody iterations are subtly different from [[persona 3|persona 3]] iterations. In Persona 4 parodies the characters sport glasses, whereas Persona 3 does not. Backgrounds are typically checker-patterned, and vary in color.

[[persona 5|persona 5]] parodies are a significant departure from the 3 and 4 variants. Rather than the split-screen, character portraits are instead rendered on the debris from a shattered-screen effect. More commonly parodied from Persona 5 is the finishing screens that show up when the All-Out Attack finishes the fight, featuring the character that initiated the attack striking a pose while a personalized message appears on screen in a style specific to that character. [[persona 3 reload|persona 3 reload]] adds a similar finishing screen, albeit with a more restrained aesthetic compared to their P5 predecessors. 

Please only use this tag for multiple characters in a picture, not for single expressions of [[!|!]].

Otherwise known as an alleyway, a narrow lane found in urban areas, often for pedestrians only, which usually runs between or behind buildings. In older cities and towns in Europe, alleys are often what is left of a medieval street network, or a right of way or ancient footpath in an urban setting. In older urban development, alleys were built to allow for deliveries such as coal to the rear of houses. Alleys may be paved, or simply dirt tracks. A blind alley has no outlet at one end and is thus a cul-de-sac.

A post that has additional commentary in the "alt" text of the image. The alt text is an additional written description of the image, supported by some sites. It's usually seen by clicking an "ALT" button in the lower left corner of the image. It's intended to provide a written description of the image for blind users, but normally it's also used by artists as extra commentary (in a similar vein to the `title` attribute of the `` element). It's called "alt text" because in HTML, the text is stored in the `alt` attribute of the `` element, like this: ``` ``` Alt text is currently supported by Twitter, Tumblr, and Bluesky. The alt text should be placed in the artist's commentary if it isn't automatically retrieved from the source. Be sure to add the [[commentary request|commentary request]] tag if the text needs to be translated. If the source has multiple images with alt text attached to them, do not feature every image's alt text in the commentary of one image, unless necessary (ex. image #2's alt text builds off of image #1's alt text). Only include the alt text of the given image. #### Examples - https://twitter.com/satsukinosora/status/1777652767097606186 - https://grumpygryphon.tumblr.com/post/735684444950790144 #### Formatting for Danbooru commentaries ``` > h6. Fan examples of "alters" include [[archer alter (fate)|archer alter (fate)]], [[lancer alter|lancer alter]] (later made [[cu chulainn alter (fate)|canon]] in [[fate/grand order|fate/grand order]]), or the "Sabatsugu" version of [[emiya kiritsugu|emiya kiritsugu]] (not to be confused with [[emiya kiritsugu (assassin)|emiya kiritsugu (assassin)]]).

Common traits of an Alter version of a character include [[white hair|white hair]], [[red eyes|red eyes]] or [[yellow eyes|yellow eyes]], [[pale skin|pale skin]], and visible red veins of [[corruption|corruption]]. Alter characters will also typically be dressed in an [[alternate costume|alternate costume]] with darker colors or stripes of black and red.

In the later installments, the concept of Alter Servant is expanded to include any servant that were corrupted or have their saint graph altered to some degree without the Holy Grail involved. Notable examples include [[atalanta alter (fate)|atalanta alter (fate)]] who is essentially an alternate noble phantasm form of [[atalanta (fate)|atalanta (fate)]] and retains the same personality.

The flag of the [[united states|United States of America]], colloquially known as the **Stars and Stripes**. It serves as a symbol of the country's unity, independence, and democratic ideals. 

The design of the American flag consists of 13 horizontal stripes alternating between red and white, representing the original 13 colonies that declared independence from [[united kingdom|British]] rule. In the top left corner, commonly referred to as the canton, there is a blue rectangle containing 50 white, five-pointed stars arranged in nine rows. These stars represent the 50 states of the United States. The design of the flag has evolved over time as new states joined the Union. The current version with 50 stars became official on July 4, 1960, after [[hawaii|hawaii]] became the 50th state.

The colors of the American flag also hold symbolic meaning. Red represents valor and bravery, white signifies purity and innocence, and blue represents vigilance, perseverance, and justice.

The American flag is widely recognized and displayed in various contexts, including government buildings, schools, homes, and during public events and holidays such as Independence Day ([[fourth of july|July 4th]]). It is treated with respect and reverence, and there are guidelines and protocols for its proper handling, folding, and display.

For images that only show patterns or other symbols representing the United States rather than the flag itself, use the [[united states|united states]] tag.

A belt of [[ammunition|ammunition]] as feeding device for belt-fed [[gun|firearms]]. Commonly [[machine gun|machine gun]], [[minigun|minigun]] or [[gatling gun|gatling gun]].

The [[rifle cartridge|cartridges]] are held in chains of looped metal links which can be connected to form belts of any length. It may disintegrate after firing or not. These disposable links are discarded (along with the empty [[shell casing|shell casing]]s) upon firing. 

Not to be confused with a [[bandolier|bandolier]], which is a belt or sash containing cartridges worn on a person's chest, or an [[ammunition pouch|ammunition pouch]], which is a [[pouch|pouch]] for holding ammunition that may be worn around the waist.

A social intrigue party game developed and published in 2018 by InnerSloth, in which players are randomly divided into [[crewmate (among us)|crewmate (among us)]]s and  [[impostor (among us)|impostor (among us)]]s. The Crewmates must attempt to complete all required tasks and/or expose the Impostors, while the secret Impostors must [[murder|murder]] or frame the Crewmates or sabotage the Crewmates' efforts.

Although released in 2018 as a relatively little-known game, it had a sudden boom in popularity in September 2020, with regular concurrent numbers of well over 250,000, reaching widespread [[meme|memetic]] status on the Internet. The game has a low entry barrier and cross-platform play, allowing users across all devices to enjoy the up-to-15-multiplayer experience. Also notable for its dark yet cute style and slapstick cartoon violence.

The game would later spawn a wide variety of post-ironic [[meme|memes]] in 2021, usually revolving around a parody of [[stonetoss (style)|stonetoss (style)]] comics, a [[when the imposter is sus (meme)|photoshopped image]] of [[jerma985|jerma985]], anything that looks like the in-game characters and/or having the name sounded like "Among Us/Amogus" or "Sus", or simply using the in-game character itself as a "punchline".

Her hair is [[short hair|short]] (or bound-up), [[black hair|black]] (with a white [[streaked hair|streak]]), and styled in the [[side drill|very uncommon]] [[side ponytail|side]][[drill hair|-drill]]. Additionally, there is an [[anchor hair ornament|anchor hair ornament]] on the end of a [[single sidelock|single sidelock]].

Her clothing is all blacks and greys. She is dressed in a [[meiji schoolgirl uniform|meiji schoolgirl uniform]] that consists of a grey [[kimono|kimono]], black [[hakama skirt|hakama skirt]] & [[obi|obi]], and [[black footwear|black]] [[high heel boots|high-heeled]] [[boots|boots]]. She also appears to wear [[black gloves|black]] [[elbow gloves|elbow]] [[gloves|gloves]]. 

She is armed with a monstrous Abyssal [[cannon|gun]] [[turret|turret]], replete with one-and-a-half horrific, [[teeth|toothy]] maws, bristling with gun barrels, disturbingly organic-looking [[mechabare|mechabare]], and a [[hose|hose]] dangling from the bottom.

While it is *very* easy to mistake her for [[ancient destroyer princess|ancient destroyer princess]], there are some key differences:

The most common of these are [[robot ears|robot ears]], [[robot joints|robot joints]], [[mechanical wings|mechanical wings]], and attached [[cable|cable]]s.

The difference between a [[humanoid robot|humanoid robot]] and an [[android|android]] is that an android looks mostly human, usually having something resembling skin (though it needn't be skin-colored) and a fully human face, while a humanoid robot is clearly non-human, with a non-human face.

An animated image in the APNG format, an unofficial, backwards-compatible extension to the PNG format created by the group behind Mozilla/Firefox. Comparable to [[animated gif|animated gif]] files, but with support for 24-bit colour and 8-bit transparency.

Not fully supported by all browsers. Internet Explorer and EdgeHTML-based Microsoft Edge will only display a preview image, but the animation should display properly in Firefox, Chrome (v. 59 onwards), SeaMonkey, Safari, Opera (prior to v. 15) or Chromium-based Edge. Also note that the animation is not preserved when previewing or resizing the image, so make sure to click on "view original" if you wish to view more than the static preview image. In addition to these browsers, there is also support for the format in a few stand-alone image browsers. 

This tag is automatically added by the site to new uploads.

A sci-fi seinen manga series by [[ark performance|ark performance]] and published in Young King Ours.

The series revolves around the crew of the submarine [[i-401 (aoki hagane no arpeggio)|i-401 (aoki hagane no arpeggio)]], a sentient ship that has rebelled against the mysterious navy, known as the Fleet of Fog that is composed of naval vessels that possess weapons and armor that completely outmatches those possessed by humans. The Fleet of Fog in 2039 took control of the seas around the world and cut off transport between continents and islands by all means except expensive SSTO (single-stage-to-orbit) space vehicle launches. The series begins in 2056 with the I-401 and its crew requested to protect a Japanese SSTO launch from the Fleet of Fog.

A 12-episode CG anime adaptation of the series titled Arpeggio of Blue Steel -Ars Nova- aired Fall 2013. A spin-off manga titled ソルティ・ロード (Salty Road) by TALI, author of 6 no Trigger, began publication October 2014

Free-to-play battle-royale game released by [[respawn entertainment|respawn entertainment]] in February 2019 for [[xbox one|xbox one]], [[playstation 4|playstation 4]], and [[computer|PC]], with a [[nintendo switch|nintendo switch]] port in 2021 and an upgraded version for [[xbox series x|xbox series x]] and [[playstation 5|playstation 5]] in 2022. A [[apex legends mobile|smartphone port]] developed in collaboration with Tencent's LightSpeed Studios was released in 2022, though it ultimately shut down in 2023. The port was treated as a separate game entirely and featured exclusive cosmetics and legends.

It quickly gained mass popularity, rivaling contemporaries such as [[overwatch|overwatch]], [[playerunknown's battlegrounds|PUBG]] & [[fortnite|fortnite]] in player & streaming view count. The game is notably very popular in Japan, where first-person shooters typically have difficulty finding a large following. It is the favorite game of many [[virtual youtuber|virtual youtuber]]s and eSports players, with both [[hololive|hololive]]/[[holostars|holostars]] and [[nijisanji|nijisanji]] having several talents who dedicate most of their stream time to playing it.

Despite not featuring the parkour and mecha elements of the main series, Apex Legends is considered a canon part of the [[titanfall (series)|titanfall (series)]] franchise. Due to how it's largely treated as a separate entity with its own spin-offs, the Titanfall series tag should not be added to Apex posts unless there's a direct reference beyond the shared weapons.

The show details humanity's new struggle against the Abductors from a mysterious realm using the Aquarion, a mecha formed from three vehicles operated by members of Neo DEAVA, a training institution for psychically-endowed teens. Among its newest members are [[amata sora|amata sora]], a boy with a mysterious power of levitation, and [[mikono suzushiro|mikono suzushiro]], a girl he saves from an Abductor attack.

An aquiline nose, also called a Roman nose or hooked nose, is a type of [[nose|nose]] which has a prominent bridge, giving the appearance of being bent or curved. *Aquiline* comes from the Latin *aquilinus*, meaning "eagle-like", alluding to the curved beak-like shape of the nose. 

If the nose has a distinct slant at the top where it meets the face, or a prominent outwards curve, it should be tagged as such.

The **[[ar-15|ar-15]]** is an American semi-automatic [[rifle|rifle]] designed in 1956 by Eugene Stoner and L. James Sullivan, based on the [[ar-10|ar-10]]. AR stands for **ArmaLite**, its original manufacturer. The early design feature a top-mounted charging handle inside the carry handle. Its selective fire variant, was eventually adopted by the U.S. military as the M16. 

Predominantly available in .223 caliber / 5.56mm, the rifle enjoys a huge popularity for its accuracy, and controllable recoil, as well as modular and customizable design despite surrounding controversies. Therefore various companies manufacture and market such rifles. 

- Any non-military issue rifle of this design is properly labelled AR-15 regardless of specific subvariant. Or for any AR-15-style rifles of less-known, unspecified model.
- Usage context is for non-military, civilian setting. Because further artistic details of fire selector can be rendered invisible or insignificant most of the time.
- This tag should not be used altogether to refer several better-known, AR-based military-grade rifles such as the [[m16|m16]], [[colt commando|colt commando]], [[m4 carbine|m4 carbine]], or [[h&k hk416|HK416]].

The Aran jumper (Irish Gaelic: Geansaí Árann) is a style of [[sweater|sweater]] that takes its name from the Aran Islands off the west coast of [[ireland|ireland]]. It is sometimes known as a *fisherman's jumper*. A classical fisherman's jumper is a bulky garment of unscoured wool with [[cable knit|cable knit]] patterns (often of various patterns) generally covering both the body and arms of the sweater; they are traditionally cream-coloured or off-white.

The crown's *cap* is lined with velvet that has a ermine base, although there are arched crowns with no cap present. Red velvet is typical of real-like royal crowns, and are frequently the basic depiction for arched crowns in artwork.

The **Arisaka** family of [[bolt action|bolt action]] rifles were a series of Japanese weapons designed by Colonel Nariakira Arisaka. They were the standard weapons of the Japanese Empire from 1898 to 1945 and were used in [[world war i|world war i]] and [[world war ii|world war ii]]. 

The Arisaka rifles were derived in part from the German Mauser, especially the 5-round internal magazine fed by a stripper clip. The most common versions were the 6.5x50mm Type 38 long rifle and 7.7x58mm Type 99 short rifle. Less common but notable variants are the folding-bayonet Type 44 carbine and Type 97 sniper rifle (both derived from the Type 38), and the Type 2 paratrooper rifle (based on the Type 99). 

Arisaka rifles were marked with [[kikumon|the Imperial Seal of Japan]] (a Chrysanthemum), designating them as the property of the Emperor.

A Chinese tower defense mobile game, developed by Hypergryph and published by Yostar. It is available in Google Playstore and iOS appstore.

The player is put in the role of the [[doctor (arknights)|doctor (arknights)]], in charge of *Rhodes Island*, an organization tasked with investigating disasters caused by a mysterious ore known as [[originium (arknights)|originium (arknights)]], and aiding those infected by [[oripathy lesion (arknights)|Oripathy]], caused by exposure to Originium. As the amnesiac Doctor clad in protective suit, the player is put in control over the characters known as Operators, tasked to eliminate the threats lurking from the rebel group known as Reunion.

The game was first announced in 2017. Between 2017 and 2019, it was briefly available for several short beta tests. The game was officially released on May 1st, 2019. International versions in Japanese and English were released Jan. 16th, 2020. The game is available in its native Chinese, Japanese, English and Korean, each with their own app clients. For the first few years of the game's lifetime, character voices were only available in Japanese regardless of region; however, Mandarin character voices were added in September 2021, with dialectal Chinese voices for the Sui siblings added later, and English and Korean character voices were added in late June 2022.

In 2022, a spinoff RPG game, [[arknights: endfield|arknights: endfield]], was announced.

**Armored Core VI: Fires of Rubicon**, is a mecha combat videogame by From Software and published by Bandai Namco. The sixth game of the [[armored core|armored core]] series and latest since 2013's [[armored core: verdict day|armored core: verdict day]], the game was released on 25 August 2023 on for PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, PC, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S.

Set in the far future on the planet Rubicon 3, the planet was once rich with a substance called Coral that could be use as an energy source and data conduit. However, the Coral caused a cataclysmic event known as the Fires of Ibis, which engulfed the planet and the surrounding star system in flames. Fifty years later, Coral was once again discovered on Rubicon 3, leading to a war between the Corporations who want to mine Coral and the local government and people trying to stop them.

The player takes the role of [[621 (armored core 6)|621]], an augmented Armored Core pilot sent to Rubicon 3 by their boss, [[handler walter|handler walter]], to work as a mercenary for the various factions in order to earn a new life for themselves.

An ArtStation sample can either have lower image dimensions, or have the same dimensions but truncated bit-by-bit quality.

ArtStation formerly had a much more complicated image sampling issue, which can be referred back to by looking at previous revisions of this article or viewing the legacy procedure for avoiding samples at [[howto:artstation|howto:artstation]]. Now a user may errantly upload from image URLs including "/small/" or "/medium/" rather than the correct "/large/" which would be replaceable by a moderator or by uploading the unsampled version and manually deleting the sample. The acronym for 'autonomous sensory meridian response'. Basically low-grade euphoria that is experienced as a tingling sensation that begins at the scalp and moves down the spine. A genre of videos intended to induce ASMR has emerged, over 15 million of which had been published on YouTube by 2021, most of which serve to help listeners fall asleep. ASMR videos often use a [[binaural microphone|binaural microphone]] for the best results.

ASMR can occur in multiple formats in illustrations:

- The acronym being displayed in faux YouTube text (post #4603304)
- A performer using the specified equipment to produce such videos (post #4792035)

- [[blowing in ear|blowing in ear]]

Artists that have done character key illustrations for the franchise include [[yaegashi nan|yaegashi nan]], [[nauribon|nauribon]] and [[hotaru (ultraroly poly)|Hotaru]].

The background story is set in the near future, where mankind is under threat by mysterious giant monsters called Huge that can only be fought by Lilies—girls who can use weapons called CHARMs to channel the power of Magie. Lilies fight in teams of five or more known as "Legions," and attend academies known as "Gardens" which train and command them.

Other parts of the media mix include ongoing stage plays since 2016; several light novels and webnovels; two anime series, *Assault Lily: Bouquet* and *Assault Lily: Fruits*; and a social game for phones and PCs, *Assault Lily: Last Bullet*, that began service in early 2021.

An infantry [[rifle|rifle]] designed for combat, with selective fire capability. The German [[stg44|stg44]] was the very first mass-produced assault rifle ever designed and introduced in battle.

In the strictest of definitions for a [[gun|firearm]] to be considered an assault rifle, it must at least follow these characteristics:
- It must be an individual weapon with provision to fire from the shoulder (i.e. a buttstock);
- It must be capable of selective fire (semi and full auto, some models may feature burst fire mode);
- It must have an [[rifle cartridge|intermediate-power cartridge]], which has more power and velocity than a pistol round but less than a standard full-power ones (i.e. 5.56×45mm NATO);
- Its [[ammunition|ammunition]] must be supplied from a detachable box [[magazine (weapon)|magazine (weapon)]].

She is very straight-forward and blunt whenever she has something to say and occasionally every now and then in her dialogue lets out ribbits (*kero* in Japanese). She is very adamant about being called by her first name, Tsuyu, and immediately corrects anybody who calls her by her last name, Asui. A majority of the time she has a "[[:>|:>]]" expression on her face no matter what mood she is in, only going away when she opens her mouth.

**Atelier Resleriana: Forgotten Alchemy and the Polar Night Liberator** is the 25th mainline game in the [[atelier (series)|Atelier series]], developed by Akatsuki Games and published by Koei Tecmo. The story is penned by novelist Takahiro, with character designs by [[umiu geso|umiu geso]], [[tokki|tokki]], and [[noco (adamas)|noco (adamas)]]. Unlike previous mainline entries in the series, it is a free-to-play game with monetization centered around a gacha system.

It follows the story of the two titular protagonists: [[resna sternenlicht|resna sternenlicht]], a novice alchemist who hopes to revive the concept of alchemy, and [[valeria (atelier)|valeria (atelier)]], an adventurer who's lost most of her memories up to three years before the events of the game.

The game was released in Japan on September 23, 2023 for mobile devices, and on January 10, 2024 for PC through Steam. The global version was released worldwide on January 25, 2024 for both mobile devices and PC.

The game heavily features characters from the wider Atelier series mysteriously transported into the world, known collectively as "wanderers".

A [[leotard|leotard]] worn for [[ballet|ballet]], [[gymnastics|gymnastics]], [[dancing|dance]], or other similar activities.

As these leotards are used for activities with a lot of movement the leotard either covers the shoulders or has a strap to prevent wardrobe accidents.  A strapless-like appearance may be achieved through the use of skin tone or see-through fabrics though.

For ballet and dance practices it is frequent that these leotards are worn with [[pantyhose|tights]] and typically feature flat colors.  For gymnastics it is most common that they're worn barelegged and it is not unusual for them to be made of a material featuring a sheen to them.

Official Gymnastic competitions have modesty rules for the appearance of the leotards worn by competitors.  While these do not bar someone from competing, violating it will immediately result in point deductions from their score.  The main restrictions on leotards are:

- May not be made of transparent material
- The neckline may be no lower than the sternum and the back may be no lower than the shoulder blades
- May not feature narrow straps
- The cut of the leotard at the top of the legs must not go beyond the fold of the crotch

The visual novel was digitally released on Steam for Windows on June 19, 2020 worldwide. Later, on December 16, 2021, the game was also released for Android, iOS and Nintendo Switch devices by iMel only in Japan.

#### Synopsis
In the near future, a sudden rise in sea levels floods the majority of the world and ends human civilization as we know it, forcing humanity to eke a living on what little dry land remains. [[ikaruga natsuki|ikaruga natsuki]] is a young man living under difficult circumstances in this new world. He has lost one of his legs in an accident which can only be replaced with a crude prosthetic, and he suffers constant bouts of phantom pain. One day, though, Natsuki rummages through his recently deceased grandmother's belongings to pay off a debt, only to awaken a young android girl name [[atri|atri]], who will go on to change his life forever

A connector commonly used for audio equipment. Sometimes called a headphone jack, jack plug, phone jack, or phone connector.

Almost all [[headphones|headphones]], [[microphone|microphone]]s and most consumer [[speaker|speaker]]s have one of these connectors. Consumer equipment usually has the small 3.5 mm plug and professional equipment has the large 6.35 mm plug. Electric guitars and effects units always use the 6.35 mm plug.

Plugs have a single prong with separately connected tip, sleeve, and usually one ring, sometimes more. Mono audio has no ring, often found on microphones; stereo audio has one ring and headsets with integrated microphones or control buttons have two or more rings.

A fictional faction of benevolent sentient [[alien|alien]] [[robot|robot]]s from the planet Cybertron. They are usually the main protagonists in the fictional universe of [[transformers|transformers]]. 

In all but [[transformers shattered glass|one Transformer story]], the "Heroic **Autobots**" are opposed by the "Evil [[decepticon|decepticon]]s", their main antagonists in Transformers. 

Both Autobots and Decepticons are sentient humanoid [[alien|alien]] robots that can transform into machines, vehicles and other familiar mechanical objects. They are typically represented by the red facial insignia they all wear. Primarily, Autobots have blue eyes, while their enemy Decepticons have red eyes. 

Autobots often turn into regular cars, trucks, or other road vehicles but some are aircraft, military vehicles, communication devices, weapons, and cyborg animals. Some can even transform into humans; they'd be classified as pretenders. Most of the Autobot groups' names have the suffix "-bot" in them. 

In [[japan|japan]], the Autobots are called **Cybertrons** (サイバトロン, Saibatoron?) except in the live-action film series and Transformers Animated, where they are referred to as Autobots (オートボット, Ōtobotto?). The *Maximals* from Transformers: Beast Wars are also known as Cybertrons in Japan, but in North America they are called Maximals and are descendants of the Autobots. In [[italy|italy]], they are called **Autorobots**. The Autobot symbol is also referred to as an "Autobrand" in issue #14 of the Marvel Comics series. 

In the Michael Bay live action films as well as in the new CGI animated series (Transformers Prime), the title Autobots is explained to be the short version of the title **Auto**nomous Ro**bot**ic Organism**s**.

#### Synopsis
The story follows a world divided into four nations: the Water Tribe, Earth Kingdom, Fire Nation, and Air Nomads. Each nation is represented by a natural element for which the nation is named. Benders of those elements have the ability to control and manipulate the [[element bending|element]] from their nation. Only the Avatar is the master of all four elements which they can bend. The Fire Nation wants to conquer the world and the only one who can stop them, the Avatar, has disappeared. 100 years have passed, [[sokka|sokka]] and [[katara|katara]] discover that [[aang|aang]] is the long-lost Avatar and join him on a journey to master all four elements and bring balance to the world.

The story is set in a world primarily influenced by Eastern culture and mythology (as well as Inuit), revolving around the reincarnations of the titular Avatar. It would be the beginning of the [[avatar legends|avatar legends]] franchise, with its sequel being [[the legend of korra|the legend of korra]].

Ayakashi Triangle, sometimes abbreviated as AyaTri, is a 2020-to-2023 Japanese manga series written and illustrated by [[yabuki kentarou|yabuki kentarou]]. It has been serialized by publisher Shueisha since June 2020, changing from [[shounen jump|Weekly Shōnen Jump]] magazine to Shōnen Jump+ in April 2022.

The series focuses on exorcist ninja [[kazamaki matsuri|kazamaki matsuri]], as he tries to defend his childhood friend, the Ayakashi Medium [[kanade suzu|kanade suzu]], from evil spirits called ayakashi. However, during a battle to save Suzu's life, Matsuri is turned into a girl after being cursed by [[shirogane (ayatora)|shirogane (ayatora)]], the King of Ayakashi. With Suzu's help, Matsuri must adjust to his new feminine form as they deal with both the friendly and the malicious ayakashi they encounter, as well as their growing feelings for each other, all while trying to break Matsuri's curse for him to return to his original form.

A group of ancient cultures located in modern day [[mexico|mexico]]. Often the term "Aztec" refers exclusively to the Mexica people of [[tenochtitlan|tenochtitlan]] (now the location of [[mexico city|mexico city]]), situated on an island in Lake Texcoco, who referred to themselves as Mexica Tenochca.

The **Aztec** people were certain ethnic groups of central Mexico, particularly those groups who spoke the Nahuatl language and who dominated large parts of Mesoamerica in the 14th, 15th and 16th centuries, a period referred to as the late post-classic period in Mesoamerican chronology.

In 1521, in what is probably the most widely known episode in the Spanish colonization of the Americas (also known as "La Conquista"), [[hernan cortes|hernan cortes]], along with a large number of Nahuatl speaking indigenous allies, conquered [[tenochtitlan|tenochtitlan]] and defeated the Aztec Triple Alliance under the leadership of Hueyi Tlatoani [[moctezuma ii|moctezuma ii]]; In the series of events often referred to as "The Fall of the Aztec Empire". 

Subsequently the Spanish founded the new settlement of Mexico City on the site of the ruined Aztec capital.

**Azur Lane** is a Chinese shipgirl-themed side-scrolling shoot 'em up mobile game developed by Shanghai Manjuu and Xiamen Yongshi and published by [[yostar|yostar]].

#### Gameplay

Like [[kantai collection|kantai collection]], the game is set during World War II and mainly features collecting and controlling moe [[personification|personification]]s of [[warship|warship]]s from major participants of [[world war ii|world war ii]]. Unlike [[kantai collection|kantai collection]], it features side-scrolling shooter gameplay with mechanics akin to those of [[touhou|touhou]]. Other gameplay elements, such as customization of a interactive backyard and marrying in-game characters, are also present. The real life factions are replaced by fictional counterparts (such as Empire of Japan being called as "Sakura Empire", United States as "Eagle Union", etc.)

Unlike KanColle, the game has made an effort to distance itself from WW2 in most aspects in order to appeal to a broader audience, pushing for most fantastical designs, the implementation of collabs unrelated to WW2 naval history, the release of shipgirls based on fictional warships without proper historical precedent, post-war era warships, WW1 warships, dark versions of its existing shipgirls (METAships), shipgirls from the Age of Sail, child and idol variants of its characters, and so on.

#### Media

The game has been adapted into several manga and novelizations. [[azur lane: crosswave|azur lane: crosswave]], a [[playstation 4|playstation 4]] / PC game, was released in 2019. A TV anime adaptation aired during Fall 2019. The game has also held an annual collaboration with [[world of warships|world of warships]] since 2017. [[azur lane: slow ahead|azur lane: slow ahead]], a slice-of-life [[4koma|4koma]] series, was adapted into an anime in early 2021.

#### History

*Azur Lane* was launched on May 25th, 2017 in China, on September 14th, 2017 in Japan, on March 27th, 2018 in Korea, on August 16th, 2018 in English, and around September 2019 in Taiwan. As of 2024, the number of players registered surpassed at least 41 million.

***Azure Striker Gunvolt*** (Japanese title: 蒼き雷霆ガンヴォルト, pronounced as アームドブルー・ガンヴォルト, Armed Blue Gunvolt) is an action side-scrolling platforming developed by [Inti Creates](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inti_Creates) with some input from [Keiji Inafune](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keiji_Inafune,) and it is Inti Creates' first independent video game series. The series serves as a spiritual successor to the [[mega man zero (series)|mega man zero (series)]] series.

The game takes place in a distant future where those born with psychic powers known as "Adapts" (EN) / "Seventh" (JP) are feared and oppressed on a regular basis by those without. A major world-wide conglomerate known as the Sumuragi Group tasked themselves into bringing peace to Adapts under their "Psychic Protection" program, but unbeknownst to the world, their so-called plan for peace turned out to be what amounts to concentration camps where a series of cruel and inhumane experiments are performed on Adapts under their program. A resistance group known as QUILL (EN) / FEATHER (JP) however surfaced in attempt to stop their atrocities. One of their newest members, a 14-year-old Adapt boy known only by his codename, "[[gunvolt|gunvolt]]", who also possesses the titular "Azure Striker" (EN) / "Armed Blue" (JP) septima, the ability to control electricity and lightning. During one mission where Gunvolt is tasked to stop Sumuragi's plans to steal the cyber diva [[lumen (gunvolt)|Lumen]] (EN) / Morpho (JP) and her septima of "The Muse" to control Adapts across the world then destroy her, Gunvolt however he discovers that the cyber diva was not a computer programmed idol, but rather the manifestation of a young girl's septimal powers named [[joule (gunvolt)|Joule]] (EN) / Cyan (JP). Not wishing to see Joule suffer through the same kind of oppression he went through, Gunvolt boldly went against his orders and rescues her from her captors.

The series later gained a sequel, *Azure Striker Gunvolt 2*, which takes place a few months after the events of its predecessor, where Gunvolt crosses paths with an Adapt-hunting avenger named [[acura (gunvolt)|Copen]] (EN) / Acura (JP) from the previous game as they encounter a group of Adapts known as Eden, whom harbor a hatred towards humans, seeking to use Joule's powers to wipe out humans and create a new utopia for Adapts. A gaiden game, *[[gunvolt chronicles luminous avenger ix|Gunvolt Chronicles: Luminous Avenger iX]]*, later follows after the events of *Azure Striker Gunvolt 1* and focuses on Copen. There are also supplementary materials that expands on the serie's world and characters, such as *Azure Striker Gunvolt: Fleeting Memories*, prequel story taking place before the first game, as well as an OVA based on the first game released through the Nintendo 3DS eShop. Gunvolt also made an appearance in *[[mighty gunvolt|mighty gunvolt]]*, a retro-inspired spin-off series of games also from Inti Creates that features a cross-over of *Azure Striker Gunvolt*, *[[mighty no. 9|mighty no. 9]]*, and *[[gal gun|Gal☆Gun]]*. The series gains a third game in *Azure Striker Gunvolt 3*, set years after the events of *Azure Striker Gunvolt 2*.

A post that is no longer available from the source link. Usually this is because the work was deleted by the artist.

Compare with [[bad source|bad source]], where the link does not point to the original image, and [[bad link|bad link]], where the source is correct but it leads to a direct image instead of a proper post.

#### Guidelines

If another source for the image is found, follow these instructions:

- If the filesize and MD5 hash are the same, then change the source field to the new source, and remove the [[bad id|bad id]] tag(s). The MD5 hash can be compared with http://onlinemd5.com/ or https://md5file.com/calculator. Note: A source is legitimate only if it's hosted by the original artist.
- If the filesizes are different and the image is inferior, then just ignore it and do not upload it.
- If the filesizes are different and the image is superior, then upload it if you consider the image worthy, then parent the original to the upload (by clicking edit on the child post and pasting in the parent ID in the parent field) and then tag the original upload with the [[duplicate|duplicate]] tag.

The Bald Eagle (*Haliaeetus leucocephalus*) is an [[eagle|eagle]] found in North America.  As an adult they feature dark brown feathers with white head and tail feathers.  Their beaks, feet, and irises are bright yellow.  The bald eagle has a body length of 70–102 cm (28–40 in) and typical wingspan between 1.8 and 2.3 m (5 ft 11 in and 7 ft 7 in).  Their mass is normally between 3 and 6.3 kg (6.6 and 13.9 lb). Males' average 4.1 kg (9.0 lb) and females average 5.6 kg (12 lb). 

The word "bald" in their name is derived from an older meaning referring to the white of their head and tail. Their species name is Latinized Ancient Greek for "white" and "head".

The Bald Eagle has cultural importance to the [[united states|united states]] and [[native american|native american]]s. It is the national [[bird|bird]] and symbol of the United States of America. It is featured on the Great Seal of the United States that was adopted by the Continental Congress in 1782.  For various [[native american|native american]] tribes it holds spiritual and religious significance, and its feathers are central to many of their religious and spiritual customs.

A tropical plant consisting of tall, green, tubular stems. It is technically a type of grass, but its woody tissue is as strong as timber, and the tallest species can grow to a height of nearly 100 feet (30 meters). Most species are native to Southeast Asia (around 64%), but the plant is also common in Latin America (around 33%). The rest are native mostly to Africa and Oceania, but North America does has 3 native species. 

Bamboo is used for a variety of things, including cooking, construction, textiles, paper, furniture, and traditional medicine.

It is a dietary staple of the giant [[panda|panda]], together with which it is frequently depicted.

In Japan, baozi are known as *manjuu*, the Japanese rendering of *mantou*. A meat-filled *manjuu* is a *nikuman*; those referred to as *manjuu* typically have a sweet filling. 

Sweet *manjuu* became even more popular due to *[[love live! school idol project|love live! school idol project]]* since it is the signature item of Homura Bakery, which [[kosaka honoka|kosaka honoka]]'s family owns and lives over. Good Smile Company, as a result, produced official Homura Bakery *manjuu* in packs.

Other names for baozi include bao, bau, humbow, nunu, pow or pau.

Bara ("Gei komi'":[https://www.fujoshi.info/geikomi] in Japan) is a Japanese genre of manga and art (usually) by and for gay and bisexual men. With heavy focus on the masculine features and appeal of [[mature male|men]]. 

While mostly dependent on an artist's personal tastes, the ‘bara’ archetype features 3 main body types:
- Bear-type bodies, (typically tagged as [[plump|plump]] or [[fat|fat]]), are generally softer and rounder looking, with varying degrees of visible musculature.
- Artists: [[suv (suv032)|suv (suv032)]], [[kuro nezumi inu|kuro nezumi inu]], [[tevit (tevit15)|tevit (tevit15)]].

- Hunks/Jocks or [[muscular|Muscular-type]] bodies, in contrast to the chiseled [[v-taper|triangular look]] of professional bodybuilders, have defined musculature that is usually more proportional overall, similar to that of athletic "strongman":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strongman], with a [[strongman waist|wider waist]] ("comparison":[https://cdn.donmai.us/original/e8/4f/e84f5efad6fd9ef1ff268d1982a564d6.jpg]), though the more [[shredded muscle|chiseled]] appearance can be a stylistic choice (see [[nikism|nikism]] for reference).
- Artists: [[tarutoru|tarutoru]], [[crow (siranui)|crow (siranui)]], [[dopey (dopq)|dopey (dopq)]].

- Twunk or otter-type bodies, tagged [[toned|toned]], *or* [[muscular|muscular]] (especially with younger or sometimes older [[mature male|mature male]]s). 
- Artists: [[itto (mentaiko)|Mentaiko]], [[homri|homri]], [[torakichi (ebitendon)|torakichi (ebitendon)]], [[kuroshinki|kuroshinki]]. 

Musculature, when depicted, is typically more exaggerated for emphasis (e.g. [[pectorals|pecs]]) along with the [[bulge|bulge]] (implying an exaggerated penis size), and both are usually rather noticeable even when the subject is wearing clothes -  abnormally so. When this exaggeration is paired with the points above, which assert a softer approach when drawing the male form, the 'bara' archetype becomes noticeable.

Common masculine features on subjects include: different degrees of [[facial hair|facial]] and [[body hair|body hair]] (especially the [[navel hair|happy trail]] leading to [[male pubic hair|pubic hair]]) - or a complete absence of it in the case of younger characters (depending on the artist's tastes), [[thick eyebrows|thick]], [[eyebrow cut|cut]] or [[forked eyebrows|bushy eyebrows]], [[sideburns|sideburns]], [[buzz cut|buzz cut]], [[large hands|large hands]], [[scar|scar]]s, [[tattoo|tattoo]]s, [[bandaid|bandaid]]s, [[bandage|bandage]]s, [[wrinkled skin|wrinkles]] (visible with [[mature male|mature]] and [[old man|old]] men), etc.

All of these characteristics lend the style a degree of flexibility that allows for further stylization as well as broader cultural mixing between communities; for instance, despite bara’s roots in opposition to them, there is substantial cross-over with the larger [[yaoi|Boys' Love]] community - which can be seen in some artists' styles (E.g [[yotti|yotti]], [[arima (arima bn)|arima (arima bn)]]). It can also be applied to non-human and humanoid characters, such as [[furry male|furry male]]s  (E.g [[wafu (youzora samo18)|wafu (youzora samo18)]], [[boogbogex|boogbogex]]).

**History and meaning:**
The word "bara" literally means "rose" in Japanese. The term originally comes from the magazine "Barazoku":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barazoku], Japan's first gay men's magazine, with the term traditionally referring to more [[bishounen|bishounen]]-esque men. As a result, the word "bara" also began being used as a slang term for any male homoerotic works in general (similar to the use of [[yaoi|yaoi]] in the West).

The word "bara" as used here is primarily Western, stemming more from its application on art more commonly known as "gei komi", "gei manga", or "mens love" in Japan, a practice that began on Japanese imageboards, where they intentionally misappropriated the term, this interpretation later being exported abroad. Whilst some Japanese gei komi creators oppose the usage of "bara" due to its earlier legacy, others have embraced it. Note that, like most Manga Demographics, bara is commonly defined in terms of the target audience, not the authors or the subject matter.

Bara conceptually often contrasts with yaoi, which is gay male media traditionally made by heterosexual women to appeal to other heterosexual women. Whereas bara is gay/bi male media made by gay/bi men for gay/bi men, that generally features romantic and sexual relationships between [[muscular|muscular]] [[mature male|mature men]] and realistic(ish) relationships, often including LGBTQ issues, [[yaoi|yaoi]] generally features androgynous, idealized, effeminate characters and melodramatic plots devoid of LGBTQ issues (like most [[yuri|yuri]], for similar root reasons). By its nature, it is also heteronormative, whether by stereotypically depicting overly emotional relationships or using concepts such as "uke" and "seme," and includes themes of homosociality, which contributed more to the clash between fans of the two genres, though nowadays there's a grey area between the two. What they share in common the most though is the fact that non-Japanese audiences have misappropriated them, with yaoi having become a generalized weeb term for anything involving gay men.

A bat-and-ball sport played between two teams of nine players. The aim is to score runs by hitting a thrown [[baseball (object)|ball]] with a [[baseball bat|bat]] and touching a series of four [[baseball base|bases]] arranged at the corners of a 90-foot diamond. 

Players on the batting team take turns hitting against the pitcher of the fielding team, which tries to stop them from scoring runs by getting hitters out in any of several ways. A player on the batting team can stop at any of the bases and later advance via a teammate's hit or other means. The teams switch between batting and fielding whenever the fielding team records three outs. One turn at bat for each team constitutes an inning and nine innings make up a professional game. The team with the most runs at the end of the game wins.

When referring to the ball and not the sport, use [[baseball (object)|baseball (object)]].
