A type of large late 19th century to mid 20th century oceangoing [[warship|warship]] characterized by its heavy armor and large guns that was ultimately rendered obsolete by advances in airplane and missile technology. 

Battleships of this time period can be roughly divided into handful of different categories:
- Pre-dreadnought - usually 4 main battery guns mounted in 2 twin turrets one fore and one aft (with some variations, French for example were quite fond of single turrets and Germans built one class of pre-dreads with 3 twin turrets all centerline), featured large secondary and tertiary batteries of small to medium scale guns meant to compensate the low rate of fire large guns had during this time period and allow ship to engage smaller targets like torpedo boats and destroyers, and heavy armor. Examples: British Majestic-class and Imperial Japanese Navy's Mikasa (sole surviving example of this type of ship).
- Semi-dreadnought - type of advanced pre-dreadnought that mounted larger guns  (usually in 8" to 10" range instead of around 6") as their secondary battery than earlier pre-dreadnoughts, were rendered obsolete were quickly by dreadnought battleships. Examples: British Lord Nelson-class and American Kearsarge-class. 
- Dreadnought battleship -  Inspired by data gathered from [[russo-japanese war|russo-japanese war]] and major technical advanced that had taken place in areas of fire control, capital ship gun rate of fire, and machinery development during late 1890s and early 1900s world's navies were looking towards building all big gun battleships. Ultimately First Sea Lord Baron John Fisher's brainchild HMS Dreadnought was the first of these ships to be completed and gave her name to all ships of this type. When HMS Dreadnought first entered service she was superior in speed, armor, and armaments to all pre-existing battleships in the world and rendered they all obsolete. Characteristics of dreadnought battleships were: main battery of 8 to 16 11" or 12" guns mounted usually in twin turrets (Italians, Russians, and Austro-Hungarians had ships with triple turrets), secondary battery in 3" to 6" range, and speed around 21 knots when compared to pre-dreadnoughs which tend to make between 15 and 18 knots. Examples: British HMS Dreadnought, HMS Agincourt, and Italian Dante Alighieri.
- Super-Dreadnought battleship - What happens when even dreadnoughts aren't enough and you need for one reason or another build ships superior to them? You arm your new battleships with significantly larger guns. When compared to dreadnoughts super-dreadnoughts are characterized by their larger guns (between 13.5" and 16"), and, to us, more normal looking turret layouts; no longer were battleships sporting wing turrets and super-firing was widely adopted. Examples: British Orion-class (first super-dreadnoughts) and American New Mexico-class.
- Fast battleship - Result of combining the speed of a [[battlecruiser|battlecruiser]] with the armor and armaments of a battleship. This type of ship first emerged during WW1 with the British Queen Elizabeth-class battleships (designed to make 24 knots which was estimated to be enough to keep up with earlier Imperial German battlecruisers in combat conditions) but really got popular during 1930s and WW2. Examples: British Queen Elizabeth-class (arguably should be considered plain old super-dreadnoughts by WW2),  American Iowa-class, and Japanese Nagato-class (capable of making 26.5 knots when commissioned which made them fastest non-battlecruiser capital ships in the world for almost 20 years).
- Treaty battleship - a battleship built under limitations of Washington Naval Treaty. 1st London Naval Treaty, or 2nd London Naval Treaty all of which heavily restricted building of new capital ships. Treaty battleships were characterized by their limited size and thus various compromises that brought to their designs. While this meant that they weren't exactly the best battleships ever built they still played major role in WW2 and ended up engaging&sinking number of vessels during that war. Examples: British Nelson-class (first treaty battleships, limited in their size and armament by Washington Naval Treaty) and American North Carolina-class (2nd London Naval Treaty).
- Super battleship - not an official term but is sometimes used in casual conversations to describe a number of extremely large battleships either designed or, in case of Japanese, built during late 1930s and early 1940s. These vessels were characterized by their massive sizes, impressive armor&armament, and utter impracticality in a world in which [[aircraft carrier|aircraft carrier]]s had became the dominant type of surface warship. Examples: Japanese Yamato-class and (never built) American Montana-class.

A 1996 [[transformers|transformers]] series that served as a massive departure from the series' norm at the time. It was fully animated in [[3d|3d]], focused on [[animal|animal]] alt forms rather than vehicles, and featured two new factions - the benevolent [[maximal|Maximals]] and evil [[predacon|Predacons]]. The series opens with the two groups crash landing on prehistoric Earth, and scanning nearby animals to use as their alt forms. The series is especially well regarded by fans and critics alike, and won a Daytime Emmy Award in 1998.

The Japanese dub of the series split the show into two parts, the second being titled *Beast Wars Metals*. The localization is notorious for taking immense liberties with, and at times ignoring elements of the source material, to the point of it being considered a gag dub by most fans. 

The series was followed up by [[beast machines|beast machines]], and had two Japan-exclusive spinoffs in [[beast wars ii|beast wars ii]] and [[beast wars neo|beast wars neo]].

Belldandy is a character in the [[aa megami-sama|aa megami-sama]] manga/anime series. She is the middle of three goddesses who come to Earth to reside with [[morisato keiichi|morisato keiichi]], and serves as his primary love interest. Initially, Keiichi thinks that her offer to grant him a wish was a prank by his senpai so, he makes a joke asking her to stay with him forever. However, Belldandy actually grants the request as a legitimate wish, and soon enough her sisters show up to see what's going on. 

Her older sister is [[urd (aa megami-sama)|urd (aa megami-sama)]], although they only share the same father, making them half sisters. Despite that, both she and her younger sister, [[skuld (aa megami-sama)|skuld (aa megami-sama)]] don't seem to mind that, and treat Urd as if they were full blooded sisters. Belldandy's younger sister looks up to her "oneesama" as Belldandy seems to be the ideal goddess, although it should be noted that despite her sweet and gentle personality, Belldandy can be quite competitive and even shows signs of jealousy whenever someone gets too close to Keiichi. Still, the vast majority of the time, Belldandy remains calm and also displays a rather mature personality, even more so than some of the older goddesses and demons in the series.

Voiced by [[inoue kikuko|inoue kikuko]].

Japanese title: 崩壊学園 (Houkai Gakuen)

A Chinese smartphone game developed by Mihoyo about three cute girls trying to make their way out from zombie apocalypse; part of the [[honkai (series)|honkai (series)]] series.

Originally just 崩坏学园 (Benghuai Xueyuan) ~ The End of School, known in English as Zombiegal Kawaii, before it was updated into Benghuai Xueyuan 2.

Since the two games are mostly unrelated, unless it's a collaboration, **do not** tag [[honkai impact 3rd|honkai impact 3rd]] when uploading posts from official sites ("Bilibili":[https://space.bilibili.com/133934], "Twitter":[https://twitter.com/Houkaigakuen],...) or posts that have **崩坏学园2**/**崩壊学園**/**Guns GirlZ** logo.

BeReal (stylized as BeReal.) is a French messaging app released in 2020, developed by Alexis Barreyat and Kévin Perreau. Its main feature is a daily notification that encourages users to share photos with friends of themselves and their day to day life given a randomly selected two-minute window every day. Critics noted its emphasis on authenticity, which some felt crossed the line into the mundane. The name "BeReal" is a pun. Its primary reference relates to its focus on users uploading unpolished photos, while also being a pun of the term b-reel.

An ongoing seinen dark fantasy action/horror manga series by [[miura kentarou|miura kentarou]] that has been adapted into a 25-episode anime, a film trilogy, and summer 2016 TV anime series.

It follows the story of [[guts (berserk)|guts (berserk)]], the Black Swordsman, who wanders the earth fighting off demons that are drawn to the [[brand of sacrifice|brand of sacrifice]] mark on his neck. Guts seeks revenge against [[griffith (berserk)|griffith (berserk)]], his former best friend, whose betrayal led to the loss of Guts' hand and eye, and nearly everyone he cared about.

Miura passed away on May 6, 2021, leaving the series unfinished.  On June 7, 2022 it was announced that Miura's Studio Gaga under the supervision of Kouji Mori, a close friend of Miura, would resume the series utilizing material left behind or talked about by Miura before his passing.

In [[berserk|berserk]], the Berserker Armor is a cursed suit of [[armor|armor]] that grants its user incredible strength and endurance by allowing its wearer to bypass the normal subconscious limits that prevent him from injuring himself when using his full strength. It can temporarily fix injuries by binding bleeding wounds, reinforcing broken bones and fixing dislocated joints. It can also send its user into a berserker rage where he cannot tell friend from foe. Long-term use of the armor can cause chronic mental deterioration, as well as severe physical effects.

When in Berserker mode, the armor takes on the appearance of the user's inner "beast." For [[guts (berserk)|guts (berserk)]], the current wearer and user of the armor, this is the [[beast of darkness (berserk)|beast of darkness (berserk)]], the demonic hellhound-like wolf that represents all the hatred and evil that dwells within his soul, which becomes stronger every time Guts uses the armor.

A [[the lego group|LEGO]] [[toy|toy]]line of constraction figures that ran from 2000 to 2010. The series features many [[science fiction|science fiction]] elements as well as influence from Maori aesthetics and language, and is notable for having incredibly expansive lore and an ongoing story throughout the line's lifetime. The lore was spread across a variety of mediums, including books, comics, video games, flash games, podcasts, and 4 feature-length films.

LEGO rebooted the line in 2015, with a new continuity and completely different art style. The reboot featured several books, graphic novels, animated web shorts, and an animated series on [[netflix|netflix]], before being discontinued in 2016.

Despite the line being in a dormant state and having no new official content releases or reprints of previous sets, the series has retained a large fanbase that consistently creates new content.

A Japanese term literally meaning **beautiful teenage boy**. The equivalent English concept is **pretty boy**. The term describes an aesthetic that can be found in disparate areas in Asia: a teenage boy, around 13 to 18 years old, whose beauty (and sexual appeal) transcends the boundary of gender or sexual orientation. Bishounen characters are fairly common in manga and anime; a heavy number of male characters show subtle signs of the bishounen style, such as slender eyes or a feminine face. 

Bishounen are usually drawn delicately, with long limbs, silky or flowing hair, and slender eyes with long eyelashes that can sometimes extend beyond the face. It's best to tag images that focus on the character's beauty, so there tends to be a heavier emphasis on solo or duo images here. Group images are fine, so long as the majority of the males exemplify this trait.

As the name suggests, the term is best used when you can still tell that the character is a male. If there are remarkable feminine traits, consider adding [[androgynous|androgynous]]. For characters where their feminine traits are at the point of making you believe that they're a female, use [[otoko no ko|otoko no ko]] instead.

Note that with [[genderswap (ftm)|female-to-male genderswaps]], this tag can apply if they possess the above-mentioned traits.

In English-speaking circles, bishounen is used somewhat more loosely than it is in Japan, effectively used for any male character with pseudo androgynous beauty, regardless of whether they are "shounen" or not (so variants covering those older than 18, ala biseinen, bichuunen, and bidanshi, find themselves incorporated, as well as those younger than 13).

The **biwa** (琵琶) is a Japanese short-necked fretted [[lute (instrument)|lute (instrument)]], often used in narrative storytelling. The biwa is the chosen instrument of Benten, goddess of music, eloquence, poetry, and education in Japanese Shinto.

The main point of differentiation between the biwa and the [[pipa (instrument)|pipa (instrument)]] (visually) is that the biwa has a bent neck, while the pipa has a straight neck, like an [[acoustic guitar|acoustic guitar]].

A 1982 American [[science fiction|science fiction]] film, directed by Ridley Scott and starring [[harrison ford|harrison ford]], [[rutger hauer|rutger hauer]], [[edward james olmos|edward james olmos]], [[daryl hannah|daryl hannah]] and [[sean young|sean young]].

The screenplay, written by Hampton Fancher and David Peoples, is loosely based on the 1968 novel [[do androids dream of electric sheep?|do androids dream of electric sheep?]] by American sci-fi writer [[philip k. dick|philip k. dick]].

While not initially a success with North American audiences, ***Blade Runner*** was very popular internationally and became a cult film. It was a hit in Japan, where it greatly influenced the "[[cyberpunk|cyberpunk]]" look of later sci-fi anime and manga like [[akira (manga)|akira (manga)]], [[bubblegum crisis|bubblegum crisis]], [[armitage iii|armitage iii]], [[ghost in the shell|ghost in the shell]] and [[appleseed|appleseed]] among many many others. 

The movie's dark style and futuristic designs by [[syd mead|syd mead]] have served as a benchmark and its influence can be seen in many subsequent science fiction films, anime, video games, and television programs.

A sequel called [[blade runner 2049|blade runner 2049]] was released in most countries on October 6, 2017. It was released in Japan on October 27, 2017.

Blake Belladonna is one of the main characters of [[rwby|rwby]], a 3DCG series produced by Rooster Teeth. 

Blake is the "B" in RWBY, and is associated with the color black. Her character design is inspired by both of the eponymous characters in the fairy tale [[beauty and the beast|beauty and the beast]].
Blake is somewhat aloof, enjoys reading, and seems to have a checkered past. 

#### Abilities
She wields a [[katana|katana]]/[[cleaver|cleaver]]/[[handgun|handgun]]/[[kama (weapon)|kama]] hybrid weapon named [[gambol shroud|gambol shroud]] (officially classified as a "Variant Ballistic Chain Scythe"). Using the [[ribbon|ribbon]] around her arm as a chain, it resembles a [[kusarigama|kusarigama]]. Her symbol is a belladonna (aka deadly nightshade) [[flower|flower]]. Her semblance (special ability) produces shadow clones. 

#### Physical characteristics
Blake has [[yellow eyes|yellow eyes]] and [[long hair|long]] [[black hair|black hair]]. 

||Her bow hides a pair of [[cat ears|cat ears]].||

She stands 5' 6" tall (including high heels).

#### Attire
Blake tends to wear black and white clothing. She usually has a [[black bow|black]] [[hair bow|hair bow]] on top of her head. Her default outfit includes a small [[black scarf|black scarf]] around her neck, a black [[vest|vest]] with long [[coattails|coattails]] on top of a white [[sleeveless shirt|sleeveless shirt]] that leaves her [[bare shoulders|shoulders]] and [[midriff|midriff]] bare, a black [[single detached sleeve|detached sleeve]] on her left arm, black [[arm ribbon|arm ribbon]]s wrapped around both forearms, [[white shorts|white]] [[shorts|shorts]] (sometimes depicted with [[garter straps|garter straps]]) [[pantyhose under shorts|over]] [[black pantyhose|black pantyhose]] (with her belladonna symbol printed on), and [[black footwear|black]] [[high heels|high heels]]. 

Her Beacon [[school uniform|school uniform]] consists of a [[white shirt|white]] [[blouse|blouse]] with [[neck ribbon|neck ribbon]], brown [[blazer|blazer]], and [[plaid skirt|plaid skirt]]. She retains her black hair bow.

A small bag full of [[blood|blood]], which has been collected from the patient or from a blood donor in order to replace that patient's blood should there be a lot of blood loss during surgery, or from exsanguination due to a critical [[injury|injury]].

Different patients/donors' blood is collected, analyzed and grouped according to blood type, of which there are four: [A, B, AB, and O](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_blood_group_systems,) depending upon inherited antigens. There is also the + and - status to indicate if the [Rh factor](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rh_blood_group_system) (or Rhesus factor) is present.

Blood bags are often seen hanging from [[iv stand|intravenous stands]] in hospitals near the patient's bed.

A Korean mobile gacha RPG created by Nexon Games (formerly NAT Games before merging), developed by MX Studio, and published by Shanghai Yostar (for Japan) and [[nexon|nexon]] (for global release). Initially referred to as Project MX during its early development phase.

The game revolves around a player character, known simply as "[[sensei (blue archive)|sensei (blue archive)]]" (先生 / teacher); assumes the responsibility of managing the city of Kivotos following the unexpected disappearance of its General Student Council president. The player's role includes resolving local problems, supervising students, and assisting different schools, all while uncovering the reasons behind the GSC president's departure. The game presents the gameplay in a 3D isometric perspective, automating most actions; player interaction primarily involves activating "Skill Cards" to unleash students' special skills.

The story begins with a prologue, and each set has volumes; starting from the 1st volume (which is Abydos) until the 5th volume (which focuses on Hyakkiyako). Main story expansions may update every week or month.

The [[blue archive the animation|Anime adaptation]] aired on April 7, 2024. The inaugural season featured the Foreclosure Task Force and Handyman 68, placing significant emphasis on the game's lore in the first volume.

Blue Archive also worked with other people on projects besides the game, such as [[world of warships|world of warships]].

**"Blue" Mary Ryan**, commonly known as **"Blue Mary"**, is a [[fatal fury|fatal fury]] and [[the king of fighters|the king of fighters]] character. She is a detective primarily serving in South Town.

She has [[short hair|short]], [[blonde hair|blonde]] [[straight hair|straight hair]] and [[blue eyes|blue eyes]]. She wears a red bra-like [[crop top|crop top]] (later switched to blue in Real Bout Fatal Fury Special, a [[red shirt|red]] [[cropped shirt|cropped shirt]] in The King of Fighters), blue gloves that go with her [[baggy pants|baggy pants]], brown boots that prevent her pants from hanging loose to the bottom, and a bomber jacket. Her most famous accessory is an oversized brown belt she wears on her hips.

Mary's fighting style is Sambo - a Russian hybrid combat style. Apart from assorted strikes and grapples, including a [[german suplex|German suplex]], her specialties include takedowns and submissions, including limb locks.

[[terry bogard|terry bogard]] is a close friend of hers, even teased as a love interest at times, though she is hesitant to commit due to the death of a previous lover. Mary is noted to have an alternate personality that comes out when she gets frustrated, one that is more sadistic in nature. She has a pet dog named Anton.

Blue Mary's appearance is openly acknowledged as inspired by [[android 18|android 18]] from [[dragon ball z|dragon ball z]].

Blue Oath (alternatively Blue Wars or Blue Vows) was a shipgirl-themed Chinese smartphone game released in China by Babeltime. A Japanese version was published by ZephyrusGames, and was available on the Android and iOS Japanese app stores. The game ran on Android, Apple iOS and Windows-based devices. By August 2023, all of the game's servers were shut down.

Gameplay was similar to [[kantai collection|kantai collection]] Arcade, although with both minor and major changes, such as an affection system (and allowing marriage at 100 affection instead of Level 99), Hot Springs for morale recovery, the ability to select damaged skins for the ship girls’ appearance and in-app purchases.

The bluebirds are a group of medium-sized, mostly insectivorous or omnivorous birds in the thrush family. Their plumage is either entirely blue, or blue with rose-beige chest/belly. 

The bluebird as harbinger of happiness is symbology found in many cultures, from Chinese to Native American, and may date back thousands of years. Songwriters frequently portray the bluebird as a muse.

Do not confuse with [[blue jay|blue jay]]s.

A photographic effect where circular [[depth of field|out-of-focus]] points of light appear in the background of the image.

Bokeh can represent known light sources in the background of an image, but can also occur in seemingly random places all over the image. The latter, known as [orbs](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orb_%28optics%29,) are from light reflected off of particles in the air which would otherwise not be visible.

[[lens flare|lens flare]] artifacts can look similar to bokeh, but are due to bright light being reflected inside the camera, and don't line up with the original light source (which may not even be visible in the image).

A lethal [[kendo|kendo]] practice [[sword|sword]] made of solid, heavy wood. It's shaped and balanced like a [[katana|katana]]. 

A **bokken** is a wooden [[weapon|weapon]] normally used for solo training, **not for sparring**. For that, the [[shinai|shinai]] is used, as sparring with a bokken will usually lead to broken bones... or worse. 

Legendary [[samurai|samurai]] swordmaster Musashi Miyamoto (1584? - May 19, 1645) fought and killed [[katana|katana]]-wielding rival samurai by using just a bokken against them.

**Bousouzoku** (暴走族, lit. "violent running gang") is a subculture of Japanese motorcycle gangs.

The stereotypical look consists of round or wrap-around [[sunglasses|sunglasses]], long [[hachimaki|hachimaki]] headbands with battle slogans, and a [[pompadour|pompadour]] hairstyle.

Other styles consist of a military-styled [[school uniform|school uniform]] (a [[gakuran|gakuran]]) or [[jumpsuit|jumpsuit]], with the gang's name on the back, and a [[sarashi|sarashi]]. Usually, any oddities on a male's school uniform is a sign of gang activity or rebellion that falls into boso-style.

Their vehicle of choice is either a large [[motorcycle|motorcycle]], or a [[car|car]], both with extensive styling and modifications (such as [[neon lights|neon lights]], low loading, etc.).

Braviary is a large, avian Pokémon with dark red feathers on its back and dark blue feathers on its underside. Its tail feathers are red, turning to yellow, and then blue at the tips. Braviary's legs are long and thick with yellow feet that each have a digit facing backward, and three facing forward. Each digit is tipped by a short, thick, black claw.

Braviary has a long, thick beak with a blue cere. On either side of the cere are Braviary's eyes, which are black with small white pupils. Sprouting from above the eyes are three large, white feathers. At the base of the feathers is a red, three-pointed design that is spread across all three feathers. On each side of Braviary's face, sprouting out from behind the feathers on its forehead, are an additional three white feathers pointing horizontally and downward. Behind the three feathers on its head is a large plume of white feathers, extending most of the way down its neck. These features combined resemble a [Native American war bonnet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States.)

Bubble tea (also known as "pearl milk tea", "tapioca tea", "boba tea", or simply "boba") is a type of [[tea|tea]]-based [[drink|drink]] invented in Taiwan. It consists of a mixture of tea, milk, or other flavorings, plus small black tapioca balls ("boba") that float at the bottom of the drink. The drink usually comes with an extra-large [[drinking straw|straw]], used to suck up and chew the tapioca balls.

In 2019, bubble tea experienced a sudden boom in popularity in Japan, with a corresponding rise in fanart featuring the drink.

Basically, in a normal gun, the [[magazine (weapon)|magazine (weapon)]] is in front and the trigger is behind. In a bullpup firearm, the trigger is in front and the magazine is behind.

C2 Kikan debuted in Comiket C75 (Winter 2008) with a doujin about food, introducing various types of food through anime personifications. They were interviewed by various TV programs for it at the time, including タモリ倶楽部 from Asahi TV and MAG・ネット from NHK. They later published several military-related doujinshi.

It's possible that the name of 'C2 Kikan' came from Final Fantasy: Unlimited, where Tanaka Kensuke, one of the main members of C2 Kikan, was the anime's general producer for, when he worked in Square Soft back in 2001.

When Tanaka Kensuke and his friend, who was working within Kadokawa Games talked with Michio Okamiya, whom he once worked with back in Square Soft, they came up with the idea of the KanColle browser game.

d: A dining facility in large institution like a school, office, camp, hospital etc. where the members of that institution come to eat, although public cafeterias exist, mostly as a cheap dining option. Cafeterias usually consist of a serving counter or counters along one wall near the entrance where one pushes along a tray and is served portions of food by the staff. The rest of the room usually consists of seating often consisting of large multi-seat tables. The cafeteria fare generally consists of a few set meals of an entree and various side dishes to complement that entree, often there is a flat fee for a meal, although one is charged for extra portions or optional dishes like deserts. Another common price scheme is each dish has it's own price and a customer chooses which dishes to purchase. Commonly a cafeteria will have a main line (or lines) consisting of a hot meal at a flat price and an a la cart line consisting of individually priced dishes like salads and sandwiches. Refers to two things: the 1926 short story that gives the [[cthulhu mythos|cthulhu mythos]] its titular cosmic entity, [[cthulhu|cthulhu]], and the tabletop role-playing game based on said mythos by Chaosium, often abbreviated as CoC, which has been releasing since 1981. For posts which refer to the short story specifically, tag it with the mythos tag.

In Japan, Call of Cthulhu is the predominant TRPG (table talk RPG) of choice in the 21st century, over Dungeons and Dragons which previously dominated TRPG circles there, building off the TRPG fan culture tradition of 'replays' (novelizations of sessions, often paired with visuals to go with the text) with play videos (prerecorded or live) on Niconico and YouTube (ex. [[yukkuri-tachi no cthulhu no yobikoe|yukkuri-tachi no cthulhu no yobikoe]]). Combined with general continued popularity for 20th century western authors such as Lovecraft, an accessible and easy-to-learn 'Basic Roleplaying' system which allows players to shape the scenarios as they wish (leading to many non-combat/horror-oriented scenarios), publisher support, player-created tools (such as CCFOLIA), and domestically-exclusive scenarios, CoC dominates. In turn, this has resulted in much fanart based on Japanese scenarios.

**Cammy White** is a character in the [[street fighter|street fighter]] series. Her *nom de guerre* is the codename **Killer Bee** (christened in [[street fighter zero (series)|Street Fighter Zero 3]] and kept for herself afterwards). She first appeared in the fighting game [[street fighter ii (series)|Super Street Fighter II]] (1993) as one of the titular "New Challengers," the four new characters introduced in that title. She is the second female character in the Street Fighter series, following [[chun-li|chun-li]]. Cammy is a female clone of [[m. bison|m. bison]], originally serving within his organization Shadaloo as both Bison's potential replacement body should his original body fail, and, until then, the leader of the [[shadaloo dolls|"Dolls"]] - Bison's personal unit of brainwashed bodyguards and underlings. She later went rogue after her encounter with [[dhalsim|dhalsim]] nullified Bison's Psycho Powered mind control. As of [[street fighter ii (series)|street fighter ii (series)]] onward to the present in [[street fighter 6|street fighter 6]], she serves as a member of Delta Red, a British special forces unit with connections to MI6. She has made it her personal mission to locate, rescue, and rehabilitate the Dolls. She collaborates closely with most of the other World Warriors on her assignments, notably [[chun-li|chun-li]]. Trained extensively in close-quarters combat, Cammy likes to strike with quick, sharp attacks like a stinging bee (hence her codename) and use takedowns to immobilize and cripple her foes. Her signature techniques include the *Spiral Arrow* and *Cannon Spike/Strike* - both flying kick attacks that send Cammy lunging feet first at sharp angles, whether straight forward, up into the sky, or down from the air - as well as the *Hooligan Combination*, where she hurls herself into close quarters to either grapple the opponent to the ground or strike from odd angles. #### Appearance - _(post #939647: [[street fighter ii (series)|street fighter ii (series)]]
"Delta Red" (original))_ - _(post #1291102: [[street fighter zero (series)|street fighter zero (series)]]
"Killer Bee")_ - _(post #386341: [[street fighter iv (series)|street fighter iv (series)]])_ - _(post #2041295: [[street fighter v|street fighter v]])_ - _(post #6369826: [[street fighter 6|street fighter 6]])_ She has 2 well known outfits/appearances depending on the Street Fighter timeline, although both have her wearing some manner of [[highleg leotard|highleg leotard]] and red gauntlet-like gloves, sporting long [[blonde hair|blonde]] [[twin braids|twin braids]], and showing off a long [[scar|scar]] on her left cheek. Her original "Delta Red" appearance, worn in every instance outside her Alpha/Zero appearances prior to Street Fighter 6, has her in a green [[highleg leotard|highleg leotard]] with a small triangle badge above her right breast and a red [[beret|beret]]. [[street fighter v|street fighter v]] adds a [[chest harness|chest harness]] and a [[thigh holster|thigh holster]] on her right leg, but loses the green patches of [[bodypaint|bodypaint]] originally seen on her legs. The bodypaint does make a return in Street Fighter 6 as part of her Street Fighter V form/"younger self" alternate skin. Her appearance in [[fortnite|fortnite]] as a Gaming Legends outfit skin adds [[pantyhose|pantyhose]] with a [[camouflage|camouflage]] pattern to her Street Fighter V outfit. In her Alpha/Zero "Killer Bee" appearance, which takes place during the time she was a member of M. Bison's Dolls, she instead wears a light blue long-sleeved [[ribbed leotard|ribbed]] [[highleg leotard|highleg leotard]] with a matching color [[garrison cap|garrison cap]] and a small yellow necktie with a black armband on her left arm. Like in her original form, she has bodypaint patches on her legs, except they are blue to match her leotard and somewhat [[lightning bolt symbol|lightning bolt]]-shaped. In [[street fighter 6|street fighter 6]], Cammy has [[short hair|cut her hair short]], and she now sports a [[blue jacket|blue]] [[cropped jacket|bolero]] with [[union jack|union jack]] print, [[black sports bra|black sports bra]] and black [[yoga pants|yoga pants]]. ##### Street Fighter V alternate costumes - [[story mode cammy|story mode cammy]] - [[battle outfit cammy|battle outfit cammy]] - [[capcom pro tour cammy|capcom pro tour cammy]] - Swimsuit (August 2016) - [[halloween cammy|halloween cammy]] - [[school uniform cammy|school uniform cammy]] - Nostalgia (Street Fighter IV Complete Alternate / 1; September 2017) - [[dolls cammy|dolls cammy]] (Street Fighter Zero) - [[holiday cammy|holiday cammy]] - Cannon Spike ([[gunspike|gunspike]]; June 2018) - [[track suit cammy|track suit cammy]] - [[killer bee cammy|killer bee cammy]] (Street Fighter Zero) ##### Alternate costumes elsewhere - [[final fight streetwise|final fight streetwise]]: [[streetwise cammy|streetwise cammy]] - [[street fighter iv (series)|street fighter iv (series)]]: [[m. bison (cosplay)|m. bison (cosplay)]] cosplay (Street Fighter IV Super Complete Alternate / 2) - [[power rangers: legacy wars|power rangers: legacy wars]]: [[stinging crane ranger|stinging crane ranger]] - [[fortnite|fortnite]]: [[fortnite cammy|fortnite cammy]] #### See also - [[cammy stretch (meme)|cammy stretch (meme)]] #### External links - Street Fighter V: [Cammy (Costumes)](https://game.capcom.com/cfn/sfv/character/cammy/costume?lang=en)

In aeronautics, control surfaces that are forward of an [[airplane|airplane]]'s main wing (and center of lift/gravity) and act similarly to tailplanes to provide pitch stability and control. 

The term **canard** is derived from the French word for "duck," which was applied to early canard-using aircraft, as observers thought they resembled ducks in flight.

The traditional term for a set of multiple decorative candlesticks, each of which often holds a [[candle|candle]] on each of multiple arms or branches connected to a column or pedestal. A single member of such a set is known as a candelabrum.

An object made of [[wax|wax]] with a [[string|string]] running from top to bottom which is set alight. Its most common shape is cylindrical.

Has seen more use in the past, but it is still used as a [[light|light]] source in some places, in religious ceremonies and as a symbol of different things such as hope.

If the candles are worn strapped to the head with a [[headband|headband]], there might be a reference to the youkai [[hashihime|hashihime]], or the curse ritual [[ushi no koku mairi|ushi no koku mairi]] (which also involves a [[mallet|mallet]] or [[hammer|hammer]], a [[straw doll|straw doll]] and [[nail (hardware)|nail (hardware)]]s).

Settings where [[candle|candles]] provide the majority of ambient light. This makes for dark scenes with amber-colored light radiating out from the candles themselves.

A device that holds one or more [[candle|candle]]s in place, also known as a **candlestick** or **candleholder**. A candlestand for several candles is called a **[[candelabra|candelabra]]**. They can be simple or highly ornate, and they can be made of various materials, from wood to brass to silver.  A subtype of candlestick is **chamberstick**, a short candlestick with a large pan to catch wax and handle, that is used in carrying a candle to the bedroom.

The [[chandelier|chandelier]] originated as a large candlestand designed to be suspended from a ceiling.

The [[menorah|menorah]] is a candelabra with particular religious significance.

A captive bead ring (ball closure ring) is a type of body [[piercing|piercing]] jewelry. The captive bead or ball fits into a small opening in the circle of the ring. The bead is slightly larger than this opening and has small indentations or depressions that correspond to the ring's end-points so that it may fit snugly against them, thus completing the circuit of the ring. Often, a hole is drilled through the bead to allow easier fitting.

Captive bead rings can also have little accessories.

The vast majority of posts under this tag reference the visual part of the flash, which comes from the opening animation of the Popotan game and has nothing to do with the Caramell song. For tagging purposes a cart is an animal or human driven two or more wheeled vehicle used for carrying loads that is pulled or pushed. They're similar to carriages, but  the carriage tag covers vehicles specifically design for passenger transport, while the cart tag is intended for vehicles designed to transport cargo.

A true cart is an open two-wheeled vehicle for carrying loads that is pulled by animals or humans, for tagging purposes these will be tagged as a "pullcart".

The term "cart" over time has evolved to also refer to a variety of small wheeled vehicles that are pushed or pulled and include vehicles that have more than two wheels.

The art of fashioning or producing items by cutting into or shaping solid material, such as wood, plastic, or [[fruit|fruit]]. [[pumpkin|pumpkin]]s have one side carved into [[jack-o'-lantern|jack-o'-lantern]]s for [[halloween|halloween]].

Five artists contribute to this site: [[tabigarasu|tabigarasu]] (たびがらす), [[takeda yukimura|takeda yukimura]] (剛田幸村), [[nanashino|nanashino]] (ななしの), pau (パぅ), and [[midori boushi|midori boushi]] (緑帽子).  On the site, their images are usually signed as such, and the gallery page indicates which image is by which artist as well.

Images are signed in the following format

Only the date given (ie http://www.caryo.net/080122_p2.jpg) = tabigarasu
Initials mb given before the date (ie http://www.caryo.net/mbmari-panntu.gif) = midori_boushi
Character name only (ie http://www.caryo.net/supa6.jpg) = Nanashino (seems to have changed to na_copyrightN.ext since at least oct 2012)
Date given then tam at the end (ie http://www.caryo.net/080311tam.jpg) = Takeda_Yukimura

When parts of the image (typically graphic or sensitive contents such as sexual organs, gore, or offensive symbolism) were obscured, typically to comply with censorship laws.

On Danbooru, this typically encompasses various Japanese pornographic materials that were censored as a result of the Japanese law. Techniques that prevent viewing sexual parts, usually [[pussy|vaginas]], [[penis|penis]]es and [[dildo|dildo]]s but occasionally [[nipples|nipples]]. Note that the [[anus|anus]] is not usually considered a sexual part in Japanese censorship.  

Common forms include [[mosaic censoring|mosaics]], [[bar censor|black bars]], mysterious [[light censor|white lights]], inverted colors, shaded bars, and the infamous [[invisible penis|invisible penis]]. [[tentacles|tentacles]] or phallic objects are commonly used to resemble genitals and generally don't need to be censored, though the point of intercourse with a vagina does. 

For obstructions that are *internal* to the picture, like a lock of [[hair censor|hair]] that just happens to cover the genitals, use the tag [[convenient censoring|convenient censoring]] instead of censored.

#### History

Obscenity in Japan has been illegal to some degree since the 19th century Meiji Era, but the Criminal Code of 1907 relating to obscenity was reinforced (or at least not overturned as other laws restricting freedom were) when American General MacArthur established Japan's modern laws after WW2.

> *Criminal Code of Japan, Article 175. (Distribution of Obscene Objects)* 
> 
> A person who distributes, sells or displays in public an obscene document, drawing or other objects shall be punished by imprisonment with work for not more than 2 years, a fine of not more than 2,500,000 yen or a petty fine. The same shall apply to a person who possesses the same for the purpose of sale.

Contrary to popular beliefs, Article 175 *does not* enforce the censorship of pornographic materials. Rather, it is the publisher of these pornographic material who "self-censored" their work as a form of loophole around Article 175, as this technically transformed the work into an "erotic" material by not fully showing the genitalia, which results into less restrictions from the law. This practice was first done by the Japanese [[pornography|pornographic]] aka the "Adult Video" (AV) industry in 1970s and has spread to other mediums.

Note that the law relates to distribution within Japan; it is not illegal for Japan-made porn intended **only** for export to be uncensored.

Obscenity laws are gradually being relaxed, but not eliminated. [[pubic hair|pubic hair]] is no longer required to be censored, for example. There are now attempts to repeal the Meiji-era/post-WW2 censorship law, though this has yet to reach deliberation.

A chaise longue (French for "long chair") is an upholstered [[couch|sofa]] in the shape of a chair that is long enough to support the legs.

It is also known as a "chaise lounge" (Primarily North American) due to a misspelling of the name during its introduction in North America.  Given the purpose of the chair was to lounge around on, the misspelled naming has stuck.

The outdoor furniture called [[lounge chair|sun loungers/lounge chairs]] are also referred to as "chaise lounges" in North America, likely due to the similar shape.

The French now use the term "chaise longue" to refer to any kind of long reclining chair, such as deck chairs and sun loungers, but for tagging purposes this tag is only for the indoor furniture.

An often ornate lighting fixture that hangs from a [[ceiling|ceiling]]. Some chandeliers have arrays of crystal prisms to scatter light throughout a room. Due to their size and the amount of light they produce, chandeliers are usually installed as focal points in large rooms such as [[dining room|dining rooms]], lounges, or [[stairs|staircases]].

This tag is distinct from [[hanging light|hanging light]] in that hanging lights are of simple design and only have one or two lamps each, whereas chandeliers are large fixtures that branch out into multiple lamps.

A chángmìngsuǒ (长命锁) or “longevity lock” is a lock-shaped ornament in China made of metal and hung around a child’s neck to pray for longevity.

Hmong girls often wear large silver locks(chang ming suo) on their chests, which are the main accessories in Miao silver jewelry.

The "chang ming suo" was very popular in Han Chinese regions during the chinese Ming and Qing dynasties. It was believed that by putting this ornament on a child after birth, it could protect them from disasters and evil spirits, ensuring their peace and longevity

Charlotte "Shirley" E. Yeager (シャーロット・E・イェーガー, Shārotto E Iēgā?) is a witch of the [[501st joint fighter wing|501st joint fighter wing]]. She originates from [[liberion|liberion]]. Possibly in reference to model and photographer Bunny Yeager, Charlotte's familiar is the [[rabbit|rabbit]].

Magnanimous in character, tall and buxom in appearance, Charlotte ("Shirley" to her friends) is a thrill-seeker who is fascinated by speed. Concerned with cleanliness, Charlotte had her personal bath transported all the way to the [[strike witches|strike witches]]' [[britannia|britannia]] base when she was transferred from the Liberion Army 363rd Fighter Wing. She is strong, confident and sociable. She is good friends with [[francesca lucchini|francesca lucchini]]. She has an orange plane named Glamorous Shirley.

She is based on [Chuck Yeager](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_yeager,) and shares many characteristics with her archetype: Yeager was the first pilot to travel faster than sound in 1947, and would later break further speed and altitude records in his life; he was a mechanic, similar to Shirley's tinkering, and flew a plane he named the Glamorous Glennis.

A chemise is essentially a [[camisole|camisole]] that ends past the waist. Usually worn as an undergarment.

In modern usage, a chemise is generally a woman's garment that vaguely resembles the older shirts but is typically more delicate, and usually provocative. Most commonly the term refers to a loose-fitting, sleeveless undergarment or type of [[lingerie|lingerie]] which is unfitted at the waist. It can also refer to a short, sleeveless dress that hangs straight from the shoulders and fits loosely at the waist. A chemise typically does not have any buttons or other fasteners and is put on by either dropping it over the head or stepping into it and lifting it up.

As lingerie, a chemise is similar to a [[babydoll|babydoll]], which is also a short, loose-fitting, sleeveless garment. Typically, though, babydolls are more loose-fitting at the hips and are generally designed to more resemble a young girl's [[nightgown|nightgown]], although many modern styles have added various sexualizing features.

Small flowers of any of several trees of the genus Prunus, especially the Japanese Cherry (*Prunus serrulata*, the suffix a Latin rendering of *sakura*). Usually seen falling or scattered as [[petals|petals]].

Cherry blossoms, especially the [[pink flower|pink]] ones of the *Prunus serrulata*, are a significant visual motif in Japanese culture; as their period of flowering that lasts little more than a week during the spring is thought to symbolically convey an awareness of the brilliant, yet impermanent nature of life. The term *mono no aware* (物の哀れ, literally 'the pathos of things') was coined by 18th century scholar Motoori Norinaga to describe this concept as a theme found in classical Japanese literature, and associated it with the cherry blossom motif. 

The white-colored autumn and winter blossoms (冬桜, *fuyuzakura*) of the higan cherry tree (*Prunus subhirtella autumnalis*) are a notable variant, coming into bloom during those seasons. 

In anime and manga, besides straightforward symbolization of youth and verve, the [[flower (symbol)|symbol]] may be used to denote gentle and/or affectionate characters; though this usage can sometimes be ironic. 

In [[touken ranbu|touken ranbu]], cherry blossoms indicate that a character has a [[gameplay mechanics|buff]].

[[cherry tree|cherry tree]]s in anime art are almost always drawn in bloom, but the actual cherries don't grow until the blossoms are long gone. For images of cherry trees bearing fruit, search for cherry fruit tree.

Distinguished from [[plum blossoms|plum blossoms]] in that cherry petals have slits at the ends of the petals. Plum petal ends on the other hand are round ("see reference":/media_assets/7899985).

A form-fitting, Chinese-themed [[dress|dress]] that has [[side slit|side slit]]s up both legs.

The traditional China dress, more properly called a *cheongsam* (Cantonese) or *qipao* (Mandarin), was introduced in Qing-era China in the 1600s but did not evolve into its current form until the early 20th century. There are many styles, but it typically is a long, form-fitting dress with a [[mandarin collar|mandarin collar]], an asymmetric left-over-right opening, high-to-medium [[side slit|side slit]]s, and embellished with Chinese [[pankou|frog fasteners]] on the lapel and the collar. It may have any variety of sleeves. 

In anime they are often stylized to be more revealing than the traditional dress, being either very short, or having very long [[side slit|side slit]]s with a [[pelvic curtain|pelvic curtain]] that barely covers anything, or having [[cleavage cutout|cleavage]] or [[back cutout|back cutout]]s.

Don't use this tag for qipao-styled clothes that aren't dresses, such as shirts or vests. Use [[chinese clothes|chinese clothes]] instead. For example, [[hong meiling|hong meiling]]'s default outfit is not a dress.

There are various types of neckline in qipao. The most common type is the **Shanghai**-style neckline, which has an asymmetrical closure with frogs leading diagonally up to the collar. The **Beijing**-style collar is a simpler symmetrical design, with a frog closure directly beneath the collar. The **Jiangnan** style is similar to the Beijing style, but features a [[clothing cutout|hole]] right underneath the collar.

***Platycodon***, commonly called Chinese bellflower, is a genus of [[flower|flower]]ing plant in the [[bellflower|bellflower]] family (*Campanulaceae*), native to East Asia. The only member of the genus is *Platycodon grandiflorus*.

Chinese bellflower produces five-petaled, star-shaped flowers that are blue, purple, pink, or white in color. A notable feature is the [[bud|bud]], which swells like a balloon before opening into a star-shaped flower, earning the flower another common name - **balloon flower** (which is also a tag, but for literal balloons). The roots of the plant are edible and used in cooking.

Not to be confused with [[balloon flower|balloon flower]], a flower made by tying up a balloon. Also not to be confused with [[flower balloon|flower balloon]], a flower-shaped balloon.

A holiday celebrating the [[new year|new year]], also called "Spring Festival" (春节), in the traditional Chinese calendar, a lunisolar calendar, falling somewhere between January 21 and February 20. It is mainly celebrated in China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macao, in countries with significant Chinese populations, and in Chinatowns elsewhere. It is broadly called "Lunar New Year" because several other "new year" holidays such as Seollal (Korean New Year) and Tết (Vietnamese New Year) are also celebrated around the same time.

Before 1873, the Japanese had celebrated New Year's festivities around the same time as Chinese New Year. Since 1873, however, when Japan adopted the widely used Gregorian calendar, New Year's festivities are being held instead on January 1.

Many of the New year traditions are said to have originated from the legend of [[nian (mythology)|nian (mythology)]].

***Choujikuu Yousai MACROSS***, translated as *Super Spacetime Fortress Macross* (or more correctly, *Hyperspace Fortress Macross*), also known in English as *The Super Dimension Fortress Macross*, is the first anime television series of the [[macross|macross]] franchise that first aired in Japan on October 3, 1982. The weekly series lasted 36 episodes.

According to concept and fictional story creator [[kawamori shouji|kawamori shouji]] it depicts "a small love triangle against the backdrop of great [[battle|battle]]s" during the first human-[[alien|alien]] war. It is set in a fictional alternate history of Earth after the year 1999 and during the period of the years 2009-2012.

It is a classic and famous vintage [[science fiction|science fiction]] series that combines transformable real robot [[mecha|mecha]], epic apocalyptic [[space|space]] combat, wartime romance, and music. It features mechanical designs by [[miyatake kazutaka|miyatake kazutaka]] and Kawamori Shouji (both of Studio Nue) and character designs by [[mikimoto haruhiko|mikimoto haruhiko]] of Artland. 

According to the creators of the show the series was heavily inspired by [[mobile suit gundam|mobile suit gundam]] and [[uchuu senkan yamato|uchuu senkan yamato]], of which most of the production staff were fans.

Macross also created one of the first anime idols [[lynn minmay|lynn minmay]], turning her [[voice actor|voice actress]] [Mari Iijima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mari_Iijima) into an instant celebrity, and launching her musical career. 

Most of its animation (with edited content, revised dialogue and a different soundtrack) was adapted outside of Japan for the first saga of [[robotech|robotech]], where it is known as **The Macross Saga**. 

In Japan the TV series were adapted into an acclaimed anime film called [[macross: do you remember love?|macross: do you remember love?]] that was released in japanese movie theaters during 1984.

**Chris Redfield** is a Special Operations Agent (SOA) of the Bioterrorism Security Assessment Alliance (BSAA), of which he is a founding member. Formerly, he served in the US Air Force; before moving on to law enforcement as a member of the RPD's Special Tactics And Rescue Service's (S.T.A.R.S.) Alpha Team. After S.T.A.R.S. were disbanded following the Raccoon City Incident, he and his partner, [[jill valentine|jill valentine]], became members of a Private Regional Biohazard Containment Unit (BCU), and took part in the fall of Umbrella in 2003. 

Chris is the older brother of [[claire redfield|claire redfield]] and one of few survivors of the mansion incident, during the Arklay Mountains outbreak in 1998. In addition to his qualification to pilot fixed-wing aircraft, Chris has been trained strictly in several fighting techniques like [[cqc|cqc]], is an expert in knife and firearm combat, and is also gifted with great accuracy.

Also notorious for punching a boulder in the climax of [[resident evil 5|resident evil 5]].

#### Appearance
Chris is a muscular man with [[black hair|black hair]] and [[blue eyes|blue eyes]]. His appearance varies throughout the series.

- [[resident evil 1|resident evil 1]]: Chris wears a [[police uniform|police uniform]] with [[white shirt|white shirt]], [[black pants|black pants]], [[bulletproof vest|bulletproof vest]], [[fingerless gloves|fingerless gloves]], and black boots.
- [[resident evil 5|resident evil 5]]: Chris has a [[green shirt|green shirt]], [[gloves|gloves]], [[grey pants|grey pants]] and a [[green footwear|green shoes]]. His appearance changes noticeably, looking much more muscular compared to Resident Evil 1 .
- [[resident evil 6|resident evil 6]]: Chris wears a similar outfit to the ones he wore in Resident Evil 5, albeit he sports a [[grey pants|grey pants]], [[green shirt|green shirt]], [[bulletproof vest|bulletproof vest]] and [[gloves|gloves]].
- [[resident evil 7: biohazard|resident evil 7: biohazard]]: In Resident Evil 7: biohazard, Chris design changed to a less muscular body and a [[brown hair|brown hair]], he sports a [[black jacket|black jacket]], [[gloves|gloves]], [[black pants|black pants]], [[bulletproof vest|bulletproof vest]], [[black shoes|black shoes]] and [[knee pads|knee pads]]. 
- [[resident evil village|resident evil village]]: Chris has a much more matured appearance in Resident Evil Village, he sports a [[black coat|black coat]] along with [[black shirt|black shirt]], [[black pants|black pants]], [[gloves|gloves]] and black shoes.

A type of optical distortion where the edges of an image have a colored, blurry halo or fringe. The RGB color channels may be noticeably offset from one another. In this respect it may sometimes resemble [[anaglyph|anaglyph]].

Chromatic aberration arises in optics because a lens does not refract light of different wavelengths (colors) in precisely the same way (technically speaking, the index of refraction of a lens material varies depending on the wavelength). So if a camera is focused such that one color is perfectly focused, all other colors will be slightly out of focus.

Digital art has inherently zero chromatic aberration since it does not rely on real-world lenses at all, yet it is often intentionally simulated for artistic effect. In small amounts it can increase realism. In progressively greater amounts it can:

- create a sense of motion (similar to [[motion blur|motion blur]]),
- convey a chaotic environment,
- indicate anxiety or paranoia,
- indicate mental derangement and/or [[mind control|mind control]]

Images with excessive chromatic aberration tend to give most people eyestrain and headaches if observed for too long.

**Chun-Li** (Traditional: 春麗. Simplified: 春丽) is a character in the [[street fighter|street fighter]] series by [[capcom|capcom]]. She is the first female playable character to appear in a 1-on-1 fighting game.

Introduced in [[street fighter ii (series)|street fighter ii (series)]], Chun-Li was the youngest member of the roster and only female character in the game, the self-proclaimed "strongest woman in the world," and while not as physically powerful as the other characters, she was by far the quickest. Her most famous attack is the *Hyakuretsukyaku* ("Hundred Crack Legs", alternately known as "Lightning Legs"), where she repeatedly kicks her opponent from a tilted standing position with incredible speed.

In the Street Fighter series, Chun-Li was an Interpol investigator from [[china|china]] who had been searching for clues to the recent death of her father. Getting into a friendly spar with an old teacher of hers and friend of her father, [[gen (street fighter)|gen (street fighter)]], he gives her a lead into who may have killed her father—the mysterious crime syndicate Shadaloo and its tyrannical leader [[m. bison|m. bison]]. After an encounter where M. Bison confirms he slew her father, a tearful Chun-Li swore vengeance and made it her life's mission to destroy Shadaloo and bring M. Bison to justice. She collaborated closely with [[guile|guile]], [[cammy white|cammy white]], [[ryu (street fighter)|ryu (street fighter)]], and the other World Warriors throughout the journey.

After M. Bison's supposedly final death during [[street fighter v|street fighter v]], her mission complete, Chun-Li retired from Interpol and opened an orphanage to live a quieter life. The most famous of her young wards - practically her adopted daughter - is [[li-fen|li-fen]].

Chun-Li is one of Capcom's most popular characters and one of the most important females in video game history, appearing in numerous cross-overs and promotions. Her oldest and arguably greatest cross-company rival is [[snk|snk]]'s [[fatal fury|fatal fury]]'s [[shiranui mai|Mai Shiranui]].

The two have fairly dissimilar personalities. Whereas Tsuruya is easily excitable and laughs a lot, Churuya seems more simple-minded, and has a deep appreciation for [[smoked cheese|smoked cheese]]. Her signature catchphrase is [[nyoro~n|nyoro~n]].

Churuya first appeared on Eretto's website in a now famous [[4koma|4koma]] (post #47838). Churuya inherited Eretto's love of smoked cheese. Notably, in the last panel Churuya utters her catchphrase [[nyoro~n|nyoro~n]] when she becomes disappointed by the lack of smoked cheese. Likely one major reason for Churuya's popularity is the sense of schadenfreude at Churuya's perpetual misfortune.

From the very start, fan reaction to Eretto's Churuya comics was wildly positive. After being linked on [[2channel|2channel]], Eretto's site would frequently go down because of all the traffic. Eretto continued to write new Churuya-san 4koma, and has even anthologized them in doujinshi.

[[churuya|churuya]] became a meme frequently used by other artists. Usually the one common factor is the last panel, where a character drawn in the style of Churuya (complete with [[:3|:3]]) says *nyoro~n* or some variation thereof.

Often translated to English as "8th-Grader Syndrome". A similar insult in English is calling someone "[[coldsteel the hedgehog|edgy]]". It is the result of trying to stand out by believing that one has special powers (especially sealed powers), a dark past, or such like. Chuunibyou can manifest as overly dramatic [[hand over eye|hand gestures]], expressions, and spoken lines; and clothing such as [[eyepatch|eyepatch]]es and [[scarf|scarves]]. If the symptoms are severe enough, even *actually* having special powers and/or a dark past may not be enough to beat chuunibyou allegations.

Only tag images where a character is actively displaying chuunibyou behavior; do not use simply because the character is a chuunibyou in the series. The tag is not meant as an abbreviation of the light novel series [[chuunibyou demo koi ga shitai!|chuunibyou demo koi ga shitai!]].

A large [[bug|insect]] belonging to the superfamily *Cicadoidea*. Notable for their large, veiny transparent wings and their loud droning mating call.

In Japan the presence and droning cries of the cicada is heavily associated with summer (particularly on hot days with muggy weather). As such the cicada or its call is often used to help set the scene for a story happening during summer. In North America, periodic cicadas are famous for appearing in huge numbers in regular intervals.

For danbooru purposes a **circle cut** (サークルカット) is a special type of advertisement for a doujin circle. There are two basic types pictures tagged as circle cut. The traditional variety has some distinct features:

- There is always a white box with a black border in the upper left corner.
- The circle name is displayed prominently on the cut, as well as textual information about what the circle intends to offer.
- They are (usually) in some standardized size, as specified by the event.
- They are [[monochrome|monochrome]] for the printed event catalog, however the circle cuts are usually in color for web catalogs.

The box is there for specific information, such as when the doujin circle will be attending an event and where their stand exactly is. The box is also used by event goers as a checkbox, often with a highlighter.

The second kind of picture doesn't need to conform to the visual template exactly, but is characterized by having been released as a direct preparation of the exposition in question. They might vary in appearance from just a character's portrait + circle name, up to entire small scenes or comics whose purpose is to announce the booth number. For example, see post #634255 and post #161515.

The [[fruit|fruit]] of the [[coconut tree|coconut palm]]. It has a hard brown shell, which holds edible white flesh; the liquid inside the cavity is called coconut milk. The entire fruit is covered by a fibrous outer husk which is usually removed before the coconut is further processed.

Coconuts vary in appearance, ranging from having a smooth green shell, to a yellow one, and of course the common brown color that is covered in bark strips.

**Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion** (コードギアス 反逆のルルーシュ *Kōdo Giasu: Hangyaku no Rurūshu*, lit. "Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion"), often referred to as simply Code Geass, is a Japanese anime series created by [[sunrise (company)|Sunrise]], directed by Gorō Taniguchi, and written by Ichirō Ōkouchi, with original character designs by manga authors [[clamp (circle)|clamp (circle)]].

Code Geass first ran in Japan on MBS from October 5, 2006, to July 28, 2007. Its sequel series, [[code geass|Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion R2]] (コードギアス 反逆のルルーシュR2), ran as a simulcast on JNN stations (like MBS and TBS) from April 6, 2008 to September 28, 2008. The series has also been adapted into various manga and light novels with the former showing various alternate scenarios from the TV series. Bandai Entertainment also licensed most parts from the franchise for English release in December 2007, airing the two TV series on Cartoon Network. Most manga and light novels have also been published in North America by Bandai.

Set in an alternate timeline, the series focuses on how the former prince Lelouch vi Britannia obtains a power known as Geass and decides to use it to obliterate the Holy Britannian Empire, an imperial monarchy and a superpower that has been conquering various countries.

A [[fish|fish]]. Famous for once being thought to have gone extinct around 66 million years ago, but were rediscovered in 1938 off the coast of [[south africa|south africa]]. Ovoviviparous, only two species survive, both critically endangered. They are easy to spot because of their strange appearance; however not all primitive or strange-looking fishes should be tagged as coelacanth. They are lobe-finned fish (from where tetrapods come), as opposed to the most common ray-finned fishes.

They are easily distinguished by their large rhomboidal anal fin, and their characteristic second dorsal fin which is lobed; ray-finned fishes either don't have a second dorsal fin, or it's not lobed. Actually, for coelacanths, all their fins are lobed except the first dorsal fin. Examples of coelacanths are post #470478 and post #974792 (at the top right, just below the sun).

Characters and/or objects match each other in color, or create a sense of symmetry.

The characters/objects must be put into multiple pairs/groups based on their color to create the sense of "coordination". If there is only one group of characters/object put together based on their color, use [[color connection|color connection]] and the corresponding "color theme":/tags?search[name_matches]=*_theme&search[category]=0&search[hide_empty]=yes&search[order]=name&commit=Search if applicable.

If it's an art centring around a specific color without the intention of "connection", use the corresponding "color theme":/tags?search[name_matches]=*_theme&search[category]=0&search[hide_empty]=yes&search[order]=name&commit=Search instead. For instance, post #4734135 is [[yellow theme|yellow theme]].

If there're multiple color groups but the characters are simply cosplaying and their matching pair isn't present (e.g. post #1490134), use [[color connection|color connection]] instead.

This technique is often associated with [[lineup|lineup]] and [[column lineup|column lineup]], such as post #5485339. When the columns are each completely monochromatically themed on a single color, it becomes [[multiple monochrome|multiple monochrome]].

If the coordinated colors are also forming a rainbow, it's also [[rainbow order|rainbow order]].

Originally the **Flavian Amphitheatre**, an elliptical amphitheatre in the centre of the city of [[rome (city)|rome (city)]], [[italy|italy]], the largest ever built in the Roman Empire, built of concrete and stone. It is considered one of the greatest works of Roman architecture and Roman engineering and is also famous as a [[gladiator|gladiator]]ial arena. The name is derived from the Colossus of Rhodes, a giant statue of Apollo which stood near (but not inside) the Amphitheatre.

The military version was called the Single Action Army, Model 1873, for reasons that should be obvious; its proper civilian product name when first introduced was "New Model Army Metallic Cartridge Revolving Pistol", which, astonishingly, failed to catch on. Action of pulling a [[pull cord|pull cord]].

The oldest of all [[phone|phones]], dominant in everyday use at least until the early 1990s. Uses cords to maintain electricity. Most often has a [[rotary phone|rotary dial]], although these were gradually superseded by push button systems from the 1980s onward.

The earliest corded phones had no integrated dialing system at all; either the connection was between two devices only, or a manual telephone exchange was needed.

The corded phone has generally been superseded by cordless phones and cellphones, but are still common in some fields.  Public phones such as payphones and emergency phones are corded either to discourage someone walking off with the receiver or because the time between uses would be far between.  Office/business phones are also commonly wired, due to considerations such of potential radio interference in an office environment where there may be many phones and wireless devices in close proximity and in consideration of corporate security.

***Cowboy Bebop*** (カウボーイビバップ) is an influential, critically-acclaimed, and award-winning 1998 Japanese neo-noir [[science fiction|science fiction]] anime series directed by Watanabe Shinichiro, written by Nobumoto Keiko, and produced by [[sunrise (company)|sunrise (company)]]. 

It is one of the most highly acclaimed anime and is regarded as one of the greatest anime series ever created. It is the highest rated anime series on IMDB top 50 anime of all time, placing at number one. 

Its 26 episodes ("sessions") comprise a complete storyline: set in 2071, the series follows the misadventures and tragedies of a group of bounty hunters, or "cowboys", traveling on their spaceship, the [[bebop (cowboy bebop)|bebop (cowboy bebop)]].

A card one uses to make purchase on credit, usually containing magnetic stripes to be read by computer systems.

The concept of credit cards is in which one buys goods & services first, paying off the costs later (and varying amounts of interest, usually on a monthly basis). First introduced in the US during the 50s, the widespread of them since then allowed for greater growth of the economy, although it also driven up household debt in the meantime. Most people in the developed world has at least one these days, usually several. Many credit card companies offer various reward points for their costumers in order to encourage spending. Some companies charge a transaction fee onto merchants, which made certain businesses to not accept them.

Credit card companies can also offer various card levels which clients can access depending on conditions, such as net worth, credit quality, and spending requirements, with each level reflective of the client's wealth and benefits which they receive from it, going from non-colored standard cards, gold, platinum, and finally [[black credit card|black]].

Urban legends or scary stories circulating on the Internet, many times revolving around specific videos, pictures or video games. The term "creepypasta" is a mutation of the term "copypasta": a short, readily available piece of text that is easily copied and pasted into a text field. "Copypasta" is derived from "copy/paste", and in its original sense commonly referred to presumably initially sincere text (e.g. a blog or forum post) perceived by the copy/paster as undesirable or otherwise preposterous, which was then copied and pasted to other sites as a form of trolling.

*A [[priest|priest]]'s staff.*

The real-life crosier (also spelled *crozier*) is a stylized, often ornately-decorated staff that is a symbol of the governing office of a high-ranking [[christianity|Christian]] priest. This staff generally comes in three forms: **hooked**, in the shape of a shepherd's crook (curled off to one side); **tau**, in the shape of a T with downwards-curving arms topped by a small [[cross|cross]]; and **serpentine**, with a pair of sculptured serpents or dragons curled back to face each other in an upwards-facing U with a small cross between them. 

The [[fantasy|fantasy]] version of the crosier tends to resemble a bastardized version of one (or several) of the above, with a small sphere or circular symmetrical  "shepherd's crook" bisected or topped by a large cross (the overall profile will often resemble a [[celtic cross|celtic cross]]). Some versions may just be a large cross mounted on the end of a staff (with the whole staff resembling a [[latin cross|latin cross]], like the [[pope|pope]]'s *ferula*). Another common fantasy variant has a scepter-like head topped off with a small cross.

[[priest|priest]]s and fantasy [[priestess|priestess]]es are often depicted holding a crosier. Some may instead be depicted wielding a generic [[mage staff|mage staff]]; such examples should not be tagged crosier.

#### Notable examples
- [[arch bishop (ragnarok online)|arch bishop (ragnarok online)]] ([[ragnarok online|ragnarok online]])
- [[pope (ragnarok online)|The Pope]] ([[ragnarok online|ragnarok online]])
- [[martha (fate)|martha (fate)]] ([[fate (series)|fate (series)]])
- [[victorious (azur lane)|victorious (azur lane)]] ([[azur lane|azur lane]])
  - Wields a golden crosier tipped with a sun cross, surmounted with a ship's bell.
- [[fan la norne|fan la norne]] ([[xenoblade chronicles 2|xenoblade chronicles 2]])

#### Tag usage notes
- Tag crosier for the priest's staff described above—both the real versions and the fantasy variants.
  - As a general rule, any fantasy staff that appears vaguely [[christianity|Christian]]-like (i.e. festooned with crosses and Christian motifs) will also tend to qualify.
- Avoid tagging crosier for 'generic' looking staves that may be better off tagged [[staff|staff]] or [[mage staff|mage staff]].
  - Fantasy [[priest|priest]]([[priestess|ess]])es are sometimes depicted holding a 'generic' crystal or gem-tipped staff without any religious trappings, one that would not look out of place being wielded by any other magic user. These examples should be tagged [[mage staff|mage staff]] and not crosier.
  - Fire Emblem characters belonging to the priest or cleric class lines tend to just wield generic [[mage staff|mage staves]] because of [[nintendo|nintendo]] being allergic towards the depiction of crosses and other religious iconography.
- **Do not** tag [[shakujou|shakujou]] (i.e. Buddhist staves) with crosier.
- The [[pope|pope]]'s staff is a Papal ferula, but this can be tagged with crosier for now.

A croupier or dealer is someone appointed at a gambling table to assist in the conduct of the game, especially in the distribution of bets and payouts. Croupiers are typically employed by casinos.

Originally a 'croupier' meant one who stood behind a gambler, with extra reserves of cash to back him up during a gambling session. The word derived from 'croup' (the rump of a horse) and was by way of analogy to one who rode behind on horseback. It later came to refer to one who was employed to collect the money from a gaming-table.

A female croupier's uniform usually consists of a shirt and tie with a [[vest|vest]], and a [[miniskirt|miniskirt]] or slacks.

A large, all-black passerine [[bird|bird]].

Scientifically, crows are one species of bird in the broader Corvidae family, which includes crows, ravens, rooks, jackdaws, jays, magpies, treepies, choughs, and nutcrackers. On Danbooru, "crow" includes all visually-similar birds in the Corvidae family.

Birds in the Corvidae family range in size from the relatively small pigeon-size jackdaws (Eurasian and Daurian) to the Common Raven of the Holarctic region and Thick-billed Raven of the highlands of Ethiopia. The 40 or so members of Corvus genus occur on all temperate continents (except South America) and several offshore and oceanic islands.

Crow species found in Japan, aside from [[magpie|magpie]]s, jays and nutcrackers, include the rook, [[carrion crow|carrion crow]], Eurasian & Daurian jackdaws, the large-billed crow, and the common raven.

**Cthulhu** is a fictional cosmic entity created by horror author [[h p lovecraft|H. P. Lovecraft]] in 1926, first appearing in the short story "The Call of Cthulhu" when it was published in Weird Tales in 1928.

Cthulhu is one of the central Great Old Ones of the [[cthulhu mythos|cthulhu mythos]]. It is often cited for the extreme descriptions given of its hideous appearance (which includes green skin, gargoyle wings and a squid shaped head), its gargantuan size, and the abject insanity inducing terror that it evokes on the persons unlucky enough to watch him.

This tag is applied to all about "Cthulhu Mythos" by [[h p lovecraft|h p lovecraft]] and his works.

Lovecraft's guiding aesthetic and philosophical principle was what he termed "cosmicism" or "cosmic horror", the idea that life is incomprehensible to human minds and that the universe is fundamentally inimical to the interests of humankind. As such, his stories express a profound indifference to human beliefs and affairs. 

His "Cthulhu Mythos" is well-known throughout the world. "[[call of cthulhu|call of cthulhu]]", a horror fiction role-playing game was named after his horror stories.

Well-developed cumulonimbus clouds are characterized by a flat, anvil-like top (anvil dome), caused by wind shear or inversion near the boundary between the troposphere and the stratosphere.  These clouds are capable of producing lightning and other dangerous severe weather, such as tornadoes and hailstones.

#### Types

- Cumulonimbus calvus: Latin for "bald", features a puffy top
- Cumulonimbus capillatus: Latin for "long hair", features ice crystal clouds that streak out at its top edge giving it a fibrous appearance
- Cumulonimbus capillatus incus: Also known as an "anvil cloud" (incus being Latin for anvil), features a flat, anvil-top shape

A [[science fiction|science fiction]] genre. Basic themes include the dehumanizing effects of technology, and the accompanying societal breakdown. Think dark and dirty, with lots of [[wire|wire]]s and [[neon lights|neon]].

**Cyberpunk** is a postmodern dystopian genre noted for its focus on **”high tech and low life"**. The name is a portmanteau of cybernetics and punk, and was originally coined by American science fiction author Bruce Bethke as the title of his short Sci-Fi story *Cyberpunk*, written in 1980.

Cyberpunk can cover numerous themes and motifs but generally involve reflecting on the current anxieties of society and amping them up to an extreme; things like mass surveillance, corporate monopolization, climate change, mass media, artificial intelligence and any other themes can thus be accomodated by a cyberpunk setting.

For the series which the genre is named after, see [[cyberpunk (series)|cyberpunk (series)]].

An organism that is made up of both **cyb**ernetic and **org**anic components. In anime, this generally refers to humans that have been altered to be partially [[robot|robot]]ic.

It can be difficult to tell a cyborg apart from an [[android|android]], especially when dealing with [[original|original]] characters and those whose origins are unknown. ***Narcissus***, commonly called daffodil, is a genus of [[flower|flower]]ing plants in the family *Amaryllidaceae*. The scientific name of the plant is often linked to the myth of [[narcissus|narcissus]], who became so obsessed with his [[narcissism|own reflection]] in water that he drowned, although it is not clear whether the flower was named after the myth or the myth after the flower. The other common name is jonquil, after a particular species of the family.

Daffodil flowers grow at about a right angle to the stem and have a cup- or trumpet-shaped center surrounded by 6 petal-like tepals (undifferentiated petals and sepals). The flowers can come in a limited variety of colors, most often white and yellow, sometimes orange. Depending on the species, the tepals may be a different color than the center.

In the east, they are considered a symbol of wealth and good fortune, and since they bloom in early spring are often associated with the Chinese New Year. The bulbs are mildly poisonous and must be handled with care but were once a part of traditional Japanese medicine.

Daisy and aster are blanket names for many similar looking [[flower|flowers]] in the expansive *Asteraceae* family. Asters are practically indistinguishable from daisies for tagging purposes.

Daisies and asters typically have a spiky-looking head made up of tiny disc florets surrounded by a multitude of long petals. Gerber daisies will also have an inner ring of ray florets around the center head.

Common daisy colors include white petals with a yellow or orange center and yellow petals with a dark brown center, but daisies & asters can come in practically **any** color.

For tagging purposes, limit this tag to flowers that look generally like a Common Daisy, a Black-Eyed Susan, a Gerber Daisy, asters, or any color variation on that basic design.
