Mode of attack used by enemies in some shooting games. Complex attack patterns, made of hundreds to thousands of projectiles fill the screen. The player must weave through tiny gaps in the barrage. End-stage boss attacks are especially spectacular, in an attempt to intimidate and dazzle the player.

Danmaku are usually made of missiles, but are sometimes combined with other hazards such as lasers, flames and lightning arcs for added challenge. 

Missiles in danmaku have been particularly creative of late, most notably in the [[touhou|touhou]] series. Throwing knives, flower petals, paper charms and even ghosts have been employed in addition to the usual shells and colored balls.

This tag is used to refer to depictions of attacks launched by  characters or weapons from known shooting games.

#### See also

- [[touhou|touhou]]
- [[danmaku comments|danmaku comments]] - a unique scrolling comments system created by [[niconico|niconico]], named after this attack

Otherwise known as scrolling comments, *danmaku* comments (not to be confused with our actual [[danmaku|danmaku]] tag) refer to the unique commenting system created by [[niconico|niconico]]. Later also adapted by other sites such as [[acfun|acfun]] and [[bilibili|bilibili]] (despite NND's owners owning the patent for it, due to a legal loophole). 

Danmaku comments are displayed as floating text that scrolls over the video, from right to left. This leads to comments flooding the screen ala danmaku when users react to big moments. Users can customize the time that their comments appear, or they can make their comments stay on the top or bottom of the screen for 3 seconds.

**Deadpool** is a mercenary and anti-hero appearing in comic books published by [[marvel|Marvel Comics]]. Created by artist Rob Liefeld and writer Fabian Nicieza, Deadpool (Wade Wilson) first appeared in *The New Mutants* #98 (Feb. 1991).

A disfigured and mentally unstable mercenary with the ability to quickly regenerate himself, Deadpool originally appeared as a villain in an issue of *New Mutants*, and later in issues of *X-Force*. The character has since starred in several ongoing series, and shares titles with other characters such as [[cable (marvel)|Cable]]. The character, known as the "Merc with a Mouth", is famous for his talkative nature and his tendency to "break the [[fourth wall|fourth wall]]", which is used by writers for humorous effect.

With his inclusion in [[marvel vs. capcom 3|Marvel vs. Capcom 3]] his ability to break the fourth wall has been taken to [a whole new level.](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S66LtJ77mRk) The character would later achieve even greater success after his [[deadpool (movie)|2016 film of the same name]], followed up by 2018's [[deadpool 2|deadpool 2]].

Deadpool & Wolverine is a superhero film based on the [[marvel|marvel]] Comics characters [[deadpool|deadpool]] and [[wolverine (x-men)|wolverine (x-men)]], is the 34th film in the [[marvel cinematic universe|marvel cinematic universe]] (MCU) and a sequel to [[deadpool (movie)|Deadpool (2016)]] and [[deadpool 2|deadpool 2]] (2018).

It integrates Deadpool from Fox's [[x-men film series|x-men film series]] with the MCU and retains the R rating of the previous films, making it the first MCU film to have such a rating.

These villainous transforming [[robot|robot]]s can take many forms, and have many different origins and stories across the numerous different Transformers media, but in almost all incarnations, they are led by [[megatron|megatron]]. They are typically represented by the purple facial insignia they all wear. Primarily, **Decepticons** have red eyes, while their enemy [[autobot|autobot]]s have blue eyes. They are usually known for their air power, especially since many of them turn into [[aircraft|aircraft]]. Decepticons often turn into [[military|military]] vehicles, construction vehicles, and even smaller-than-human-sized objects. 

In [[japan|japan]]'s version of the franchise, the Decepticons are called **Destron** or **Deathtron** (Japanese: デストロン Desutoron). The one exception to this naming convention is Car Robots, where the sub-group referred to as "Decepticons" in the Robots in Disguise adaptation, is known in Japan as the Combatrons (the Japanese name of the G1 subgroup known as the Combaticons). The overall name of the Robots in Disguise villain faction is **Destronger**. However, the Japanese version of Transformers Animated uses Decepticon (ディセプティコン). 

The title Decepticons is derived from the word *"deception"* in the English language.

**Dennou Shoujo SHIRO** (電脳少女シロ), romanized in Japan as **Siro** is a [[virtual youtuber|virtual youtuber]] and aspiring Japanese [[idol|idol]]. She made her YouTube debut on June 28, 2017, making her one of the first VTubers in the world. Her channel features a wide variety of content, including gaming and other popular trends, but also her own musical performances as well. 

She has a demure and feminine personality with a fondness for cats and eating sweets. Despite this, she doesn't hesitate when killing in games, which has contributed to a [[yandere|yandere]] personality in some of her videos. Her self-described charm point is her own two [[ahoge|ahoge]], or [[antenna hair|antenna hair]]. She is sometimes listed as a "Ninja", but this is likely due to an inability to properly translate "Dennou", which would roughly mean "Electric Brain", another term for artificial intelligence.

Fans have taken to calling her a dolphin (イルカ) due to the strange sounds she makes when laughing.

American desert camouflage in service 1981-1995. Officially called Six-Color Desert Pattern, and colloquially known as chocolate-chip or cookie dough. The uniform which it was applied to was called the Desert Battle Dress Uniform (DBDU). The design was influenced by the rocky California desert. While more effective than Tri-Color desert, it proved ineffective when it saw widespread use during the Persian Gulf War. Though no longer used by the United States, variants of the pattern continue to be worn by many armies worldwide.

It's pattern is a tan base, with dark and lighter brown splotches and stripes moving throughout it. White spots with a black semi-border are randomly placed on the pattern, meant to resemble rocks.

An [[image sample|image sample]] from DeviantArt.

DeviantArt image URLs sometimes contain either the string "200H" or "PRE". These URLs point to scaled down images, not the full size. 200H URLs point to small thumbnails, scaled down to 200 pixels. PRE URLs point to medium-sized samples, displayed on the art page by default if the full-sized image is too large. If you remove the "200H/" or "PRE/" parts from one of these sample URLs, the resulting URL will point to the full-sized version instead.

This tag should be used when the image uploaded to Danbooru is one of these scaled down versions.

It is Danbooru policy to either replace samples or delete them. See [[image sample|image sample]] for more information. See [[howto:deviantart|howto:deviantart]] for how to upload from DeviantArt correctly.

Diffraction spikes manifest as multiple spikes radiating from a point of light, similar to a [[lens flare|lens flare]] which manifests as overall haziness and artifacts in the image.

[[sparkle|sparkle]], [[glint|glint]], and **diffraction spikes** all refer to similar patterns of bright lines radiating from a point. They are not clearly differentiated, and usage tends to be context-sensitive. In general:
- [[sparkle|sparkle]] is considered the base case. Usually four lines at right angles radiating from a point. Associated with eyes, liquid or particulate matter (e.g. raindrops, snow, sand), or nothing (appearing mid-air). Can appear in large numbers.
- [[glint|glint]] is associated with solid objects, especially ones which are metallic and/or sharp. Usually appear singly or in small numbers.
- **Diffraction spikes** is the technical term for the phenomenon in general, but is used less often. Can be used for more realistic-looking effects or conversely when appearing extremely large and exaggerated. More likely than sparkle and glint to be asymmetric or to have more than four radiating lines.

A type of [[aircraft|aircraft]], usually cigar-shaped, that floats by means of a large balloon, usually filled with hydrogen or helium.

There are three types of dirigibles:

- **Blimps** have a non-rigid airframe; its shape is maintained by the pressure of the gas within.

Disneyland is the name applied to any of several of [[disney|disney]]'s [[amusement park|theme parks]] around the world, including the original in California.

**Tokyo Disneyland** (東京ディズニーランド, Tōkyō Dizunīrando) is a 115 acre (465,000 m²) theme park at the Tokyo Disney Resort located in Urayasu, Chiba, Japan, near Tokyo. The park was constructed by Walt Disney Imagineering in the same style as Disneyland in California and Magic Kingdom in Florida. Also at Tokyo Disney Resort is [[tokyo disneysea|tokyo disneysea]] (東京ディズニーシー, Tōkyō DizunīShī) and Ikspiari (イクスピアリ), the domestic equivalents of DisneySea and Downtown Disney.

There are seven themed areas in the park: the World Bazaar; the four classic Disney lands: Adventureland, Westernland, Fantasyland and Tomorrowland; and two mini-lands: Critter Country and Mickey's Toontown. The park is noted for its extensive open spaces, to accommodate the large crowds that visit the park. In 2009, Tokyo Disneyland hosted approximately 13.65 million guests, ranking it as the third-most visited theme park in the world, behind its American sister parks, Magic Kingdom and Disneyland.

A sequel/prequel, *[[dissidia 012 final fantasy|dissidia 012 final fantasy]]*, was released in March 2011. A team-vs-team spinoff, *[[dissidia final fantasy nt|dissidia final fantasy nt]]*, first developed in arcades in 2015, was later ported to [[playstation 4|playstation 4]] and Steam (platform). A tie-in *gachapon* RPG, *[[dissidia final fantasy opera omnia|dissidia final fantasy opera omnia]]*, was released concurrently, and still receives updates and new characters.

A [[tight clothes|tight]], muted color [[pencil dress|pencil dress]] with low neckline to show [[cleavage|cleavage]], usually accompanied with an open, [[cropped jacket|cropped jacket]] of the same color. The [[long sleeves|long sleeves]] may alternatively be part of the dress. A [[meme attire|fashion meme]] originating from South Korea.

In South Korea, it is often joked on the Internet that the new town area of Dongtan (동탄) has an unusually high number of rich, young married women wearing such dresses, spending time at shopping malls or cafes while their husbands are at work. Dongtan New Town is statistically one of the youngest in the country in terms of average age of residents, with one district scoring as low as 33.5 in September 2023. The township has been perceived as where a number of young married couples wishing to keep the capital area in close reach reside, where most infrastructures of South Korea are concentrated at an extreme density.

The meme has gained traction in 2023 and the name Dongtan has since been used on any young woman dressed in any revealing clothes, practically replacing any sexually suggestive keyword in Korea, with characters such as [[dongtan lady (k pring)|dongtan lady (k pring)]] popping up.

The game was officially released in English as a [[wii|wii]] WiiWare game. While it costs 1200 Nintendo Points, the WiiWare version came with several modes the original did not possess, such as the ability to play as fan-favorite, [[curly brace|curly brace]]. This version was later sold as [[nintendo dsi|DSiWare]] as well. 

It has gotten a full-scale remake on the [[nintendo 3ds|nintendo 3ds]].

For tagging purposes, this tag refers to the white or mostly white birds, such as the "dove of peace" that is commonly associated with the term "dove." 

The term dove is frequently used interchangeably with the term pigeon.  When used more specifically, the term refers to smaller members of the bird family Columbidae, whose members are referred to by either the terms dove or pigeon. Members of this family fall under two major groups based on their diet, with one group predominately eating seeds and the other predominately eating fruits.

A Y or L shaped rod used for divining the location of water, oils, gravesites, or finding radioactive materials. Dowsing rods are sometimes used in a way not too dissimilar from a Ouija board, in which you ask a question and if the Dowsing rod moves the answer is yes.  It can be made from a variety of materials. 

Dowsing can also be conducted with a pendulum made of a crystal, or other materials, to find the location of materials. It works in a similar fashion to the rods, with the crystal pointing in the direction of the desired objective.

There are modern electronic Dowsing rods, notably used by the Iraqi military to detect explosives, but none have proven effective.

[[nazrin|nazrin]] from the [[touhou|touhou]] series is associated with both the rod and the crystal method of dowsing.

Doya-gao (ドヤ顔) is a facial expression conveying a self-satisfied, cocky, or [[smug|smug]] attitude. To enhance the comedy effect, one may use this expression on a character who is overly proud of something they failed at, or that they have no reason to be proud of.

Doya probably comes from Kansai Japanese "Dou ya?" meaning asking someone "How about that?" or "How well am I doing?". The phrase carries an inside meaning of "I looked cool just now, didn't I?"

A few trademarks of doyagao are a cocky expression, featuring a tight [[closed mouth|closed-lip]] [[smile|smile]], [[closed eyes|closed]] or [[sparkling eyes|sparkling eyes]], [[v-shaped eyebrows|v-shaped eyebrows]], and a proud [[puff of air|huff]], along with [[hands on own hips|hands on one's hips]] or chest, and a general air of "I totally nailed it just now", when the character didn't nail it at all.

Due to the anime's relative unpopularity in Japan, it aired for only two years between 1996-97 before being cancelled. GT would be considered non-canon with Dragon Ball's revival in 2013 and the later airing of [[dragon ball super|dragon ball super]]. Elements introduced by GT would later be picked up by the Dragon Ball video games, notably [[dragon ball heroes|dragon ball heroes]], keeping exposure to the series well after its cancellation.

Developed by Bandai off the heels of [[dragon ball z|dragon ball z]] [[dragon ball kai|Kai]], **Dragon Ball Heroes** is an arcade trading card game ([[carddass|carddass]]) using the [[dragon ball|dragon ball]] property, later renamed to **Super Dragon Ball Heroes**. It is infamous in the West for its perceived fan service, giving characters access to forms they previously hadn't obtained/used, and just generally being absurd in its plotlines.

Starting with *Dragon Ball Heroes: God Mission*, more plot elements were introduced into the game (largely drawn from [[dragon ball online|dragon ball online]], similarly to [[dragon ball xenoverse|dragon ball xenoverse]] that same year), and has since developed it through several mediums, including the arcade game itself, its manga adaptations ([[toyotarou|toyotarou]]'s Victory Mission, and the more faithful Nagayama Yoshitaka serializations), its handheld console adaptations on Nintendo platforms, and an anime adaptation starting from its-then-latest storyline, *Universe Mission*. All of these adaptations have story elements that add or diverge from the original arcade game, and could thus be considered their own separate timelines to some extent, similarly to its relation to the Xenoverse series.

Dragon Ball Heroes would largely be confined to Japanese shores, but from July to October of 2018, the arcade game was shown in 7 North American towns as part of an American tour, marking its first appearance overseas. The 2019 game *Super Dragon Ball Heroes: World Mission*, the fourth console adaptation of the arcade game for Nintendo Switch, would be the first to not only properly release in English, but also internationally.

Currently, the arcade game is set to cease operation before November 2024. It will be available as a separate mode in the game Dragon Ball Super Divers, which will replace the Dragon Ball Heroes machines.

The fourth [[dragon ball|dragon ball]] series created as the "definitive" sequel to [[dragon ball z|dragon ball z]], with the story being set 6 months after the defeat of [[kid buu|kid buu]]. The anime began airing on July 5, 2015, with the manga appearing just slightly before on June 20. [[toriyama akira|toriyama akira]] is credited for the "original story & character design concepts", in addition to his role as series creator, as well as providing more direct corrections and feedback for the manga. [[toyotarou|toyotarou]], the Super mangaka, is also credited with "character design concepts".

Crucially, while the anime and manga follow the same base story notes provided by Toriyama, the way those notes are approached can differ significantly between the two, even when each side collaborates on select elements. While the anime has ended on March 25, 2018, with only new movies coming out since then, the manga has continued on.

An immensely popular Japanese RPG series developed by [[square enix|square enix]]—formerly by Enix separately—with character designs by [[toriyama akira|toriyama akira]]. The series—especially the earliest games—heavily influenced the development of the genre in Japan. The series was never as popular in the west as *[[final fantasy|final fantasy]]* due to delayed releases and the closure of Enix's North America office in the 1990s, but its profile has grown since the 2003 Square Enix merger.

The first in the long-running *[[dragon quest|dragon quest]]* series of video games.  Although a very simple game by modern standards, it did establish many of the modern tropes of console RPGs.

It was originally released in 1986 for the [[famicom|famicom]], and brought to North America in 1990, though its name was changed to *Dragon Warrior* in that market due to a previous copyright on the *Dragon Quest* title.  The game has since been ported and enhanced numerous times, with versions being made for the [[super famicom|super famicom]], [[game boy color|game boy color]], and mobile devices.

Full title: *Dragon Quest II: Akuryo no Kamigami* (悪霊の神々, lit. "Pantheon of Evil Spirits")

The second game in the *[[dragon quest|dragon quest]]* series, and the first in which the player controls a party of adventurers rather than just a single character.  Set one hundred years after the first game, the plot follows the descendants of the first *Dragon Quest*'s hero as they struggle to free their world from the domination of the evil wizard Hargon.

Originally released for the [[famicom|famicom]] in 1987, an English version was published for the NES in 1990 under the title *Dragon Warrior II*.  It has since been re-released several times, often combined with the original game, most notably for the [[super famicom|super famicom]] and [[game boy color|game boy color]].

*[[dragon quest builders 2|dragon quest builders 2]]* follows after this game, which expands on the nature of the villains.

#### See also

- DQ Wiki article: http://dragonquest.wikia.com/wiki/Dragon_Quest_II

The third game in the *[[dragon quest|dragon quest]]* series, originally released in 1988 for the [[famicom|famicom]] and later brought to North America (as *Dragon Warrior III*) in 1991.  Enhanced remakes have since been made for the [[super famicom|super famicom]] and [[game boy color|game boy color]], though only the latter was released outside of Japan.

This game was the first to include a gender option for the main player-character.  It also introduced character classes to the series: [[soldier (dq3)|soldier]], [[priest (dq3)|priest]], [[mage (dq3)|mage]], [[fighter (dq3)|fighter]], [[merchant (dq3)|merchant]], [[jester (dq3)|jester]], and [[sage (dq3)|sage]]. The Super Famicom remake introduced an additional [[thief (dq3)|thief]] class.

*Dragon Quest IV* is the fourth installment of the *[[dragon quest|dragon quest]]* video game series, and the last to appear on the [[famicom|famicom]].

The game is divided into five chapters, each introducing one or more of the main characters and the final chapter gathering them together under the Hero/Heroine's leadership.

The main female characters are [[alena (dq4)|alena (dq4)]], [[minea (dq4)|minea (dq4)]] and [[manya (dq4)|manya (dq4)]]; there is also the option for a [[heroine (dq4)|female protagonist]]. A rarely drawn side character is [[lucia (dq)|lucia (dq)]], who is a temporary party late in the game. Another is [[cynthia (dq4)|cynthia (dq4)]], an elf girl who is the Hero/Heroine's childhood friend.

DQ4 introduced the [[dancer's costume (dq)|Dancer's Costume]] and is the only Dragon Quest game to feature the [[pink leotard (dq)|Pink Leotard]].

The game has been remade for the [[playstation 1|playstation 1]], [[nintendo ds|nintendo ds]], and iOS/Android. The DS port is subtitled "Chapters of the Chosen" in English. The remakes also add an optional 6th chapter.

*Dragon Quest IX: Hoshizora no Mamoribito* (ドラゴンクエストX 目覚めし五つの種族 オンライン) (Dragon Quest IX: Sentinels of the Starry Skies) is the ninth game in the *[[dragon quest|dragon quest]]* series of RPGs. It was released on the [[nintendo ds|nintendo ds]] in Japan in 2009, and in the rest of the world in 2010.

It was the first game of the *Dragon Quest* series to feature multiplayer gameplay, and the first to be initially released (rather than as a port) for a handheld console.

*Dragon Quest V* (subtitled "Hand of the Heavenly Bride" in English) is the fifth installment in the *[[dragon quest|dragon quest]]* video game series.  The game is noteworthy as the first 16-bit installment of the series, and for its central conceit of following the [[hero (dq5)|main character]] from childhood to maturity, seeing how the world and other characters change as he ages.  The player must also famously make a marriage decision between two (or, in some versions, three) different girls who will offer themselves to the hero, one of whom will eventually become the mother of his children.
 
Originally developed by Chunsoft and published by Enix Corporation, Dragon Quest V was released for the [[super famicom|super famicom]]. It has since been remade for the [[playstation 2|playstation 2]] and [[nintendo ds|nintendo ds]].  Only the DS version has been officially released in English.

Since its launch in 2012, the game has been released on the Nintendo Wii, Wii U, the 3DS and Switch, as well as the PlayStation 4, Android & iOS, and Windows.

The **SVD** (Russian: Снайперская винтовка Драгунова, СВД) is a Soviet 7.62×54mmR semi-automatic [[sniper rifle|sniper rifle]], designed in 1963 by Yevgeny Dragunov. Having a reliable short-stroke gas piston system, the SVD is not based on the [[kalashnikov rifle|AK]] despite similar appearance. It is issued with a standard PSO-1 [[scope|telescopic sight]] and standard 10-round [[magazine (weapon)|magazine]].

The original SVD is identifiable by its pistol grip integrated with the buttstock, and two-piece front handguards with long rectangular perforations, while their length leaves the gas tube exposed.

A duffel bag, also known as a gym bag, is a cylindrical [[bag|bag]] carried over the shoulder, made from canvas or similarly rugged materials. It can be closed with a [[drawstring|drawstring]] or [[zipper|zipper]]. Older military-style designs historically had a single closure on one end; modern variants tend to have zippers along the length of the top and may have multiple compartments for easy storage.

Due to their large size and durability, duffel bags are typically used for hauling sporting equipment and/or uniforms. Travelers may carry them as an alternative to [[suitcase|suitcases]].

#### See also

Duffel coats were originally made from duffel, a thick woolen fabric also used to make [[duffel bag|duffel bag]]s. The name comes from Duffel, a town in Belgium where the fabric originated.

A post that is the same or inferior to an already existing post. This tag only applies to inferior posts that were uploaded **after** an already existing identical post.

Duplicates should not be confused for the following:

- [[image sample|image sample]], an image typically used by sites to load images faster.
- [[md5 mismatch|md5 mismatch]], an post that has a different md5 from the file at the source.
- [[revision|revision]], a post that has been revised by the artist from a previous version.
- [[variant set|variant set]], posts with a similar base, but non-trivial differences.
- [[scan|scan]], a post that has been scanned from another source.

A few cases where the tag applies:

- Images with [[pixel-perfect duplicate|identical pixel data]], but different metadata.
- Lower resolution versions of the same post.
- [[resized|resized]] posts. Note that duplicate resized posts should not be tagged with [[md5 mismatch|md5 mismatch]].
- Images of generally lower quality; often a result of [[jpeg artifacts|jpeg artifacts]].

Before you upload something, check if it has already been uploaded by using the [IQDB image search](http://danbooru.iqdb.org/) or the "Find similar" button.

Most duplicates are tagged manually; only [[pixel-perfect duplicate|pixel-perfect duplicate]]s are tagged automatically. There is no automated system in place to accurately tag non pixel-perfect duplicates given how easy it is to confuse them for the above (with the exception [[image sample|image sample]]s where the original is already uploaded).

###### Notes:
- **Do not flag a duplicate post for deletion if your only reason is that the post is a duplicate.**
- Don't add the duplicate tag on posts with visual differences ([[variant set|variants]], [[revision|revisions]], [[textless version|textless version]]s etc.).
- Avoid uploading visually identical posts.
  - Check for differences with [DuplicateBooru](https://duplicatebooru.zipfiled.info/) if you are unable to confirm with your own eyes.

#### Related tags

Not to be confused with [[multiple sources|multiple sources]], although they may overlap sometimes.

- [[multiple sources|multiple sources]] is about outside sources -- it means that multiple copies are available outside Danbooru.
- [[duplicate|duplicate]] is about Danbooru -- it means that we have multiple copies of the same image.

#### See also

- [[help:upload|help:upload]]
- [[help:image source|help:image source]]

Since Easter frequently occurs in either March or April, it also uses images and colors related to the season of spring.

A girl with a cheerful sort of "face forward" personality, her fighting style is the very essence of cleverness. Because her body can't handle the high-speed maneuvers of dog fighting for an extended period of time it was necessary for her to learn a style that married careful observation of the target to a single decisive blow and follow-through escape. Possibly metaphorical, references are made to her "true form" surfacing, as if she never developed her condition. Part of this form is her familiar upgrading to the [[kyuubi|kyuubi]], or nine-tailed, ascendant spirit foxes of Japanese mythology.

Her Pilot archetype is Edmund Roßmann. According to her profile in SWII Vol. 3's booklet, her nickname "Paula" is based on the Latin "Paulus," meaning "small." (This also parallels Edmund Roßmann's nickname of "Paule," a male variant.)

**Ehoumaki** (恵方巻き, lit. "[[ehou|Lucky-Direction]] [[makizushi|makizushi]]") refers to the custom in the Kansai region of eating a *futomaki* (a type of [[sushi|sushi]]) on the evening of [[setsubun|setsubun]] (February 3rd) while facing "Ehou" (the lucky direction that changes according to the year) or to the [[makizushi|makizushi]] itself. Much like [[valentine|valentine]]'s Day chocolate, it is almost a man-made custom spread by promotional activities of concerned bodies for reasons purely related to profit and sales.

In the 1970s, it spread through the Kansai region thanks to [[nori (seaweed)|nori]] distributors/wholesalers and [[sushi|sushi]] shops, and in the 2000s, it spread throughout Japan thanks to the [[convenience store|convenience store]] industry. In other words, this custom is very new to places outside of Kansai.

Eila Ilmatar Juutilainen (エイラ・イルマタル・ユーティライネン, Eira Irumataru Yūtirainen?) is a witch of the [[501st joint fighter wing|501st joint fighter wing]], originating from [[suomus|suomus]] and affiliated with the Suomus Air Force. She is referred to as "Illu" by her friends, and is sometimes named Diamond Ace. Her familiar is the black [[fox|fox]].

Eila's magic ability Foresight (未来予知, Mirai Yochi) grants her a limited ability to predict the future. Her hobby is fortune-telling with tarot cards, although the accuracy of her predictions is questionable at best. Similar to stereotypes of her familiar (the black fox), she has a reputation for mischief, being fond of pranks amongst her colleagues and is somewhat mischievous.

Eila is often partnered with 501st Night Witch [[sanya v. litvyak|sanya v. litvyak]], and perhaps as a result (perhaps it is simply chemistry) the two have become very close; Eila is often portrayed as fiercely protective of her younger squadmate and takes on a sometimes awkwardly nurturing role during down-time. Whether this interest is romantic or plain, big-sisterly fondness is up for interpretation. 

Eila is based on the #1-ranked Finnish flying ace (and #1-ranked non-German flying ace) [Eino Ilmari Juutilainen](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eino_Juutilainen.) Like Eila, he bore the nickname "Illu" amongst his friends. Her magic ability, Foresight, is a reference to Eino having never been hit by enemy fire.

She has an older sister, [[aurora e. juutilainen|Aurora E. Juutilainen]].

One of the main factions in [[warhammer 40k|warhammer 40k]], the Eldar (stylized as Aeldari) are a highly-psychic, [[elf|elf]]-like race whose history stretches back millions of years before the current setting. Once the most powerful empire in the galaxy, the Eldar would fall to unprecedented decadence and corruption, resulting in the formation of the Chaos god Slannesh and the fall of their empire (and with it, finishing off humanity's already-weakened pre-[[imperium of man|Imperial]] government, starting the Age of Strife). A few would survive aboard massive Craftworlds, having seen the impending fall and evacuating ahead of time. The Fall, however, continues to haunt their species, as Eldar who die and whose souls are not transferred to a special Soulstone are instead consumed by Slannesh.

In recent editions given the increased threat [[chaos (warhammer)|chaos (warhammer)]] poses to the galaxy, some Eldar groups have begrudgingly cooperated with the Imperium of Man, given their common enemy.

The Eldritch Abomination is a type of creature defined by their complete disregard for the natural laws of the universe as we understand them and the love for body horror. Their physical form (if they even have one) is so bizarre, it even can make someone mad just by looking it. All Lovecraftian Horrors ([[cthulhu|cthulhu]], [[hastur|hastur]], [[nyarlathotep|nyarlathotep]] etc.) are of this type.

An electrical device with revolving vanes used for ventilation and general comfort. One should not stick their finger between the grills. You can make alien sounds by [[fan speaking|speaking in front of this device while it's running.]]

This tag is generally used for corded or battery-powered fans. Electric fans mounted to ceilings should just be tagged [[ceiling fan|ceiling fan]] instead.

A [[guitar|guitar]] that uses a pickup to convert the vibration of its strings into electrical impulses. The most common guitar pickup uses the principle of direct electromagnetic induction. The signal generated by an electric guitar is too weak to drive a loudspeaker, so it is amplified before sending it to a loudspeaker.

This musical instrument is widely used in rock music.

Generally distinguishable from stovetop kettles by featuring a window to view the water level, having control buttons on it, having a port to connect to its electric base, or simply having an electric cord coming out of it.  Many such electric kettles feature a metal and plastic exterior.  Some feature all glass sides, but not a glass bottom given the presence of the heating element in the base.

While the smaller details of her design are often changed each time she is drawn, there are several constants: long to very long [[white hair|white hair]] with [[sidelocks|sidelocks]] and a [[hime cut|hime cut]], some sort of strange [[headgear|headgear]], [[blue eyes|blue eyes]] (sometimes depicted by fan artists as green), a form-hugging black (formerly blue) [[bodysuit|bodysuit]], and a sleeveless blue [[microdress|microdress]] with [[neon trim|neon trim]].

A fantastical humanoid race characterized by their lithe frame, great finesse, youthful appearance despite long lifespans, and [[pointy ears|pointy ears]]. Codified by [[tolkien's legendarium|Tolkienian literature]].

In anime-styled works, elves' characteristic were further stylized into simply a "human with pointy ears", with them almost always have [[blonde hair|blonde hair]]. As a result, they are often indistinguishable from half-elves. Many works (particularly NSFW) also exploit elves' longetivity by either depicting them as being more endowed than ordinary human or as a "[[loli|loli]] baba" (mature adult in child-like body) stereotypes.

Elizabeth F. Beurling is a witch in the [[507th joint fighter wing|507th joint fighter wing]] (AKA "Silent Witches", AKA "Suomus Misfits"). Her home country is "Faraway Land", which is a Britannian commonwealth that is analogous to Canada. Her familiar was originally the dachshund, however was later canonically changed to the Irish Setter. Her weapons are a Bren Mk. 1 Light Machinegun and a Gurkha knife. Her hair is brown in the ilustratons but described as grey in the prose.

Elizabeth is the "bad girl" of the Suomus Misfits: she is cold and often distant in demeanor, feeling no need to engage in niceties and openly resentful of authority or bureaucracy. Furthermore, she is a chain smoker and likely an alcoholic. Under this exterior, however, is a girl who is fond and even protective of her squadmates. Her relationship with [[elma leivonen|elma leivonen]] and [[anabuki tomoko|anabuki tomoko]], in particular, are portrayed as close, if tumultuous.

Elizabeth is based on the #1 ranked Canadian RCAF ace George F. Beurling, known varyingly as the "Malta Spitfire" and "The Knight of Malta" for his success in the area. Both carried reputations for resenting authority, a sometimes astounding natural talent for aerial combat, and switching corps, however unlike Elizabeth, George was a strict non-smoker.

An indie roguelike game, available in English and Japanese.  The game is known for its peculiar sense of humor.  It was created by a single author, but was abandoned unfinished.  It has since been taken up as an open-source project by multiple modders as "Elona+" and received expansions, but the original plot is likely never to be finished as it was intended.

"Elona" is a portmanteau of "Eternal League Of NefiA", a mysterious (to the point of being only mentioned once in the unfinished plot) organization apparently behind fate. 

Elona takes place on a world called Irva, where the world is tormented by the blowing of the etherwinds, which cause mutations that kill humanoids and make monsters more powerful and ferocious.  Because the etherwinds come from the Vindale Forest, home of the [[elf|elf]]-like Elea, the world stands ready to bring war to Vindale.

Elona blends standard RPG tropes with a Lovecraftian theme (including a Sanity meter).  It also features guns, cyborgs, steampunk, references to the likes of [[aliens (1986)|aliens (1986)]] and [[bioshock (series)|bioshock (series)]] and many other dissimilar tropes to create an oddball fantasy/sci-fi kitchen sink.

You can read a translation of the plot here: ~~http://elona.squares.net/forum/viewtopic.php?f=3&t=5025 ~~

Emoji are Unicode characters designed to represent pictograms and [[emoticon|emoticons]]. The term itself, however, is most often used to refer to the pictograms and emoticons themselves. The word "Emoji" comes from the Japanese word "絵" (*e*, "picture") + "文字" (*moji*, "character"). Its resemblance to the word "emoticon" is purely coincidental.

Emoji as we know them originated as a proprietary system by a Japanese mobile phone operator [[ntt docomo|ntt docomo]] using a Unicode private-use block to encode their emoticons. While other mobile providers used many other systems for emoji, this system was the most compact implementation used at the time (and the closest to the current one).

The very first Emoji were actually Unicode Dingbats, of which, quite a few are now official Emoji. Emoji became a standardized system with its implementation in Unicode 6.0 in 2010 but it's only around 2014-2015 that their use exploded and became commonplace to the point that they became a cultural phenomenon with real world merchandise and even a movie about them.

Lines drawn in a burst pattern, radiating outward from a part of the image to which the artist wants to draw attention. They cause the area surrounded by the lines to stand out more in the viewer's eye.

These are not the same as [[speed lines|speed lines]], which indicate motion; emphasis lines indicate *focus*, rather than motion.

A similar technique used in filmography is to focus the camera toward a specific part of the shot (sometimes off-center) while allowing other parts of the image to become unfocused, thus drawing extra attention to the focused area.

England is one of the four constituent countries of the [[united kingdom|united kingdom]]. It shares land borders with [[scotland|scotland]] to the north and [[wales|wales]] to the west; the Irish Sea is to the northwest, the Celtic Sea to the southwest, while the North Sea to the east and the English Channel to the south separate it from continental Europe. Most of England comprises the central and southern part of the island of Great Britain in the North Atlantic. The country also includes over 100 smaller islands such as the Isles of Scilly and the Isle of Wight.

Its capital city, [[london|london]], also serves as the capital of the United Kingdom as a whole. It served as the host of [[2012 summer olympics|2012 summer olympics]].

When hair poofs out above a [[scarf|scarf]] (or similar apparel, like [[headphones around neck|headphones around neck]]).

It is named after the fins near the tip of the mantle of the Japanese flying [[squid|squid]], which in turn takes its name from Emperor [[napoleon bonaparte|napoleon bonaparte]] due to the fins' resemblance to his [[bicorne|bicorne]].

Users on pixiv largely refer to this look as えんぺら (enpera), but on other sites such as Nicoseiga the term マフモコ (mafumoko) may also be used. This phrase in particular is a contraction of two words: マフラー (muffler, [[scarf|scarf]]) and モコ (moko, onomatopoeia for soft and fluffy).

A genus of flowering [[cactus|cacti]]. Its [[flower|flower]]s are famous for blooming at night instead of during the day. Some species, such as *Epiphyllum oxypetalum*, bloom for only one night and wilt in the morning. Nowadays there are also day-blooming hybrids.

Epiphyllum represents a layered flower with thin, long outer petals and thicker, shorter inner petals. Common epiphyllums are white, but hybrids can also be orange, pink, red and yellow. Common names include **climbing cactus**, **Dutchman's pipe cactus**, **[[orchid|orchid]]  cactus** and **queen of the night**.

Its Japanese name 月下美人 *(gekka-bijin)* literally translates to "beauty under the moon". The one-night bloom of *Epiphyllum oxypetalum* is often used as a metaphor for the transience of beauty.

When an offensive, harsh or blunt expression is replaced with an mild, indirect or vague one. 

Visual euphemisms exist, too, such as the one used for [[akiyama mio|akiyama mio]]'s accidental [[pantyshot|pantyshot]] in the [[k-on!|k-on!]] anime (a stripped bowl of rice) or when [[swastika|swastika]] or the [[hammer and sickle|hammer and sickle]] are replaced with more innocuous symbols to avoid offending the audience and/or so the work won't run afoul of laws banning the public display of either symbols.

An orthographic euphemism is spelling a word deliberately wrong (e.g. "porn" becomes "pr0n", "n0rp" or "prawn") to circumvent censorship algorithms on the usenet, websites, social media apps, etc.

**Euphonium** (from the Greek word *εὔφωνος*, meaning "well-sounding" or "sweet-voiced") is a conical-bore, baritone-voiced brass [[instrument|instrument]]. The euphonium is a valved instrument; nearly all current models are piston valved, though rotary valved models do exist.

A person who plays the euphonium is sometimes called a *euphoniumist*, *euphophonist*, or a *euphonist*, while British players often colloquially refer to themselves as *euphists*, or *euphologists*. Similarly, the instrument itself is often referred to as *eupho* or *euph*.

Visually, the euphonium has a similar appearance to its better known cousin, the [[tuba|tuba]], the difference being the former is slightly smaller and has a slightly higher pitch than the latter.

A science-fiction MMORPG developed by Icelandic company CCP Games. It is currently the only single-shard MMORPG in existence, meaning all players share a single world (called New Eden) of over 14,000 star systems, running on the gaming industry's most powerful server.

Players take control of a 'capsuleer', an augmented human (there are no alien species in the universe, with the possible exception of the reclusive Jove, who were originally humans as well, but have undergone extensive genetic modification, resulting in what is practically a new species) whose consciousness is transferred to a clone in the event of death, making the capsuleer immortal. Capsuleers travel in small capsules (hence the name) that protect them from various dangers in space, and which, in turn, are docked into larger ships, creating a conduit between the capsuleer brain and the ship systems in order to pilot the ship.

Expansions used to be issued twice a year, but towards the end of 2014, CCP Games switched to a release cycle of 4-6 weeks between expansions.

The game is (in)famous for its steep learning curve, stemming from the many opportunities and possibilities players are faced with, all of which are available from day one.

An [[esports|esports]] [[fighting game|fighting game]] tournament held annually in [[las vegas|las vegas]], Nevada, [[united states|united states]]. Generally considered the *de facto* world championship for most fighting games, due to its large turnout.

#### Notable events that have inspired fanart
- 2004: [[evo moment|evo moment]], where during a *[[street fighter iii (series)|Street Fighter III]]: 3rd Strike* match between [[umehara daigo|umehara daigo]] and [[justin wong (gamer)|Justin Wong]], Umehara fully parries a [[chun-li|chun-li]] super performed by Wong with little life left on his [[ken masters|Ken]], to turn the tables on Wong and win the round. The video of this moment and the wild crowd reaction to it became a viral hit on the Internet and inspires many tributes.
- 2013: The Evo organizers announce 7 games for the event, and announce an 8th game will be decided by a donation drive for cancer research, with the game whose community donates the most money getting the spot at the tournament. The two games raising the most money during the drive are *[[skullgirls|skullgirls]]* and *[[super smash bros.|super smash bros.]] Melee*, with *Melee* ultimately winning out and getting the spot in the tournament. 
- 2014: French player Luffy wins the *[[street fighter iv (series)|Ultra Street Fighter IV]]* tournament with [[rose (street fighter)|Rose]], being the first non-Asian player to win an Evo *SFIV* tournament. 
- 2015: During a *[[guilty gear xrd|guilty gear xrd]]* match between Woshige and Ogawa, Woshige celebrates too early after winning a round and his unattended [[millia rage|millia rage]] is swiftly beaten by Ogawa's [[zato-1|zato-1]] in the decisive round of the match.
- 2018: The first Evo event outside the United States is held in Tokyo, Japan as [Evo Japan 2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evo_Japan_2018.)
- 2024: In a moment during a *[[street fighter iii (series)|Street Fighter III]]: 3rd Strike* Losers Quarterfinals match popularly dubbed "[[evo moment|evo moment]]", [[hugo andore|Hugo]] main [[hayao (gamer)|hayao (gamer)]] managed to execute an air parry against FrankieBFG's Ken, then narrowly avoiding Ken's spinning kick with a Standing Heavy Kick (which is widely considered the worst nornal move in the game), and proceed to deal match-winning blow while living on the "magic pixel". Another notable moment within the match was when Hayao performed a [[split|split]] while playing the game.

The **Grumman F-14 "Tomcat"** was a large and heavy twin-engine [[fighter jet|jet fighter]]-interceptor, first of the "Teen" series of US jet fighters and the last "Cat" manufactured by Bethpage, New York-based Grumman "Iron Works" Aerospace Corporation. The swing-wing two-seater entered service with its main user, the [[united states navy|united states navy]], in 1974 and was retired in 2006. However, [[iran|iran]], the only country that the F-14 was exported to (prior to the 1979 revolution), still operates the type with local modification.

The F-14 is widely recognized in various forms of pop culture. It was prominently featured in the movie [[top gun|top gun]], in a large number of air combat [[video game|video game]]s and flight simulators, and furthermore is the visual model on which the [[macross|macross]] [[vf-1|vf-1]] *Valkyrie* is loosely based.

The F-14 was armed with an M61 20mm cannon in the nose and carried TARPS and ROVER systems for reconnaissance. Air-to-air weapons included the long-range AIM-54 Phoenix, AIM-7 Sparrow and AIM-9 Sidewinder. For ground attack missions a variety of freefall and precision guided munitions could be carried.

The **Boeing F-15 Eagle** is a twin-engined [[fighter jet|fighter jet]] developed by McDonnell Douglas (now part of Boeing). It is one of the most easily recognized of the "Teen" series of fighters, with its prominent bubble canopy, dual vertical tailfins, sawtoothed elevators, and broad delta wing. It was designed in the 1960-1970s under the Fighter Experimental program as a replacement for the [[f-4 phantom ii|f-4 phantom ii]] and to counter aircraft like the [[mig-25|mig-25]] with record-setting climb performance and impressive top speed while retaining good dogfight capability. Sometimes called the "Twin-tailed Tennis Court," due to its large size.

The air superiority models' armament includes air-to-air missiles and an internal 20mm cannon. The F-15E Strike Eagle variant, optimized for ground attack missions, carries an additional crew member in a second seat.

The **Lockheed Martin F-22 Raptor** is an American fifth generation single-seat, twin-engine state-of-the-art advanced fighter [[aircraft|aircraft]] that uses stealth technology. It was designed primarily as an air superiority fighter, but has several additional capabilities that include ground attack, electronic warfare and reconnaissance. 

The F-22 was developed from the original YF-22 prototype flight tested during 1990. The first mass produced F-22s first flew in 1997 and were officially introduced several years later in 2005. 

The F-22 is the first mass produced fifth generation aircraft ever created and is still considered the most advanced operational fighter jet in the world. Lockheed Martin Aeronautics and Boeing Defense continue to be major partners in maintaining the United States of America Raptor fleet.

JP: ハヤブサ *hayabusa* (falcon, peregrine falcon)

A type of [[bird|bird]] of prey with thin, tapered wings, which enable them to fly at high speed and change direction rapidly. This group of about 40 species includes kestrels, hobbies, merlins, gyrfalcons and [[peregrine falcon|peregrine falcon]]s. Unlike hawks and eagles, falcons kill prey with their beaks, which have a tooth-like ridge.

A male falcon is called a tiercel (British spelling: tercel); downy [[chick|chick]]s are eyas.

The technique of hunting with trained captive birds of prey is known as falconry.

The Japanese word for falcon, ハヤブサ, is a synonym for the peregrine falcon. Kestrels are チョウゲンボウ (*chōgenbō*).

If there isn't any text in the image at all, use your best judgement; [[open mouth|open mouth]], [[leaning forward|leaning forward]], [[closed eyes|closed eyes]], etc. are all good markers. 

Notably, Japanese children can be heard saying 「我々は宇宙人だ」, or "We are aliens", in front of a fan, owing to the alien-like voice distortion the fan produces.

Fate/Apocrypha is based around a parallel world to the [[fate/stay night|fate/stay night]] canon, where the Holy Grail was removed from Fuyuki City after the third War. The plot focuses on the reappearance of the Grail at Trifas during the 2000s (around the time the fifth Fuyuki War would have occurred) and the rivalry between the Black and Red Factions, each composed of renegades and loyalists to the Mage's Association, respectively, each summoning seven Servants of each type, with the Grail itself summoning [[jeanne d'arc (fate)|jeanne d'arc (fate)]] as mediator.

Fate/EXTELLA (フェイト/エクステラ, localized as *Fate/EXTELLA: The Umbral Star*) is an action game for the [[playstation 4|playstation 4]], [[playstation vita|playstation vita]], PC, and [[nintendo switch|nintendo switch]], taking place in the [[fate/extra|fate/extra]] world. It has a sequel of its own, [[fate/extella link|fate/extella link]].

Fate/EXTELLA takes place after the Moon Holy Grail War depicted in [[fate/extra|fate/extra]], but **in a slightly different continuity from its events** (similar to the three classic [[fate (series)|fate (series)]] routes). The plot is divided into several arcs, representing different but linked timelines. In each arc the player takes control of a different Hakuno, who must work with their Servant to overcome competing parties.

Fate/EXTRA CCC  (フェイト／エクストラ) is a RPG and action game for the [[playstation portable|playstation portable]] and a "sequel/companion" game to [[fate/extra|fate/extra]], released in Spring 2013.

The game is set on the Far Side of the Moon Cell, where [[bb (fate/extra)|bb (fate/extra)]] used her abilities to create the Sakura Labyrinth. She brought over various Masters and Servants from the Moon Cell Holy Grail War on the Near Side, some taken instantly before their deletion and others brought during the sixth week. The story is described as [[fate/extra|EXTRA]]'s "[[heaven's feel|heaven's feel]]" route. Essentially, it's an alternate continuation of its events.

Many of the supporting characters from [[fate/extra|fate/extra]] return.

The Fender Precision Bass, also known as the Fender P Bass, is an electric [[bass guitar|bass guitar]] that was introduced by [[fender musical instruments corporation|Fender]] in 1951. It is widely regarded as the first commercially successful electric bass guitar and has since become a staple instrument in popular music.

The Precision Bass features a solid body made of ash or alder wood, a bolt-on maple neck, and a rosewood or maple fingerboard. It is equipped with a split single-coil pickup that produces a distinctive, punchy sound with a strong low-end response. The P Bass also features a unique design that allows for easy and precise tuning, making it a popular choice for bass players who demand accuracy and reliability.

Two basic designs exist. The original design (seen on post #1233086) was based on the [[fender telecaster|fender telecaster]]. In 1957, Fender introduced new, now more common design (seen on post #741032 ) based on the [[fender stratocaster|fender stratocaster]]. The original design was reintroduced in 1968, but was renamed to Telecaster bass. 

Within anime and manga, [[yamada ryo|yamada ryo]] from [[bocchi the rock!|bocchi the rock!]] is associated with the instrument, playing one with a white body, a white pickguard and a rosewood fretboard.

Designs and prototypes were made around 1953 which were subsequently set into production without minor changes including colors and finishes. Noted and recognised as a revolutionary and innovative guitar at the time, the Stratocaster quickly gained worldwide renown and became one of the most popular electric guitars in history, with its basic design still being used and modified by many other guitar manufacturers to this day. The [[fender stratocaster|fender stratocaster]], alongside the [[fender telecaster|fender telecaster]], have been used across a wide range of musical genres by countless musicians, with the Strat being associated with legendary guitarists like [[yngwie malmsteen|yngwie malmsteen]], [[eric clapton|eric clapton]], and [[jimi hendrix|jimi hendrix]].

The Telecaster is a solid-body [[electric guitar|electric guitar]] that was introduced in 1951 by [[fender musical instruments corporation|Fender]]. It is considered one of the most significant guitar designs in history, having influenced numerous musicians across a variety of genres. The Telecaster's versatility and distinctive sound have made it a popular choice among musicians in various styles of music, including country, rock, blues, and punk.

Features a relatively simple design, with a single-cutaway body made of either ash or alder wood, a bolt-on maple neck, and a rosewood or maple fingerboard. The guitar's unique bridge design allows for precise intonation and sustain. It is equipped with two single-coil pickups, which produce a bright and clear tone that has become a hallmark of the Telecaster sound.

Since its introduction, the Telecaster has undergone numerous changes and variations, including different pickup configurations, finishes, and neck shapes. However, its fundamental design has remained largely unchanged, making it a timeless and enduring symbol of electric guitar innovation and craftsmanship.

The Fig Sign is a hand gesture made with the hand and fingers curled into a fist and the thumb thrust between the middle and index fingers (or more rarely the middle and ring finger).  While not readily known in the US and many other English speaking countries, the same hand sign is used while playing the children's game I've Got Your Nose. 

The origin of the gesture is unknown and its meaning varies depending on where you are in the world.  In some places the gesture is used for good luck, particularly when used on small decorative hands carved into this gesture that are used as charms, in others, it's used as a mild version of the [[middle finger|middle finger]] (such as in Russia, where it is called colloquially "кукиш/kukish" or "дуля/dulya", and is seen as a rude way to reject, deny, or dismiss someone).  The meaning of the gesture in the images on Danbooru will commonly mean something akin to "let's fuck."

A form of remote weapon unique to the [[nu gundam|nu gundam]]/[[hi-nu gundam|hi-nu gundam]] (and retroactively, its testbed unit, the [[delta gundam kai|delta gundam kai]]). Despite their name, the fin funnels equipped on Nu Gundam/Hi-Nu Gundam are in function "[[bit (gundam)|bits]]", since they have built-in generators rather than the E-caps used by [[funnels (gundam)|funnels (gundam)]]. While this made them much more expensive to construct, and allowed less modules to be equipped than the standard, this had the enormous benefit of giving the fin funnels a tremendously long operational time. Circling the battlefield on their own, the fin funnels could be utilized in far more creative and strategic ways than standard funnels.

The actual beam fired by the fin funnels was also more powerful, given that they are emitted by a generator instead of an E-cap, allowing for better performance compared to Zeon's funnels. The fin funnels also had the ability to generate a unique beam shield, known as a "fin funnel barrier", to provide a defense against both beam weaponry and solid projectiles with lower outputs compared to the beam shield's power consumption. Although these unique funnels proved incredibly effective and flexible in purpose, they were also much larger than the standard funnel, making them easier targets to shoot down. With the help of the [[psycho frame|psycho frame]] technology, Nu Gundam/Hi-Nu Gundam pilot [[amuro ray|amuro ray]] can utilize these fin funnels more effectively by thoughts alone.

It should be noted that the Hi-Nu Gundam is capable of recharging and refueling its fin funnels, thanks to the upgrades on its backpack.

This tag can also refer to fin-shaped remote weapons or those that physically resemble the Nu Gundam/Hi-Nu Gundam's fin funnels.

A popular, long-running role-playing game series by [[square enix|square enix]].

Final Fantasy first appeared in 1987 in reaction to Enix's [[dragon quest|dragon quest]]. Contrarily to what is often said, while Square wasn't doing great at the time, the first game wasn't made as a last ditch attempt to save the company. It did end up being a great commercial success and as a result, subsequent titles (each set in a different universe) were published ever since.

d:
Sixth JRPG developed by Square Co., Inc. (now [[square enix|square enix]]) for the [[final fantasy|final fantasy]] series, and one of the most popular games of the series. It was the last Final Fantasy for the SNES, released 2 April 1994. It saw a United States release on 20 October 1994 as *Final Fantasy III*, as it was the third game in the series to see release there. It was later re-released on the PlayStation (1999) and Game Boy Advance (2006), both cases using the game's original title in their English release.

The world is engulfed in a struggle between the Gestahlian Empire, which seeks the Espers - godlike entities of pure magic - to use them to conquer the world and the rebel group Returners. Amidst the conflict, fourteen men and women are also seeking not only an end to the Empire's ambitions, but also the truth of the Espers and the world, all the while stopping [[kefka palazzo|an insane Gestahlian general]] from wreaking havoc.

*Final Fantasy VI* is noted for its comparatively large cast of playable characters, somewhat more complex character interactions than was typical for a console RPG at the time, introduction of [[steampunk|steampunk]] elements to a traditional sword-and-sorcery milieu, a famous [[opera|opera]] scene, and a shocking development about midway through the game in which ||the villain actually *succeeds* in his stated goal of destroying the world.  The remainder of the game is spent traversing a post-apocalyptic version of the world, reuniting your scattered party members in a last-ditch effort to prevent the villain's final takeover.||

The seventh JRPG developed by Squaresoft (now [[square enix|square enix]]) in the [[final fantasy|final fantasy]] series, and arguably the most popular game in the series. First released on the PlayStation in 31 January 1997 (after a 3-year hiatus), and then re-released for personal computers in 1998.

The story is about Avalanche, an ecoterrorist organization combating the conglomerate Shinra Electric Power Company which is destroying the world's ecosystem by extracting mako for electricity. One of their latest recruits is acerbic mercenary [[cloud strife|cloud strife]], himself a former member of SOLDIER, Shinra's mako-enhanced supersoldier corps. Soon, however, Avalanche would face an even greater enemy in the form of [[sephiroth|sephiroth]], another former SOLDIER intent on absorbing the planet's power and becoming a god.

A remake, aptly titled [[final fantasy vii remake|final fantasy vii remake]], was announced at Sony's 2015 E3 conference. The remake is a multi-game series, the first installment of which was released in April 2020. It would be followed up by [[final fantasy vii rebirth|final fantasy vii rebirth]] in February 2024.

Groundbreaking arcade two player, cooperative, beat 'em-up [[video game|video game]] released by [[capcom|capcom]] in 1989.

It was ported to the Super Famicon and [[super nintendo|super nintendo]] home consoles and had two sequels exclusive for those two systems initially, as well as a Mega-CD/[[sega|sega]]-CD port and a [[game boy|game boy]] port (notable because it added character designs from the [[street fighter zero (series)|street fighter zero (series)]] series). There also have been several subsequent compilations of this video game for modern consoles in recent years.

***Final Fight*** is included in the 2005 compilation *Capcom Classics Collection* Volume 1 for the [[playstation 2|playstation 2]] and [[xbox (original)|xbox (original)]], and in the 2006 portable version *Capcom Classics Collection Remixed* for the [[playstation portable|playstation portable]]. 

More recently, the arcade version of Final Fight was released in a two-in-one bundle titled *Final Fight: Double Impact*, alongside the arcade game [[magic sword|magic sword]], for the [[xbox 360|xbox 360]] Xbox Live Arcade and the [[playstation 3|playstation 3]] PlayStation Network in 2010. 

Developers of the game have declared that it was partially inspired by the [[double dragon|double dragon]] arcade hit Game from 1987 and also by an American 80s action/musical film called *[Streets of Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streets_of_fire) * of which many of the production staff were fans.

The game is connected to the [[street fighter|street fighter]] universe, with several characters from Final Fight have either made playable debut or featured as cameo.

##### Featured Heroes - See [[list of fire emblem characters|list of fire emblem characters]]. ##### Hero Classifications At the time of writing, Heroes in the game can be grouped into the following types: **Details:** - Regular: Refers to Heroes in their standard, default versions. Often as they'd be seen during their respective games. - Fallen: Refers to Heroes as corrupted versions of their regular selves. The game treats them as regular Heroes for many purposes. - Brave: Refers to Heroes as idealized versions of themselves manifested by the imagination of the people. Determined each year by voting, their appearance, personality and weapons vary greatly. The game treats them as regular Heroes for summoning purposes but as Special Heroes for others. - Resplendent: Refers to Heroes (Regular or Brave) wearing special regalia associated to one of the game-original kingdoms. - Special: Catch-all term used to refer to Heroes wearing costumes themed after various festivities or events, be they game-specific or game-equivalents. - Day of Devotion (Valentine's Day equivalent) - Spring (Easter equivalent) - Bridal (self-explanatory) - Children (loli/shota versions) - Desert Festival (themed around desert locales from different games) - Wind Festival (themed around wind tribes) - Flame Festival (themed around flame tribes) - Picnic (has not been re-used) - Hot Springs (has not been re-used) - Summer (Swimsuits) - Harvest Festival (Halloween/Oktoberfest equivalent) - Thief Festival (themed around phantom thieves) - Ninja Festival (self-explanatory) - Pirate Festival (self-explanatory) - Day of 12 (has not been re-used; game-specific) - Winter Festival (Christmas equivalent) - New Year's (self-explanatory) - Legendary: Refers to Heroes typically in their end-game states. - Mythic: Refers to Heroes that are myths from their own timelines (gods, progenitors etc) or FEH-original characters - Emblem: Refers to Heroes that are protagonists of mainline games as interpreted within [[fire emblem engage|Engage]]'s system, where they're spirits/stands existing wtihin special rings. - Rearmed: Refers to Heroes wielding special, cursed weapons. Valuable in-game due to their special properties during inheritance. - Attuned: Refers to Heroes wielding special skills. Valuable in-game due to their special properties during inheritance. - Ascended: Refers to Heroes often in their post-game state. Valuble in-game due to brining extremely-limited items with them. #### External Links - [Official Website](https://fire-emblem-heroes.com/) - [Official Twitter (JP)](https://twitter.com/fe_heroes_jp) - "Fire Emblem Heroes Wiki":[https://feheroes.gamepedia.com/Main_Page] - "Wikipedia: Fire Emblem Heroes":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire_Emblem_Heroes]

A catchall tag for weapons depicting guns with firing mechanisms that predate the use of [[cartridge|cartridges]] and relied on an external mechanism to ignite the powder in the gun. 

The firing mechanisms this tag includes are: 

- [[caplock|caplock]]: A mechanism where a hammer strikes a percussion cap of shock-sensitive explosive that ignites and sends flame into the barrel igniting the gunpowder in the gun barrel.  Replaced the flintlock. 
- [[flintlock|flintlock]]: A mechanism where a hammer holding flint strikes a piece of steel and produces sparks. The sparks fall into a pan of gunpowder and ignites the powder. A small hole from the pan to the barrel allows flame to travel and ignite the powder in the barrel. Replaced the matchlock and wheellock. 
- [[matchlock|matchlock]]: A mechanism where a small lever, called a serpentine, holds a piece of slow burning match cord and lowers it into a pan of powder. The powder ignites and flame travel through a small hole in the pan into the barrel igniting the powder in the barrel. 
- [[wheellock|wheellock]]: A mechanism where a small arm, called a "dog", holds a piece of pyrite that strikes down against a spinning wheel of steel. This produces sparks that ignite a pan of powder that sends flame through a hole in the barrel and ignites  the powder in the barrel. 

If the weapon's firing mechanism is easily identifiable, use one of the more specific tags under this tag. If the weapon's firing mechanism is not easily identifiable, but is recognizable as a pre-cartridge firing mechanism, then just use this tag only and do not guess at one of the more specific types.

**The Five Star Stories** (ファイブスター物語, Faibu Sutā Monogatari?) is a space opera and [[mecha|mecha]] manga series created by [[nagano mamoru|nagano mamoru]], building on his work on the anime series [[juusenki l-gaim|juusenki l-gaim]]. 

The first volume of the manga was published in April 10, 1986 and is still ongoing.

The story is staged at an alien cluster of four major planetary systems. The God of Light, [[amaterasu (five star stories)|amaterasu (five star stories)]], the immortal emperor of the Grees Kingdom on the planet Delta Belune, is destined to rule the whole Joker System. He and [[lachesis (five star stories)|lachesis (five star stories)]], his bride and fatima, are the main characters of this epic [[science fiction|science fiction]] story.

An anime film adaptation of the first volume, directed by Yamazaki Kazuo, was released in 1989.

**As of March 31, 2021, uploading flash files is no longer possible.** See forum #183397 for details.

This tag is for games, [[music video|music video]]s, and [[animated|animations]] created using Adobe Flash.

While Flash enjoyed success from the late 1990s to the late 2000s (especially because of the failure of the Java platform in the web), it eventually declined as JavaScript and other browser-agnostic platforms like HTML5 and WebGL matured. Adobe, recognizing that Flash lost its relevance over time, announced in 2017 that in-browser Flash plugins would no longer be supported after December 2020; all major browsers permanently removed Flash support by the end of January 2021.

As of March 2021, Danbooru is set up to automatically load all Flash posts using Ruffle.js, which uses "WebAssembly":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WebAssembly] to emulate Flash in modern browsers as a part of the broader "Ruffle Project":[https://ruffle.rs]. While this means you can view Flash posts without falling back on an outdated browser that's old enough to still support the original Flash Player, please keep in mind that Ruffle's core emulation of Flash **is still in an alpha state** and it's less likely to work with files that are newer and/or more complex. See [[ruffle compatible|ruffle compatible]] for posts that have been manually confirmed to work with the version of Ruffle.js that Danbooru is currently using.

The **FAL** (*Fusil Automatique Léger*, "Light Automatic Rifle") is a Belgian-designed 7.62×51mm NATO **[[battle rifle|battle rifle]]**. It was developed between 1947-1953 by "Dieudonné Saive":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dieudonné_Saive] at [[fn herstal|fn herstal]]. Known as "the right arm of the Free World", it was the second most widely used [[military|military]] [[rifle|rifle]] in the world (after the AK) during the [[cold war|cold war]], being used by 77 different nations. was nearly adopted by the United States Army as well, but was rejected in favor of the M14.

Identifying characteristics include the tubular charging handle on the left side on the receiver, the shape and location of the [[muzzle device|muzzle device]] and front sight post, and barrel length exposed before the perforated triangular handguard (useful for differentiating it from Heckler & Koch [[weapon|weapon]]s of similar profile, such as the [[h&k g3|G3]]). This tag applies to any full-length FAL variants, such as the British L1A1, Austrian StG58, and the Israeli IMI Romat with tubular handguard.

Later depictions from the era of color film gave the monster [[grey skin|grey]] or [[green skin|green skin]].

**Frieza** is one of the main antagonist of the [[dragon ball|dragon ball]] franchise, first introduced in [[dragon ball z|dragon ball z]] as the titular main antagonist of the Frieza Saga. 

The Emperor of Universe 7, he was responsible for the genocide of the Saiyans. His goal in the original appearance is to find the Namekian [[dragon ball (object)|dragon ball (object)]]s to grant him the wish for immortality. He first appears in his [[1st form frieza|1st form]], before going through each ([[2nd form frieza|2nd form]] and [[3rd form frieza|3rd]]), before revealing his [[final form frieza|final form]] (which he can charge up to [[full power frieza|full power]]). His last appearance in the original manga would see him [[mecha frieza|mechanically enhanced]].

Best known for his cold, arrogant, and egotistical altitude, along with his sadistic tendencies towards his enemies or anyone belonging to the race he deemed inferior, both verbally and physically. This later became an archtypical trait of several all-powerful and self-centered villains in various manga and anime. He also has a rivalry with his non-canonical older brother, [[cooler (dragon ball)|cooler (dragon ball)]].

His [[frieza clan|clan]] is known for having multiple forms and named after cold objects. He returns in [[dragon ball super|dragon ball super]] with new forms, [[golden frieza|golden frieza]] and [[black frieza|black frieza]], themed after credit card levels, the first featuring prominently across Frieza's appearances in Super.

Frutiger Aero is a visual aesthetic primarily utilized in the 2000s to early 2010s for commerical purposes, focusing on the mix of nature with technology, as well as an overall "glossy" look.

The name, coined by the Consumer Aesthetics Research Institute, originates from the "Aero" style from [[windows 7|windows 7]], and the Frutiger font.

Color palettes tend to consist of whites, blues and greens, and the occasional orange. Glossy textures are very common, as are semi-transparent elements. [[lens flare|lens flare]]s and [[bokeh|bokeh]] are also frequently seen, along with "swirly" freeform shapes.

Common thematic elements include colorful [[tropical fish|tropical fish]] and other marine life (often jumping out of a body of shimmering blue [[water|water]]), [[glass|glass]], bright green [[grass|grass]], [[bubble|bubble]]s, the [[aurora|aurora]] phenomenon, [[blue sky|blue skies]], technology of the time period (i.e. [[flip phone|flip phone]]s, 2000s [[computer|computer]]s, [[digital media player|digital media player]]s), and contemporary and retrofuturistic architecture.

A visual aesthetic popular in the mid-late 2000s to early 2010s, and a derivative of [[frutiger aero|frutiger aero]], mixing flat minimalist design styles with overall maximalist imagery.

Common visual elements include gradients, "bloom" or "flourish" shapes, glossy textures, [[bokeh|bokeh]], [[abstract background|abstract background]]s, [[splatter|splatter]] effects, [[no lineart|lineless]] vector drawings, shapes such as [[star (symbol)|star (symbol)]]s and circles, and [[silhouette|silhouette]]s. Bright color palettes consisting mainly of lime green, electric blue, hot pink and neon orange are a staple.

Common thematic elements and motifs include nature imagery similar to Frutiger Aero, [[animal|animal]]s like [[bird|bird]]s and [[butterfly|butterflies]], [[speaker|speaker]]s and [[audio visualizer|audio visualizer]]s, [[flower|floral]] imagery, and music motifs such as [[piano keys|piano keys]] and [[musical note|musical note]]s.

It derives its name from the "Metro" theme of [[windows 8|windows 8]].

The resident doujin artist and [[yaoi|yaoi]] fan of [[itoshiki nozomu|itoshiki nozomu]]'s class. Outside class, she often imagines various male-on-male pairings from various anime and manga, including her own teacher and some of her male classmates. Her tastes are often considered abnormal, in contrast to her orderly long-time classmate [[kitsu chiri|kitsu chiri]]. Her surname is a corruption of "腐女子" - "[[fujoshi|fujoshi]]" ("rotten girl"), a term for yaoi fangirls - and her given name derives from the former venue of the [[comiket|comiket]] before it moved to [[tokyo big sight|tokyo big sight]].

Literally translated as ***rotten girl***, the original meaning is basically a female fan of [[yaoi|yaoi]]. 

The term is more recently being used simply to identify a female [[otaku|otaku]], similar to how the western term "fangirl" has grown to be synonymous with girls who write slash fanfiction of their favored series. It should be noted that the concept of "yumejoshi" (an otaku girl that follows heterosexual girl-targeted works like Otome and Teen's Love) has also come into use, though it is much less infamous than its yaoi counterpart.

While the term [[otaku|otaku]] could be used for males and females, fujoshi specifically identifies females. Male fans of yaoi are called [[fudanshi|fudanshi]] instead. The equivalent words for overzealous fans of [[yuri|yuri]] are [[himejoshi|himejoshi]] and [[himedanshi|himedanshi]].

**Gachimuchi** (or **Wrestling Series**) is a [[meme|meme]]tic universe which revolves around male porn actors (mostly from Can-Am Productions) flexing their muscles, wearing and doing [[bdsm|bdsm]] stuff, and doing *gay pants wrestling* (from where the tag gets its name, "Gachimuchi" meaning *buff man in underwear* in Japan) in homoerotic films taken out of context. Started when [[niconico|niconico]] members uploaded a video of [[billy herrington|billy herrington]] and [[danny lee|danny lee]] doing *pants wrestling* under the title "**本格的 ガチムチパンツレスリング**" (*Professional Pant Wrestler Fighting Seriously*) in 2007. This later spawned tons of parodies around *pants wrestling* and related people that acted in non-pants wrestling porn with a pants wrestler as an actor in the aforementioned porno.

It is often paired with [[manatsu no yo no inmu|manatsu no yo no inmu]] (Inmu-chu) and [[kuso miso technique|kuso miso technique]] ([[yaranaika|yaranaika]]) as the "Holy Homo Trinity" (御三ゲイ), since all three were well-known homoerotic memes that were popular within Japanese communities in the 2000s.

While Gachi parodies did find their way outside of Japan, most prominently between 2007 and 2012, it wasn't until later from 2015 onwards that it spread even further under the name **gachiGASM** (named after the BTTV emotes for [[twitch.tv|twitch.tv]] featuring Billy Herrington's iconic face) and spawned countless more sub-memes.

While Gachimuchi's popularity has decreased with the Japanese (being supplanted by Inmu on Niconico), Gachimuchi is currently extremely popular internationally. On the Chinese video site [[bilibili|bilibili]], the Chinese started making parodies of their popular TV series and movies, and also parodies of Japanese anime. Many Gachimuchi videos became some of the most viewed videos on Bilibili (one having had over 5 million views). This popularity would, however, lead to Bilibili attempting to squash the community on the site, leading to it dispersing across other Chinese communities. It also became popular in Russia, where a live-action parody was made of it. 

The tag used for Gachimuchi on Bilibili and in Chinese communities is **哲♂学 (Learning♂Philosophy)**.
