**Gainax Company, Limited** (株式会社ガイナックス, *Kabushiki-gaisha Gainakkusu*) was a Japanese anime studio famous for works such as [[honneamise no tsubasa|honneamise no tsubasa]], [[top wo nerae!|top wo nerae!]], [[fushigi no umi no nadia|Nadia: The Secret of Blue Water]], [[neon genesis evangelion|neon genesis evangelion]], [[flcl|flcl]] and [[tengen toppa gurren lagann|tengen toppa gurren lagann]] which have gone on to critical acclaim and commercial success, as well as for their association with award-winning anime director and studio co-founder [[anno hideaki|anno hideaki]]. The company was headquartered in Koganei, Tokyo, before moving to Mitaka, Tokyo.

The studio was formed in the early 1980s as [[daicon|daicon]] Film by university students [[anno hideaki|anno hideaki]], [[sadamoto yoshiyuki|sadamoto yoshiyuki]], Yamaga Hiroyuki, [[akai takami|akai takami]], Okada Toshio, Takeda Yasuhiro, and [[higuchi shinji|higuchi shinji]]. Their first project was to make an animated short for the 20th Annual Japan National SF Convention, also known as [[daicon iii|daicon iii]], held in 1981 in Osaka, Japan. The group made a much bigger splash at the 22nd Annual Japan National SF Convention, [[daicon iv|daicon iv]], in 1983.

The Daicon IV short firmly established Daicon Film as a talented new anime studio. The studio changed its name to Gainax in 1985, basing the term 'Gainax' on an obscure Tottori Prefecture term for 'giant' and the English suffix 'x'.

Since Gainax originated as a group of fans, it was known for maintaining ties to the general [[otaku|otaku]] community, allowing doujinshi of its work, fan-made action figures, and promoting series like Evangelion at private festivals and so on.

Until Neon Genesis Evangelion, Gainax typically worked on stories created in-house, but the studio increasingly developed anime adaptations of existing manga like [[kareshi kanojo no jijou|kareshi kanojo no jijou]] and [[mahoromatic|mahoromatic]].

The Animage Anime Grand Prix has been awarded to Gainax for Nadia: The Secret of Blue Water in 1991, Neon Genesis Evangelion in 1995 and 1996, and [[the end of evangelion|the end of evangelion]] in 1997.

Much of Gainax's former staff and series left Gainax starting in the late 2000s; notably Anno Hideaki formed [[studio khara|studio khara]] and obtained the rights to Evangelion, several staff members (including those involved in [[tengen toppa gurren lagann|tengen toppa gurren lagann]]) left to make [[trigger (company)|Studio Trigger]], and Gainax sold their rights to FLCL to I.G. Production. [[gonzo (studio)|Gonzo]] is also made of former Gainax staff, having left in the early 90s.

On May 29, 2024, Gainax filed for bankruptcy with the Tokyo District Court, which was publicly announced over one week later on June 7. The remainder of its properties were split between the various Gainax splinter companies and former staff previously mentioned.

The classic gamepad is a [[game controller|game controller]] that can be held conveniently in two hands and does not require any particular mounting surface nor an exact fixed posture from the user. The game pad provides basic functions to control a game such as Start/Pause, Select, 4- or 8-way navigation, and various different actions via other buttons (numbering from two to roughly a dozen). Among the first gamepads were those game controllers bundled with the U.S.-market [[nes|Nintendo Entertainment System]] or Japanese-market [[famicom|famicom]].

Videogame consoles through the 8-, 16- and 32-bit eras still feature gamepads as basic controllers and these may include analog thumbsticks. However, gamepads should be considered separate from [[joystick|joysticks]].

"Gate - Thus the JSDF Fought There", or simply "Gate". 

A light novel series by Yanai Takumi, based on his own online novella, illustrated by [[izuka daisuke|izuka daisuke]]. 

In August 20XX, a portal to a parallel world known as the "Gate", suddenly appeared in [[ginza (tokyo)|Ginza, Tokyo]] where monsters and human warriors wearing ancient armor poured out of the portal, killing everyone in their way and trying to claim the area as their own. This would later be known as the "The Ginza Incident". Immediately after the attack, the [[japan ground self-defense force|japan ground self-defense force]]s launches a counter attack, repelling and pushing the invaders back to the Gate and reclaiming Ginza. 

A manga adaptation is adapted by [[sao satoru|sao satoru]]. A TV anime adaptation aired Summer 2015 with a continuation in Winter 2016.

Due to the overall theme, the series have been chosen by the [[japan self-defense force|japan self-defense force]] as a promotional and a recruiting tool for the JSDF since 2016.

A type of [[heavy machine gun|heavy machine gun]] with multiple rotating barrels.

The original Gatling gun was invented by Richard Jordan Gatling and first used in the [[american civil war|american civil war]] and was a direct ancestor of today's [[machine gun|machine gun]]s. Though not automatic in operation, it has a hand[[crank|crank]] for the user to [[firing|fire]] the shots and, rechamber a flesh [[ammunition|ammunition]] from its [[drum magazine|drum magazine]], in the place of the spent cartridge, for each of its six barrels as they rotates. Gatling-style rotating barrels are still used in modern heavy machine guns such as the [[m61 vulcan|m61 vulcan]], the [[gau-8|gau-8]], and the [[m134 minigun|m134 minigun]], typically to increase the sheer volume of firepower while reducing the wear of each individual barrel for continued usage.

On Danbooru, [[gatling gun|gatling gun]] refers to any kind of [[heavy machine gun|heavy machine gun]] with multiple rotating barrels, not just the original Civil War-era Gatling gun. If the said gatling gun were small enough to be carried by a person, then the tag [[minigun|minigun]] is applicable.

A "genderswap" refers to the almost magical version of a sex change, wherein a character of one sex turns into one of the other sex without any medical involvement. 

This tag can also apply to an image of a character of one sex depicted as one of the opposite sex (e.g. a male version of a female character or vice versa). May also apply to male-to-[[futanari|futanari]], but since futanari is not wholly female, female-to-futanari may also qualify. A being with no sex depicted as any of these may technically count.

This tag can also be applied to an [[otoko no ko|otoko no ko]] if the character is given female traits such as the presence of actual [[cleavage|cleavage]] or the obvious absence of a [[bulge|bulge]] at the crotch. For [[reverse trap|reverse trap]]s, the absence of cleavage or presence of a bulge applies.

If a character is genderswapped often enough, the genderswapped version may be given its own name. For male-to-female genderswaps, this is often the normal character's name with "ko" appended to it. (子 "Ko" meaning "child" is a common ending for Japanese girls' names.) For female-to-male genderswaps, "o" is sometimes added. 

Known in Internet circles as Rule 63, wherein there is a female or male version of any given male or female character, respectively.

**Notes:** 
- If the person has only swapped bodies with another from the opposite sex, but the body itself has not changed, then use [[personality switch|personality switch]] instead.
- The "女体化" tag may also on occasion be used to describe female [[personification|personification]], rather than a genderswap.
- If a character in canon is genderswapped but rarely shown in their original form (such as [[mai natsume|mai natsume]] or [[tanya degurechaff|tanya degurechaff]]), the tag only applies if said original form is included or somehow alluded to.

In English, *Yohane the Parhelion*. Also subtitled *Sunshine in the Mirror*, it is a *[[love live! sunshine!!|love live! sunshine!!]]* fantasy spin-off with an anime that debuted in 2023.

The first mention of an anime was as an April Fool's 2022 joke on the official *Love Live!* YouTube channel (the original has since been deleted from the official channel, but not before being "translated":[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XSflX-60EAI]). On June 26, 2022, a "separate dedicated twitter account":[https://twitter.com/GJ_yohane/status/1541041754958630913] as well as a live announcement at an Aqours live confirmed that the spin-off was in the works.

The series casts Aqours in a completely new setting, set in a fantasy world version in the land of "Numazu", named after the Shizuoka Prefecture city and its surroundings (including Uchiura) that *Sunshine!!* is set in, and stars [[tsushima yoshiko|tsushima yoshiko]] as [[yohane (genjitsu no yohane)|yohane (genjitsu no yohane)]] (Yoshiko's preferred fallen angel name). It tells "the story that no one knows about a girl that everyone knows," where she journeys and meets fantasy versions of other characters.

In June 2023, "*Blaze in the Deepblue*":[http://yohane-bid.com/en/], a 2D action platform video game for the series in the vein of *[[metroid|metroid]]* and *[[castlevania (series)|castlevania (series)]]*, was announced after it itself was an April Fool's joke in 2023. Developed by Inti Creates, it is the first *Love Live!* console game released November 16, 2023 for [[nintendo switch|nintendo switch]], [[playstation 4|playstation 4]] and [[playstation 5|5]], [[xbox one|xbox one]] and [[xbox series x|Series X/S]] and [[steam (platform)|steam (platform)]].

**Genryuusai Maki** (源柳斉 真紀 Genryūsai Maki), more commonly known simply as **Maki** (マキ?), is a character in the [[final fight|final fight]] and [[street fighter|street fighter]] [[video game|video game]] series, who originally appeared in the [[super nintendo|super nintendo]] beat 'em up [[final fight|final fight]] 2 as one of the game's main characters. 

Maki is a blond-haired red-clad female ninja who happens to be the younger sister of Guy's fiancee Rena (麗奈). Like [[guy (final fight)|Guy]], Maki is also trained in the Bushin style of ninjutsu and uses many of the same abilities and techniques.

Maki was well received by critics and fans alike, becoming one of the most popular Street Fighter characters despite appearing only in [[capcom vs snk 2|capcom vs snk 2]] and portable versions of [[street fighter zero (series)|Street Fighter Alpha 3]].

***GENSHIKEN*** (げんしけん) is a very popular manga created by [[kio shimoku|kio shimoku]] about living in an [[otaku|otaku]] club. Is basically a "slice-of-life" comedy series focusing in otaku life and its consequences. 

The title is a shortening of the club's official name, **GEN**dai **SHI**kaku Bunka **KEN**kyūkai (現代視覚文化研究会), which is translated as ***The Society for the Study of Modern Visual Culture***.

Serialized in Kodansha's *Afternoon* from 2002-2006, the manga series continued for a second season as Genshiken II (*Genshiken Nidaime* or *Genshiken Second Generation*), which was released in December 2010 and ended in August 2016. 

The original manga was also adapted into two separate TV anime series by Genco in 2004 and 2007, as well as a 3 episode OVA in 2006. Additionally, Kio Shimoku announced in the manga that a new TV anime adaptation of the *Second Generation* manga was in the works with the title *Genshiken Nidaime* (げんしけん 二代目 - *Genshiken Second Generation*), later airing in Japan from July 6 to September 29, 2013.

A *Genshiken Second Season OAD* or Original Animation DVD was bundled with the limited edition of the 15th volume of the Genshiken manga. It was released in Dec 20, 2013 with the title *Genshiken Nidaime No Roku DVD* (げんしけん オリジナルアニメDVD). The story is set between the events of Genshiken 2 and the Genshiken Nidaime series so none of the new characters from Nidaime appear in this anime.

A spin-off, [[kujibiki unbalance|kujibiki unbalance]], was produced by Ajia-do Animation Works in 2006, along with a manga, illustrated by [[koume keito|koume keito]].

[[spotted flower|spotted flower]], a manga periodically illustrated and produced by Kio outside of Afternoon since 2009, is loosely based on Genshiken.

The first game in the *[[gensou suikoden|gensou suikoden]]* RPG series. It follows the story of [[tir mcdohl|tir mcdohl]], the son of a top general in the Scarlet Moon Empire. Tir soon becomes involved in (and eventually the leader of) a rebellion against the Empire after becoming the host of the Soul Eater Rune.

The second game in the *[[gensou suikoden|gensou suikoden]]* series, which takes place three years after the first game. It takes place in Dunan, immediately northwest of the Scarlet Moon Empire/Toran Republic of the first game, and follows the story of [[riou (suikoden)|riou (suikoden)]] and [[jowy atreides-blight|Jowy Atreides]], who become hosts of the two halves of the Rune of the Beginning and leaders in the war between the Jowston Alliance and Highland Kingdom. Numerous characters from the first game play major roles, resulting in *Gensou Suikoden II* introducing the fewest new characters of any game in the main series.

*[[gensou suikogaiden|gensou suikogaiden]]* is a side story to *Gensou Suikoden II*, overlapping considerably with its story.

The third game in the *[[gensou suikoden|gensou suikoden]]* series. It takes place 18 years after the first game, and is set just west of *[[gensou suikoden ii|gensou suikoden ii]]*'s Dunan region. The game revolves around a war between the Grassland tribes and the Zexen Confederacy, with later interference by Holy Kingdom of Harmonia, the sole superpower in the *Gensou Suikoden* world. *Gensou Suikoden III* is unique in the series in that it follows three different main characters: [[hugo (suikoden iii)|Hugo]] (son of one of the Grassland tribal chiefs), [[chris lightfellow|chris lightfellow]] (Captain of the Zexen Knights), and [[geddoe (suikoden)|geddoe (suikoden)]] (a mercenary initially working for Harmonia). The True Fire Rune is also central to the story, and while the player gets to decide which of the main characters becomes its host, canonically it goes to Hugo, with Chris getting her father's True Water Rune and Geddoe keeping the True Lightning Rune which he already possessed.

The fourth game in the *[[gensou suikoden|gensou suikoden]]* series. It is the first prequel game of the series, taking place 150 years before *[[gensou suikoden i|gensou suikoden i]]*. It takes place among the Island Nations, to the south of *Gensou Suikoden I*'s Scarlet Moon Empire, during an invasion by the Kooluk Empire which was engineered by "Merchant of Death" Graham Cray, and follows exiled Gaien Knight [[lazlo (suikoden)|lazlo (suikoden)]]. Lazlo, following the usual *Gensou Suikoden* formula, becomes the host of a True Rune (the cursed Rune of Punishment) and the leader of the rebel military. Due to its location, travel and major battles in the game are carried out by ship instead of on land. It also has the fewest returning characters of any game in the series, with four characters from previous games who were already established as immortal being present.

Due to its simplified gameplay (especially the reduction of party size from the traditional six to only four), annoyingly frequent random battles, and a story that never really lives up to its potential, *Gensou Suikoden IV* is widely considered the worst in the series.

The fifth and so far last game in the main *[[gensou suikoden|gensou suikoden]]* series, taking place 143 years after *[[gensou suikoden iv|gensou suikoden iv]]* and 7 years prior to *[[gensou suikoden i|gensou suikoden i]]*, in the Queendom of Falena (to the south of *Gensou Suikoden IV*'s Island Nations). It follows [[freyjadour falenas|freyjadour falenas]], the prince of Falena, as he leads a rebellion against the usurpers who overthrew his mother. Unlike every other game of the series, Freyjadour does not become the host of a True Rune.

Perhaps in response to the mixed reaction to *[[gensou suikoden iii|gensou suikoden iii]]* and generally negative reaction to *Gensou Suikoden IV*, *Gensou Suikoden V* hearkens back heavily to *[[gensou suikoden ii|gensou suikoden ii]]*, which is widely regarded as the high point of the series. Many *Gensou Suikoden II* characters appear or are alluded to in *Gensou Suikoden V*, and the gameplay eliminates most of the changes introduced in later games in favor of an upgraded version of *Gensou Suikoden II*'s battle system. This effort to restore fans' faith in the series seems to have worked, as *Gensou Suikoden V* is generally regarded as the second best of the series, with many even ranking it as the best.

**GERWALK** (**G**round **E**ffective **R**einforcement of **W**inged **A**rmament with **L**ocomotive **K**nee-joint) is a [[vtol|vtol]] transformation mode of the [[vf-1|vf-1]] [[variable fighter|variable fighter]] from [[macross|macross]] (and other related transformable [[mecha|mecha]]) where the nose and wings of the fighter [[jet|jet]] are stuck on "chicken [[walker (robot)|walker (robot)]]" legs with two arms. The legs are formed by the aircraft's engines and intakes, bent down and forward. The arms are stored between the engines in fighter mode and fold out to the sides, reaching around from behind the legs.

Legend tells that when [[kawamori shouji|kawamori shouji]] first designed the VF-1 *Valkyrie*, he did not include this mode initially at all. However, after receiving a prototype of a toy based in the VF-1 he noticed that the legs of the figure were very very loose and constantly fell down during transformation into jet mode, so it resembled a unused walker mecha design called "Gawalk" that he developed years before for another show. Thus he adopted the mode in the mecha and changed its name into "Gerwalk" afterwards.

***Ghost in the Shell*** (*Kōkaku Kidōtai*, literally *"Mobile Armored Riot Police"*) is a Japanese multimedia [[science fiction|science fiction]] and [[mecha|mecha]] [[cyberpunk|cyberpunk]] franchise created in 1989 by [[shirow masamune|shirow masamune]]. It is comprised of: Shirow's original manga (1989/1991, 2002 and 2003); two animated films (1995 and 2004) directed by Mamoru Oshii; two anime series ([[ghost in the shell stand alone complex|Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex]] in 2002-2003 and *Ghost in the Shell: S.A.C. 2nd Gig* in 2004-2005), and their sequel OVA (*Ghost in the Shell: S.A.C. Solid State Society* in 2006); as well as several video games and novels.

The series focuses on the activities of the counter-terrorist organization [[police|Public Security Section 9]] (公安9課), set in a futuristic, [[cyberpunk|cyberpunk]] Japan.

An American live action adaptation was released in [[ghost in the shell (2017)|2017]]. The movie is directed by Rupert Sanders and written by Jamie Moss, William Wheeler and Ehren Kruger. The film stars [[scarlett johannson|scarlett johannson]], [[kitano takeshi|kitano takeshi]], Michael Pitt, Pilou Asbæk, Chin Han and Juliette Binoche.

**Ghostbusters** is a 1984 American supernatural comedy film directed and produced by [Ivan Reitman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Reitman) and written by [Dan Aykroyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Aykroyd) and [[harold ramis|harold ramis]].

The film stars [[bill murray|bill murray]], Aykroyd, and Ramis as three eccentric parapsychologists who start a ghost-catching business in New York City. [[sigourney weaver|sigourney weaver]] and [Rick Moranis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Moranis) co-star as a client and her neighbor, and [Ernie Hudson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernie_Hudson) as the Ghostbusters' first recruit.

Aykroyd conceived the film as a project for himself and fellow [[saturday night live|saturday night live]] alumnus [John Belushi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Belushi) , with the "Ghostmashers" travelling through time and space. He and Ramis dramatically rewrote the script following Belushi's death and after Reitman deemed Aykroyd's initial vision financially impractical.

Ghostbusters was released in the United States on June 8, 1984. It was a critical and commercial success, receiving a positive response from critics and audiences and grossing US$242 million in the United States and more than $295 million worldwide. It was nominated for two Oscars at the 57th Academy Awards for Best Visual Effects and Best Original Song (for the eponymous theme song), but lost to Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom and The Woman in Red respectively. 

The film launched the Ghostbusters media franchise, which includes a 1989 sequel, [[ghostbusters ii|ghostbusters ii]]; two animated television series, [[the real ghostbusters|the real ghostbusters]] and [[extreme ghostbusters|extreme ghostbusters]] as well as several video games. 

A [[ghostbusters (2016)|reboot]] starring Kristen Wiig, Melissa McCarthy, Kate McKinnon, and Leslie Jones was released in July 2016 but received negative reviews and was a box office bomb.

An official sequel to the original films titled Ghostbusters: Afterlife was released on November 19, 2021. A fourth film, Ghostbusters: Frozen Empire, was released on March 22, 2024.

Solid body [[electric guitar|electric guitar]] created and manufactured by American [[instrument|instrument]] maker [[gibson brands inc|Gibson]] since 1958. Built with a futuristic design in mind alongside its closest sibling the [[gibson explorer|Explorer]], it was initially deemed a failure with less than 100 units being built and sold between 1958 and 1959. Solid body [[electric guitar|electric guitar]] manufactured by [[gibson brands inc|Gibson]] since 1952, designed with input by famed jazz guitarist Les Paul whose name ended up as the name of the [[guitar|guitar]] itself, work and prototypes commenced in 1950, with 1951 prototypes being strikingly similar to the final product until its introduction in 1952. The Les Paul eventually caught big success in a seemingly endless array of genres, pinning it as one of the most well known and popular guitars along with its contemporaries, the [[fender telecaster|fender telecaster]] and [[fender stratocaster|fender stratocaster]]. It's similarly been used by musicians far and wide, including [[slash (musician)|Slash]], Joe Perry and James Dean Bradfield among others.

The Les Paul also holds a strong cult following in Japan. Within anime and manga, [[k-on!|k-on!]]'s [[hirasawa yui|hirasawa yui]] is most associated with the Les Paul, using a Cherry Sunburst Les Paul Standard (now Traditional). Other prominent characters include [[idolmaster million live!|idolmaster million live!]]'s [[julia (idolmaster)|Julia]] using a TV Yellow Les Paul Special, [[bang dream!|bang dream!]]'s [[mitake ran|mitake ran]] with a red Les Paul copy, and [[bocchi the rock!|bocchi the rock!]]'s [[gotoh hitori|gotoh hitori]] with a black Les Paul custom.

Original Les Pauls were released with goldtop finishes, P90 ("soapbar") pickups and either stopbars or tailpieces. Prominent Gibson versions of the Les Paul include:
- Standard, most famous example in anime being Hirasawa Yui's model.
- Junior/Special, lighter glossier model with soapbar pickups with the Junior only sporting a single pickup, most commonly seen being used by iDOLMASTER's Julia.
- DC/DC Lite, a double-cutaway version, famously used in Japan by [[b'z|b'z]] guitarist [[matsumoto takahiro (b'z)|Matsumoto Takahiro]]. (post #2361213)
- Custom, featuring gold hardware, most commonly seen in either black or white. (post #1867738)

However, Lester Polsfuss (Les Paul) hated the new design and demanded that his name not be associated with the guitar. The name change would eventually occur in 1963, being renamed SG which literally stands for *Solid Guitar*. The SG eventually became Gibson's best selling model of all time and has been used by famous musicians by the likes of [[ac/dc|ac/dc]]'s [[angus young|angus young]], [[frank zappa|frank zappa]] and [[radiohead (band)|Radiohead]]'s Thom Yorke.

Among anime and anime-themed characters, [[nitroplus|nitroplus]]'s [[super sonico|super sonico]] and [[angel beats!|angel beats!]]'s [[yui (angel beats!)|Yui]] are the most prominent.

Common visual traits of the SG include a short and round double-cutaway body, four control knobs, double humbucker setup and a tune-o-matic bridge with stopbar, with certain models (specially earlier) sporting a tailpiece instead.

**Ginga Tetsudou 999**, also known as **Galaxy Express 999**, is an epic and classic [[science fiction|science fiction]] manga series created and first drawn by [[matsumoto leiji|matsumoto leiji]] in 1977. There is a manga version, a TV version, movie versions, and manga sequels (the "Eternal" series).

Matsumoto was inspired to create Galaxy Express 999 by the idea of a steam train running through the stars in the 1934  [[fantasy|fantasy]] novel *Night on the Galactic Railroad* by Miyazawa Kenji.

A little known fact is that the *999* in the title of the series is supposed to be pronounced *three nine* in English, instead of the *nine hundred ninety-nine* or the *nine nine nine* most westerners use.

A boy who acts recognizably feminine but can still be easily identified as male. "Onee" type boys will often be of this demographic, owing to girlish speech patterns or hobbies.

Most characters of this type will have an interest in topics typically associated with femininity (dandy-style fashion, beauty, cute things, etc.) and often are depicted in coquettish poses. They may wear [[high heels|high heels]], [[jewelry|jewelry]], [[makeup|makeup]] and/or [[nail polish|nail polish]]. Common hairstyles may be wavy or flipped.

Not to be confused with [[otoko no ko|otoko no ko]] (sometimes referred to as "femboys" in English), which is a boy whose *physical appearance* is feminine regardless of his personality. Also not to be confused with the term and archetype of "okama", though characters of either type can have girly boy traits. [[crossdressing|crossdressing]] does not automatically make a character a "girly boy" either.

The sparkle of a polished or metal object. This should come from a physical object, such as [[jewelry|jewelry]], a [[sword|sword]], or [[teeth|teeth]].

[[sparkle|sparkle]], **glint**, and [[diffraction spikes|diffraction spikes]] all refer to similar patterns of bright lines radiating from a point. They are not clearly differentiated, and usage tends to be context-sensitive. In general:
- [[sparkle|sparkle]] is considered the base case. Usually four lines at right angles radiating from a point. Associated with eyes, liquid or particulate matter (e.g. raindrops, snow, sand), or nothing (appearing mid-air). Can appear in large numbers.
- **Glint** is associated with solid objects, especially ones which are metallic and/or sharp. Usually appear singly or in small numbers.
- [[diffraction spikes|diffraction spikes]] is the technical term for the phenomenon in general, but is used less often. Can be used for more realistic-looking effects or conversely when appearing extremely large and exaggerated. More likely than sparkle and glint to be asymmetric or to have more than four radiating lines.

In Jewish folklore, a golem is an artificial being made from inanimate matter, traditionally clay or mud, which is then animated by supernatural means. The resulting entity is physically robust and can be directed to perform work, but is usually not fully sapient; lacking both initiative and common sense. Thus its instructions must be carefully worded, [[too literal|lest certain mishaps ensue.]] Essentially, a magical, pre-industrial [[robot|robot]].

In modern fantasy, a wider range of base materials can be used, with the hardness/toughness of the material serving as an indicator of the golem's strength (e.g. a stone golem is stronger than a mud golem, and an iron golem is stronger still.)  This is extremely common in RPGs.  Golems may even be depicted as intelligent, although a tendency towards being either dim-witted, subservient or both remains.

A traditional passenger-carrying [[boat|boat]] of Venice, Italy, measuring a law-regulated 10.85m in length and having an maximum breadth of 1.40m. It is often sculled by a single person standing on the rear deck, with the [[oar|oar]] resting on an oarlock. Gondolas with multiple rowers also exist, an example being the *traghetto* or ferry gondola. 

*Gondole* can be differentiated from other boats by being asymmetrical, with one side being slightly longer than the other, and by the presence of a *ferro*, a stylized S-shaped bow ornament made of metal whose design represents elements of Venice and whose weight counterbalances that of the gondolier.

Gondolas figure prominently in [[amano kozue|amano kozue]]'s anime and manga series [[aria (manga)|aria (manga)]].

**Granblue Fantasy** (グランブルーファンタジー *Guranburuu Fantajii*), officially abbreviated as **Granblue** (グラブル *Guraburu*), is a mobile turn-based RPG by [[cygames|cygames]], with a Japanese-only release in March 2014, and an English-language release in April 2016. The official anime released in 2017, followed by a second season in 2019. 

The gameplay is heavily reliant on the player's summons and weapons obtained from the gacha system and from in-game raids. The player can equip a maximum of ten weapons and five summons at a time and this is generally referred to as the "weapon grid" and "summon pool".

Granblue is infamous for its competitive week-long event (Guild Wars/Unite & Fight/古戦場) where players farm chunks of meat and try to score more points than their opponent crew for hours at a time. Art is occasionally drawn depicting this in game event, one example being [[post guild war celebration|post guild war celebration]]s.

#### Races

Most characters in Granblue Fantasy are divided into 5 races. 

- Human. Most characters fall into this.
- [[erune|erune]], whose notable features are their animal ears and clothing that expose their backs.
- [[harvin|harvin]], dwarf sized humanoids.
- [[draph|draph]], humanoids with prominent horns on their heads. Males are tall and muscular, while females are noticeably shorter than the average person, while having big breasts.
- Primal. Primal beasts are creatures that were crafted by the Astral beings long ago. A good number of them (usually humanoid) end up joining the player's crew for one reason or another. 

#### Protagonist

The player is represented by either [[gran (granblue fantasy)|gran (granblue fantasy)]] or [[djeeta (granblue fantasy)|djeeta (granblue fantasy)]] based on their gender selection and this can be changed at any time. The player may also change their class at any time which also changes their costume.

A male [[humboldt penguin|humboldt penguin]] who lived at [Tobu Zoo](http://www.tobuzoo.com/global/english/) in Saitama Prefecture. Grape-kun obtained Internet fame in 2017 for his interactions with a cardboard cutout of *[[kemono friends|kemono friends]]*' [[humboldt penguin (kemono friends)|Hululu the Humboldt Penguin]] character placed in his enclosure as part of a promotional event, prompting many to consider Grape-kun an old friend of hers, a secret admirer, or as being hopelessly in love with her while being stuck in the third dimension, the latter leading many animanga fans to sympathize with the penguin. He became a sensation, receiving many visitors and a plethora of online fanart depicting him alongside Hululu and even a visit from Hululu's anime voice actress, [[chikuta ikuko|chikuta ikuko]].

He was distinguishable from other Humboldt penguins at the Tobu Zoo by the purple [[armband|armband]] on his left flipper.

According to zoo staff, Grape used to have a wife called Midori (distinguished from her green flipper band, *midori* being the Japanese word for that color), but at some point she abandoned Grape-kun and found a new lover— a rather exceptional occurrence in a species that usually forms lifelong pair bonds, and a source of suggestion as to why Grape-kun grew so attached to the Hululu cutout.

Grape-kun passed away from a sudden illness on October 12, 2017, at the age of 21. A temporary message board was set up near his enclosure for visitors to leave parting words, and many additionally left gifts such as artwork and flowers.

#### Plot
Born to a wealthy mother [[akezawa emi|akezawa emi]], [[hanma baki|hanma baki]] is one of many offspring of [[hanma yujiro|hanma yujiro]], who inseminated women around the world in an attempt to create his "perfect successor". Having endured Yujiro's harsh training to become the "strongest creature on Earth", Baki was soundly defeated by his father in a "graduation" fight, which resulted in his mother Emi being killed by Yujiro for her "weak genes".

Baki's initial admiration of Yujiro turns into hatred and he swore to surpass his monstrous father to avenge his mother. Baki later enters an underground fighting tournament with no rules, facing many of the strongest fighters of various styles, in which Baki seeks to use this brutal combat to hone his prowess in hope of defeating Yujiro one day.

(Shamelessly lifted directly from Wikipedia at http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gravity_Rush)

**Gravity Rush**, known in Japan as **Gravity Daze** (グラヴィティデイズ/重力的眩暈:上層への帰還において彼女の内宇宙に生じた摂動?) is a video game developed for the PlayStation Vita. Directed by Keiichiro Toyama and written by Naoko Sato (previously known for the Siren series and the first Silent Hill), the core mechanic of the game is the player's ability to manipulate gravity, allowing unique movements and navigation. The graphics are cel-shaded, which in Toyama's opinion stand out from the western photorealistic trend.

The game started off back in 2008 as a PlayStation 3 project called Gravité, before being eventually transferred to PS Vita. AI and visuals were slightly simplified during the process. However, Gravity Rush director thinks overall Vita suits the game better, because of "its handy and accessible nature" and "the impression of a different world existing beyond the screen" the player gets by tilting the device.

A greenhouse is normally characterized by the following:

- A building largely made up out of framing and glass panels
- A building that has been made economically and with an eye for keeping costs low. 
- A building which main purpose is the growing of and the caring for plants
- Often a free-standing building not attached to other types of buildings

This is in contrast with a [[conservatory|conservatory]], a building that is often confused with a greenhouse as the main purpose of a conservatory is to be used as a living space, with plants sometimes intermixed.

A few examples of a greenhouse are the following:

- A large building on a farm filled with rows and rows of plants being grown for consumption or sale.
- A small building in a private garden or "allotment garden":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allotment_(gardening)] used mainly for the growing of plants.
- A building that is of the same type of either of the two described above but is empty or used for the storage of other objects is still a greenhouse as well.
- A botanical garden can also be called a greenhouse although it often overlaps with a conservatory.

It evolves from [[frogadier|frogadier]] starting at level 36. It is the final form of [[froakie|froakie]]. 

Greninja is a large, bipedal, frog-like Pokémon. Its body and legs are dark blue, with single large white bubbles on its legs and arms and white spots over its eyes. On the sides of each of its upper thighs is a light blue, four-pointed star, which resembles a shuriken. Its back feet have two toes, while its front feet have three toes. Its feet are webbed, and it has a yellow chest and a yellow-and-blue face. It has eyes with white sclera, red irises, and white pupils. A large, projecting dark blue stripe runs down the middle of its head, with projecting light blue stripes in between its large, yellow ears. Its mouth is hidden behind a large, pink tongue that wraps around Greninja's neck and extends outward behind its head. 

It has one alternate form: [[ash-greninja|ash-greninja]].

A completely colorless, black-and-white image. The image is composed exclusively of shades of black, white, and grey. It is very common for [[comic|comic]]s and [[doujinshi|doujinshi]] to be in greyscale.

The image may have small highlights of color (known as [[spot color|spot color]]s), but the image as a whole should be predominately greyscale.

Don't use color tags like [[black eyes|black eyes]] or [[black hair|black hair]] when tagging greyscale images. The exception is color background tags, so tagging [[white background|white background]], [[grey background|grey background]], or [[black background|black background]] is fine.

#### Guidelines

- For completely colorless art, use [[greyscale|greyscale]].
- For a post consisting of a single color that isn't grey, use [[monochrome|monochrome]], not [[greyscale|greyscale]].
- For a mostly greyscale post with a small amount of color as a highlight, use [[greyscale|greyscale]] and [[spot color|spot color]].
- For a post using a mix of color and greyscale, use [[partially colored|partially colored]], not [[greyscale|greyscale]].
- For a colorless foreground and colorful background, use [[greyscale with colored background|greyscale with colored background]], not [[greyscale|greyscale]] or [[partially colored|partially colored]].
- For a post that has solid black shadings, use [[greyscale|greyscale]] and [[high contrast|high contrast]].
- For posts with a small variety of colors but more than two actual colors, use [[limited palette|limited palette]], not [[greyscale|greyscale]] or [[monochrome|monochrome]].

Guan is broad term for any type of hat in of [[hanfu|hanfu]] headwear. It tends to cover the full top of the head; for Hanfu headwear that only covers the [[topknot|topknot]], see [[xiao guan (headdress)|xiao guan (headdress)]].

Please see the subtypes and use them instead, as guan is unspecific. 

The Guan was typically a formal form of headwear which was worn together with its corresponding court dress attire. There were sumptuary laws which regulated the wearing of Guan; however, these laws were not fixed; and thus, they would differ from dynasty to dynasty. There were various forms and types of Guan.

As the character Guan (冠) is of a homonym another Chinese character pronounced Guan (官) which literally means official; the Guan (冠) became the symbol of officials. Note, this should not be confused with [[futou|futou]] which essentially replaced the Guan as Chinese court wear around the [[tang dynasty|tang dynasty]] (but continued to be worn by Confucian literati until the [[ming dynasty|ming dynasty]], where it became the exclusive headwear of the royal family).

#### Subtypes

  - [[mian guan|mian guan]] - Emperor's hat
  - [[xiezhi guan|xiezhi guan]] - Hat once worn by lawyers.

**Guile** (**ガイル**) is a video game character in [[capcom|Capcom's]] [[street fighter|street fighter]] series of fighting games. Although his role in the Street Fighter story is minimal, he is considered the third leading male character in the series, after [[ryu (street fighter)|ryu (street fighter)]] and [[ken masters|Ken]], largely due to his effectiveness as a character and his popularity.

When Guile was a Lieutenant in the United States Air Force, he befriended his superior officer, [[charlie nash|Charlie]] and asked him to teach him in his unique form of fighting, which Charlie agreed to do. Guile learned the style, but his hot temper caused him to be not as proficient in the moves as Charlie was (shown in how Charlie can shoot Sonic Booms with just one hand while Guile needs both.)

Guile has a wife, Julia (ユリア), and daughter, [[chris (street fighter)|chris (street fighter)]] (クリス, known as Amy internationally). Also, Julia and [[eliza masters|Eliza]] are actually sisters, making Ken and Guile brothers-in-law. However, this is not often discussed because, despite mutual respect as fighters, they do not think very highly of one another — Guile believes Ken to be a spoiled rich kid; Ken feels Guile is just another meathead soldier. In [[street fighter iv (series)|street fighter iv (series)]], if Ken beats Guile, he'll refer to him as his "brother-in-law". 

There's also a [[meme|running gag]] about his theme music from Super Street Fighter II "fitting in" or "going with" every scene or moment imaginable.

The inspiration for his character comes from [[rudolph von stroheim|JoJo's Rudolph von Stroheim]].

A domestic species of rodent originating from South America, related to the [[capybara|capybara]]. The guinea pig is tailless and herbivorous, with a stout, "potato-like" body shape and a size approximately twice that of a common rat. To the uninitiated, the guinea pig may resemble an oversized hamster.

Guinea pigs are highly vocal rodents and are noted for making a characteristic "wheek" sound when excited or hungry. This sound is rendered as "pui" in Japanese onomatopoeia. 

The scientific name of the species is *Cavia porcellus*. It is sometimes also called "cavy" by breeders and owners. Guinea pigs were frequently used as experimental animals in research; hence the word "guinea pig" is often also used metaphorically to refer to experimental subjects.

**Mobile Suit Gundam 0080: War in the Pocket** (*Kidō Senshi Gandamu 0080 Poketto no Naka no Sensō*) is a six episode 1989 Japanese [[science fiction|science fiction]] and [[mecha|mecha]] original video animation series. 

**It is the first OVA series in the [[gundam|gundam]] franchise** and also the **first main Gundam anime to feature a female Gundam pilot main protagonist**. It was directed by Takayama Fumihiko, written by Yamaga Hiroyuki with character designs by [[mikimoto haruhiko|mikimoto haruhiko]].

As suggested by its subtitle, *War in the Pocket*, it is a small personal "coming of age" series; a serious side story focusing on the experiences of an idealistic and naive [[child|eleven-year-old civilian boy]] during the last part of [[mobile suit gundam|the One Year War]] and his learning of the [[real life|real life]] meanings of friendship, love, [[war|war]] and [[death|death]]. 

A crude, [[realistic|realistic]] and significant departure for the Gundam franchise at the time, Gundam 0080 has received wide acclaim from critics over time.

The realism in the series and its focus in side story regular soldier and civilian characters paved the way for other more serious Gundam works like [[gundam 0083|gundam 0083]] and [[gundam 08th ms team|gundam 08th ms team]].

**Mobile Suit Gundam F91** (Japanese: 機動戦士ガンダムF91フォーミュラ ナインティワン, Hepburn: *Kidou Senshi Gandamu Foumyura Nainti Wan*, **Mobile Suit Gundam Formula 91**) is a 1991 anime film set in the [[gundam|gundam]] universe. 

It was written and directed by [[mobile suit gundam|original Gundam]] creator [[tomino yoshiyuki|tomino yoshiyuki]]. It was Tomino's attempt to launch a new U.C. Gundam saga, set 30 years after [[char's counterattack|char's counterattack]]. He re-teamed with character designer [[yasuhiko yoshikazu|yasuhiko yoshikazu]] and [[mecha|mecha]] designer [[ookawara kunio|ookawara kunio]]  for the occasion.

Originally planned as a full-length television series, Gundam F91 hit a production snag due to staff disputes, and the project was stopped after the screenplays for the first thirteen episodes were written. It was then decided that what was made of the show would be condensed into a theatrical feature. The film was first released in [[japan|japan]] on March 16, 1991.

Set in **U.C. 0123** (44 years after [[mobile suit gundam|the original Gundam]]), the story of Gundam F91 revolves around teenage space colonist [[seabook arno|seabook arno]], his girlfriend [[cecily fairchild|cecily fairchild]], and the efforts of the [[crossbone vanguard|crossbone vanguard]] militia to establish an aristocracy known as "Cosmo Babylonia". In keeping with Gundam tradition, the civilian Seabook is forced by circumstance to pilot the [[f91 gundam|f91 gundam]], coincidentally designed in part by his estranged mother, Dr. [[monica arno|monica arno]].

**Gundam Reconguista in G** (ガンダム Gのレコンギスタ *Gandamu G no Rekongisuta*), also known as **G-Reco** (Gレコ *G-Rekko*), is a 2014 [[science fiction|science fiction]] Anime TV series and the thirteenth incarnation of Sunrise's [[gundam|gundam]] franchise, created by [[tomino yoshiyuki|tomino yoshiyuki]]. 

The new series is Tomino's first major Gundam project since the 2005 Mobile Suit [[zeta gundam|zeta gundam]] film trilogy and his latest Gundam TV series since [[turn a gundam|turn a gundam]]. Reconguista debuted in fall 2014. The series lasted 26 episodes which were broadcasted in Japan from October 2014 until March 2015. A series of 5 recap films based on the anime were released from 2019 to 2022. 

Reconguista is set in the "Reguild Century", an era set long time after the [[mobile suit gundam|Universal Century]], and follows the adventures of a pilot trainee named [[bellri zenam|bellri zenam]] (*Beruri Zenamu*) in Capital Guard, an organization protecting an advanced [[space elevator|space elevator]]. 

The character designer for this series is Yoshida Kenichi. The [[mecha|mecha]] designers are [[yasuda akira|yasuda akira]], Gyōbu Ippei and Yamane  Kimitoshi. Kanno Yugo is providing the soundtrack.  A manga adaptation illustrated by [[oota tamon|oota tamon]] began publication in 2014.

The **Mobile Suit Variations**, simply known as **MSV** to fans, are variations on the mechanical designs of [[gundam|gundam]] franchise, particularly those of [[mobile suit gundam|mobile suit gundam]]. Most of them never appeared in animated form.

These [[mobile suit|mobile suit]] [[mecha|mecha]] variations are official designs, including their own histories and in many cases their own pilots with detailed backstories. Some were cancelled or alternative designs originally created for an animated production, while others are promotional variations used as the basis for unique [[gunpla|model kits]]. 

While never seen in their own animation series, most of the MSV machines (as well as the backstories and pilots created for them) are considered canonical, and a feature in other side-stories, manga, or (mostly) in [[video game|video game]]s.

Originally conceived as an animated television series that would serve as a sequel to [[gundam zz|gundam zz]], the project was canceled in favor of [[char's counterattack|char's counterattack]]. [[japan|japan]]ese hobbyist magazine [[model graphix|model graphix]], with whom Gundam Sentinel was co-planned, reinvented the project as a photo-novel and serialized the story in monthly installments. Strong fan reaction in favor of Gundam Sentinel prompted merchandising company Bandai to release a line of model kits based on the series.

Gundam Sentinel is primarily known for launching the career of now-prolific [[mecha|mecha]] designer [[katoki hajime|katoki hajime]]. Also, Gundam Sentinel is the only Gundam property that is not fully owned by Sunrise and Bandai. Due to their involvement in pre-production, Model Graphix holds a copyright claim on the series. This makes Sentinel the only Gundam series that Bandai must pay royalties on in order to create merchandising based on the property, such as model kits or [[video game|video game]] appearances.

Popular animated [[gundam|gundam]] series from the 90s. Began airing in 1995 and features a group of several young protagonists who operate different types of Gundam [[mobile suit|mobile suit]]s.

Extremely popular in the West during the year 2000, where it was broadcast in the [[toonami|toonami]] block of [[cartoon network|cartoon network]] and had many action figures released as well in several popular toy stores in the USA, a first for a Gundam show.

***Gundam ZZ*** is the 1986 sequel to *[[zeta gundam|zeta gundam]]*. It was created by a mostly new creative staff, with series creator [[tomino yoshiyuki|tomino yoshiyuki]] being the main returning member. The first half of *Gundam ZZ* is infamous for being significantly more comedy-oriented than previous and subsequent [[gundam|gundam]] series. However, the tone of the series changes and becomes more serious in the second half, concluding the story of Zeta.

ZZ is set in the year **Universal Century 0088**, beginning almost immediately after the end of *Zeta Gundam* (and the final battle of The Gryps War). It follows the story of [[judau ashta|judau ashta]], [[pilot|pilot]] of the [[aeug|aeug]] [[zz gundam|MSZ-010 ZZ (Double Zeta) Gundam]], during **The First [[neo zeon|neo zeon]] War**, a conflict originated due to [[haman karn|haman karn]]'s declaration of war on the now weakened [[earth federation|earth federation]].

Gundam ZZ is notable because it is the first Gundam series where an underage group of pilots (*The [[gundam team|gundam team]]*) operate more than two different types of Gundams. This trope would be used years later in other very popular Gundam series like [[gundam wing|gundam wing]] in the mid 90s and [[gundam 00|gundam 00]] the next decade.

The story of ZZ continues in [[char's counterattack|char's counterattack]].

Gundula Rall is a veteran witch of the [[502nd joint fighter wing|502nd joint fighter wing]], originating from [[karlsland|karlsland]]. Behind [[gertrud barkhorn|Barkhorn]] and [[erica hartmann|Hartmann]], she is Karlsland Airforce's (and, therefore humanity's) 3rd greatest ace. Her familiar is the [[wolf|wolf]].

Strong and confident, Rall takes to her role as commander with relish, acting as more of a brash, frankly-spoken older sister than the more motherly nagging of [[aleksandra i. pokryshkin|Pokryshkin]] and nurturing of [[shimohara sadako|Shimohara]]. Unlike many in her position, however, she doesn't let herself get too serious, and is laid back and good-humored on a personal level.

Her Ace Archetype is Günther Rall. Like Gundula, he was [[world war ii|world war ii]]'s third highest-scoring ace.

**Gyaru** (ギャル), also known as gal, is a Japanese [[fashion|fashion]] style that peaked in the 2000s. Although it has generally declined in real life, it still has many followers and remains popular in various Japanese media, particularily the manga & anime industry.

It has many diverse substyles, with some commonalities. Gyaru style typically involves styled and coloured hair, trendy and often sexy gyaru-style clothing (especially from the shops in the mall Shibuya 109), and heavy makeup, with a focus on false [[eyelashes|eyelashes]], enlarging the eyes, contouring, and circle lenses. Additionally, many gyaru use the "gyaru-moji" (ギャル文字) style of typing and certain specialized slang (ギャル語). There are also certain common hobbies among gyaru: dancing [[para para|para para]] was at one time a very popular activity in gyaru circles.

Two common elements of gyaru looks, especially in anime and manga representations, are tanned skin ([[ganguro|ganguro]] - especially for older or throwback styles) and bleached hair. However, not every gyaru has tanned skin or bleached hair, and not every character with tanned skin and bleached hair is a gyaru.

In mainstream media, gyaru are usually depicted as either an energeric or an extroverted character, while adult media depicted either as a high-school student [[prostitution|prostitute]] or a character with unusually high sex drive.

Originating from Japan's [[gyaru|gyaru]] culture, it is a hand gesture that first extends the arm forward and turns the palm up and down after making a V-shape by hand.

The male counterpart to [[gyaru|gyaru]]. While the term originated from the styles reported on by fashion magazine *Men's Egg*, it has since gone on to become a moniker for the youth subculture that wore it.

Like their female counterparts, typical gyaruo attire comes in different flavors. The most common depictions have [[tan|tan]]s or [[dark skin|dark skin]], [[blonde hair|blonde hair]], or some sort of loose fashion. However, not everyone who is tan or blond may be part of the gyaruo subculture.

Also spelled as "gyaru-oh" or "gal-o":[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1EKTw50Uf8M] alternately. Due to their flashiness, 2010s japanese youth tend to associate them with the term "charao" (チャラ男).

The G3 is a West German 7.62×51mm NATO **[[battle rifle|battle rifle]]** developed by [[heckler & koch|heckler & koch]] in the 1950s, based on the earlier Spanish [[cetme model 58|cetme model 58]]. It became the standard [[bundeswehr|bundeswehr]] service [[rifle|rifle]] from 1959 until early 1990s. Utilizing roller-delayed blowback mechanism, and having major variants available with fixed buttstock or retractable metal one, its design also became the basis of other H&K [[weapon|weapon]]s such as the [[h&k mp5|MP5]] [[submachine gun|submachine gun]].

The **G36** is a 5.56×45mm NATO [[assault rifle|assault rifle]], designed in early 1990s and manufactured by [[heckler & koch|heckler & koch]] in Germany. It was intended to supplant the failed [[h&k g11|G11]] project and the [[h&k g41|G41]] which was too heavy, the G36 features a conventional configuration with short-stroke piston operation. Notable variants include the shorter [[h&k g36k|G36K]], the shortest [[h&k g36c|G36C]], and the [[h&k mg36|MG36]] [[light machine gun|light machine gun]].

The [[weapon|weapon]] is characterized by a large carrying handle with an integrated [[optical sight|optical sight]] and skeletonized [[folding stock|folding stock]]. It lacks a front sight post as well. The G36 can be fitted with a [[bipod|bipod]] or an [[underbarrel grenade launcher|underbarrel grenade launcher]].

A type of Japanese [[headband|headband]] made of cloth or twine worn to signify dedication to extreme effort. 
A plane hachimaki is commonly used in a sports day / festival of Japanese school to indicate the team color and to try to increase their motivations / kiai (気合, "fighting spirit").
Another common type of hachimaki is printed a red circle of Japanese flag or previously rising sun emblem or / and a short inspirational slogan meant to be displayed across the forehead.

If the headband is twisted, that is called a [[nejiri hachimaki|nejiri hachimaki]] which is commonly worn by participants of a Japanese festival.

Personification of the Hachisuka Kotetsu sword. Uchigatana class. Historically, the sword was the treasure of the Hachisuka Clan.

In *[[touken ranbu|touken ranbu]]*, Hachisuka has a strong aversion to the "counterfeit" Kotetsu swords, including [[nagasone kotetsu|nagasone kotetsu]]. He takes pride in the fact that he and his self proclaimed brother [[urashima kotetsu|urashima kotetsu]] are the real deal. In addition to this he's also a bit of a narcissist, seen in his fieldwork quote. Despite all of these negative qualities, he still secretly has respect for Nagasone, but doesn't want to admit it.

He's one of the five swords the player can choose when starting the game, alongside [[kashuu kiyomitsu|kashuu kiyomitsu]], [[yamanbagiri kunihiro|yamanbagiri kunihiro]], [[mutsu-no-kami yoshiyuki|mutsu-no-kami yoshiyuki]], and [[kasen kanesada|kasen kanesada]].

He has long [[purple hair|purple hair]] and [[blue eyes|blue eyes]], with [[white gloves|white gloves]], a [[full armor|full]] [[gold armor|golden]] [[armor|armor]] set, and golden [[armored boots|armored boots]]. In his casual mode he has a [[high ponytail|high ponytail]] coupled with a golden [[kimono|kimono]] and [[haori|haori]] with golden [[sandals|sandals]]. The over saturation of gold on his person references the fact that the ornate mountings of the original sword (in addition to the inscription on the sword) are colored gold. Because of this, fans see more than a [[look-alike|passing resemblance]] to him and [[aries muu|aries muu]].

The Hadouken (波動拳, "Surge Fist") is a special attack that originated in the classic [[capcom|capcom]] fighting video game series [[street fighter|street fighter]]. The practitioner thrusts his or her palms forward, sending a surge of spirit energy (or ki) flying towards the opponent. It is referred to colloquially as the "Fireball", even though most versions of the Hadouken do not involve the use of fire.

Not to be confused with the [[kamehameha (dragon ball)|kamehameha (dragon ball)]]. The Hadouken is a ball rather than a beam, though the Shinkuu Hadouken in the VS. series of fighting games is a beam possibly as an homage and that Ryu probably wouldn't be able to keep up with the other fighters if it wasn't a beam.

The "Hadouken" was inspired by the [[wave motion gun|wave motion gun]] ("Hadou hou") from the legendary [[uchuu senkan yamato|uchuu senkan yamato]] science fiction series from the 70s.

A **hagoromo** (羽衣, lit. "Feather Robe") is a long, thin [[shawl|shawl]] often associated with far-east celestial beings and deities.

Despite being thin, it is often depicted being able to remain upright in the air on its own. The cloth was modeled after ancient China's clothing called, *pi-bo* (披帛).

Tales associated with the hagoromo include the Japanese legend of *tennin* (spirtual beings who wear hagoromo) and some folkloric stories set in China, for example, [[orihime (tanabata)|orihime (tanabata)]] and [[hikoboshi|hikoboshi]].

Buddhist deities' hagoromo-like shawls are called "天衣" (Chinese: *tian yi*, Japanese: *tenne*, *ten'e*, or *ten'i*). On Danbooru, tian yi should be tagged as hagoromo for convenience.

A [[rou-kyuu-bu!|rou-kyuu-bu!]] character.

The smallest of the girls who very often reacts with "Oh~" or "Ah~", and has a huge collection of plush toys. Despite looking like she is the most innocent and naive of the team, her behavior occasionally suggests otherwise, appearing much more perceptive and even wise than her age would imply.

Generally, Hinata is a sweet and innocent girl. Similar to Maho, she is outgoing, energetic and happy-go-lucky, but sometimes displays a rather bizarre way of thinking. But unlike Maho, Hinata is very well-behaved. Hinata also often comes across as air-headed. On the other hand, as her nickname "Innocent Charm" suggests, she can be manipulative by using her cuteness to get others to do things for her.

Hinata views Subaru as a big-brother-like figure, and doesn't mind making physical contacts with him. As seen in several moments she loves hugging him and being carried on his back, her "Koala Attack" of fan-service, and even wants to sleep with him in same bed. However like all girls in the team, Hinata also has deeper feelings for Subaru, and becomes slightly anxious if Subaru gets too close to other girls. Especially in Episode 4 and Episode 7 of first season, she eagerly wants to know if Subaru has feelings to her, when he "confesses" to Airi.

Being the elder one of the Hakamada sisters, Hinata cares about her little sibling, Kagetsu, very much. She will do anything to make Kagetsu happy as long as she doesn't interfere in her personal life.

[[katawa shoujo|Katawa Shoujo]] character.

Shizune is one of [[nakai hisao|Hisao's]] classmates, as well as the student council president who supervises every aspect of Yamaku's school festival. She has short dark blue hair and eyes, and wears glasses. She is deaf and mute, communicating primarily through sign language. Her friend [[mikado shiina|Misha]] is almost always at her side, translating everything Shizune signs and signing back to her, allowing for communication with other people. 

Shizune is strong-willed and very competitive.  Her favorite game is Risk and she even tries to be first to complete class assignments.

The primary [[shrine|shrine]] of [[gensokyo|gensokyo]] in [[touhou|touhou]] and the personal residence of [[hakurei reimu|hakurei reimu]].

The Hakurei Shrine sits on the border between [[gensokyo|gensokyo]] and the rest of Earth proper, existing on both sides as the anchor of the Great Hakurei Barrier and accessible from either side, though the Earth-side version is said to appear old and abandoned. Outside world items appear on the grounds from time to time, but no one knows how to consciously cross from one side to the other save for [[yakumo yukari|yakumo yukari]] and Reimu, the latter of whom will send outsiders home if asked.

[[ibaraki kasen|ibaraki kasen]], [[ibuki suika|ibuki suika]], [[yakumo yukari|yakumo yukari]], and Reimu's best friend [[kirisame marisa|kirisame marisa]] are frequent guests. The old turtle spirit [[genjii (touhou)|genjii (touhou)]] and the Three Fairies of Light ([[sunny milk|sunny milk]], [[luna child|luna child]], and [[star sapphire|star sapphire]]) live in a spring and a tree behind the shrine, respectively. [[mima (touhou)|mima (touhou)]] once haunted the grounds, but has been absent from the games since the PC98 era and is only assumed to still be present. The inchling princess [[sukuna shinmyoumaru|sukuna shinmyoumaru]] also lived at the shrine in a converted birdcage for a period of time. [[clownpiece|clownpiece]] has taken up residence in the basement since the events of [[legacy of lunatic kingdom|legacy of lunatic kingdom]]. Since becoming animate, [[komano aunn|komano aunn]] has taken it upon herself to be the shrine's guard dog. And others ([[hinanawi tenshi|hinanawi tenshi]], [[yorigami shion|yorigami shion]], etc) have also taken up temporary residence over the years. The patron god of Hakurei Shrine is unknown, even to Reimu, though theories include Yukari, Mima, and [[dragon god (touhou)|the Great Dragon]].

**Han Juri** (*katakana*: **ハン・ジュリ**, *hangul*: **한주리**) is a character in the [[street fighter|street fighter]] series. She makes her debut in [[street fighter iv (series)|Super Street Fighter IV]]. She is the first [[korea|Korean]] character in the Street Fighter series, and the only one that uses [[taekwondo|taekwondo]] so far. She is voiced by [[kitamura eri|kitamura eri]] in Japanese and Jessica Strauss in English.

She is described as being an "evil, mean and nasty" member of S.I.N. who is a main character in the SFIV storyline. The character was created by request of many Korean fans who wished for [[capcom|capcom]] to add a Korean character in Street Fighter, something already established by [[snk|snk]] and [[namco|namco]]. 

She is depicted as being overtly [[sadism|sadistic]] and often makes denigrating and [[sexually suggestive|sexually suggestive]] remarks toward her opponents. ||According to [[menat|menat]], this cruel demeanor is simply a facade to hide her emotional pain and suffering as a result of her traumatic experience after her parents were killed by [[m. bison|M. Bison]], who blinded her left eye, along with her mistreatment after she was captured as a test subject by Shadaloo and S.I.N.||

Juri's left eye was replaced with a "Feng Shui engine," a device capable of enhancing one's power with ki energy, in which she typically covered it with her [[eyepatch|eyepatch]] or [[diagonal bangs|diagonal bangs]]. Normally, she has [[purple eyes|purple eyes]], but she may appear as a [[heterochromia|heterochromic]] when she uses the Feng Shui engine in her left eye, causing it to become [[blue eyes|blue]].

Ironically, Juri is initially met with negative reception from some Korean fanbases, primarily due to her "non-authentic" appearance, albeit these negative connotations would be dissipated afterwards. Her creation is also seen as a rib to [[the king of fighters|the king of fighters]] as all the Korean characters in that franchise, particularly [[kim kaphwan|kim kaphwan]], are either representatives of Justice or evildoers who redeem themselves, while she is (at least initially) a servant of evil.

Han'eri (半襟, はんえり) is a decorative piece of cloth worn over a juban collar to add style or color to an outfit. About 16.5cm (6") wide by 110cm (43") long. Also added to protect the juban collar, as it's easily removable for washing. 

Often embroidered with flower motifs or geometrics. Can be made of polyester, crepe, satin, linen, leno weave gauze, or Shioze silk.

If embroidered, the embroidered section is usually about 25cm (9.5") long. It's located about 20cm up from the end of the fabric. There are some unusual haneri where the design embroidered on each side is different (see blue/purple haneri below).

The word "*Hana fuda*" literally means "flower cards." The pictures used for them represent the beauty of Japanese nature.

A traditional Japanese custom of sitting among newly bloomed [[cherry blossoms|cherry]] or [[plum blossoms|plum]] [[tree|trees]] in the early spring (ranging from late March through late April from the south to north of Japan's main islands, and in January in Okinawa). It is often accompanied by [[picnic|picnicking]], drinking, and other activities. 

The appeal of viewing tree blossoms itself is found in the very brief period of flowering, which lasts seldom over a week before the petals have all fallen, and the leaves of their trees begin to sprout. This is considered a symbolic motif representing the beauty and impermanence of life. Owing to the cultural significance of the practice, Japan's national weather service keeps an annual forecast to inform the public as to when cherry trees are predicted to blossom. 

Viewing plum blossoms (ume) is an older practice which started in the Nara period, and was eclipsed during the Heian period by the popularity of viewing cherry blossoms. Many older Japanese today prefer ume viewing (sometimes known as 梅見, *umemi*), as they find that sakura viewing parties may be too crowded and raucous.

The high-waisted silhouette is derived from the traditional Chinese [[qixiong ruqun|qixiong ruqun]].

Historical styles of clothing worn by the Han Chinese. Most styles have a “y” shape collar, but there are also styles with a rounded collar.

There are several styles that are at times mistaken for kimono (most notably [[ruqun|ruqun]]). You can typically distinguish between them based on the hairstyle and headwear. Males' hair may be pulled back into a simple ponytail or bun or held by a coronet. Emperors or princes may wear [[mian guan|mian guan]]. If nothing else, [[huadian|huadian]] (forehead mark), or the [[tuanshan|circular fan]] is an easy distinguishing mark. 

Hanfu differs from [[qing dynasty|Qing]] era clothing. Hanfu specifically refers to clothing worn during dynasties wherein the tuling class was made up of the majority Chinese ethnic group, the Han. The Qing Dynasty was ruled by the [[manchu clothes|Manchu]] ethnic minority. The frog button and mandarin collar style clothes, often simply refered to as Chinese clothes, are not Hanfu, as they are not Han clothing, but in fact Manchu. This goes too for other erhnic minority clothing in china, such as [[miao clothes|miao clothes]] or [[uygur clothes|uygur clothes]]. These fall under the umbrella of [[chinese clothes|chinese clothes]], along with hanfu.

A hanging scroll, called by the generic terms 立軸 (*lìzhóu*) in China and 掛軸/掛け軸 (*kakejiku*) in Japan, is an illustration or piece of [[calligraphy|calligraphy]] affixed to a [[scroll|scroll]] of cloth or paper.

When hanging scrolls first took their modern form during the [Northern Song Dynasty](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_Dynasty%23Northern_Song.2C_960.E2.80.931127&rct=j&q=Northern+Song+Dynasty&usg=AFQjCNFIrrx4svMf0c5D1xR1PQ26uXs3XQ&sa=X&ei=4IjqTrWKL-edmQWm_oWdCg&ved=0CDMQygQwAA) of China, they were strongly characterized as portable murals to be used in religious ceremonies, but later came to be appreciated as art objects.

In the [Japanese Way of Tea,](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_tea_ceremony) these scrolls are called 掛物 (*kakemono*), and are emphasized as an indispensable piece of equipment for the [[tea ceremony|tea ceremony]]. Japanese *kakejiku* are typically displayed in a special alcove for art objects called the [*tokonoma*.](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokonoma)

The Sculptor God Crafted by Utter Isolation The stage six boss of [[touhou|touhou]] 17: [[wily beast and weakest creature|wily beast and weakest creature]]. She is a god that can bring her sculpted idols to life with faith. She is the creator of [[joutouguu mayumi|Joutouguu Mayumi]] and her [[haniwa (statue)|haniwa]] army. She has [[pink eyes|pink eyes]] and wears a [[green headscarf|green headscarf]] atop her [[long hair|long]], [[blue hair|blue hair]]. She is adorned with a [[magatama necklace|magatama necklace]]. Her [[green apron|green apron]] hangs over her [[yellow dress|yellow dress]] with a [[single strap|single strap]] and is filled to the brim with an assortment of [[tools|crafting tools]], such as [[knife|knives]], [[paintbrush|brushes]], and [[pliers|pliers]]. She wears a pair of [[sandals|sandals]]. Summoned by the enslaved human spirits of the Primate Spirit Garden, she and her idols took control over the Primate Spirit Garden and posed a threat to the Animal Realm at large. Since her idols had no flesh, soul or desire, the beast spirits could not resist them. Hence, the beasts executed their plan of pretending to invade Hell in order to recruit the protagonists, kickstarting the plot of Wily Beast and Weakest Creature in the process. #### See also - pool #18399 - That's not how you use a Haniwa! #### External links - [Touhou Wiki: Keiki Haniyasushin](https://en.touhouwiki.net/wiki/Keiki_Haniyasushin)

She has long [[blonde hair|blonde hair]] and [[blue eyes|blue eyes]] and wears a black uniform with a white skirt. Commonly seen wearing a pair of [[goggles|goggles]] on her head. Her familiar is a [Steller's Sea Eagle](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steller%27s_sea_eagle,) which gives her a pair of [[head wings|head wings]].

A legendary witch from Karlsland, who is called the "Star of Africa" due to her stunning looks and extraordinary skill in combat. She has the ability of "deflection shooting", which makes it look like she shoots at empty space and the enemy flies into the bullets of their own volition.

Her ace archetype is [Hans-Joachim Marseille](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hans-Joachim_Marseille.) Like Hanna, Hans-Joachim carried the nickname "Star of Africa" and a strong celebrity status for his success in North Africa and his agreeable appearance and personality.

The **harmonica**, also **French harp**, **blues harp**, and **mouth organ**, is a free reed wind [[instrument|instrument]] used worldwide in nearly every musical genre, notably in blues, American folk music, jazz, country, and rock and roll. There are many types of harmonica, including diatonic, chromatic, tremolo, octave, orchestral, and bass versions. A harmonica is played by using the mouth (lips and/or tongue) to direct air into and out of one or more holes along a mouthpiece.

The [[summer uniform|summer uniform]] instead features a [[puffy short sleeves|puffy short-sleeved]] [[blue dress|blue-ish]] [[white dress|white]] [[sailor dress|sailor dress]] with a [[breast pocket|breast pocket]] on the wearer's left. 

Note that in live performances, the cast usually wear only the skirt part of the winter uniform along with a themed t-shirt in encores.

Unlike the other entries of Love Live!, they don't change their neckerchiefs to other colors when they move up a class.

A magical [[hand fan|hand fan]] made of feathers, commonly possessed by [[tengu|tengu]]. Hauchiwa may resemble a maple leaf, but they are not actually made of leaves.

In folk tales, these fans sometimes have the ability to grow or shrink a person's nose, but usually they are attributed the power to stir up great winds.

[[shameimaru aya|shameimaru aya]] from [[touhou|touhou]] is one of the more notable hauchiwa-possessing characters, and is frequently depicted with one. While hauchiwa typically have a vaguely leaf-like appearance anyway, Aya's resembles a [[maple leaf|maple leaf]] (down to its coloring and use of fewer feathers in order to specifically achieve a leaf-like shape).

Do not tag hauchiwa with [[leaf fan|leaf fan]], as the former is not made out of leaves, despite some hauchiwa having superficially similar appearance to a maple leaf.

Some Tengu characters may carry an actual [[leaf fan|leaf fan]] instead of a hauchiwa, e.g. [[kurama (urusei yatsura)|kurama (urusei yatsura)]] from [[urusei yatsura|urusei yatsura]]. Tag these examples as [[leaf fan|leaf fan]] instead of [[hauchiwa|hauchiwa]], as they are not made out of feathers.

Visually, there will likely be no difference between hay and straw on Danbooru, so no distinction is made here. In agriculture, there is a major difference between straw and hay. Straw is a by-product from harvesting crops and has little to no nutritional value. Hay is a product deliberately grown and harvested before seeding when the plants will contain a high concentration of nutrients, thus making them useful as feed for animals.

She's a young [[asian|asian]] woman with long [[brown hair|brown hair]]. Misa is also [[claudia lasalle|claudia lasalle]]'s best friend. 

In [[real life|real life]] during 1983 the character of Hayase Misa won the first [[animage|animage]] Grand Prix Award ever for "Best Female Character" in Japanese anime.

Most of them cover from head to toes and some are completely airtight.

The Healin' Garden, a secret world where Earth is healed, is under attack by the Byougenzu, who are trying to infect the Earth.
In order to salve it, three medical trainees of Earth, the Healin' Animals, along with Latte, the little princess of the Healin' Garden who holds a special power, escaped in search of their partners!
Now, three ordinary girls are able to transform into Pretty Cure with the power of the Healin' Animals and fight against the Byougenzu!
The Pretty Cure are in charge of defending Latte and the precious Earth and all her creatures by taking care of them.

A [[meme attire|meme outfit]] consisting of a [[turtleneck leotard|turtleneck leotard]] made of a ribbed material resembling a sweater. The outfit is sold by [[uniqlo|uniqlo]] and is made of HeatTech, a thin material designed to wick away moisture and hold body heat. The outfit comes in [[red leotard|red]], [[black leotard|black]], or [[grey leotard|grey]].

The leotards worn by the [[shadaloo dolls|shadaloo dolls]] are visually similar except for the neckties, but they should not be referred as such due to the difference in colors as well as overall design. The leotard as sold by Uniqlo is not a thong leotard and does not have the backless design. Furthermore, it is secured by buttons at the crotch.

This tag used to be referred to as "[[turtleneck leotard|turtleneck leotard]]," but the ambiguity of the tag name led to it being populated by images with literal turtleneck leotards and not necessarily the HeatTech one, thus the need for the rename.

She also carries ornaments of [[moon (ornament)|the moon]], [[earth (ornament)|the Earth]], and [[underworld (ornament)|the Spirit World]] with her, representing her ability to exist in 3 locations at once. Her hair and eye color change according to the ornament she wears in her hat: red when it's the Spirit World, [[blue hair|blue]] when it's [[hecatia lapislazuli (earth)|Earth]], and [[blonde hair|blonde]] when it's the [[hecatia lapislazuli (moon)|moon]], although it's not uncommon to see her with "other objects on her head.":/pools/10382

**Heisei** (平成, lit. "becoming peaceful" or "peace everywhere") is the official name of the era of Japanese history spanning from 1989 to 2019.

Beginning immediately after the death of [[emperor hirohito|emperor hirohito]] and the ascension of Crown Prince [[emperor akihito|Akihito]] to the Chrysanthemum Throne, the Heisei era followed the [[shouwa|shouwa]] era (1926-1989), the [[taishou|taishou]] era (1912-1926), and the [[meiji|meiji]] era (1868-1912). The Heisei ended on May 1, 2019, when Akihito abdicated and his son [[emperor naruhito|Naruhito]] succeeded him as emperor, marking the beginning of the [[reiwa|reiwa]].

#### See also

- [[heisei retro|heisei retro]]

#### External links

- [Wikipedia: Heisei period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heisei_period)

Aesthetic and fashion style based around nostalgia for the [[heisei|heisei]] period, primarily featuring elements associated with '90s and 2000s Japanese childhood, especially that of young girls and the clothing that was marketed to them during the time. It is closely related to [[yume kawaii|yume kawaii]] and [[y2k fashion|y2k fashion]]. In the West, it is often referred to as "cutecore".

Common themes include [[chibi|chibi]] [[animal|animal]]s and mythical creatures such as [[unicorn|unicorn]]s, [[rainbow|rainbow]]s, [[bokeh|bokeh]] and [[sparkle|sparkle]]s, [[sticker|sticker]]s, [[charm (object)|charm (object)]]s, colorful plastic [[jewelry|jewelry]], [[randoseru|randoseru]], sweet food such as [[fruit|fruit]] and [[cake|cake]], bright [[pastel colors|pastel colors]], shaped [[hairclip|hairclip]]s and [[hair bobbles|hair bobbles]], [[magical girl|magical girl]] themes, and symbols such as [[heart|heart]]s, [[star (symbol)|star (symbol)]]s and [[musical note|musical note]]s.

Brands like [[mezzo piano|mezzo piano]] and [[angel blue|angel blue]] are popular, as are [[sanrio|sanrio]] characters and [[tamagotchi|tamagotchi]], and [[flip phone|flip phone]]s, especially with [[cellphone charm|cellphone charm]]s.

For specifically **adults** wearing children's clothing, see [[jojifuku|jojifuku]]. (Do keep in mind, however, that the 女児服 tag is often used for both concepts on sites like Pixiv.)

One of [[oda nobunaga|oda nobunaga]]'s favorite swords. His name comes from the incident where a servant angered his owner and hid behind a table to no avail because Oda used Hasebe to slice through the table and kill that servant. Shortly afterwards, he gave the sword to someone who wasn't even one of his trusted people. Because of that incident, Hasebe resents him. 

Hasebe is portrayed as being serious, dutiful and extremely loyal to the Saniwa, to the point that his opening lines are "If it's an order from the Master...". Artists tend to give him a comically serious personality who's utterly obsessed with pleasing the Saniwa (a trait that often comes into play in more comedic side works, such as *Hanamaru* or the official Anthalogy; see pool #11476 for this portrayal). He is also presented as a foil to fellow swords [[ookurikara|ookurikara]] and [[shokudaikiri mitsutada|shokudaikiri mitsutada]].

He has [[short hair|short]] [[brown hair|brown hair]] and [[purple eyes|purple eyes]]. His standard outfit are purple [[robe|robe]]s, [[white gloves|white gloves]] and [[sode|sode]] on each shoulder. His casual outfit is a purple and white [[track suit|track suit]]. His [[heshikiri hasebe (kiwame)|Kiwame]] form has him dress similarly to a [[priest|priest]], reflecting how his later owner, Kuroda Yoshitaka, converted to Christianity later in life.

He is featured in *[[touken ranbu: hanamaru|touken ranbu: hanamaru]]* as one of the major supporting characters, as the [[saniwa (touken ranbu)|saniwa (touken ranbu)]]'s secretary sword. His loyalty to the Saniwa is more exaggerated in this version.
