Pronounced "Kamen Rider Faiz", the 4th installment of the Heisei [[kamen rider|kamen rider]] series and the 13th installment in overall. It is a joint collaboration between Ishimori Productions and Toei, and was broadcast on TV Asahi from January 26, 2003 to January 18, 2004. It was also the first series to use TV Asahi's current logo.

Lead Rider of [[kamen rider agito (series)|Kamen Rider Agito]], eleventh show of the Kamen Rider series and second of the Heisei generation.

Tsugami Shouichi is a mysterious man who one day washed ashore with no memories, having taken his name from a letter found with him. For some reason he can transform into the mystic warrior Agito to fight the Lords, monsters responsible for mysterious deaths throughout Tokyo.

Agito's default form, Ground Form, has a black-and-gold color scheme, but can also change forms to suit combat situations - the blue Storm Form, the red Flame Form, the fused Trinity Form, and the final Burning and Shining Forms.

Lead Rider of [[kamen rider blade (series)|Kamen Rider Blade]], fourteenth show of the Kamen Rider series and fifth of the Heisei generation.

Kenzaki Kazuma is an orphan whose zeal to protect the defenseless earned him a place in BOARD, a clandestine organization fighting the Undead, monsters who represent species vying for supreme reign over the world. Kenzaki was given the Rider System-02 - Blade - to help him fight off the Undead menace.

Blade has an indigo color scheme, and is patterned after the Hercules beetle (*dynastes hercules*) and the Spades suit. He also has access to the winged Jack Form, as well as the powerful King Form.
n: 仮面ライダーブレイド

d:
Titular protagonist of *[[kamen rider build (series)|Kamen Rider Build]]*, Sento Kiryu is an amnesiac scientist working for Touto, one of the three governments of a Japan physically and politically split by a massive wall created by the Pandora's Box, a mysterious artifact brought from Mars. Besides scientific work, he also moonlights as Build, fighting off the Smash, mutated humans experimented upon by the mysterious Faust organization.

As Build, Sento uses Fullbottles, which were his own creation, to change his appearance and combat capabilities, using a combination of Fullbottles based on organic and inorganic matter, such as his default blue-and-red RabbitTank form.

**Kamen Rider DCD** (better known as Kamen Rider Decade) is the 10th installment of the Heisei era Kamen Rider series. Closely tied with Kamen Rider Battle: Ganbaride, this series focuses on [[kadoya tsukasa|kadoya tsukasa]] (played by Inoue Masahiro) on his journey to save the Nine Worlds from evil.

The series aired from January 25, 2009 to August 30, 2009 on TV Asahi.
n: 仮面ライダーディケイド

d:
The "Destroyer of Worlds".
Lead Rider of [[kamen rider dcd|kamen rider dcd]], nineteenth show of the Kamen Rider series and tenth of the Heisei generation.

[[kadoya tsukasa|kadoya tsukasa]] is an arrogant photographer with no memory of his past, driven to save his own dimension by traveling to 9 other dimensions under the protection of the 9 previous Heisei Riders.

Decade has a magenta color scheme, and is based on the shield bug *graphosoma lineatum* and barcodes. He can transform into the nine previous Heisei Riders, as well as use their abilities via the Kamen Ride Cards. He can also transform into Decade Complete Form, which can conjure "doppelganger" versions of the nine previous Heisei Riders' final forms.

Lead Rider of [[kamen rider den-o (series)|Kamen Rider Den-O]], seventeenth show in the Kamen Rider series and eighth of the Heisei generation.

Nogami Ryotaro is an extremely unlucky young man who happens to be a "Singularity Point" - he can exist outside his "home timeline" and be immune to permanent possession by Imagin, monsters who seek to alter history in their favor by offering a "contract" with discontented people. Having won the allegiance of 4 (later 5) Imagin, he transforms into Den-O.

Besides the basic Plat Form, Den-O can change his aura armor depending on which Imagin is in possession, altering his style: Sword Form with hot-headed [[momotaros|momotaros]] (red, default), Rod Form with smooth-talking [[urataros|urataros]] (blue), Axe Form with boisterous [[kintaros|kintaros]] (yellow), Gun Form with cheerful [[ryutaros|ryutaros]] (violet), and (to a lesser extent) Wing Form with princely [[sieg|sieg]] (white). He later earns two fusion forms: Climax and Liner Forms.

Lead Rider of [[kamen rider w|kamen rider w]], twentieth show of the Kamen Rider series and eleventh of the Heisei generation.

Self-proclaimed "hard-boiled" private eye [[hidari shoutarou|hidari shoutarou]] and his enigmatic assistant [[philip (kamen rider)|Philip]] combat Dopants, humans turned into monsters via [[gaia memory|Gaia Memories]] to wreak havoc in the city of Fuuto, using their "true" Gaia Memories and the Double Driver to merge into Double.

Double has two halves split down the middle, with Shotaro forming the body and left half, and Philip the mind and right half. Each half has 3 forms, making for 9 combinations, of which the most prominent is CycloneJoker. Other forms include FangJoker (where Philip becomes the body and Shotaro being the mind) and CycloneJoker Xtreme (with both men merged as one).

Lead Rider of [[kamen rider 555|kamen rider 555]], thirteenth show of the Kamen Rider series and fourth of the Heisei generation.

Inui Takumi is a lone wolf who was made the reluctant protector of a suitcase containing the Faiz Gear, using its contents to become Faiz and eliminate Orphnochs, monsters who feed on humans and are said to be humanity's next evolutionary step.

Faiz has a black color scheme with red "photon blood" vessels running across the suit. His design is inspired by the firefly and the Greek letter Φ.

He can change into two advanced forms: the speed-oriented Accel Form and the power-oriented Blaster Form.
n: 仮面ライダーファイズ

d:
Titular Rider of [[kamen rider fourze (series)|Kamen Rider Fourze]], twenty-second show of the Kamen Rider series and thirteenth of the Heisei generation, as well as a celebration of the series's 40th anniversary.

[[kisaragi gentarou|Kisaragi Gentaro]] is a self-styled delinquent and second-year transferee to Amanogawa High School who wants to make friends with his schoolmates. After witnessing an attack by the Zodiarts, constellation-themed monsters derived from human hosts wielding Zodiart Switches, he receives the Fourze Driver from his childhood friend [[joujima yuuki|Jojima Yuuki]] and transforms into Kamen Rider Fourze to fight the Zodiarts. Together with Yuuki and reluctant loner [[utahoshi kengo|utahoshi kengo]], Gentaro founds the Kamen Rider Club to investigate potential Zodiarts and urban legends involving past Kamen Riders.

Fourze uses Astro Switches, 40 switch-like devices divided among the Switch Sockets corresponding to his arms and legs, of which four must be equipped at once to allow him to transform, and which can be used to equip his limbs with weapons or change his appearance.

**"LOCK ON! ORANGE ARMS! HANAMICHI ON STAGE!"**

Titular protagonist of [[kamen rider gaim (series)|kamen rider gaim (series)]], twenty-fourth show of the Kamen Rider series and fifteenth of the Heisei generation.

Kazuraba Kota is a former dance crew member who has decided to help out with his older sister Akira. One day he finds a Sengoku Driver, together with a mysterious orange Lockseed, a trinket from a popular game involving Inves, small creatures said to come from an alternate dimension. Using the Driver and the Lockseed, he transforms into Kamen Rider Gaim as he battles not only rogue Inves, but also other Kamen Riders.

Gaim is notable for his [[samurai|samurai]]-inspired design, and uses different fruit-themed Lockseeds to change his appearance and combat abilities (such as Strawberry, Pineapple and his default Orange Arms).

The title character of [[kamen rider geats (series)|Kamen Rider Geats]]. Patterned after a fox.

[[ukiyo ace|ukiyo ace]] is a mysterious, seemingly ageless man with a confident personality and the skills to back it up. Calling himself "the Star of the Stars of the Stars", he is a constant favorite to win the Desire Grand Prix, having done so many times in a row, yet somehow not satisfying his ultimate wishes.

Lead Rider of [[kamen rider hibiki (series)|Kamen Rider Hibiki]], fifteenth show of the Kamen Rider series and sixth of the Heisei generation.

Hibiki is a veteran Oni Rider, having given up his humanity and his old name - Hidaka Hitoshi - to fight the Makamou, human-eating monsters who can only be defeated with the power of pure sound. When not fighting, Hibiki takes on his form when he was still Hitoshi.

Hibiki fights using *bachi* sticks, which were used for *taiko* drums. He can also upgrade into Hibiki Kurenai and finally Armed Hibiki.

*"Walking the path of heaven, ruling over all."*

Lead Rider of [[kamen rider kabuto (series)|Kamen Rider Kabuto]], sixteenth show of the Kamen Rider series and seventh of the Heisei generation.

[[tendou souji|tendou souji]] is an enigmatic young man who has trained for 7 years in anticipation of the Kabuto Zecter, with which he combats the Worms, monsters feeding on and imitating humans, which came from a meteorite which destroyed Tokyo's Shibuya ward 7 years ago.

Kabuto is patterned after the Japanese rhinoceros beetle ("kabutomushi", *trypoxylus dichotomus*). He has four forms - the bulky Masked (initial) and the sleek Rider (default) Forms, and the powered-up Hyper Kabuto and its winged Clock-Up Hyper Kabuto Forms. His special ability is Clock-Up, which gives him superspeed.
n: 仮面ライダーカブト(ライダー名)

d:
Lead Rider of [[kamen rider kiva (series)|Kamen Rider Kiva]], eighteenth show of the Kamen Rider series and ninth of the Heisei generation.

[[kurenai wataru|kurenai wataru]] is a very shy violin maker living in a "haunted house", who only goes out of his mansion to fight as Kiva against Fangires, stained-glass-themed monsters who feed on human souls.

Kiva's red default form is patterned after a vampire. Other forms include the blue, sword-wielding Garulu Form (werewolf), the green, gun-wielding Bashaa Form (gill-man), and the violet, hammer-wielding Dogga Form (Frankenstein's monster). He can also wield the fused DoGaBaKi form, as well as the almighty Emperor Form and its bat-like Flight Style.

Protagonist and sole Rider of [[kamen rider kuuga (series)|Kamen Rider Kuuga]], tenth show of the Kamen Rider series and the first of the Heisei generation.

[[godai yuusuke|godai yuusuke]] is a free-spirited, multi-talented man said to possess 1,999 different skills, who, one day, finds an ancient relic which embeds itself into his body and allows him to transform into the fabled warrior Kuuga to fight the Grongi, monsters from an ancient civilization who kill people for sport.

Kuuga has multiple forms - the basic but very weak Growing Form (white), the balanced Mighty Form (red; default), the speed based and staff wielding Dragon Form (blue), the ranged based and gun wielding Pegasus Form (green), and the power based and sword wielding Titan Form (purple), as well as the upgraded, golden trimmed "Rising" forms for the latter four, the Amazing Mighty Form (black), and the most powerful but also the most dangerous, the Ultimate Form (also black), which has two eye colors: black if he loses control of himself or red if he retains his will.

Titular Rider of [[kamen rider ooo (series)|kamen rider ooo (series)]], twenty-first show of the Kamen Rider series and twelfth of the Heisei generation.

[[hino eiji|hino eiji]] is a world-traveling vagrant with no long-term job, whose recent stint as a museum guard drags him into a tournament between the Greeed, five creatures competing for the title of "Multi King" after an 800-year-slumber. Finding himself an unwitting pawn of the bird-type Greeed Ankh, Eiji fights the Yummy, monsters materialized by Greeed from human desires and which serve as their pawns, as Kamen Rider OOO.
Like [[kamen rider double|his immediate predecessor]], OOO takes on various Combos by placing three Core Medals ([[o medal|o medal]]s taken from the Greeed) at once on his OOO Driver, his default Combo being the [[tatoba (ooo combo)|TaToBa (Hawk/Tiger/Grasshopper) Combo]].

Lead Rider of [[kamen rider ryuki (series)|Kamen Rider Ryuki]], twelfth show of the Kamen Rider series and third of the Heisei generation, as well as the first Rider from the same generation to be given an American adaptation, *Dragon Knight*.

Rookie journalist Kidou Shinji finds himself in the middle of the Rider War, a deathmatch between 13 Kamen Riders, upon making a contract with [[dragreder|dragreder]], a Mirror Monster (themselves responsible for mysterious deaths throughout the city), to transform into Ryuki, fighting both Mirror Monsters and other Riders, as well as uncovering the truth of the Rider War.

Ryuki has a red color scheme and is modeled after both the Chinese dragon and a knight. He also uses Advent Cards to enhance his combat capabilities. Finally, he can upgrade into the bulkier, more powerful Ryuki Survive Form.

Titular Rider of [[kamen rider wizard (series)|Kamen Rider Wizard]], twenty-third show of the Kamen Rider series and fourteenth of the Heisei generation, as well as the franchise's first magic-based Rider.

[[souma haruto|souma haruto]] is the survivor of a magic ritual under a solar eclipse that turned other human sacrifices like him into Phantoms, monsters that feed on their hosts' despair before killing and then imitating them to spread despair in turn. His ordeal granted him the ability to use magic, and with a set of rings and the Wizardriver given to him by a man in white, he sets off to bring hope and fight his fellow Phantoms as Kamen Rider Wizard.

Wizard's combat abilities are affected by Wizard Rings, which are divided into two types: Transformation Rings (on his left middle finger), which change his appearance and elemental specialty (Flame, Water, Hurricane and Land Styles); and Magic Rings (on his right), which give him miscellaneous powers, such as controlling WizarDragon, his personal Phantom.

**Kamikaze Kaitou Jeanne** (also known as **Phantom-Thief Jeanne**) is a fantasy shoujo manga series written and illustrated by [[tanemura arina|tanemura arina]]. The story is about the adventures of a high school girl, [[kusakabe maron|kusakabe maron]], who is the reincarnation of [[jeanne d'arc|jeanne d'arc]] and transforms into a [[magical girl|magical girl]] [kaitou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kait%C5%8D#Genre) to collect the scattered pieces of God's power which are also coveted by [[demon|demon]]s hiding in beautiful art works.

The manga was published by *Shueisha* in *Ribon* between February 1998 and July 2000. The individual chapters were collected and published in seven tankoubon volumes. It is licensed for English-language release by CMX Manga. The series was adapted by [[toei animation|toei animation]] as a 44-episode anime television series that was broadcast on *[[tv asahi|tv asahi]]* from February 1999 to January 2000. The series was re-issued by *Shueisha* in 2007, with all chapters fitting into only 6 volumes, instead of the original 7; all volumes had new covers.

Distinguishable by her [[brown hair|brown hair]], headwear that resembles [[rabbit ears|rabbit ears]], and is usually seen wearing a jean [[miniskirt|miniskirt]] with black [[thighhighs|thighhighs]] and a long sleeved shirt.

Owner of the shop Karindou and a magician, she's roughly a millennium in age. She also has a knack for keeping and creating (generally odd) things inside a store room which exists in some other limitless dimension.

She is usually lazy and feckless, and only occasionally shows her serious side when the people she cares about are under threat.  She was once known and feared as a godslayer, but has been hiding for so long nobody really remembers her anymore, and she'd rather just do nothing but relax for all eternity.  

Her headband is actually a magic dampener made of angel wing that restricts her huge magic potential so that she can cast basic utility spells, rather than only destructive ones.  She prefers using her magic for her own convenience, and often uses it on silly and/or stupid things, like using dimensional magic to transform pudding into swimming pool size.

Her mentor and "mother" is [[elza straherz|elza straherz]].  Their relationship is complicated by Elza's perversion, but she is nevertheless respectful of Elza's knowledge.  At times, she actually reverts to a more childish personality in the face of Elza on the rare occasions Elza actually starts acting the mother.

She is "mother" to [[ujikintoki tamaryu|Tamaryu]] as well as [[ujikintoki kinka|Kinka]] and [[ujikintoki ginka|Ginka]], herself.  In truth, Seren is immortal and was exiled in the first place because she slew Tamaryu's previous incarnation, used Tamaryu's body as magical ingredients for a potion to grant herself immortality, only to wind up caring for Tamaryu's new form.  

Like Elza, her physical form is actually of her own choosing - she actually has a more busty true form, but chooses a more sporty form willfully, and has [[breast envy|breast envy]] simply because "it's more fun to long for things you don't have".  

When she temporarily was in her child form, she had to use a cat ear headband, and was in danger from the pedophillic advances of [[tatsuta rindou|tatsuta rindou]].

**Kämpfer** (German for "Fighter") is a light novel series by Tsukiji Toshihiko, with illustrations by [[senmu (senmudayo)|senmu (senmudayo)]]. The series contains 15 volumes published by *Media Factory* under their *MF Bunko J* imprint between November 2006 and March 2010. The main series covers 12 volumes, while the remaining three are short story collections. A manga adaptation by [[tachibana yuu|tachibana yuu]] started serialization in the April 2008 issue of *Monthly Comic Alive*. A 12-episode anime adaptation aired in Japan between October and December 2009 on *TBS*, concluded in spring 2011 with *Kämpfer für die Liebe*. The series has extensive use of the German language.

#### Plot

[[senou natsuru|senou natsuru]] discovered that he can morph into a female fighter (Kämpfer) after receiving a plush doll gift from his friend, [[sakura kaede|sakura kaede]]. Suddenly, he discovered himself in a deadly fight between Kämpfers. The party responsible for the fight is rumored to be as Moderators and they are mysterious.

The best-known of [[ukiyo-e|ukiyo-e]] master [[katsushika hokusai (1760)|katsushika hokusai (1760)]]'s ”"36 Views of Mt. Fuji":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirty-six_Views_of_Mount_Fuji],” this piece depicts a large wave cresting over fishing skiffs in a bay near [[kanagawa|kanagawa]], with [[mount fuji|mount fuji]] itself dwarfed by the wall of water and offered little contrast from the roiled skies above.

Because it has become an iconic representation of Japanese art, the motif is frequently used in modern works where it tends to impart a sort of "traditional" feel.

**Kannazuki no Miko** (lit. *[[miko|Priestesses]] of the Godless Month*) is a manga series created by the duo [[kaishaku|kaishaku]]. The series was serialized in fourteen chapters by *Kadokawa Shoten* and in *Shounen Ace* in 2004 and 2005, and collected in two bound volumes. The series was adapted as an anime television series broadcast in 12 episodes on *TNK* between October and December 2004. A drama CD was released on November 25, 2004 by *Geneon* based on the anime version.

The series centers on the [[yuri|yuri]] relationship of the two main characters, [[kurusugawa himeko|Himeko]] and [[himemiya chikane|Chikane]], with elements of [[magical girl|magical girl]] and [[mecha|mecha]] themes helping to carry the plot. An anime series that includes several characters similar to those of *Kannazuki no Miko* called *[[kyoushirou to towa no sora|kyoushirou to towa no sora]]* aired in Japan between January and March 2007.

Because it was one of the first yuri romances in an anime that was played as a straight romance, it's become iconic for yuri romance, especially its ED artwork, featuring the memetic [[miko embrace|miko embrace]].  (The pose is essentially synonymous with yuri.)

The manga and anime were originally released in English under the original Japanese title by Tokyopop and Geneon USA respectively. After Geneon USA's shutdown, distribution rights for the anime were transferred to Sentai Filmworks, who now distribute the series under the English title **Destiny of the Shrine Maiden**.

Kanno Naoe is a Witch of the [[502nd joint fighter wing|502nd joint fighter wing]], originating from Fuso and affiliated with the Fuso Imperial Navy. She is also known by the pet name of "Nao" (ナオ). Her familiar is the bulldog.

Naoe can be described, in one word, as Napoleonic; despite her small size, she bold and daring in the air, brash and sometimes belligerent socially. It's an attitude she forces on herself because of the war with the [[neuroi|neuroi]]: when her Witch abilities woke up, she roused herself by repeating the prayer: "to fight a Neuroi, one should have a ferocious personality". This attitude doesn't lend itself well to teamwork or cooperation, but under Flight Lieutenant [[aleksandra i. pokryshkin|Pokryshkin]] this is dampened somewhat, perhaps because she resembles an elder sister of Naoe's childhood, whom she remembers fondly.

Naoe is based on Japanese flying ace [[kanno naoshi|kanno naoshi]] (菅野直). One of his nicknames was Bulldog, Naoe's familiar is a reference to this. Besides that, he was also nicknamed "Destroyer" and "Yellow Fighter".

*Kantai Collection* (艦隊これくしょん *Kantai Korekushon*, lit. "Combined Fleet Collection"), abbreviated as *KanColle* (艦これ *KanKore*), is a Japanese free-to-play shipgirl-themed game developed by [[c2 kikan|c2 kikan]] under [[kadokawa|Kadokawa Games]] and published by [[dmm|dmm]]. It is currently available exclusively in Japanese, though it has started to introduce some English-language graphical assets, and accessing the game for non-Japanese players requiring unconventional means.

#### Gameplay

Gameplay is centered upon building squadrons composed of individual characters represented as cards with different attributes, and then sending said squadrons out on missions. The player takes on the role of an [[admiral (kancolle)|admiral (kancolle)]] (提督 *teitoku*) and organises their fleets in battle in order to win. Combat is largely automated, and manual actions by the player include micromanagement such as building and repairing.

Each of the characters are moe [[personification|personification]]s of [[world war ii|world war ii]] naval [[warship|warship]]s, which are depicted as cute girls known as "ship girls" (艦娘, *kanmusu*). These personified warships are based on real life vessels which are explained in detail within the game; the physical characteristics, appearances and personalities of each of the girls correlate in some way to the real life vessel.

Originally, the roster of the shipgirls was designed to be limited to the IJN and major players of the Imperial Japanese Army, and its final mission being an attack on the base, akin to how World War 2 played out for Japan. Due to the game's popularity, it has since introduced shipgirls from other Axis nations and wartime rival factions, including ships from the U.S. Navy, the British Royal Navy and even the somewhat-neutral Swedish Navy. 

As of early 2022, KanColle features ships from following navies: Imperial Japanese Navy, Imperial Japanese Army, Maritime Safety Agency/Japan Coast Guard, United States Navy, British Royal Navy, Royal Australian Navy, Dutch Koninklijke Marine, French Marine nationale, Italian Regia Marina, German Kriegsmarine, Военно-морской флот СССР, Swedish Svenska marinen, and Republic of China Navy. With the most numerous non-Japanese navies being United States Navy and Regia Marina.

#### Media

The game has developed into a much larger media franchise; various media including multiple manga series and light novels have been released, in addition to an officially licensed [[tabletop rpg|tabletop role-playing game]]. A [[playstation vita|playstation vita]] game was released February 2016. A [[kantai collection (anime)|television anime adaptation]] aired Winter 2015, with a sequel season airing in 2022, and an anime movie was released in 2016. There is also a Japan only 3D arcade game [[kancolle arcade|kancolle arcade]] that was released in 2016.

#### History

The web browser game was launched on April 23, 2013, originally designed to run in Adobe Flash. An Android app version was released on August 1st, 2016. As of January 2015, the game had 2.5 million registered players. The game migrated to HTML5 prior to worldwide decommissioning of Adobe Flash in browsers.

**Karate** (空手) is a [[martial arts|martial art]] developed in the Ryukyu Kingdom. It developed from the indigenous Ryukyuan martial arts (called *te* (手), "hand"; *tii* in Okinawan) under the influence of [[china|Chinese]] martial arts, particularly Fujian White Crane. Karate is now predominantly a striking art using punching, kicking, knee strikes, elbow strikes and open-hand techniques such as knife-hands, spear-hands, and palm-heel strikes. Historically, and in some modern styles, grappling, throws, joint locks, restraints, and vital-point strikes are also taught. A karate practitioner is called a *karateka* (空手家).

**Karategi** (空手着 or 空手衣) is the formal Japanese name for the traditional [[uniform|uniform]] used for [[karate|karate]] practice and competition.

A *karategi* is somewhat similar to a *[[judogi|judogi]]* (柔道着 or 柔道衣, "Judo uniform") as it shares a common origin; however, the material and cut of the uniform is generally much lighter and looser fitting. The heaviest of *Karategi* are only 0.5 kg (16 oz) compared to some *[[judogi|judogi]]* at 1 kg (35 oz). Because of the nature of [[karate|karate]] training which emphasizes striking, kicking and a more limited range of standing throws compared to [[judo|judo]] the karategi has evolved in a manner that maximizes mobility and speed without the extremely coarse and strong fabric required for grappling and throwing found in [[judo|judo]]. They are made from smooth cotton which may be brushed or ribbed for unrestricted movement and added comfort. Reinforced stitching is common, as to compensate for the stresses put on the *[[gi|gi]]*.

After her 15th anniversary on April 2023, she received an [[kasane teto (sv)|updated voicebank]] under the [[synthesizer v|synthesizer v]] engine, which would boost her popularity even further.

Her official profile lists her as a "chimera", so she is sometimes given characteristics like a forked tail or wings. Her character item is a loaf of french bread. 

Her voice provider is [[oyamano mayo|oyamano mayo]].

Oyamano initially used the name Oyama Nobuyo as a reference to famed singer and voice actress [[ooyama nobuyo|ooyama nobuyo]]. Since the latter is most known as the voice of [[doraemon (character)|doraemon (character)]], fans had Teto share similar traits. Teto's [[catchphrase|catchphrase]] **君は実に馬鹿だな** "You really are an idiot, aren't you?" also originated from a [[doraemon|doraemon]] comic.

Do not tag Kasane Teto as a [[vocaloid|vocaloid]]. She is either an UTAU or a SynthV.

**Sakura Kasugano** (**春日野 さくら**) is a character in the [[street fighter|street fighter]] series. She is introduced as a 16-year-old (as of [[street fighter zero (series)|Street Fighter Zero 3]]) Japanese schoolgirl who has an intense fixation with [[ryu (street fighter)|Ryu]]. She has managed to copy and learn some of Ryu's techniques but really wants him to train her personally. In her most recent appearance in [[street fighter v|street fighter v]]'s new *Arcade Edition*, she has graduated high school and has taken a job at an arcade to make ends meet, but she still persists in fighting and training.

Sakura has typically fought in her school's uniform, a short-skirted [[serafuku|serafuku]] with the [[popped collar|collar popped]] and [[red buruma|red buruma]] underneath. She wears a red top under her uniform, red gloves, and a [[white headband|white headband]] (given to her by Ryu before Street Fighter Zero 2). As of Street Fighter V, she has replaced the school uniform with the [[employee uniform|employee uniform]] of the arcade she works at. She has short brown hair. 

Chronologically, Sakura first appeared in [[shiritsu justice gakuen|Shiritsu]] [[justice gakuen|justice gakuen]], where she had started to participate in street fighting after watching Ryu win the first World Warrior tournament. A type of Japanese [[sword|sword]] (*nihontou*), and is often called a "samurai sword" because of its historical associations with feudal-era Japan.

The katana is characterized by its distinctive appearance: a curved, slender, single-edged blade, circular or squared [[tsuba (guard)|guard]], and long grip to accommodate two hands (the hilt is often given a distinctive wrapping of silk known as *[[tsuka-ito|tsukaito]]*).

The sword preceding the katana is called a [[tachi (weapon)|tachi (weapon)]]. The general difference between a tachi and a katana is how they are carried. The tachi is suspended from one’s waist belt with the cutting edge facing down, while the katana is thrust through the waist belt, edge facing up. Also, in general the tachi is more curved and longer than the katana.

"**Katawa Shoujo** is a bishoujo-style visual novel set in the fictional Yamaku High School for disabled children, located somewhere in modern Japan. Hisao Nakai, a normal boy living a normal life, has his life turned upside down when a congenital heart defect forces him to move to a new school after a long hospitalization. Despite his difficulties, Hisao is able to find friends—and perhaps love, if he plays his cards right."

The game was released on January 4, 2012. 

The story behind the game's development is quite unusual. The original idea for the game stems from a one page sketch by the artist [[honjou raita|honjou raita]]. A translated version of the page (post #22437) was posted on 4chan on January 4, 2007. The post received a huge response and eventually a group of people emerged that was highly dedicated to realizing the creation of the game. These people formed Four Leaf Studios and continued to work on it.

The hairstyle's name stems from a person - during the early Edo period, Katsuyama was the pseudonym of a high-ranking courtesan popular in Yoshiwara during the early Edo period. Mage translates to 'hairstyle'. #### Examples - !asset #22075057: "Source: Kotobank":[https://kotobank.jp/word/%E5%8B%9D%E5%B1%B1%E9%AB%B7-825399] - _(post #2601133)_ - _(post #7069255)_ - _(post #3883878)_ - _(post #7444606)_ #### See also - [[japanese clothes|japanese clothes]]

Kazama Jin is one of the main characters of the [[tekken|tekken]] series.

First appearing in [[tekken 3|tekken 3]], Jin is the son of [[kazama jun|kazama jun]] and [[mishima kazuya|mishima kazuya]]. He was raised by his mother; Jun, for most of his young life until he turned 15, when his mother was supposedly murdered by [[ogre (tekken)|ogre (tekken)]], an ancient being known as "Toshin, the God of Fighting." He was taken in by his grandfather, [[mishima heihachi|mishima heihachi]] who taught him Mishima Style Karate. Jin was able to defeat Ogre, winning the King of Iron Fist Tournament 3 but was betrayed and almost shot dead by Heihachi.

From [[tekken 4|tekken 4]] onward, he would use traditional Karate instead of Mishima style to fall more in line with his mother's teachings and to distance himself from his Mishima heritage. In [[tekken 5|tekken 5]], his [[dark persona|dark persona]], [[devil jin|devil jin]] became a playable character, using his moveset from games prior to Tekken 4. 

In [[tekken 6|tekken 6]], after defeating [[mishima jinpachi|mishima jinpachi]] in the previous tournament. Jin was declared the new head of the Mishima Zaibatsu. He used his new leadership to wage a world war, and to host the King of Iron Fist Tournament 6. However, he was bested by [[lars alexandersson|lars alexandersson]].

Jin is characterized by his altruism, as evident by his interactions with [[ling xiaoyu|ling xiaoyu]] and [[hwoarang (tekken)|hwoarang (tekken)]]. He plans to end the Mishima bloodline by killing Heihachi, Kazuya and then himself. 

Jin's outfits usually consist of black pants or hooded jackets with a flame motif. In Tekken 3 and [[tekken tag tournament|tekken tag tournament]], he had a school uniform alternate costume alongside Xiaoyu, as they both attended the same high school. In Tekken 6, he wears a business suit alternate costume and an emperor outfit designed by [[clamp (circle)|clamp (circle)]]. His [[tekken 7|tekken 7]] outfit was designed by [[kozaki yuusuke|kozaki yuusuke]].

Hinted by [[hieda no akyuu|hieda no akyuu]] to exhibit a rather polite facade, provided she or her flowers are not harmed. Once described by ZUN as "Youkai moe~", possibly meant as a pun given that the literal meaning of moe is "budding" and Yuuka controls flowers. Otherwise referred to as **Kemomimi Oukoku**, it is the name of the managing brand behind 3DCG artist [[nekomasu (nekomasu1)|nekomasu (nekomasu1)]]'s channels since early 2018. Run by the artist, he is also referred to as Virtual Nojaloli Kitsunemusume YouTuber Ojisan and appeared as [[mikoko (kemomimi oukoku kokuei housou)|mikoko (kemomimi oukoku kokuei housou)]] on the channel.

Nekomasu would "announce":[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6IPh2ggvdZ4] in July 2018 that the channel was shifting to be more akin to a virtual variety channel, and that the channel had been sold to [[livecartoon|LiveCartoon.LLC]]. The channel rebranded as a result, going from "Kemomimi VR Channel" to  "Virtual Program Channel" (バーチャル番組チャンネル; briefly バーチャル番組連盟 at first) as Nekomasu moved away from YouTube, opting for Twitter and Niconico, branding himself "Virtual Nojaloli Kitsunemusume *Former* YouTuber Ojisan" and eschewing the VTuber handle altogether, not considering himself one at all.

The original channel would go dormant after August 2019, and a new successor channel, simply titled Kemomimi Oukoku, would emerge later in October, its host gradually becoming a new model, Nekomasu-chan. The original channel would end up losing its branding entirely by May 2020, just becoming "_" as it continued to lay dormant. It wouldn't be until January 3rd, 2021 that the channel was once more returned to Nekomasu, being renamed to "Kemomimi Oukoku「Kitsune」", with all the LiveCartoon era videos becoming unlisted.

A Japanese multimedia franchise about the fictional *Japari Park*, where various animals—both real and mythological— have been [[personification|anthropomorphized]] into animal girls, referred to as *Friends*, by the mysterious power of a curious substance called *Sandstar.*

Originally envisioned as a multimedia project, a mobile game published by Nexon was released in 2015, with a tie-in anime series set after the events of the game due to air some time later. The project was not without its turbulence, as the mobile game ended its services in late 2016—just one month before the anime aired in early 2017, the first season of which was financially restricted, resulting in poor animation quality and mixed reviews from initial critics and viewers.

Despite the 2015 game being closed down early—thus failing to give anime viewers context as had been planned—the anime was a surprise hit, due in no small part to scripting by director [[tatsuki (irodori)|Tatsuki]]; the show received very high ratings and viewership, miraculously reviving the dying franchise into a breakout success.

**Kenshiro** (**ケンシロウ**), or just **Ken** as he is often called, is the central character of the [[hokuto no ken|hokuto no ken]] manga, anime, and other related works.

He is the 64th successor to the Hokuto Shinken art of combat, after his adopted father, Ryuken. He is considered "one of the greatest" successors in Hokuto Shinken history, due to his knowledge of certain legendary techniques like *Musou Tensei*. He is also known for his famous catchphrase: [[you are already dead|「お前はもう死んでいる。」]] ("*Omae wa mou shindeiru.*" / "You are already dead.")

After the nuclear war, his fiancee [[yuria (hokuto no ken)|Yuria]] was taken by [[shin (hokuto no ken)|Shin]], who defeated Kenshiro and craving the infamous seven scars on his chest. Kenshiro along with two orphanted children who later joined his cause, [[bat (hokuto no ken)|Bat]] and [[lin (hokuto no ken)|lin (hokuto no ken)]], started his journey to taking back his fiancee from Shin. This would leading to several chains of events involving him saving the innocents from various ruthless bandits factions for their survival, and that made Kenshiro being later called as **"The Savior of century's end"**. 

#### Known moves

- 五指烈弾 (*Goshi Retsudan*)
  - Causes the opponent's fingers to explode.

- 北斗百裂拳 (*[[hokuto hyakuretsu ken|hokuto hyakuretsu ken]]*)
  - Kenshiro's trademark technique, in which Ken strikes the opponent's body with a relentless flurry of punches aimed at key pressure points, resulting in full body explosion. Usually delivered with Kenshiro's famous *"ATATATATATATATATA"* kiai.

- 二指真空把 (*[[nishi shinkuu ha|nishi shinkuu ha]]*)
  - An arrow shot towards the user is caught between two fingers and then deflected back towards the opponent.

- 岩山両斬波 (*[[ganzan ryouzan ha|ganzan ryouzan ha]]*)
  - A hand chop which splits the opponent's skull in half.

- 北斗残悔拳 (*[[hokuto zankai ken|hokuto zankai ken]]*)
  - A technique that causes the opponent to explode three seconds later so he can repent for his sins before he dies.

- 北斗飛衛拳 (*Hokuto Hiei Ken*)
  - A flying jump kick Kenshiro uses to defend himself against [[shin (hokuto no ken)|Shin's]] *Nanto Gokuto Ken*.

- 北斗龍撃虎 (*Hokuto Ryuu Geki Ko*)
  - Places the opponent in a temporary death-like coma. Ken's counterpart to [[rei (hokuto no ken)|Rei's]] *Nanto Ko Ha Ryuu*.

- 天破活殺 (*Tenha Kassatsu*)
  - A powerful aura blast which strikes the opponent's vital points in the shape of the Big Dipper.

- 北斗有情猛翔破 (*Hokuto Ujou Moushou Ha*)
  - An uppercut that causes opponents to die peacefully without any pain. ||Used as the finishing move to kill Souther.||

- 無想転生 (*Musou Tensei*)
  - The ultimate secret technique of Hokuto Shinken. It makes the user untouchable to all incoming attacks.
    - [[hakurei reimu|Hakurei Reimu's]] strongest spellcard, 「夢想天生」 "Fantasy Heaven", is a homonym to this move and offers the same benefit of invulnerability.

From Wikipedia:
"A key frame in animation and filmmaking is a drawing that defines the starting and ending points of any smooth transition. The drawings are called "frames" because their position in time is measured in frames on a strip of film. A sequence of keyframes defines which movement the viewer will see, whereas the position of the keyframes on the film, video or animation defines the timing of the movement. Because only two or three keyframes over the span of a second do not create the illusion of movement, the remaining frames are filled with inbetweens."

In other words, it is a raw still shot that was used directly for the producing the animation. This covers parts, or even all of, the draft sketch to test out plot flow, pre-color scenes, cel that was used for the animation, or complete film still. It is primarily used to complete the animation, since key frames themselves do not show any movement; it is important however, if not most important in developing animations.

It is not necessarily same thing as [[anime screenshot|anime screenshot]], which captures the final material in presented medium. Key frames in general strictly internal-use only.

The Japanese word 原画 (*genga*) can mean "key frame", but more literally means "original illustration". Thus works tagged with this on Pixiv should not be automatically tagged as key frame here.

See also [[official art|official art]], [[production art|production art]].

The other primary mecha featured in the show are the three-form transformable fighter called the Armo-Fighter AFC-01 [[legioss|legioss]] and another three form heavy mecha called AB-01 [[tread|tread]].

All the human and alien mechanical designs for the series were created by [[aramaki shinji|aramaki shinji]] and [[kakinuma hideki|kakinuma hideki]] respectively.

Mospeada became ***The New Generation*** in the [[robotech|robotech]] American adaptation of the series.

A stylized depiction of a 16 petal [[chrysanthemum|chrysanthemum]] flower, used by the Emperor of Japan and the Imperial Family. It is most notably seen on the bows of warships of the [[imperial japanese navy|imperial japanese navy]] and on the covers of Japanese passports. Be careful not to confuse it with the 5 petal [[sakuramon|sakuramon]].

For clear examples, check the [[obi|obi]]'s of Akiha (post #15614) and Megurine Luka (post #568974), and the bottom-right side of Yuyuko's kimono (post #570756).

d:
*Kimi no koto ga Dai Dai Dai Dai Daisuki na 100-nin no Kanojo* (*The 100 Girlfriends Who Really, Really, Really, Really, Really Love You*) is a harem romantic comedy manga written by Rikito Nakamura and illustrated by [[nozawa yukiko|nozawa yukiko]]. It began serialization on December 26, 2019.

It follows high school student [[aijou rentarou|aijou rentarou]], who in his lifetime fell in love and confessed to exactly 100 girls, only to be rejected by all of them. While praying in a shrine, Rentarou is approached by the God of Love, who reveals that he, due to an error, is destined to have 100 soulmates. However, he also tells Rentarou that if he does not return the feelings of any of his soulmates, they will suffer an accident and die. Not wanting this to happen, Rentarou is determined not to let any of his soulmates die as he meets and dates them all at the same time.

A kimono (着物) is a type of traditional [[japanese clothes|Japanese clothing]]. It consists of a long, [[wide sleeves|wide-sleeved]] robe, closed at the front forming a "y" shape. It is held closed with a wide belt-like [[sash|sash]] called an [[obi|obi]].

Kimonos are often worn with other traditional accessories, such as [[zouri|zouri]] (traditional wooden sandals), [[tabi|tabi]] (split-toe socks), and [[kanzashi|kanzashi]] (traditional hair ornaments). A [[kinchaku|kinchaku]] (small cloth drawstring bag) is often carried while wearing a kimono.

King Dedede is the self-proclaimed king of Dream Land, [[kirby|Kirby's]] #1 rival, and a recurring antagonist in the *[[kirby (series)|Kirby]]* games. Typically caring only for himself, he likes to mess with others because he thinks it's fun. He even once stole all of Dream Land's food. Sometimes, he does do good deeds, and will even team up with Kirby more often than he'd like to admit.

A [[kaiju|kaiju]] from [[godzilla (series)|Godzilla]] series, first appeared in its own standalone movie *Ghidorah, the Three-Headed Monster* (1964). Since its debut, King Ghidorah has the most theatrical appearance of any kaiju within the series bar Godzilla itself, thus it is often considered an arch-enemy of [[godzilla|godzilla]].

King Ghidorah is a large, yellow, [[multiple heads|three-headed]] [[dragon|dragon]] with an ability to shoot lightning bolt from its mouth. It is typically depicted as an alien kaiju who brought devastation upon any planet it made a landfall.

In some depictions, each head of King Ghidorah has its own personality, which led to the characters within that media to name each of Ghidorah's head based on their behavior.

Manga series created by Yoshinori Nakai and Takashi Shimada under the name Yudetamago. Originally serialized in *Weekly Shounen Jump* from 28 May 1979 to March 1987 for 387 chapters and later collected in 36 volumes. It was adapted into two anime series: a 137-episode series that aired on NTV from 3 April 1983 to 1 October 1986, and a 46-episode series (*Kinnikuman: Scramble for the Throne*) that also aired on NTV from 6 October 1991 to 27 September 1992, in addition to seven theatrical films (1984-1986) and a television special (7 April 1984).

After 24 years, it returned in *Shuu Play News*, Shueisha's web version of *Weekly Playboy* on 28 November 2011. An additional 22 volumes have been published, numbered 37 to 58 as of 3 March 2017.

The series involves an intergalactic stand-off between various heroes and villains with [[wrestling|wrestling]] as a center theme.

This game returns to the traditional game mechanics the franchise is known for (hence the American name). He goes to Castle Dedede to investigate, but before he could confront [[king dedede|king dedede]], a [[taranza|mysterious spider mage]] appears from behind and captures the king. A former [[virtual youtuber|virtual youtuber]] and 4th generation member of [[hololive|hololive]]. A [[dragon girl|dragon girl]] in human form.

She has [[very long hair|very long]] [[orange hair|orange hair]] with a single [[blonde hair|yellow]] [[streaked hair|lock of hair]] near her forehead. Her regular hairstyle is [[straight hair|straight hair]] with an [[ahoge|ahoge]], [[hair intakes|hair intakes]] held with a [[black hairband|black hairband]], [[fanged bangs|fanged]] [[blunt bangs|blunt bangs]], [[sidelocks|sidelocks]] and a [[side braid|side braid]]. She also has a pair of [[dragon horns|dragon horns]] with a [[horn bow|bow]] on her right horn, [[pointy ears|pointy ears]], [[red eyes|red eyes]] with [[white pupils|white]] [[slit pupils|slit pupils]], a long purple [[dragon tail|dragon tail]] (which she had a running gag of it being a [[butt plug|butt plug]] [[anal tail|tail]]). She also has quite [[large breasts|large breasts]], with her subsequent outfits making them [[huge breasts|noticeably larger]].

She is fluent in English, and quite eccentric (due to being a half-American). Hosted a morning "news show"-esque 20-minute program on weekdays named "AsaCoco" (Morning Coco), which usually ended up creating absurd memes - such as [[himemori luna|himemori luna]]'s English Corner, where the cute, childish princess constantly spews out obscenities, and most notably the drug "[[asacoco|asacoco]]", a potent stimulant available to be delivered in a wide variety of forms ranging from needles to anal plugs.

Despite her wild antics, insane gags and frequent foul language (which often got her into trouble with YouTube), she is very eager to help her friends if need be and has a mature, big sister-like approach to troublesome situations (though usually laced with some of her personal brand of humor to break the seriousness if it's too much).

She was considered to have the second largest bust in hololive after [[tsukumo sana|tsukumo sana]], even toppling [[shirogane noel|shirogane noel]]'s K-night cups. She was also significantly taller than the rest of the hololive girls (180 cm, compared with [[omega alpha|omega alpha]], who is the second tallest at 175 cm without counting the gigantic Sana), especially the rest of the 4th generation (Kanata, Towa and Watame are all about 150 cm tall, Luna is the shortest at 140 cm, boosted to 150 cm with her shoes and crown).

She was the real-life roommate of [[amane kanata|amane kanata]], and the apartment that they lived in together was called by other visiting hololive members as the "KanaCoco House". This means that they could (and had several times) make appearances on each other's streams.

She is in fact a big [[ryuu ga gotoku (series)|ryuu ga gotoku (series)]] fangirl and has been known to play games of the series. In fact, her name and her title of "Chairwoman" ("会長" - *Kaichou*) are direct references to [[kiryu kazuma|kiryu kazuma]].

Kiryu Coco reached one million YouTube subscribers on February 17, 2021.

She announced her graduation from Hololive on June 8, 2021. Her final act was a live concert on July 1, 2021, which became one of the most viewed live streams in Hololive and VTuber history, reaching over 498,000 concurrent viewers.

Her character design is by [[yaman|yaman]].

A mystical shapeshifter in Japanese folklore whose normal form is that of a [[fox|fox]]. Every 100 years, a kitsune will gain a new [[tail|tail]], up to nine at 800 years. These tails symbolize the amount of knowledge and magical power the kitsune has gained over its long life.

A kitsune with all nine tails would usually be classified as a [[kyuubi|kyuubi]].

The **kodachi** (小太刀; "short sword") is a traditional Japanese sword that is similar in length to a [[wakizashi|wakizashi]], but is intended to be wielded as a primary weapon rather a companion to a [[katana|katana]].  A kodachi typically has a slightly more curved blade and a longer grip (for two-handed use) compared to the wakizashi.  The typical purpose of the kodachi was to allow those not of the [[samurai|samurai]] class (and thus forbidden to carry a katana) to be armed.

Since they are school girls, they use their [[school uniform|school uniform]] as their fashion statement, often wearing their uniform skirts very short and paired with [[loose socks|loose socks]].

**Koihime Musou: Doki Otome Darake no Sangokushi Engi** (lit. *Love Princess†Unmatched ~Throb☆Romance of Three Kingdoms Filled with Girls~*) is a Japanese adult visual novel and strategy game based on the classic Chinese novel [Romance of the Three Kingdoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romance_of_the_Three_Kingdoms.) It was developed by *BaseSon*, and was first released on January 26, 2007, for the PC as two DVD-ROMs, followed by a re-release on April 11, 2008, containing an extra CD-ROM. The gameplay in *Koihime Musou* follows a linear plot line, which offers pre-determined scenarios and courses of interaction, and focuses on the appeal of the female main characters. A [[playstation 2|playstation 2]] version, titled **Koihime Musou** (恋姫†夢想) developed by *Yeti* and published by *Regista* was released on October 30, 2008. A new version of *Koihime* with many new characters **Shin Koihime Musou: Otome Ryouran Sangokushi Engi** (真・恋姫†無双 〜乙女繚乱☆三国志演義〜) was released on December 26, 2008. A third version of *Koihime* **Shin Koihime Musou: Moe Shouden** (真・恋姫†無双～萌将伝～) was released on July 23, 2010.

*Koihime Musou: Doki Otome Darake no Sangokushi Engi* has made several transitions to other media. A manga adaptation by Japanese illustrator [[hizuki yayoi|hizuki yayoi]] was first serialized in the Japanese magazine *Dengeki G's Festival! Comic* on April 26, 2008. An anime adaptation produced by *Doga Kobo* began broadcasting on July 8, 2008, and several seasons have continued.

*Note: All characters are loosely based on characters of the novel Romance of the Three Kingdoms and are grouped in the faction/kingdom they belong to and called by their Japanese names.*

She is currently guarding [[hakurei reimu|hakurei reimu]]'s shrine.

At the sides of her head are either [[komainu ears|komainu ears]] or a set of horns. ZUN says that she has a [[tail|tail]], but it isn't visible in her official art.

She wears a [[cloud print|cloud-printed]] [[red shirt|red]] [[kariyushi shirt|kariyushi shirt]] that has [[buttons|buttons]] and a [[heart|heart]] shape in the middle of it, [[cloud print|cloud-printed]] [[white shorts|white shorts]] with a red trim on the pants legs, and [[geta|geta]].

He originally haunted a [[komainu|komainu]] but left for the city when the shrine was demolished. He is confused and frightened by urban life and modern technology, but loves [[soft serve|soft serve]] [[ice cream|ice cream]].

He carries his belongings on his back in a [[furoshiki|furoshiki]], and in [[youkai watch 2|youkai watch 2]] also carries a [[coin purse|coin purse]]. He can appear as a human by putting a [[leaf on head|leaf on his head]].

He frequently uses the word *mongee* (meaning "amazing"/"extremely"/"wow!", similar to *sugoi*) and ends sentences with *zura*.

d:
**Kono Subarashii Sekai ni Shukufuku wo!** (English: * KonoSuba: God's Blessing on this Wonderful World!* or *KonoSuba* for short) is a 17 volume comedy light novel series written by Akatsuki Natsume (暁なつめ) and illustrated by [[mishima kurone|mishima kurone]] that was published between 2013 to 2020. The series has various spin-off light novels and there are manga adaptations of the main series and spin-offs. A TV anime adaptation was produced by [[studio deen|studio deen]] and aired in 2016 with a second season airing in 2017. A film adaptation of one of the volumes was produced by [[j.c. staff|j.c. staff]] and was released in 2018. A third season produced by Drive (studio) aired in 2024. Several game adaptations have also been released.

The story revolves around [[satou kazuma|satou kazuma]], a teenage boy who is [[isekai|reincanated]] into the [[mmorpg|mmorpg]]-like world, and his adventures with his seemingly powerful yet comically unreliable party members.

*[[granblue fantasy|granblue fantasy]]* character.

An [[erune|erun]] fashion designer that uses a [[quill|quill]] and [[easel|easel]]. Her eyes are [[blue eyes|blue]] and her hair is [[long hair|long]] and light [[grey hair|grey]] with [[blunt bangs|blunt bangs]]. She wears an elaborately patterned, [[showgirl skirt|showgirl skirt]]-like [[asymmetrical clothes|monochromatic]] dress with a feathered collar and [[thighhighs|thighhighs]]. Her outfit is sparsely adorned with gold jewelry with the most prominent piece being a large [[hair ornament|hair ornament]] on the left side of her head.

Sometimes paired up with [[lunalu (granblue fantasy)|Lunalu]] due to the fact that they are both illustrators.

Lesser known for her overall character and personality and more so for being absurdly broken and causing mass hysteria amongst players when she was released. In short, she could only be described as poorly tested out before she was introduced as her skills could last for **hundreds** of turns and casted **nearly every** buff. To make a comparison, the longest buffs in the game may last for only five or so turns. The sheer absurdity of her skills made even beginner players with unsubstantial weapon and summon pools do ludicrous amounts of endgame damage. Stronger veteran players ended up able to beat the hardest raids in the game with ease by themselves in minuscule time with her. Nearly a day after her release she was finally given a harsh nerf followed by a public apology and a distribution of refunds given to those who rolled in the gacha during the period of time between her release and nerf.

*Kote* are Japanese arm & [[shoulder armor|shoulder armor]], a form of armored sleeve usually covering from the forearms all the way to the shoulder.  They are typically made by stitching many small plates into a padded sleeve.

*Kote* that only cover the forearms are called *han kote*, and are also covered by this tag.

*[[kurokote|kurokote]]* are a subtype of *kote*, usually made from black iron plates, which give them their color and name.

**Koutetsujou no Kabaneri** (甲鉄城のカバネリ, lit. *Kabaneri of the Iron Fortress*) is an anime series by Wit Studio. The series is directed by Tetsurou Araki and written by Ichirou Oukouchi, with music by Hiroyuki Sawano and original character designs by Haruhiko Mikimoto. The series premiered on Fuji TV's Noitamina block on April 8, 2016.

A mysterious virus appears during the industrial revolution, infecting humans into Kabane and rapidly spreads. Kabane are aggressive, undead creatures that cannot be defeated unless the glowing heart, which is protected by a layer of iron, is pierced. Unfortunately, most melee weapons and the steam pressure guns used by the Bushi are not very effective against them. On the island country Hinomoto, people have built fortress-like stations to shelter themselves from these creatures. People access the stations and transport wares between them with the help of armored steam locomotives called Hayajiro. One day a Hayajiro hijacked by the Kabane crashes into Aragane station and they overrun the city. A young engineer called Ikoma uses the opportunity to test with success his anti-Kabane weapon, the TsuranukiI Zutsu, but is infected in the process, although he manages to resist the virus and become a Kabaneri, a human-Kabane hybrid. Assisted by Mumei, another Kabaneri who appears to help them, Ikoma and the other survivors of the station board the Hayajiro Kōtetsujō and depart to seek shelter elsewhere, fighting the hordes of Kabane along the way.

[Kunrei-shiki romanization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunrei-shiki_romanization) is the system for romanizing Japanese characters officially promoted by the Japanese government and taught in schools. It's intended to maintain consistency with the way kana are written without being a literal representation of the way the syllables actually sound (e.g., "sa", "si" and "sya" instead of "sa", "shi" and "sha".) For this reason, many English speakers find that it looks strange and prefer to use [Hepburn romanization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hepburn_romanization,) which is also used in the spelling of tags throughout Danbooru.

See also: [[romaji text|romaji text]].

One of the main characters in [[snk|SNK's]] [[the king of fighters|King of Fighters]] video game series, Kusanagi Kyou was first introduced in [[the king of fighters '94|the king of fighters '94]] as the leader of the Japan team. He is the rival of [[yagami iori|yagami iori]] and the boyfriend of [[kushinada yuki|Yuki]].

He was first introduced as a cocky delinquent high school student who is the heir of his clan, Kusanagi, one of the three clans that sealed the legendary snake entity, [[orochi (kof)|Orochi]], 1,800 years ago. His clan wields pyrokinetic powers, an inherited power that few members obtain. They, along with the [[yagami iori|Yasakani]] and [[kagura chizuru|Yata]] clans, keep one of the three sacred treasures used to contain Orochi long ago. His family's treasure is the Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi and his family crest is the sun, represented in a stylized halo of fire. His official nickname is **Scion of the Flame**.

Some fans always remember Kyo as an eternal school boy, just like when [[kagura chizuru|Chizuru]] remembered him as one. This leads to the creation of [[kusanagi (clone)|KUSANAGI]] in [[the king of fighters 2003|KOF 2003]], and the 2 Kyo clones [[kyo-1|kyo-1]] and [[kyo-2|kyo-2]] in [[the king of fighters '99|KOF '99]].

The Major is also an expert in systems hacking, infiltration, [[close quarters combat|close quarters combat]], [[martial arts|martial arts]], and is extremely proficient with many types of ballistic weapons.

Kusazuri (草摺) are the plated armor skirt commonly seen on traditional Japanese samurai armor, attached at the bottom portion of the [[dou|dou]], the chest armor.  They are composed of a grid of small plates (*lamés*) made from laminated leather or iron and riveted together in a fashion similar to *[[sode|sode]]* shoulder guards.

Their role is to protect the waist and upper thighs while still giving flexibility, much like their Western equivalent, [[faulds|faulds]] and tassets.  

A related piece of armor is the [[haidate|haidate]], a set of similarly-constructed thigh guards worn underneath the *kusazuri* but affixed directly to the thighs instead of swinging freely.

The simple cloth equivalents found on kendo *[[bougu|bougu]]* training armor are called *tare*.

A one-shot [[bara|bara]] manga by Yamakawa Jun'ichi, released in 1987. The title translates literally as *Shit Soup Technique*.

Two gay men, the young [[michishita masaki|michishita masaki]] who is sensitive to handsome men, and [[abe takakazu|abe takakazu]], a car mechanic who's sitting on a park bench, engage in [[yaranaika|one of the most iconic encounters in eromanga history]] and end up having [[sex|sex]] in a bathroom stall.

Due to the memorable quotes and reaction faces, the manga later spawned the [[yaranaika|"Yaranaika?"]] [[meme|meme]] in 2002. These memes and resulting interest in the manga itself would spark a boom in [[yaoi|yaoi]] and [[yuri|yuri]] content that continues on to this day. It is often paired with [[manatsu no yo no inmu|manatsu no yo no inmu]] (Inmu-chu) and [[gachimuchi|Gachimuchi Pants Wrestling]] as the "Holy Homo Trinity" (御三ゲイ), since all three were well-known homoerotic memes that were popular within Japanese communities in the 2000s.

For April Fools 2023, an anime "adaptation" of the manga was announced, entitled Shin Yaranaika, to be produced by Anime Tokyo and Studio Leo, and directed by Itou Pierre, as a medium-length all-ages OVA. Later that month, more details on the project were revealed before a crowdfunding campaign was launched to aid in funding the project. The project would meet its crowdfunding goal in late May, and a release date for April Fools 2024 was announced later in October.

Kusuriya no Hitorigoto (English title: The Apothecary Diaries) is a series of light novels by Hyuuga Natsu. It originally started as a web novel in 2011, but its first volume was picked up by Ray Books in 2012 and subsequently published by Hero Bunkoban. There are two manga adaptations; the former (Kusuriya no Hitorigoto) by [[nekokurage (gen'eikai tsuushin)|Nekokurage]] in Big Gangan, and latter (Kusuriya no Hitorigoto: Maomao no Koukyuu Nazotoki Techou) by [[kurata minoji|kurata minoji]] in Sunday Gene-X. A Historical Fantasy, it is set in a Chinese inspired land.

The **Kliment Voroshilov Model Two (KV-2)** [[tank|tank]] was an early [[world war ii|world war ii]] [[soviet|soviet]] heavy tank that shared the same chassis with the earlier [[kv-1|kv-1]] with the exception of a large turret housing the very powerful M10 howitzer. 

It saw limited action in the early stages of the war, one notable event being a lone KV-2 that pinned the lead elements of the German advance for a day.

This heavy tank was feared among the Germans for its very powerful armament combined with a very thick and resistant armor. It was known to be able to destroy even the heavier German tanks with a single salvo from its cannon, and could also withstand several shots from the enemies most powerful guns.

Its main flaws were low mobility and a very high profile due to its unusually tall and heavy turret, designed to house the howitzer. As well as slow reload time.

Due to its unique characteristics, the KV-2 has gained popularity among the tank enthusiastists, especially after its inclusion in various video games, such as [[world of tanks|world of tanks]] and [[war thunder|war thunder]].

It will then become [[white kyurem|white kyurem]] (with Reshiram) or [[black kyurem|black kyurem]] (with Zekrom).

Along with [[reshiram|reshiram]] and [[zekrom|zekrom]], Kyurem is a member of the Tao trio, which exists in the legends of the Unova region.

As both Black Kyurem and White Kyurem, it is the game mascot of Pokémon Black 2 and White 2, respectively. 

Kyurem is a gray and blue, bipedal Pokémon of indefinable but seemingly draconic basis. Kyurem has a blue head and snout and has yellow eyes without pupils, has a pair of pointed light bluish horns on its head and a yellow crest on its skull. Three pointed teeth jut out the bottom of either side of its jaws, which are frozen shut by the ice covering its head. Its long, gray neck has lines running around its whole body, legs, arms and tail. It has two arms, each with its own claw and each arm is jointed together from its oddly shaped blue wings, which are believed to be used for flying and storing cold air. Each wing has two spikes of ice. The ice covering the wings can break, revealing gray tendril-like appendages on Kyurem's back. The right side of its body seems to be damaged in some way, as the wing and horn on its head on that side are shorter; the right side of its head also has a spiked edge near its jaw hinge that is absent from its left. Its legs are somewhat slender, and has three sharp ice-like claws on each enormous foot. Its tail has three blue conical spikes on its tip, and appears to be some sort of propulsion device or a container of energy.

Traditional Japanese [[archery|archery]] is called Kyuudou (弓道). The [[bow (weapon)|bow (weapon)]], called a [[yumi (bow)|yumi (bow)]], is constructed in a very special way such that it can be easily used while riding on a horse. This is done by modifying the design of the bow itself such that the main point of recurve on the bow is below its center.  

The bow itself will be quite long, yet the arrow is still fired in the same manner as the English long bow; its main difference being the lower firing position and the bow usually extend several feet above the archer's head.

Women are frequently seen wearing a breastplate while practicing; this is a [[muneate|muneate]]. Its purpose is to protect the breasts from the snap of the bow string when it is fired.

L85, or "Land Service, 1985", is a standard [[assault rifle|assault rifle]] of the British Armed Forces. Originally named SA80 (standing in for "Small Arms for the 1980s"), it is a [[bullpup|bullpup-style]] assault rifle evolved from an earlier British EM-2 prototype designed to test the viability of intermediate cartridges as well as taking design cues from Armalite's AR-18 rifle. The L85A2 variant remains in service today, as well as other variants such as the shorter-barreled L22A2 and L86 LSW, its light [[machine gun|machine gun]] variant.

The SA80 family was the last weapon to be manufactured by Royal Small Arms Factory in Enfield before its closure. Thus, a significant portion of the guns produced were highly unreliable and flawed in many places. The rifle then had its production switched to other factories, until eventually being upgraded by Heckler and Koch, producing the A2 variant in the year 2000. While its quality did finally improve, the damage was already done; it is considered to be a very unreliable rifle by just about everyone, especially the soldiers that used it in the 1991 Gulf War.

Easily distinguished by its stocky, spartan appearance and oftentimes tan-colored heat shield in front of the gun. Newer models may have Picatinny rails attached in front instead.

A [[monster girl|monster girl]] whose upper body is human and whose lower body is [[snake|snake]]-like. Lamia and naga are often rendered so similarly as to make it merely a matter of style which one a serpent-legged character will be called.

The term [naga](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nāga) comes from Hinduism and Buddhism, and literally means "cobra". Naga can appear with varying degrees of humanity, but typically have fully human torsos. The term [lamia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamia) comes from Greek, though its original usage did not possess snake-like qualities. It was only in the 1600s that [Robert Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Burton_(scholar)) ascribed the familiar qualities, which were subsequently popularized by [John Keats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Keats) in his poem [lamia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamia_(poem),) published in July 1820.

The Japanese, apparently not having either of these myths as a major part of their tradition, tend to ascribe lamia/naga with personalities like those they associate with snakes in general and lamia are often the tsundere types.

The **Lanchester** is a British 9×19mm Parabellum [[submachine gun|submachine gun]] manufactured by the "Sterling Armaments Company":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sterling_Armaments_Company] between 1941 and 1945. It is a copy of the German [[mp28|mp28]]/II. It was primarily used by the [[royal navy|royal navy]] during [[world war ii|world war ii]], and to a lesser extent by the [[royal air force|royal air force]] Regiment (for airfield protection). The [[weapon|weapon]] took its name after "George Herbert Lanchester":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Lanchester], who was charged with producing the weapon at the Sterling Armaments Company.

The Lanchester had a heavy wooden buttstock, a machined-steel action and breech block, a [[magazine (weapon)|magazine]] housing made from brass (later steel) and a mounting on the muzzle for use of a long-bladed 1907 [[bayonet|bayonet]]. The weapon was produced in two versions, Mk.1 and Mk.1*. The Mk.1* has no fire selector (full-auto only) and has simplified iron sights.

In popular culture depiction, the Lanchester is the signature weapon of [[mika (blue archive)|mika (blue archive)]] from [[blue archive|blue archive]].

Use this tag when a character's seemingly larger than normal hand size. More specifically, the hands tend to be as big as their head, or slightly bigger.  This does not take into account [[perspective|perspective]] or [[foreshortening|foreshortening]].
The opposite is [[small hands|small hands]].

Having hands larger than normal is generally considered to be a masculine trait that some find attractive, so much so it has become a trope in the [[yaoi|yaoi]] genre, often called "Yaoi hands".
However, having larger hands can be a character design choice as well, especially as a way to imply that the character isn't completely "human". 
However since this design choice is not very common, the hand sizes for such characters tend to be more variable, especially in fan art.

Not to be confused with [[oversized forearms|oversized forearms]].

> Legend of the Cryptids is a trading card, massively multiplayer online role-playing fantasy game created and published by developer Applibot. The game revolves around the on-going conflict between the humans and Cryptids, and a malevolent Cryptid devouring entity known as the Shadow King, who's goal is the destruction of the world of Neotellus and all of its inhabitants.
> 
> The gameplay revolves around collecting cards based on the game's Cryptid inhabitants, and using them to participate in various Events and Quests, as well as in battles with other players.

**Leon Scott Kennedy** is a rookie cop assigned in Raccoon Police Department (R.P.D.). In 1998, Leon would later meet [[claire redfield|claire redfield]] and arrive together in Raccoon City. Realizing the chaos brought by the outbreak, the two became separated and arrive at the city's police station to seek shelter. The two arrived at the precinct for their own purposes as they find for possible ways to escape the city as the station was also swarmed by the undead.

After the events of Raccoon City, Leon departs and was apprehended by the US military, eventually becoming a STRATCOM agent alongside with a fellow agent, [[jack krauser|jack krauser]].

#### Appearance
Leon is a tall man with [[blonde hair|blonde]] or [[brown hair|brown]] hair in a [[curtained hair|curtained fashion]] and [[blue eyes|blue eyes]]. His appearance varies throughout the series.

- **Resident Evil 2**: Leon wears a [[police uniform|police uniform]] with [[blue shirt|blue shirt]], [[blue pants|blue pants]], [[elbow pads|elbow pads]], [[fingerless gloves|fingerless gloves]], and black boots. In the 1998 version, Leon wears a police uniform containing [[shoulder pads|shoulder pads]] and a [[body armor|body armor]] with the "R.P.D." logo imprinted on it. In the 2019 remake, Leon wears a more modern uniform, now containing numerous [[pouch|pouches]] and a [[knee pads|knee pad]]. The R.P.D.'s  patch is also imprinted on the blue shirt.
- **Resident Evil 4**: Leon has a [[brown jacket|brown jacket]] along with a [[black shirt|black shirt]], [[fingerless gloves|fingerless gloves]], [[black pants|black pants]], and a pair of [[black footwear|black shoes]]. After losing his jacket, a [[holster|holster]] can be seen wrapped around his torso.
- **Resident Evil: The Darkside Chronicles**: During the events of Operation: Javier, Leon wears a similar outfit to the ones he wore in *Resident Evil 4*, albeit he sports a [[green pants|green pants]] with a [[camouflage|camouflage]] pattern and lacks a jacket.
- **Resident Evil 6**: Leon has a much more matured appearance in *Resident Evil 6*, he sports a [[leather jacket|black leather jacket]] along with [[black shirt|black shirt]], [[white pants|white pants]], and black shoes.

One of the four main characters of [[hunter x hunter|hunter x hunter]].

Leorio is initially introduced as a very selfish narcissist who places great emphasis on material wealth. Despite his assertions that he is only after money, he eventually reveals to [[kurapika|kurapika]] that he lost a close friend to a debilitating illness and this inspired him to become a doctor and earn money in order to help the sick and poor. He believes that all things in the world (lives, dreams, etc.) can be bought and that becoming a Hunter will provide him with the necessary funds for his medical education. In the Hunter Exam, Leorio meets [[gon freecss|Gon]], [[killua zoldyck|Killua]] and [[kurapika|kurapika]], the other three main characters of the series.

#### Appearance

Leorio is a tall, manly-looking, fairly [[toned|toned]] young man with small [[brown eyes|brown eyes]], [[black hair|black hair]], and a [[spiked hair|spiked]] crew cut. He typically wears a dark blue [[business suit|business suit]], [[black footwear|black]] [[shoes|shoes]], and teashade [[glasses|glasses]].

Some of the characters such as Killua near at the beginning of the story mistake Leorio for an old man, but he is actually a lot younger than he looks, being a teenager at the start of the series.

In [[kill la kill|kill la kill]], Life Fibers are an organic cells of extraterraestial origin woven into clothing, which enhances its wearer's abilities to a superhuman degree: They can bestow superhuman strength, speed, agility, resistance to injury, awareness and other superpowers.

One class of such clothing is called "Goku Uniforms" and is divided into three categories based on how much Life Fibers they have woven into them; the more Life Fibers a Goku Uniform contains, the more powerful the wearer becomes at the risk of being overwhelmed, killed and/or consumed by the Life Fibers. A One-Star Goku Uniform has 10% Life Fibers, a Two-Star has 20%, a Three-Star has (most likely) 30%, etc. Clothes made entirely made of Life Fibers are called Kamui and are, at least in [[senketsu|senketsu]]'s case, sentient.

An inflatable [[vest|vest]] worn while on the water to prevent drowning. Often bright orange or yellow, but they come in all colors.

Usually worn by [[military|military]] [[pilot|pilot]]s attached to the navy of different countries.

Also known as a life jacket.

A ring-shaped flotation device designed to be thrown to a person in the water to provide buoyancy and to prevent drowning. It differs from an [[innertube|innertube]] because it is often made of solid buoyant material (rather than being air-filled) and is colored to maximize visibility in the water. It also may have a provided line to pull the casualty holding onto it.

Note: The term "life buoy" is most common in British English. In American English these are better known as "life preservers".

An ornamental ring designed to look like a ship's [[lifebuoy|lifebuoy]], a ring with a distinctive red and white striped pattern.  A common ornament for shipgirls, such as [[bremerton (azur lane)|Bremerton]] from [[azur lane|azur lane]] and [[amatsukaze (kancolle)|Amatsukaze]] from [[kantai collection|kantai collection]].

A person who supervises the safety of people at [[beach|beach]]es, [[pool|pool]]s, [[waterpark|waterpark]]s, and the like, rescue those who are [[drowning|drowning]], and tend to those with other emergencies. They are trained in swimming and [[first aid|first aid]] and have aids that help them do their various functions.

Typically distinguished from other beachgoers by their [[red one-piece swimsuit|red]] [[red male swimwear|swimwear]] and/or the [[whistle around neck|whistles]] around their necks.

A [[abyssal ship|abyssal ship]] introduced in the Winter 2015 event as the boss of the 3rd event map.

She is the composite dark fallen form of [[naka (kancolle)|Naka]] and [[agano (kancolle)|Agano]], who were both lost in the Battle of Truk, which the event is based on, and is also the reason she has design elements from both.  The reason for her body being abyssal below the waist is the fact Naka and Destroyer Oite, who tried to save Agano's crew after Agano was torpedoed and sunk, were attacked at Truk and sunk with both being blown in half; all but 20 of Oite's crew were lost and all the surviving Agano crew-members that were saved by Oite were lost as well.

Thus she has been given the nickname "Nakano" (那賀野) by fans.

She is voiced by [[kayano ai|kayano ai]] who also voiced [[katori (kancolle)|katori (kancolle)]]. Katori, like Naka and Agano, was also lost in the Battle of Truk.

A boss-tier special enemy character in [[kantai collection|kantai collection]]. 

Like many [[abyssal ship|abyssal ship]]s, she has [[pale skin|pale skin]], and [[long hair|long]] [[black hair|black hair]]. Unlike most Abyssals, she notably has [[parted bangs|parted bangs]], and an all-black version of the [[dress|dress]], [[boots|boots]] and [[elbow gloves|elbow gloves]] that a *[[sendai (kancolle)|Sendai]]*-class would wear, replete with single-[[cannon|cannon]] [[turret|turrets]], although her left arm is dominated by a large toothy maw bearing [[torpedo|torpedo]] launchers and a glowing orb.  Another salient point is that she wears a bondage-style [[blindfold|blindfold]] over her eyes with two curly [[horns|horns]] sticking out of them.

The character design is an unmistakable reference to [[jintsuu (kancolle)|Jintsuu]], and considering the event, is a reference to the IJN *Jintsuu*'s sinking in the "Battle of Kolombangara":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Kolombangara], where *Jintsuu* remained behind to let the destroyers escape, winding up being completely destroyed (split in half by torpedoes) by the Allied attack force.

Some LMGs are based on the existing service [[assault rifle|(assault) rifle]], such as the [[rpk|rpk]].

***Convallaria*** is a poisonous woodland flowering plant in the family *Asparagaceae*, native to cool temperate climates in North America, Europe, and Asia. Its Japanese name is 鈴蘭 / スズラン (*suzuran*) and its Chinese name is 鈴蘭 / 铃兰 (*Linglan*).

The [[flower|flower]]s come in clusters, dangling from curved, alternating offshoots from a main stem (aka raceme) and are bell-shaped and (usually) [[white flower|white]]. All parts of the plant are poisonous, including its red berries.

Not to be confused with [[snowbell (flower)|snowbell (flower)]]s, as they bear a strong resemblance to lily of the valley. Visual points to note: *Snowbells* have a green or yellow spot on the tip of each petal; each flower-bearing stem (called a pedicel) ends in a "bulb" (receptacle) to which a flower is attached. A good visual example is post #2894988 with snowbells on the left and lilies of the valley on the right. Also, not to be confused with [[bellflower|bellflower]] whose flowers typically have a longer, less rounded bell shape.

Often associated with the characters [[medicine melancholy|medicine melancholy]] and [[suzuran (arknights)|suzuran (arknights)]].

The lion dance is a a form of traditional dance in Chinese culture and other Asian countries in which performers mimic a lion's movements in a lion costume to bring good luck and fortune. It is is usually performed on big occasions such as cultural and religious festivals, important occasions such as business opening events, special celebrations or wedding ceremonies and notably the [[chinese new year|chinese new year]].

The *lion dance* is sometimes mistakenly referred to as [[dragon dance|dragon dance]]. An easy way to tell the difference is that a lion is normally operated by only one or two dancers and has a tail, while a dragon is longer and needs many people holding a stick. See post #5041424 for comparison.
