**Little Witch Academia** is a 2013 animated short produced by *[[trigger (company)|trigger (company)]]* for *Anime Mirai 2013*. The short was created and directed by [[yoshinari you|yoshinari you]] and written by Ootsuka Masahiko and was released in theaters on March 2, 2013. *Trigger* later began streaming the short with English subtitles on YouTube from April 19, 2013.

On July 5, 2013, Trigger announced at [[anime expo|anime expo]] that a new episode, tentatively titled ***Little Witch Academia 2***, would be developed in response to the reception the first episode received. The project will begin production in late 2013 following the airing of [[kill la kill|kill la kill]], with a goal to release it for winter 2014. Whilst initially having the funds for a twenty minute episode, Trigger launched a [[kickstarter|kickstarter]] campaign to extend its runtime by fifteen minutes. The Kickstarter was launched on July 9, 2013 and met its $150,000 goal within five hours. A stretch goal of $500,000 was added to produce a making of documentary and audio commentary for the Bluray release. The Kickstarter raised a total of $625,518. Ootsuka has stated that if the sequel performs well, they may potentially look into producing a television series or full length film. A television series was eventually made for the series in Winter 2017, and was premiered on Netflix.

Note that this tag is only for single strands of hair, these will be usually drawn in a single stroke, either in black, white, or a shade of the color of the hair.  It is **not** for bundles, spikes, wedges, or clumps of hair. It is **not **for [[ahoge|ahoge]], [[antenna hair|antenna hair]], [[cowlick|cowlick]]s, [[sidelocks|sidelocks]], or the like. For those, be sure to include the appropriate tag. If a bit of hair has a distinct border of another color, or a significant width or taper, it is almost certainly not applicable for this tag.

Although they might be drawn similarly, this is also **not** for [[stray pubic hair|stray pubic hair]], or [[body hair|body hair]].

Note that this phenomenon is often very hard or impossible to see in thumbnails, be cautious when gardening this tag.

An aquatic plant belonging to the Nelumbonaceae family of flowering plants. The lotus has prominent blooms (of pink or white hues) rising 8-12 inches above the water, each with a flattened central seed pod structure and fully circular leaves with centrally-attached stems. These features help distinguish it from the [[water lily flower|water lily flower]] (Nymphaea), with which it is often confused.

*Nelumbo nucifera* (also known as the Sacred or Indian Lotus) will probably be the plant of interest to Danbooru image taggers, being a divine symbol in Hinduism and Buddhism. It conveys the virtues of purity and non-attachment; it is associated with beauty, elegance, and grace.

**Love Live!** is notable for being one of the first to link the fictional idol character with the [[real life|real life]] semi-idol group consisted of a newly recruited [[voice actor|voice actress]] specifically for the character (with an exception of some members of the first installment who already have an existing voice acting and music career). With the annual "Love Live Fest!" featuring a concert of the voice actress of each group. This format would later be replicated by its sister franchise [[bang dream!|bang dream!]], which were fully managed by Bushiroad themselves.

The third entry in the [[love live!|love live!]] franchise. Originally announced as a spinoff of the [[love live! school idol festival|love live! school idol festival]] mobile game under the working title *PERFECT Dream Project*, it was later revealed at Tokyo Game Show 2017 to be a brand new idol group who would be the main story focus of the upcoming [[love live! school idol festival all stars|love live! school idol festival all stars]]. It follows the members of the Nijigasaki High School Idol Club, comprised of the three most popular N (Normal)-Rarity idols voted in from *School Idol Festival*, plus new characters introduced in *All Stars*.

Unlike the other Love Live! titles before it, this entry has a large emphasis on solo idols and their individualities, so much so that they forgo joining the Love Live! competition altogether.

An anime adaptation was announced in December 2019 and started airing on October 2020.

Love Live! School Idol Festival is a rhythm game released for iOS and Android, based on the [[love live!|love live!]] franchise. It was published by Bushiroad and KLab and was released on the April 16, 2013 for iOS and June 6, 2013 for Android devices.

An English version was released on May 11, 2014 under the title "School Idol Festival" at version 1.6.

On January 31, 2023, it was announced that the game would be "terminating services":[https://lovelive-sif-global.bushimo.jp/notification] on March 31, 2023.

Following on the success of the game, Bushiroad announced at the 2017 Tokyo Game Show that they would be making a follow-up game, [[love live! school idol festival all stars|love live! school idol festival all stars]], featuring the members of µ's and Aqours along with new members from the Perfect Dream Project interacting in a brand new storyline.

t: love live! school idol festival all stars
d:
A mobile rhythm game by Bushiroad branded as a Rhythm Action RPG, following on the success of *[[love live! school idol festival|love live! school idol festival]]* and released on September 26, 2019 in Japan and February 24-25, 2020 internationally. The game was announced at Tokyo Game Show 2017 and was especially notable for the actresses who play the leaders of title groups µ's and Aqours ([[nitta emi|nitta emi]] and [[inami anju|inami anju]]) sharing a stage for the first time, which foreshadowed the members of µ's and Aqours interacting for the first time as part of the game's storyline.

The main cast includes not only all 18 combined members of µ's and Aqours but also marks the debut of the original nine members of the [[love live! nijigasaki high school idol club|Nijigasaki High School Idol Club]], including three members who had previously appeared as Normal-rarity characters in *LL: SIF* and won a popularity poll. The nine new members' actresses were also announced at TGS 2017. [[mifune shioriko|mifune shioriko]], [[zhong lanzhu|zhong lanzhu]] and [[mia taylor|mia taylor]] also initially appeared in this game as rival characters before joining Nijigasaki.

In a break with the anime premise, *All Stars* has both µ's, Aqours and Nijigasaki in high school at the same time and includes interactions between members of all three groups as part of the story. Other features include fully rendered dances, skill tree development and features to recognize players who had already been playing *LL: SIF* using SIF IDs.

Game service ended on June 30, 2023. It also marks the end of [[kusunoki tomori|kusunoki tomori]]'s role as [[yuki setsuna|yuki setsuna]].

Use this tag for game-original characters, references to events or interactions from the game or for costumes exclusive to the game.

*Lovebrush Chronicles*, known as *For All Time* in its native Chinese, is a mobile otome game by PC and mobile game company NetEase Interactive Entertainment. It received an English localization on October 20th, 2023 for Android and iOS devices. 

The player plays as an art major freshman at St. Shelter Academia and the author behind the popular manga "In Passing", who soon finds out that she has the ability to travel to different dimensions and summon her own arts for combat after being sent to Godheim - the world featured in her manga. In these parallel universes, their inhabitants are incarnations of the people from your world. From then on, you embarks on an endless voyage across time and space to learn the truth and protect what you hold dear alongside or against familiar faces. 

The game combines story-driven visual novel with adventure and RPG elements. Outside of the main storyline, the player can spend time with the love interests with various activities or working to increase your reputation in school.

The **Luger P08** is a German semi-automatic [[handgun|handgun]] that saw use in both [[world war i|world war i]] and [[world war ii|world war ii]]. Other than its iconic appearance, the P08 uses a complex toggle-lock mechanism. It was the very first [[handgun|handgun]] chambered in popular 9×19mm Parabellum [[ammunition|round]]. 

The [[p08 (girls' frontline)|Luger P08]] can also be fitted with a long barrel and a drum magazine. This tag is also applicable to its full auto variant (**Artillery Luger**) that has those features, often fitted with a [[shoulder stock|shoulder stock]]. The handgun became highly-prized war trophies by Allied soldiers.

A character from [[street fighter|street fighter]] series, first debuted as the last DLC characters in [[street fighter v|street fighter v]] and serving as one of the main protagonist in [[street fighter 6|street fighter 6]].

While he was still young, Luke lost his father Robert after the latter sacrifice himself in protecting civilians from terrorist attack. Inspired by his father's deeds, Luke joined the [[united states army|united states army]] under [[guile|guile]]'s supervision. Feeling that military life is not fit for him, Luke resigned from the army and began his career as an PMC contractor and an MMA coach.

A brash, hot-blooded, yet rightous character. Luke was designed to appeal the "new generation" of players by depicting him enjoying various hobby and modern culture, including playing video games. He is also depicted as a rival to the fellow hot-blooded fighter [[jamie siu|jamie siu]] since their childhood.

Luke's initial reception by fans were mixed-to-negative, as he was set up by [[capcom|capcom]] to succeed [[ryu (street fighter)|ryu (street fighter)]] as the new leading cast of the franchise, though his popularity gradually improves, partly due to his English voice actor, Aleks Le, who has done various [[meme|meme]] and shitposting video about him using his Luke character and often interact with the fanbase in various Luke-related tweets.

##### Official bio

A contractor for a PMC, Luke uses his elite military background to teach mixed martial arts. His days off are spent eating junk food, playing PC video games, and fighting, but make no mistake—Luke plays to win.

- **Hates:** Terrorism, horror games
- **Likes:** Travelling, PC games, wacky T-shirts, his late father
- **Height:** 185cm / 6'1 
- **Weight:** 90kg / 198 lbs

[[spread legs|spread legs]] that form an M shape.

The feet should be around [[ass|ass]] level, knees around chest level, and legs spread to the sides such that if you traced them, you would get something close to the letter M. If you can only see one bent leg and the other is not bent, or if you can only see one leg whatsoever, do not use this tag. Basically, you want to be able to see the full M shape.

There is also the matter of perspective, such as post #1118605 or post #350502. Again, if you can see that the leg is clearly bent despite the perspective, then this tag can apply.

Be careful when tagging [[squatting|squatting]] with this tag, since it's actually difficult for someone to make the perfect M shape while trying to balance their waist/buttocks in a low squatting position. The upper legs need to be distinctly raised upward and the lower legs bent in such a way that you can make out the M shape, like in post #3775778.

Do not use for [[leg lock|leg lock]] or [[wariza|wariza]]. **M. Bison**, known as **Vega** in Japan and neutrally referred to as **Dictator** to avoid inter-region confusion, is one of the main villains and primary bosses of the [[street fighter|street fighter]] games.

His first chronological appearance is in [[street fighter zero (series)|Street Fighter Zero 2]], as the head of an elusive criminal and military organization known as Shadaloo. Along with his aspirations for world conquest, M. Bison has been working on perfecting a lethal and deadly energy that will exponentially increase his fighting ability, an inherently evil energy he refers to as "Psycho Power".

Throughout the series, M. Bison occasionally attempts to increase his power by transferring his energy form into an artificially created physical body, thus increasing the limit of Psycho Power he can posses. His attempts were usually thwarted due to either the protagonist's actions destroying his physical body, or that the intended new body rebelled against him. His most famous duplicate body is [[cammy white|cammy white]].

[[rose (street fighter)|rose (street fighter)]] is the other half of his soul, spiritually bound to him and wielding Psycho Power's opposite, Soul Power.

Though he has made numerous enemies, his most persistent and personal of foes include [[chun-li|chun-li]] and [[guile|guile]], both seeking to avenge the death of her father and his friend [[charlie nash|charlie nash]], respectively.

After suffering a supposedly final death in [[street fighter v|street fighter v]], he mysteriously returned in [[street fighter 6|street fighter 6]] in a weakened amnesiac form.

The **M14** is an [[united states|American]]-designed 7.62×51mm NATO **[[battle rifle|battle rifle]]**, developed in 1954 by Earle Harvey and Lloyd Corbett at Springfield Armory, adopted by the U.S. military in 1959. Its design was heavily based on the earlier [[m1 garand|m1 garand]], but uses standard 20-round detachable magazines instead of 8-round internal one and select-fire capability.

It began to be supplanted in 1963 by the [[m16|m16]] [[rifle|rifle]], eventually being fully adopted into the U.S military by 1969. It continues to be used in secondary (marksman) roles due to its firepower, longer range and accuracy.

The [[rifle|rifle]] had initial bad notoriety due to the original design's tendency to jam with dirt or in some weather conditions, but is also regarded effective thanks to its low weight and high accuracy.

An American single-action, semi-automatic [[handgun|handgun]] designed by [[john moses browning|john moses browning]]. Its short-recoil operation with a reciprocating slide highly influenced modern pistol designs.

The [[m1911|m1911]] is visually identifiable by its external hammer, a beaver tail safety, both grip panels being held by two [[screw|screw]]s and a thumb safety. Chambered for the .45 ACP [[cartridge|cartridge]], the standard [[magazine (weapon)|magazine]] capacity is seven rounds. In 1924, the M1911 was largely revised into the **M1911A1**, with a shorter trigger and a longer back spur. It was the standard sidearm of the [[united states|U.S.]] [[military|military]] from 1911 to 1985.

This tag applies to any M1911-styled handgun, regardless of specific model.

The **M1918 Browning Automatic Rifle** (BAR) is an American selective-fire rifle, or technically [[light machine gun|light machine gun]] chambered for .30-06 Springfield cartridge and designed by [[john moses browning|John Browning]] in 1917 for the American Expeditionary Forces in Europe as a replacement for the [[chauchat|chauchat]]. The [[weapon|weapon]] is recognizable by its bottom-folding bipod installed on the muzzle, rectangular one-piece forearm, and a [[flip-up sight|flip-up rear sight]] with a windage knob.

This tag also apply to any foreign-produced variants, such as the Polish **Browning wz. 28** which notably has a pistol grip (post #6539181) or the French **MAS mle 1922**.
In anime the BAR is best known for its usage by [[charlotte e. yeager|charlotte e. yeager]] from [[strike witches|strike witches]].

An American single-shot, muzzle-loading [[40mm grenade|40mm]] [[underbarrel grenade launcher|underbarrel grenade launcher]]. It was designed to replace the [[m79|m79]], which was a stand-alone weapon. The under-barrel design gave soldiers the advantage of having quicker switch of both [[rifle|rifle]] and [[grenade launcher|grenade launcher]], making them more adaptable in combat. The M203 was originally designed designed for the [[m16|m16]] and [[m4 carbine|m4 carbine]] but can be fitted to many other rifles without modification.

The Medium Tank M3 was an American [[tank|tank]] used during [[world war ii|world war ii]]. Design commenced in July 1940, and the first M3s were operational in late 1941. The U.S. Army needed a medium tank armed with a 75 mm gun, and coupled with the United Kingdom's demand for 3,650 medium tanks immediately, the Lee began production by late 1940.

The tank's peculiar design of outfitting the main 75 mm gun in a casemate on the left side of the hull, as well as a fully traversable turret with 37 mm gun, was a compromise meant to produce a tank as soon as possible while the [[m4 sherman|m4 sherman]] is still under development.

The **M4 Carbine** is an American 5.56mm NATO [[assault rifle|assault rifle]] introduced in 1994. It is based on the shorter and lighter version of the [[m16a2|m16a2]]. 
This tag applies to all variants of the rifle, such as the M4 with SOPMOD II set of attachments, Mk 18 CQBR carbine with shorter upper receiver, and many more.

If you are seeing what appears to be M4-like rifle on images that takes place before the mid-1990s (i.e. during Vietnam War), the protruding barrel length is notably shorter in comparison with the forearm, or if the [[gun|gun]] lacks more recent tactical features like Picatinny rails (post #6130843 for example) - then it is the [[colt commando|colt commando]].

The **M4 Sherman** (named for the American Civil War Union General [William Tecumseh Sherman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Tecumseh_Sherman) ) was the primary [[tank|tank]] used by the U.S. during [[world war ii|World War II]]. Tall, fast, versatile, moderately armored, with a sloped glacis and a rounded turret housing a 75mm or 76mm gun, the reliable M4 saw worldwide use in both the Pacific (where it excelled) and the European theaters of the war.

While the tank proved to be quite superior against the light armor used by the [[imperial japanese army|imperial japanese army]] in the Pacific, the much heavier and potent tanks of the German [[wehrmacht|wehrmacht]] became very dangerous foes for the Sherman, which was even nicknamed "The Tin Coffin" or "The Coffin on Tracks" by American crews operating it in the European theater. 

Nevertheless, its superior numbers and the fact that it was very easy to produce (in vast numbers), maintain, repair and modify (European crews eventually added extra armor and more potent anti-tank armament) proved crucial for the American war effort and made the Sherman tank a very successful combat machine design in the end.

More extensive modifications undertaken during the [[cold war|cold war]] - specifically, the fitment of the [[amx-13|amx-13]]'s turret and gun on the M4 chassis by Egypt, and the addition of more powerful engines and a tweaked 105mm F1 gun taken from the [[amx-30|amx-30]] by Israel (the later receiving the designation of M-51 or Super Sherman) gave the old design a new lease of life decades after its retirement, proving the tank's capabilities could be expanded much further beyond its original specifications.

The **MAC-10** is an American compact [[submachine gun|submachine gun]]/machine pistol first manufactured by Military Armament Corporation in 1964. Chambered in either 9×19mm or .45 ACP.  It has a top-mounted charging handle that also acts as a safety when twisted.

The **MAC-11** is the smaller variant, chambered in .380 ACP. Both [[weapon|weapon]]s are recognizable by its [[uzi|Uzi]]-like ergonomics but lacks pistol grip and handguard panels, boxier appearance due to less receiver stamping indentations, short strap that acts like a [[vertical foregrip|vertical foregrip]], and a retractable wire stock. May have a threaded barrel for [[suppressor|suppressor]]s.

Macaws are colorful, long-tailed [[parrot|parrots]] with proportionally large, powerful beaks. There are 19 species in various colors, including combinations of red, green, yellow and blue. 

Most macaw species have white or white-striped-with-black facial patches which are as unique as fingerprints, though some such as the [[hyacinth macaw|hyacinth macaw]] have sparse color highlights instead.

When tagging macaws some confusion may exist between [[red-and-green macaw|red-and-green macaw]] and [[scarlet macaw|scarlet macaw]] as they are both large, red macaws with blue wing tips, the way to tell them apart is that the [[scarlet macaw|scarlet macaw]] has a bright yellow area in the middle of the wings while the [[red-and-green macaw|red-and-green macaw]] as the name suggests has green and blue wing tips.

Visual comparison can be seen here: https://i.pinimg.com/originals/de/b1/05/deb105e83abdfb1d03882e70b9505220.jpg

The **machete** ( /məˈʃɛti/; Spanish pronunciation: [maˈtʃete]) is a large cleaver-like cutting tool. The name is Spanish, meaning "little sledgehammer." The blade is typically 32.5 to 60 centimetres (12.8 to 24 in) long and usually under 3 millimetres (0.12 in) thick. 

In the English language, an equivalent term is matchet, though it is less commonly known.

The member #3 of the *Phantom Troupe*. Machi is one of the coldest members in the Phantom Troupe, almost never losing her cool or displaying any feelings. Machi is fiercely loyal to [[chrollo lucilfer|chrollo lucilfer]], going so far as to challenge two other members of the Troupe for his sake; moreover, she stated that she would hunt [[hisoka morow|hisoka morow]] down if he were to kill Chrollo. She is very confident in her strength, and if threatened, she replies accordingly.

##### Visual Characteristics
Machi is a short young woman with a petite build. She has [[pink hair|pink]], [[messy hair|messy]], [[medium hair|mid-back hair]] that is usually [[tied hair|tied]] into a [[ponytail|ponytail]], and [[blue eyes|blue eyes]]. She is one of the few Phantom Troupe members that prefers to wear traditional [[japanese clothes|japanese-style clothing]]. She looks like a modern day [[ninja|kunoichi]]. Her usual outfit consists of [[bike shorts|bike shorts]] matched with a [[short sleeves|short-sleeved]] uwagi, an [[obi|obi]] worn around her waist and an [[obijime|obijime]] is tied over it, a pair of [[fingerless gloves|fingerless gloves]] with a [[pincushion|pincushion]], [[tabi|tabi]] boots or [[socks|socks]] with [[zouri|zouri]], and [[leg warmers|leg warmers]] that cover from the ankles up to her knees.

In the 1999 anime adaptation, her hair is [[purple hair|dark purple]] and her eyes are [[yellow eyes|gold]].

A [[gun|firearm]] designed for sustained automatic fire. Machine guns are distinguished from [[assault rifle|assault rifle]]s and [[battle rifle|battle rifle]]s by size and ammunition capacity. Machine guns are divided into three categories:
- [[light machine gun|light machine gun]]: Fires intermediate-power [[ammunition|cartridges]] (except earlier and [[world war ii|world war ii]] designs like the [[bren lmg|Bren]]). Light enough to be operated by one personnel. Are either belt-fed or [[magazine (weapon)|magazine]]-fed.
- Medium and general-purpose machine gun: Fire full-power [[rifle cartridge|rifle cartridge]]s and serve in both infantry and emplaced roles. It typically require a crew to operate, due to their bulk.
- [[heavy machine gun|heavy machine gun]]: Fires large-caliber cartridges (at least 12 mm but less than 20 mm), dedicated for anti-materiel role. Because of their weight and large size, HMGs are typically restricted to stationary positions.

***MACROSS*** (マクロス, *MA-KU-RO-SU*) is a long-running and popular series of military [[science fiction|science fiction]] [[mecha|mecha]]/Real Robot anime, created by [[kawamori shouji|kawamori shouji]] of Studio Nue in 1982.

The franchise features a fictional alternate history of Earth and humanity after the year 1999. It is sponsored by [Big West Advertising](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_West_Frontier) .

The franchise is also notable for incorporating "love triangle" drama and musical elements akin to that of an idol anime as a plot device. Typically explained as being a source of inspiration for the protagonists and, in later series, a source of "sonic power" for various mecha within its fictional universe.

***The Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?*** (超時空要塞マクロス 愛・おぼえていますか) is an animated movie based around the first Macross television series that was released in Japanese movie theaters on July 7, 1984.

The movie is a film adaptation of [[choujikuu yousai macross|choujikuu yousai macross]], with new improved animation and designs. The storyline of the movie does not fit directly into the Macross chronology, and was originally an alternate-universe retelling of the story, but was later established as part of the [[macross|macross]] universe. 

Within the Macross continuity it is also a popular movie (ie. a movie within a television series), a fact shown in [[macross 7|macross 7]]. However, other Macross sequels like [[macross frontier|macross frontier]] have used visual elements from both the first T.V. series and this animated film.

In [[real life|real life]] the premier of this anime film adaptation in Japan during the mid [[1980s (style)|80s]] was a great success. It received a huge marketing campaign that generated very long lines of fans; many of them camped outside cinemas the night prior to the movie's first release (something unheard of at the time for an anime related work). These events were dramatized in the anime comedy [[otaku no video|otaku no video]] from 1991.

A [magatama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magatama) is a curved, "comma-shaped" bead or jewel, usually worn on a necklace. Often made of jade, magatama were produced in prehistoric Japan, and are associated with ancient Japanese mythology. (Similar jewels were found in ancient Korea, where they are called "gogok":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gogok].) A famous example is the Yasakani no Magatama, one of the three [[japanese regalia|imperial regalia of Japan]]. Sometimes worn for its religious meaning, sometimes just as a fashion accessory.

Tables especially designed for [[mahjong|mahjong]]. They are typically square with green felt and wooden edges to keep the tiles in. "Automatic mahjong tables":[https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%85%A8%E8%87%AA%E5%8B%95%E9%BA%BB%E9%9B%80%E5%8D%93] have a function to automatically handle tile shuffling and wall building.

A thick, blocky tile used in the game of [[mahjong|mahjong]]. Mahjong tiles are traditionally made of bamboo and bone, although most modern tiles are made of plastic.

A mahjong set usually consists of 144 tiles. They are:
- 108 suited tiles. There are three suits, each numbered 1 to 9 with four tiles each number, thus 36 per suit:
  - Circles
  - Bamboos (1 Bamboo actually has a bird pictured to deter cheating by adding more bamboo lines)
  - Characters (Chinese numerals with 萬, *man*/*wan* written on the lower part)
- 28 honor tiles that are suitless:
  - 16 Wind tiles, four each for North (北), South (南), East (東), and West (西).
  - 12 Dragon tiles, with four tiles for each "color":
    - Red Dragon, symbolized by a red 中
    - Green Dragon, symbolized by a green 發
    - White Dragon, which is blank in Japanese sets (Some other sets have White Dragon tiles with a decorative blue rectangle on each to distinguish them from replacement tiles.)
- 8 optional "flower" tiles, so called because they are often depicted with flowers (many sets have them, but some including Japanese sets don't):
  - 4 tiles representing actual flowers: plum (梅), orchid (蘭), chrysanthemum (菊), and bamboo (竹)
  - 4 tiles representing seasons: spring (春), summer (夏), autumn (秋), and winter (冬)

**Mahou Shoujo Madoka Magica**, also known as **Puella Magi Madoka Magica**, is a multimedia franchise focusing on a world in which young girls can make a contract with [[kyubey|kyubey]] to become [[magical girl|magical girl]]s - in return, becoming duty-bound to fight [[witch (madoka magica)|Witches]]. Known for its surprisingly dark tone.

#### List of works

##### [[mahou shoujo madoka magica (anime)|mahou shoujo madoka magica (anime)]]
The first, and original installment in the series, a winter 2011 anime series animated by [[shaft (company)|shaft (company)]], with character designs by [[aoki ume|aoki ume]] and written by [[urobuchi gen|urobuchi gen]]. 

14-year-old [[kaname madoka|kaname madoka]] was approached by a mysterious creature named [[kyubey|kyubey]], who offers her a pact to become a magical girl who fights Witches, creatures born from darkness responsible for murders and suicides in her home city - all the while learning the deeper, darker secrets behind her mission.

###### [[mahou shoujo madoka magica movie 1 & 2|mahou shoujo madoka magica movie 1 & 2]]
Adaptations of the original 2011 anime, released in October 2012, titled ***Beginnings*** and ***Eternal***. Most notable for Beginnings' theme song, [[luminous (madoka magica)|luminous (madoka magica)]] and certain design changes, such as adding a [[fortissimo|fortissimo]] [[musical note hair ornament|hair ornament]] to [[miki sayaka|miki sayaka]]'s Magical Girl form. 

###### [[mahou shoujo madoka magica manga|mahou shoujo madoka magica manga]]

A manga adaptation of the 2011 anime, released in 2011, illustrated by [[hanokage|hanokage]]. Featured certain changes, such as [[soul gem|soul gem]]s being pink for all characters, and minor plot divergences.

###### [[mahou shoujo madoka magica novel|mahou shoujo madoka magica novel]]

A novel adaptation of the 2011 anime, released in 2011. Written by the member of Nitro+, Ninomae Hajime, and illustrated by [[yuupon|yuupon]].

##### [[mahou shoujo kazumi magica|mahou shoujo kazumi magica]]

Manga series written by Hiramatsu Masaki and illustrated by [[tensugi takashi|tensugi takashi]], serialized in [[manga time kirara|Manga Time Kirara Forward]]; and the first spinoff. Released from 2011 to 2012.

Follows the story of [[kazumi (madoka magica)|kazumi (madoka magica)]], who found herself amnesiac after she was kidnapped.

##### [[mahou shoujo oriko magica|mahou shoujo oriko magica]]

The second spin-off manga of Mahou Shoujo Madoka Magica, created by [[mura kuroe|mura kuroe]] with draft by Magica Quartet, published by Houbunsha. Released in 2011.

Follows the story of [[mikuni oriko|mikuni oriko]], a Magical Girl with the power of foresight.

##### [[mahou shoujo madoka magica mobage|mahou shoujo madoka magica mobage]]

Madoka Magica's first mobile game, released in 2011. It met its end of service in 2012.

It featured new costumes and storylines focusing on the anime's cast, as well as four new characters. 

##### [[mahou shoujo madoka magica portable|mahou shoujo madoka magica portable]]

A 2012 game released for PlayStation Portable.

Notable for first introducing the main cast's ||Witch forms||.

##### [[mahou shoujo madoka magica plus|mahou shoujo madoka magica plus]]

Madoka Magica's second mobile game, released in 2012. It met its end of service in 2015.

It featured a plethora of cards with costumes for the anime's cast, and later down the line, [[momoe nagisa|momoe nagisa]] as well.

##### Manga Time Kirara Magica (pool #19682)

Madoka Magica's own bimonthly manga magazine, which ran from 2012 to 2017 for 30 volumes.

It featured one-shots, multi-chapter series and interviews.

##### [[mahou shoujo madoka magica online|mahou shoujo madoka magica online]]

Madoka Magica's online game, which ran from 2012 to 2015.

##### [[mahou shoujo madoka magica: hangyaku no monogatari|mahou shoujo madoka magica: hangyaku no monogatari]]

Madoka Magica's third movie, and the first continuation of the 2011 anime. Released in 2013.

##### [[mahou shoujo tart magica|mahou shoujo tart magica]]

The series' third major spinoff, released from 2013 to 2017 in Manga Time Kirara Magica.

Set in medieval France, it is focused on the story of a Magical Girl version of [[jeanne d'arc (madoka magica)|jeanne d'arc (madoka magica)]].

##### [[mahou shoujo suzune magica|mahou shoujo suzune magica]]

The series' fourth major spinoff, released from 2013 to 2014 - originally as a standalone release, then in Manga Time Kirara Forward.

Focusing on [[amano suzune|amano suzune]], a Magical Girl who hunts both other Magical Girls and Witches.

##### [[mahou shoujo madoka magica: concept movie|mahou shoujo madoka magica: concept movie]]

First shown during the Madogatari exhibition in 2015, this short "movie" showcased concepts for future installments after Rebellion.

##### [[magia record: mahou shoujo madoka magica gaiden|magia record: mahou shoujo madoka magica gaiden]]

Madoka Magica's mobile gacha game released in 2017, that later got a stage play adaptation in 2018, two manga adaptations in 2018 and 2019, and an anime, which was released from 2019 to 2021.

The game primarily features an original cast, with [[tamaki iroha|tamaki iroha]] as its protagonist, though characters from the 2011 anime and other spin-offs also appear.

##### [[mahou shoujo madoka magica: walpurgis no kaiten|mahou shoujo madoka magica: walpurgis no kaiten]]

Continuation to Rebellion announced in 2021. The movie is set to release in winter 2025.

##### [[null mahou shoujo|null mahou shoujo]]

A spin-off light novel released in the 10th Anniversary Book in 2021.

Focuses on [[kiriha kosane|kiriha kosane]], a 24 year old woman who couldn't have become a Magical Girl, as she lacks both a brain and a soul.

Mai Natsume is the protagonist of the manga [[blazblue remix heart|blazblue remix heart]] and [[blazblue variable heart|blazblue variable heart]], illustrated by [[sumeshi (ambivalince)|sumeshi (ambivalince)]], as well as of two side-stories in [[blazblue: chronophantasma|BlazBlue Chronophantasma Extend]] and appears as a playable character in [[blazblue: central fiction|blazblue: central fiction]]. She's voiced by [[hayami saori|hayami saori]] in Japanese, and [[stephanie sheh|stephanie sheh]] in English.

She was a classmate and friend of [[noel vermillion|noel vermillion]], [[tsubaki yayoi|tsubaki yayoi]], [[makoto nanaya|makoto nanaya]], [[kajun faycott|kajun faycott]] and [[shiori kirihito|shiori kirihito]] during their time at the Military Academy. After leaving the academy Mai worked for [[kokonoe (blazblue)|kokonoe (blazblue)]] at Sector Seven.

Mai is the vessel of the Nameless Grimoire, which allows her to read people's thoughts or memories or obtain information about objects by tasting them. Her true name is Mai Hazuki and she's the heir of the Hazuki Family, one of the twelve noble families that govern the world. Shortly prior to the events of Remix Heart, the Nameless Grimoire inadvertently fused with her body and transformed Mai from a boy into girl. She was not able to reverse the transformation and her father sent her to the Torifune Military Academy under an alias. While Mai initially wanted to return to her previous form, she eventually became female in both body and mind, came to accept her new form and now considers herself to be a woman.

Mai was given a powerful magic spear called [[outseal|outseal]] by Kajun in Variable Heart, that she used ever since as her preferred weapon.

She has [[very long hair|very long]] [[blue hair|blue hair]], [[purple eyes|purple eyes]], and [[huge breasts|huge breasts]].

As Mai's own media almost always portrays her in female form, she only warrants the [[genderswap (mtf)|genderswap (mtf)]] tag for pics that include her male form or otherwise allude to her originally being male. See topic #11614 for details.

A genie-like magical life form created by the evil alien sorcerer Bibidi to conquer the Kais and thus to take over the universe, millions of years before the events of Dragon Ball take place. He was temporarily sealed away and brought to Earth; however, Bibidi was killed and Buu remained hidden. In [[dragon ball z|dragon ball z]], he's revived by Bibidi's son, [[babidi|babidi]] in order to carry on his father's plan to conquer the entire universe.

Buu is known for having various different forms, the most notable ones being:
- [[fat buu|fat buu]]
- [[evil buu|evil buu]]
- [[super buu|super buu]]
- [[kid buu|kid buu]]

**Manatsu no Yo no Inmu** (真夏の夜の淫夢, lit. "A Midsummer Night's Lewd Dream"), or **Inmu** (淫夢) for short, is a series of [[meme|memes]] that spawned from Japanese gay porn videos. The titular video was released in 2001 by Coat Corporation, but the term has expanded to include other works by other companies like Acceed, Samson Video, etc.

The meme originally started around mid-2005, after the Japanese baseball player [[tadano kazuhito|tadano kazuhito]] was involved in a scandal after his past identity as one of the gay porn actors in the original *Inmu* movie was leaked. Leading to his dismissial from the Japanese baseball league and subsequent move to the United States.

It's often paired with [[gachimuchi|Gachimuchi Pants Wrestling]] (Wrestling Series) and [[kuso miso technique|Shit Soup Technique]] ([[yaranaika|yaranaika]]) as the "Holy Homo Trinity" (御三ゲイ) since all three were well-known homoerotic memes that were popular within Japanese communities in the 2000s. However, when [[niconico|niconico]] emerged in the late 2000s, it was considered an arch-enemy of [[gachimuchi|gachimuchi]] and fans would often flame each other's videos. While Gachimuchi would become popular internationally and more recognized after several Gachi MADs were uploaded (and re-uploaded) on [[youtube|youtube]], it would later be supplanted by Inmu on Nico Nico Douga and within the Japanese community after more videos of [[yajuu senpai|yajuu senpai]] were uncovered around the 2010s.

Fans typically refer to an actor in one of the works by an initialism of their name (e.g. Tadano -> TDN, Yajuu Senpai -> YJSNPI, etc.) with either "Aniki" (兄貴, lit. "Big Brother") or "Aneki" (姉貴, lit. "Big Sister") attached to them at the end, corresponding to the actor's gender. This is called "TDN Notation" (TDN表記).

Inmu is often linked with the [[cookie (touhou)|Cookie☆]] series of [[touhou|touhou]] memes, after they latched onto the original video that started the meme (even coining the name it now uses), and the developments thereafter relating to said video.

まんがタイムきらら (Manga Time Kirara) is a Japanese manga magazine published by Houbunsha, and is the first one focusing on moe [[4koma|4koma]] comic strips. Common themes include (but not limited to) slice-of-life and light-hearted [[yuri|yuri]]. The magazine, itself a spin-off of the Manga Time magazine, has spawned some number of sister magazines that are similarly named, including Manga Time Kirara Carat, MAX, Forward, Miracle, and Magica. 

Several of the series have been successful enough to receive anime adaptations. The openings of the anime adaptions are known for featuring the [[kirara jump|kirara jump]].

The magazine also has a cross-over game, [[kirara fantasia|kirara fantasia]], that brings together characters from different series in a fantasy setting.

"Marine Day (海の日, Umi no Hi), also known as 'Ocean Day' or 'Sea Day', is a public holiday in Japan usually celebrated on the third Monday in July. During most of his adventures, he often teams up with his brother [[luigi|luigi]] and their partner [[yoshi|yoshi]] for extra support, as they are the only two characters he fully trusts to help him. Marivel (or Mariabelle in Japan) is a Crimson Noble (in Japan, ノーブルレッド "Noble Red") - a near-immortal vampire - in *[[wild arms 2|wild arms 2]]*. She is friends with [[anastasia valeria|anastasia valeria]], but is otherwise too scared to make friends because she outlives them. Marivel is a technological genius, controlling two robotic familiars named Hob and Nob, using the golem Quebley in battle, and fixing [[kanon (wild arms 2)|Kanon]]'s cybernetics. Marivel can join the party as an optional character; while not needed for the story, her tools help unlock various extras that can't be accessed otherwise, including most of the optional boss battles.

While [[mirabelle graceland|mirabelle graceland]]'s name and Crimson Noble race are the same as Marivel's, they are not the same character. 

Marivel also makes cameo appearances in *[[wild arms 3|wild arms 3]]* (not in person, but as a character in a serialized childrens' story that's found in books throughout the game) and *[[wild arms 5|5]]*.  Humorously, her cameo in *5* is that of a black market dealer who sucks the characters' levels in exchange for rare items, living up to her vampiric origins. Marivel is also well known for being a terrible singer; she's so bad, she attracts monsters.

One of the three main characters, the Marui triplets. Futaba is the middle triplet but often seems to be from a whole different family. Unlike her sisters, she's endlessly cheerful and outgoing, and shows great affection to their [[marui soujirou|father]]. She's a born athlete and dresses the part, going [[barefoot|barefoot]] almost constantly and wearing her hair in a samurai [[topknot|topknot]]. 

Judging by image count, Futaba is the least popular of the triplets for fanart. Ironically, she's an artist herself and apparently has real talent for it -- her art has been known to fool people into thinking it's real. 

(What does she draw? Boobs. On everything. All the triplets are porn fans. Yes, at 12.)

One of the three main characters, the Marui triplets. Hitoha is the youngest, quietest, and most likely to vanish into some dark corner. She's rarely outright mean like Mitsuba, but she has a sort of natural gloomy atmosphere that keeps others at a distance. Generally she's comfortable with that, but not always -- she'd love to share her interest in Gachi Rangers with somebody, and the one friend who *does* try to get close is [[matsuoka sakiko|an occult freak]] who thinks she's possessed.

The Master Sword, also known as the "Blade of Evil's Bane" is [[link|link]]'s iconic weapon in [[the legend of zelda|the legend of zelda]] series. It was forged by the Ancient Sages to vanquish beings of evil who would use the [[triforce|triforce]] to wicked ends, and can only be wielded by those who are pure of heart and strong of body.

The Master Sword is a double-edged longsword with no fuller (central blade groove), and either a purple, gold or blue hilt, depending on the game. The hilt has a noticeably large cross-guard in relation to the pommel, and interestingly, it is somewhat reminiscent to the seal of the royal family. The blade has a large ricasso (unsharpened blade portion near the hilt suitable for a second grip), although Link is never portrayed using it in any of the games. Engraved on the blade is the Triforce, and embedded in the cross-guard is what appears to be a yellow gemstone.

***Masters of the Universe*** (commonly abbreviated ***MOTU*** and sometimes referred to as ***He-Man and the Masters of the Universe*** or just ***He-Man***, after the lead hero) is a [[science fiction|science fiction]] and [[fantasy|fantasy]] American media franchise created by the [Mattel toy company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mattel) in the early 80s.

Although featuring a vast line-up of characters, the main premise revolves around the conflict between the heroic [[he-man|he-man]] and the evil [[skeletor|skeletor]] on [[eternia (planet)|planet Eternia]]. 

Since its initial launch, the franchise has spawned a variety of products, including six lines of [[action figure|action figure]]s, four animated television series, several comic series, and a live action feature film (The [Japanese title](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%83%9E%E3%82%B9%E3%82%BF%E3%83%BC%E3%82%BA/%E8%B6%85%E7%A9%BA%E3%81%AE%E8%A6%87%E8%80%85) is usually only used for the movie).

The first cartoon series was broadcasted from 1983 to 1985. It became extremely popular in several different countries. 

A second animated spin-off series called [[she-ra princess of power|She-Ra: Princess of Power]] was released in 1985. It also became quite popular, but not as much as the first series. It was rebooted in 2018 as [[she-ra and the princesses of power|she-ra and the princesses of power]].

Designer Roger Sweet claims to be the chief creator of He-Man and MOTU, although this is not officially acknowledged by Mattel and is disputed by some other contributors. The earliest storybooks and much of the original backstory were written by Donald F. Glut, while the final production sculpt of the very first 1982 He-Man [[action figure|action figure]] was done by Tony Guerrero.

Okina is a hidden god with a wide range of public faces, those being an Earth mother goddess, a god of noh, a god of stars, a god of silkworm breeding, a god of hindrances, a god of discriminated peoples, et cetera. As one of the Sages of Gensoukyou, she protects Gensoukyou from the Outside World. Her servants are [[teireida mai|teireida mai]] and [[nishida satono|nishida satono]]. She is based on Matarajin, a Buddhist deity. Her abilities let her create doors on the back of anything, hence she is sometimes depicted in fanworks with [[door|door]]s.

She bears a striking resemblance to [[junko (touhou)|junko (touhou)]] from [[legacy of lunatic kingdom|legacy of lunatic kingdom]], and her abilities and position are similar to those of [[yakumo yukari|yakumo yukari]].

Matarajin is sometimes conflated with Hata no Kawakatsu (alluded to in-game via her comments on [[eternity larva|eternity larva]] and her status as a God of Noh), which has led some fanworks to depict Okina as being close to [[toyosatomimi no miko|toyosatomimi no miko]] and [[hata no kokoro|hata no kokoro]].

A character from [[fate/zero|fate/zero]].

He has [[short hair|short]] [[black hair|black hair]] with an [[ahoge|ahoge]], but after being infected with the Matou crest worms, his hair changes to [[white hair|white]]. He wears a blue [[hoodie|hoodie]] and a black [[turtleneck sweater|turtleneck sweater]].

Kariya is the white sheep of the Matou family and the first in many generations to have any real talent for magecraft. However, due to his disgust with his family he severed ties with them ten years prior, earning him the ire of family head [[matou zouken|Zouken Matou]]. Kariya has loved [[tohsaka aoi|Aoi Tohsaka]] since they were childhood friends, so upon seeing [[tohsaka tokiomi|Tokiomi Tohsaka]] apparently abandoning [[matou sakura|one of the girls]] he views almost as his own daughters he vows to protect her. While Kariya has no interest in the Grail, he made a deal with Zouken that should he win the Grail for him, Sakura will be taken from the horrible abuse Zouken intends for her and released back to the Tohsaka family. 

However, despite his noble intentions, Kariya simply lacks the training to participate as an equal and is inflicted with parasitic worms that will boost his abilities in exchange for rapidly degrading his health. Making matters worse, Zouken forces him to summon [[berserker (fate/zero)|a Berserker class Servant]], all previously summoned examples of which have killed their Masters either directly or through the staggering power they consume in battle. Berserker and Kariya cannot interact directly due to Berserker's madness, but Kariya can issue orders, and sometimes glimpses Berserker's thoughts while sleeping, though these only disturb him.

[[fate (series)|fate (series)]] series character and one of the main characters in [[fate/stay night|fate/stay night]].

She has [[purple eyes|purple eyes]], [[long hair|long]] [[purple hair|purple hair]], and a [[red ribbon|red]] [[hair ribbon|hair ribbon]]. At school she wears the standard [[homurabara academy school uniform|homurabara academy school uniform]], while her casual clothes are a [[pink shirt|pink shirt]] and a [[yellow skirt|yellow]] [[long skirt|long skirt]].

In [[fate/zero|fate/zero]], Sakura is [[tohsaka rin|tohsaka rin]]'s sister and the younger daughter of [[tohsaka tokiomi|Tokiomi]] and [[tohsaka aoi|Aoi]]. She was given away to the Matou family because the laws of the mage world prevented Tokiomi from training more than one of his daughters to carry on his family's tradition, and Tokiomi didn't want Sakura's potential to go to waste. However, [[matou zouken|Zouken]] is not really training her as a mage but instead putting her through hell. [[matou kariya|matou kariya]] made a deal with Zouken to win the Holy Grail in exchange for Sakura's freedom to return to the Tohsaka family, which he fails to do at the end of the series.

In [[fate/stay night|fate/stay night]], Sakura is [[emiya shirou|Shirou]]'s timid underclassman and [[matou shinji|Shinji]]'s adopted sister. She has been friends with Shirou since the previous summer when he was injured in an accident and she began visiting him with the excuse of taking care of him while he couldn't care for himself. Despite coming from the Matou family, Shinji claims she has been kept in the dark regarding magic as in a traditional magus household only the successor will be taught any magecraft (even though it's later revealed it's a lie and she's [[medusa (rider) (fate)|Medusa Rider]]'s true master). Though she is respectful of her brother and defends his misconduct, he is in turn an abusive jerk towards her. Further, despite her upbeat attitude with Shirou, she is actually nearly silent and much gloomier when away from the Emiya household or Taiga and has no real friends apart from those two.

In [[heaven's feel|heaven's feel]], Sakura becomes the love interest of the story and secrets about her life and the Matou family are slowly revealed.

***Mazinger Z*** (マジンガーZ *Majingā Zetto*) is a classic and extremely influential and popular giant [[super robot|super robot]] manga that ran in *Weekly Shonen Jump* from 1972 until 1973. The series was created by [[nagai gou|nagai gou]] (Kiyoshi Nagai).

The story tells the adventures of [[kabuto kouji|kabuto kouji]], the young brave pilot of Mazinger Z, a powerful [[mecha|mecha]] with super powers that fights against evil hostile giant [[robot|robot]]s called "mechanical [[monster|beasts]]".

Due to its popularity the original manga was turned into a 92 episode anime that debuted also in late 1972 and ended in 1974. It has spawned several notable sequels and spinoff series, among them [[ufo robo grendizer|ufo robo grendizer]], [[mazinkaiser|mazinkaiser]], and [[robot girls z|robot girls z]].

Mazinger Z was broadcast in several countries and became very famous worldwide. Its fame in some European countries was such that even [a giant statue of the titular robot](http://trip-n-travel.com/listicle/16496/) was erected in the province of Tarragona, [[spain|spain]], in the year 1979. 

It was also a very popular anime in [[mexico|mexico]] during the 1980s, where it was dubbed into [[spanish text|Spanish]] directly from the Japanese version, keeping all the original Japanese character names intact and broadcasting all the complete 92 episodes, unlike the version later aired in the [[united states|U.S.]] (which was called ***Tranzor Z*** and was not very popular due to its severe censorship and many absent episodes).

Mexican director [[guillermo del toro|guillermo del toro]] has cited this show as a very important influence on his movie [[pacific rim|pacific rim]]. The comic [[karmatron y los transformables|karmatron y los transformables]] was also heavily influenced by Mazinger.

This tag should be used for the original manga/anime and related media. For the franchise as a whole use [[mazinger (series)|mazinger (series)]].

A post that doesn't exactly match the post at the source.

A post can be a MD5 mismatch for several possible reasons:

- The file was modified by the uploader, for example, by editing it or resaving it. Uploaders shouldn't modify files.
- The file was [[revision|revised]] by the artist. The revised version may be uploaded as a new post.
- The file is an [[image sample|image sample]]. Ask for the file to be replaced with the full version in topic #16765.
- The file was modified by the source site, for example, by recompressing it to a lower quality. Nothing can be done here.
- The source is not where the file originally came from. The uploader got the file from a different source. The source should be changed to point to the original source.

An MD5 hash is a signature used to tell if two files are the same. Two files with the same MD5 hash are exactly the same. Two files with different MD5 hashes are different files, even if they look the same. They may have differences that can't be seen by the naked eye, such as different image compression or quality levels, or different image metadata.

This tag is added automatically by a bot.

A [[date pun|date pun]] for the Japanese word *niku* (肉) "meat". It can be on the 29th of any month, or on February 9th (2/9), as the digits 2/9 are "ni"/"ku" in Japanese.

Meat is a euphemism for "excess flesh" in Japanese, and eating red meat is likewise depicted as an easy way to get fat quickly, so pictures of [[curvy|curvy]], [[plump|plump]], and [[fat|fat]] girls start appearing on these days in greater numbers, sometimes alongside actual [[meat|meat]].

Alternatively, some artists consider "meat day" as a celebration of characters *with* meat, in other words, [[muscular|muscular]].

**Rockman**, known as **Mega Man** outside of Japan, is a 1987 2D action-platform [[video game|video game]] developed and published by [[capcom|capcom]] for the [[nintendo|nintendo]] [[famicom|famicom]]/Nintendo Entertainment System (NES). 

It was directed by Kitamura Akira, with Matsushima Nobuyuki as lead programmer, and is the first game of the Mega Man franchise and the original video game series. Mega Man was produced by a small team specifically for the home [[game console|game console]] market, a first for Capcom, who previously focused on [[arcade|arcade]] titles.

The game begins the struggle of the [[android|android]] and player-character [[mega man (character)|Mega Man]] against the mad scientist [[dr. wily (mega man)|dr. wily (mega man)]] and the six "Robot Masters" under his control. Mega Man's nonlinear gameplay lets the player choose the order in which to complete its initial six stages. Each culminates in a boss battle against one of the Robot Masters that awards the player-character a unique weapon. Part of the strategy of the game is that the player must carefully choose the order in which to tackle the stages so that they can earn the weapons that will be most useful for future stages.

Critics praised Mega Man for its overall design, though the game was not a commercial success. Mega Man established many of the gameplay, story, and graphical conventions that would define the ensuing sequels, subseries, and spin-offs in the [[mega man (classic)|mega man (classic)]] franchise. 

The first game has since been featured in game compilations, including Mega Man Legacy Collection for Windows, [[playstation 4|playstation 4]], [[xbox one|xbox one]], [[nintendo 3ds|nintendo 3ds]], and [[nintendo switch|nintendo switch]], rereleased on mobile phones, and become a part of console emulation services. It received a full 3D remake titled [[mega man: powered up|mega man: powered up]] in 2006.

**Rocman 2**, known outside of [[japan|japan]] as **Mega Man 2**, is a 2D action [[video game|video game]] developed and published by [[capcom|capcom]] for the [[nintendo|nintendo]] [[famicom|famicom]]/Nintendo  Entertainment System. 

It was released in Japan in 1988 and in North America and PAL regions the following years. Mega Man 2 continues the heroic [[android|android]] [[mega man (character)|Mega Man]]'s battle against the evil [[dr. wily (mega man)|Dr. Wily]] and his rogue [[robot|robot]]s. It introduced graphical and gameplay changes, many of which became series staples.

Although sales for the [[mega man 1|original Mega Man]] were unimpressive, Capcom allowed the team to create a sequel. They worked concurrently on other Capcom projects, using their free time to develop the game, using unused content from the first game. Tateishi Takashi composed the soundtrack, with Sakaguchi Yoshihiro serving as a sound programmer.

**Mega Man 2 is the bestselling Mega Man game of all time**, with more than 1.5 million copies sold. Critics praised its audio, visuals and gameplay as an improvement over the first game. Many publications rank Mega Man 2 as the best game in the series and one of the greatest video games of all time. 

It has been featured in game compilations, including Mega Man Legacy Collection for Windows, [[playstation 4|playstation 4]], [[xbox one|xbox one]], [[nintendo 3ds|nintendo 3ds]], and [[nintendo switch|nintendo switch]], become a part of console emulation services, and appeared on mobile phones.

The series from which [[shin megami tensei|shin megami tensei]] emerged from, otherwise known as Digital Devil Story.

The original series of books consists of Digital Devil Story: Megami Tensei (Goddess Reincarnation), Digital Devil Story 2: Mato no Senshi (Warrior of the Demon City), and Digital Devil Story 3: Tensei no Shuuen (Demise of the Reincarnation). The story of the book series would see high school student [[nakajima akemi|nakajima akemi]] develop a computer program, which would summon demons from another realm. The program would go out of control and unleash a horde lead by Lucifer, whom Akemi has to defeat with the help of [[shirasagi yumiko|shirasagi yumiko]], a transfer student that became interested in him ||and is the titular Megami Tensei. By the end of the third book, Akemi and Yumiko lose against Lucifer.||

The first Digital Devil Story would spawn an OVA adaptation, and two different games - one developed by Telenet for Japanese computers, and the far more famous Atlus game for the original Famicom. The follow-up of the Atlus game, [[megami tensei ii|megami tensei ii]], would diverge from the books substantially and ultimately lead to [[shin megami tensei i|shin megami tensei i]]. References to it can still be found in later Megaten games.

**Megatron** is one of the most well-known villains of the [[transformers|transformers]] franchise. He is the powerful and merciless leader of the antagonist faction, the evil [[decepticon|decepticon]]s.

His original alternate mode is a grey and silver [[walther p38|walther p38]] [[handgun|handgun]] with several attachments. His vehicular mode varies in each depiction, but he usually transforms into a [[military|military]] vehicle. Notably as [[m1 abrams|m1 abrams]] main battle tank in the [[transformers (live action)|live action movie]].

Megatron's first G1 design was created by designer Ohno Kouhjin for the *Diaclone* japanese [[transformation|transformation]] [[robot|robot]] [[toy|toy]] series in the early 80s.

> Motto: *"Peace through tyranny...!!!"*

A traditional women's fashion ensemble from turn-of-the-century Japan. It typically consists of a [[kimono|kimono]] (often with simple decorative patterns), a [[hakama skirt|hakama skirt]] worn over it at the waist, and high [[lace-up boots|laced boots]], sometimes with a [[hair bow|hair bow]].

In the later years of the [[meiji|meiji]] Era, the Japanese government began to encourage the establishment of women's junior high schools. Typical Japanese women's clothing at the time, however, was more showy and elaborate than modest or functional. As a result, this style quickly rose in popularity as a more practical alternative for women attending school. Even in the present day, it is traditional attire for women at some college graduation ceremonies, "as seen here":[https://ganbaregenki.files.wordpress.com/2012/06/hakama2.jpg?w=640].

Despite the name of the tag, this is *not* explicitly worn by schoolgirls, and it is *not* restricted to depictions of the Meiji era (especially since the style remained popular into the Taisho era).

Although this outfit looks quite similar to some types of traditional Japanese [[waitress|waitress]] attire, the two should not be confused with one another (Although [[bashamichi|in some cases]], it may be difficult). As a rule of thumb, if the girl in question is wearing [[tasuki|tasuki]] or has rolled-up/pushed-up sleeves, then these may be indicators of a waitress uniform (as well as less-subtle signs such as [[name tag|name tag]]s, [[menu|menu]]s, serving trays, etc.)

Character from the [[street fighter|street fighter]] series, first appearing in the second DLC season of [[street fighter v|street fighter v]].

She can summon multiple [[crystal ball|orbs]] that can be shot away or retrieved. Her name may be a reference to the [menat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menat,) an artifact linked to the cult of the Egyptian goddess [Hathor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hathor.) Menat travels the globe to convey various premonitions.

Menat is a slim woman with [[dark skin|dark skin]] and [[green eyes|green eyes]]. She has [[short hair|short]] dark [[purple hair|purple hair]] styled into a [[bob cut|bob]] with [[blunt bangs|blunt bangs]] covering her entire forehead. She wears soft [[purple lips|purple lips]] and [[eyeshadow|eyeshadow]]. Her outfits are in Egyptian motif; she wears a dark [[purple leotard|purple]] [[short sleeves|short sleeved]] [[leotard|leotard]] and a purple [[shawl|shawl]] in both of her shoulders wrapping her waist resembling a side belt, a blue and gold [[usekh collar|usekh collar]] and a [[tiara|gold tiara]] on her head. On her legs, she wears a pair of [[purple legwear|purple]] [[toeless legwear|toeless]] [[thighhighs|thighhighs]]. In her second costume, Menat wears a white mummified [[revealing clothes|revealing]] suit, with [[bandages|bandages]] all over her body, a pair of purple, toeless thighhighs and [[fingerless gloves|fingerless]] [[elbow gloves|elbow gloves]].

The male's fur is predominantly dark blue with accentuations of white, while the female's color scheme is reversed. The male's ears are mostly blue with some accents of white, and the tips are pointed straight; the female's ears are entirely white, and the tips are curled. The collar of fur around the male's neck is white and in a pointy style, while the female's collar is blue with a curl rising up to its face. The male's eyes are spring green with darker green pupils, while the female's eyes are yellow with red pupils. The male's tails each have a white stripe just before ending in white, while the tails themselves end in a point; the female's tails are blue at the base and end in white fluffy curls.

**Metal Gear Solid** (メタルギアソリッド, Metaru Gia Soriddo?, commonly abbreviated as **MGS**) also known as **Metal Gear Solid: Tactical Espionage Action** is a stealth action [[video game|video game]] directed by [[kojima hideo|kojima hideo]]. The game was developed by Konami Computer Entertainment Japan and first published by [[konami|konami]] in 1998 for the [[playstation 1|playstation 1]] video game console. 

It is the sequel to Kojima's early MSX2 computer games [[metal gear (series)|metal gear (series)]] and Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake. The game featured cinematic cutscenes rendered using the in-game engine and graphics, as well as voice acting in numerous codec sequences.

Metal Gear Solid follows [[solid snake|solid snake]], a soldier who infiltrates a nuclear weapons facility to neutralize the terrorist threat from FOXHOUND, a renegade special forces unit. Snake must liberate two hostages, the head of DARPA and the president of a major arms manufacturer, confront the terrorists, and stop them from launching a nuclear strike ||using an advanced combat [[mecha|mecha]] known as [[metal gear rex|metal gear rex]]||.

Metal Gear Solid was very well received by critics and sold many units. It is recognized by many experts as one of the best and most important video games of all time, and heralded as the game which made the stealth genre popular. 

The commercial success of the title prompted the release of an expanded version for the PlayStation and PC, titled *Metal Gear Solid: Integral*; and a remake with enhanced graphics, *Metal Gear Solid: The Twin Snakes* was later released for the [[nintendo|nintendo]] [[gamecube|gamecube]]. The game has also spawned numerous sequels, prequels and spin-offs, including several games, a radio drama, comics, and novels.

A direct sequel called [[metal gear solid 2: sons of liberty|Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty]] was released in 2001.

**Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty** is a 2001 stealth action [[video game|video game]] developed by [[konami|konami]] Computer Entertainment Japan and published by Konami. Released on November 13, originally for the [[playstation 2|playstation 2]] it is the fourth [[metal gear (series)|Metal Gear game]] written and directed by [[kojima hideo|kojima hideo]]. It is the seventh overall game in the series and is a direct sequel to the original [[metal gear solid|metal gear solid]], having [[solid snake|solid snake]] as a protagonist. 

An expanded edition, titled **Metal Gear Solid 2: Substance**, was released the following year for [[xbox (original)|xbox (original)]] and Microsoft Windows in addition to the PlayStation 2. A remastered version of the game was later included in the Metal Gear Solid HD Collection for the [[playstation 3|playstation 3]], [[playstation vita|playstation vita]], and [[xbox 360|xbox 360]].

The story revolves around the Big Shell, a massive offshore clean-up facility seized by a group of terrorists who call themselves the titular "Sons of Liberty". They demand an enormous ransom in exchange for the life of the President of the United States and threaten to destroy the facility and create a cataclysmic environmental disaster if their demands are not met. The motives and identities of many of the antagonists and allies change throughout the course of the game, ||as the protagonists discover a world-shaking conspiracy constructed by a powerful organization known as the Patriots.||

Metal Gear Solid 2 received acclaim for its gameplay, graphics, and attention to detail. However, critics were initially divided on the protagonist and the philosophical nature and execution of the game's storyline, which explores themes such as the Information Age, [[meme|meme]]tics, social engineering, political conspiracies, censorship, artificial intelligence, existentialism, postmodernism, virtual reality, and the internal struggle of political liberty and freedom of thought. 

The game was a commercial success, selling seven million copies by 2004. It has since been considered to be **one of the greatest video games of all time**, as well as a leading example of artistic expression in video games. The game is often considered ahead of its time for dealing with [[real life|real life]] themes and concepts, such as post-truth politics, fake news, alternative facts, and echo chambers, that became culturally relevant in the 2010s.

A direct sequel called [[metal gear solid 4: guns of the patriots|metal gear solid 4: guns of the patriots]] was released in 2008.

#### See also

**Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater** (メタルギアソリッド3 スネーク・イーター, Metaru Gia Soriddo Surī Sunēku Ītā?, commonly abbreviated to MGS3) is an award-winning stealth action video game directed by [[kojima hideo|kojima hideo]]. Snake Eater was developed by Konami Computer Entertainment Japan and published by [[konami|konami]] for the [[playstation 2|playstation 2]], and was released on November 17, 2004 in North America; December 16, 2004 in Japan; March 4, 2005 in Europe; and on March 17, 2005 in Australia. 

The game, which serves as a prequel to the entire [[metal gear (series)|metal gear (series)]] series, was followed by two direct sequels titled [[metal gear solid: portable ops|metal gear solid: portable ops]] and [[metal gear solid: peace walker|metal gear solid: peace walker]].

Set in the Cold War era [[soviet|soviet]] Union, the story centers on FOX operative Naked Snake as he attempts to rescue a weapons designer and sabotage an experimental superweapon. While previous games were set in a primarily urban environment, Snake Eater adopts a 60s Soviet jungle setting, with the high tech, near-future trappings of previous Metal Gear Solid games being replaced with the wilderness. While the setting has changed, the game's focus remains on stealth and infiltration, while retaining the series' self-referential, fourth wall-breaking sense of humor. The story of Snake Eater is told through numerous cut scenes and radio conversations.

The **Metroid** (**メトロイド**) games are a series of video games produced by [[nintendo|nintendo]]. One of the company's most successful franchises, the [[science fiction|science fiction]] series spans through several Nintendo systems, with the first game, Metroid, released in 1986 for the Famicon and in 1987 for the [[nes|Nintendo Entertainment System]]. 

The Metroid games chronicle the missions of bounty hunter [[samus aran|samus aran]] in a [[science fiction|science fiction]] setting which contains many similarities to the [[alien (1979)|alien (1979)]] film franchise. Central plot elements are the [[metroid (creature)|metroid (creature)]] organisms and the [[space pirate (metroid)|space pirate (metroid)]]s which try to exploit the Metroids' powers. The gameplay combines adventure based on exploration and item-gathering with platformer and shooter dynamics. The Metroid games are famous for their nonlinear gameplay, where one can complete a game with a fraction of the items available in the game. 

For the titular alien lifeform, use the [[metroid (creature)|metroid (creature)]] tag.

The **MG34** is a 7.92×57mm Mauser [[ammunition belt|belt-fed]] **[[machine gun|machine gun]]** used by Nazi Germany before and during [[world war ii|world war ii]]. Introduced in 1934, it was considered the first [[machine gun|machine gun]]. It features a quick-change barrel, a tubular [[barrel shroud|barrel shroud]] with circular perforation, conical [[muzzle device|muzzle device]] and [[flip-up sight|flip-up iron sights]].
The MG34 was not suitable for quick mass production and costly. So it was supplanted by the [[mg42|mg42]] despite both remained in service.

The **MG42** (*Maschinengewehr 42*) is a German [[world war ii|world war ii]]-era open-bolt [[machine gun|machine gun]], chambered for the 7.92×57mm Mauser round. It supplanted the earlier [[mg34|mg34]] in 1942 due to lower manufacturing cost thanks to dominant stamped metal parts. Its highest cyclic rate of fire at 1200 RPM, made the [[weapon|weapon]] gained the nickname *Hitler's Buzzsaw*.

The [[mg42 (girls' frontline)|mg42 (girls' frontline)]] is recognizable by its [[barrel shroud|barrel shroud]] with squared-off profile and larger perforations. It is [[ammunition belt|belt-fed]] and also accepts [[dual drum magazine|dual drum magazine]]s.

***Mighty No. 9*** is a side-scrolling action game, co-developed by [Keiji Inafune](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keiji_Inafune,) Comcept LLC, and [Inti Creates](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inti_Creates) together with an all-star team of experienced [[mega man (series)|mega man (series)]] developers. It shares the spirit and DNA of the classic Mega Man series, while also introducing new innovative gameplay elements.

The game follows the titular Mighty No. 9, [[beck (mighty no. 9)|Beck]], along with his companion [[call (mighty no. 9)|Call]] as they their battle against the Mighty Numbers after a viral outbreak causes nearly every robot in America to go berserk and turn against mankind.

The project and its multiple stretch goals were successfully funded on Kickstarter from September 1st until October 2nd 2013 with more than $4,000,000 pledged. Its release date was originally planned for April 2015, but was delayed multiple times until it was finally released on June 21, 2016 for home systems. Meanwhile, it has yet to be released for any portable system.

Due to a host of problems behind the scenes and the finished product coming out somewhat underwhelming, it is regarded as one of the worst games of 2016 and has been set as an example of crowdfunded projects gone wrong. With the negative reception towards the game and Inafune, *Mighty No. 9* unfortunately ended up becoming his swan song and his company was bought out by [[level-5|Level-5]]. Despite this, Beck (and later the other Mighty Numbers) would go on to feature prominently in the *Mighty Gunvolt* series of spin-offs, which have been met with much more positive reception.

Tag refers to any image referencing the [[marvel|Marvel Comics]] character Miles Morales, who is one of the many alternative versions of the iconic superhero costume [[spider-man|spider-man]]. 

Most versions of Miles depict him as an African-American teen boy with either a faded buzz cut or dreadlocks. He [[superhero costume|wears]] a [[spider-man (miles morales)|variation]] of the iconic Spider-Man suit with a black base and red outlines instead of red and blue. His origin story and his movie debut ([[spider-man: into the spider-verse|spider-man: into the spider-verse]]) portray him struggling to live up to the original Spider-Man's legacy after his untimely death, as well as the responsibilities and isolation that comes with his great newfound powers.

He was created in the early 2010s, and is notable for being the first (widely recognized) Spider-Man of African and Latino ancestry. While others such as Spider-Punk and Spider-Man 2099 existed, Miles was created during President Barack Obama's second term, and was created in part because of what Obama represented to his supporters as the first black president of the United States. This allowed Marvel to push him into the attention of their most dedicated fans. Marvel was soon able to make him known to general audiences with his appearances in the Insomniac Games' [[spider-man (2018 game)|Spider-Man games]], Into The Spider-Verse, and numerous children's cartoons in the late 2010s.

A **special forces** (derived from *special operations forces*) is an elite [[military|military]] [[soldier|infantry]] unit being tasked for risky or demanding operations by the government or the army. An individual served in the special forces are known as a "military operator", or "operator" for short.

This tag covers images with military operator(s) armed with "tactical" [[gun|firearms]] (which may consist of prototype or advanced [[weapon|weapon]]s, especially those with the various mounted accessories such as [[laser sight|laser sighting system]], [[optical sight|optical sight]]s and/or [[suppressor|suppressor]]s). They are also usually seen equipped with [[tactical clothes|tactical]] loadout that may consist of [[ghillie suit|ghillie suit]]s, [[bulletproof vest|bulletproof vest]]s, [[camouflage|camouflage]]d [[military uniform|military uniform]]s, [[helmet|helmet]]s, [[night vision device|night vision device]]s, [[radio|radio]]s and more. 

Certain SOF groups, such as the US Green Berets, British [[special air service|SAS]], and Soviet/Russian [[spetsnaz|spetsnaz]] (also [[vdv|vdv]]), can be distinguished by coloured [[beret|beret]]s. These are, respectively, green berets, red berets, beige berets and blue [[military hat|berets]].

A term generally used to refer to specific Western [[minecraft|minecraft]] content on platforms such as YouTube and Twitch, especially those surrounding survival multiplayer servers (SMPs) and the communities that develop from them. Some creators stream themselves acting out elaborate LARPs in SMPs, which inspire artists to draw fanart of those creators, as well as those who more generally stream Minecraft. Both art of the streamers and art of the Minecraft servers they stream goes here.

The term is applied more on a cultural level than on a literal level - YouTubers that play Minecraft once often aren't considered to fall into this category as they do not have wider connections to the scene as a whole, which is largely collaborative and overlaps often.

Please note that the [[real life|real life]] copytag should only be used for posts actually depicting content creators in real life and not their personas or in-game characters. Minna-Dietlinde Wilcke (ミーナ・ディートリンデ・ヴィルケ, Mīna Dītorinde Viruke?) is a Witch of the [[501st joint fighter wing|501st joint fighter wing]] attached with the [[karlsland|karlsland]] Air Force. She became renowned as the Ace of Spades (スペードのエース, Supēdo no Ēsu), although some also call her by the pet name of Fürstin (フュルスティン, Fyurusutin). Her familiar is the [[wolf|wolf]]. 

She is skilled at leading operations and squad management and, rather than pursuing her own individual military gains, she focus on the efficient military performance of the squad as a whole. She also has a tendency to look after her subordinates, which causes some to have a motherly impression about her.

Minna's inherent magic is called Three Dimensional Space Understanding Ability (三次元空間把握能力, Sanjigen Kūkan Haaku Nōryoku). Classified in the perception-lineage, it makes possible to perceive and discern all nearby targets in every direction, sorting out their position, number and classification.

Her ace archetype is [Wolf-Dietrich Wilcke](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolf-Dietrich_Wilcke.) Similar to Minna, Wolf-Dietrich bore the nickname "Fürst" amongst his friends and squadmates. 

Due to a scene in the second season she is often drawn with a noteworthy [[ass|ass]].

A central antagonist in the [[tekken|tekken]] series, with the main story revolving around his quest for power and revenge. He was also famous for his incredible resilience.

Years before the first Tekken tournament, Heihachi took over the title of Mishima Zaibatsu CEO from his father [[mishima jinpachi|Jinpachi]] and threw his son [[mishima kazuya|Kazuya]] off a cliff.

He hosted the first Tekken tournament to see if any fighter was worthy enough to beat him. It seemed that no one was able to meet the criteria until his son Kazuya, thought dead, confronted him. In an ironic twist, Kazuya defeated Heihachi and threw him off the same cliff, making him the new CEO of the Mishima Zaibatsu.

In the subsequent releases, Heihachi was often seen being killed by several powerful opponents, only to survive and return in the next game to exact revenge. He was (seemingly) being killed off for good in [[tekken 7|tekken 7]] after being weakened by [[akuma (street fighter)|akuma (street fighter)]]'s [[shun goku satsu|shun goku satsu]] & thrown into lava by Kazuya. However, he would later made his unexpected return in [[tekken 8|tekken 8]].

[[tekken|tekken]] character. Intially introduced as the series' protagonist before turned into secondary antagonist/anti-hero in the later installments.

Years before the first Tekken tournament, Kazuya's father [[mishima heihachi|Heihachi]] took over the title of Mishima Zaibatsu CEO from his father [[mishima jinpachi|Jinpachi]] and tried to toss Kazuya from atop a ravine in an attempt to avoid repeating his father's fate.

Heihachi hosted the first Tekken tournament to see if any fighter is worthy enough to beat him. But it seems that no one is able to meet the criteria until Kazuya, whom he threw atop a ravine years ago, meets him. In an ironic self-fulfilling prophecy, Kazuya eventually defeats Heihachi and tosses him onto the same ravine that Heihachi used to throw Kazuya, making him the new CEO of the Mishima Zaibatsu. He would lose this position to his father once more, with him instead opting to take over G Corporation.

In the subsequent installments, Kazuya began to slowly corrupts into an evil persona as a result of his [[devil (tekken)|demonic]] gene from his [[mishima kazumi (tekken)|late mother]]. As a result, his son [[kazama jin|Jin]] turned against him and challenged Kazuya for the title of CEO of the Mishima Zaibatsu, their battle ultimately culminating with the eighth Tekken tournament.
