Artwork in which more than one medium or material has been employed, such as a combination of [[traditional media|traditional media]] and digital (computer-based) media. 

Images where the use of traditional media isn't apparent to the viewer (e.g. traditional line art existed but was mostly obliterated by digital colors) count as neither traditional media nor mixed media. 

Likewise, if 3D assets are used, it must be apparent that they are 3D assets. If they are traced and colored over by hand, that is not mixed media. (e.g. post #5889413)

This tag can also be used for images with a 2D foreground drawing over a [[3d|3d]] or [[photo background|photo background]].

The main character of the anime and manga series *[[aria (manga)|aria (manga)]]* and its predecessor, *Aqua*, Akari is a gondolier in a small company located in a reconstruction of Venice (Neo-Venezia) on Aqua, a water planet terraformed from Mars. Akari's mentor in Aria Company is [[alicia florence|alicia florence]], and their company mascot is [[aria pokoteng|aria pokoteng]].

Akari has [[green eyes|green eyes]] and [[pink hair|pink hair]]. For the majority of the series she has [[short hair with long locks|short hair and long]] [[sidelocks|sidelocks]] with [[parted bangs|parted bangs]] or [[hair intakes|hair intakes]] (often showing her [[forehead|forehead]]) and adorned with [[hair tubes|hair tubes]] or [[hair ribbon|hair ribbon]]s. [[aged up|Adult]] Akari has [[very long hair|very long hair]] and hair tubes that are lower down than usual, with her sidelocks [[hair over shoulder|resting on her shoulders]] and looping back into a [[ponytail|ponytail]]. This hairstyle is sometimes called a 'momitail' (もみーテール).

Akari is usually depicted wearing her Aria Company *undine* [[aria company uniform|uniform]], which is colored white with blue trim and features a [[bowtie|bowtie]] and a circle-and-arc [[logo|logo]] in front and black company patches with yellow lettering on the left sleeve and [[hat|hat]]. There are summer and winter variations: the summer uniform is topped by a short-sleeved, [[sailor collar|sailor-collared]] shirt, while the winter uniform is characterized by a v-tailed mantle, long sleeves, and [[purple pantyhose|purple pantyhose]].

One of Japan's oldest hairstyles, worn by **men** in the ancient period. It consists of two ponytails, could be long or short, one on either side of the head. These are looped down and back up, each then being secured in place with some sort of wrapping (string, [[hair tie|hair tie]] or [[hair tubes|hair tubes]]... ). Mizura was worn differently according to social status.

Mizura may be confused with [[shuangyaji|shuangyaji]], but this style is for **women** & **girls**, and is often higher up on the head or lower back, being more varying.

**Mobile Suit**, often abbreviated as **MS**, is the official name of all the [[mecha|mecha]] in the [[gundam|gundam]] anime [[science fiction|science fiction]] series. It basically refers to any (mostly) humanoid [[giant|giant]] [[robot|robot]] (stands from about 15 to 20+ meters) that is piloted by a human soldier (aside from [[g gundam|g gundam]], which uses the term **Mobile Fighter**).

As said above, most mobile suits are humanoid-shaped, though there are some which are not, such as the [[bucue|bucue]] and [[lagowe|lagowe]] from [[gundam seed|gundam seed]].

This fictional term was first mentioned and introduced  in the very first episode of the original Gundam series, [[mobile suit gundam|mobile suit gundam]] from 1979.

[[tomino yoshiyuki|tomino yoshiyuki]], creator and writer of the series, explained that the concept of a manned robot was inspired by the [[super robot|super robot]] shows of the [[1970s (style)|70s]] that began with the [[mazinger z|mazinger z]] anime from 1972. 

The name is also a tribute to the [[mobile infantry|mobile infantry]], a fictional military organization of [[space marine|space marine]]s that uses [[power armor|power armor]] in the novel [[starship troopers|starship troopers]] from 1959.

It is also known as *First Gundam* because it became the origin of all [[gundam|gundam]] metaseries.

It is notable because it helped to create the [Real Robot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mecha_anime_and_manga#Real_robot) genre of piloted mecha and has spanned a very successful franchise lasting over 40 years. Because of its popularity many consider it the [[japan|japan]]ese [[star wars|star wars]]. 

Set in the far future, during the year **Universal Century 0079** (79 years after the creation of the first permanent colony in [[space|space]]), it follows the story of [[amuro ray|amuro ray]], the teen pilot of the [[rx-78-2|rx-78-2]] mobile suit mecha during the [[earth federation|earth federation]]-[[zeon|zeon]] conflict known as "The One Year War".

The story of this U.C. series continues in [[zeta gundam|zeta gundam]].

Tomino, the main writer of the original Gundam, has cited the 1959 novel [[starship troopers|starship troopers]] as an important inspiration. He even coined the term "[[mobile suit|mobile suit]]" used to name the piloted mecha from the anime series as a reference to the novel's own "[[mobile infantry|mobile infantry]]". 

Due to copyright issues the series was called **Gungal** in the [[genshiken|genshiken]] anime comedy series.

This tag is for the 1979 TV series and related media only. For the franchise as a whole, use the [[gundam|gundam]] tag.

A type of hairstyle of which both side of the wearer's head is shaven, leaving a long strip of it down the middle of the scalp. Known and seen more when it is standing up due to gelling. Also known as a "Mohican," especially in Japan.

An improvised [[fire|incendiary]] [[bomb|bomb]] made simply by filling a glass [[bottle|bottle]] with fuel or any flammable substance, sealing it with a piece of cloth and then [[burning|lighting]] the cloth on fire when used. The bottle is tossed at the target, which immediately is covered by the [[burning|burning]] fuel after the bottle breaks upon contact.

It has been used in violent [[rioting|riot]]s, by different gangs and various non-state combatants different parts of the world.

Its common name comes from an insulting reference from Finnish soldier (who used the "cocktail" to great effect during the Winter war, and later [[world war ii|world war ii]]) to [[soviet|soviet]] foreign minister [[vyacheslav molotov|vyacheslav molotov]], who was responsible for the partition of [[finland|finland]] during [[joseph stalin|joseph stalin]]'s regime. At one point, Molotov claimed that the bombing campaign during the Winter war was a "humanitarian operation", which spawned a sarcastic remarks among the Finnish population referring to the Soviet bombs as "Molotov's basket". Molotov himself, obviously, highly disliked the name.

Momotarou Densetsu is a series of games by [[hudson|hudson]] directed by Sakuma Akira with art design by Doi Takayuki that started out as an RPG series in 1987. It was popular enough to spawn several spin-offs and an anime that itself received a further anime spin-off.

It's especially notable for the highly successful spin-off [[momotarou dentetsu|momotarou dentetsu]], a railway-based digital board game series that has outlived the success of the main series.

The games feature characters inspired by Japanese folk tales and various mythological sources. Each game also almost always have a voyeuristic [[onsen|onsen]] or [[bath|bath]] scene [hidden in each game](https://namegepo.nomaki.jp/game_momohuro.html) (NSFW) somewhere.

note: not to be confused with [[momotarou|momotarou]], the Japanese legend from which Momotarou Densetsu gets its inspiration.

**Princess Mononoke** (Japanese: もののけ姫, *Mononoke-Hime/Monster Princess/Spirit Princess*) is a 1997 Japanese animated epic historical [[fantasy|fantasy]] film written and directed by [[miyazaki hayao (person)|Miyazaki Hayao]], animated by Studio Ghibli and produced by Suzuki Toshio.

"Mononoke" (物の怪?) actually is not a name, but a general term in the Japanese language for a spirit or monster. 

The film was first released in Japan on July 12, 1997, and in the United States on October 29, 1999.

Princess Mononoke is a period drama set specifically in the late Muromachi period of Japan but with numerous fantastical elements. The story concentrates on the involvement of the outsider [[ashitaka|ashitaka]] in the struggle between the supernatural guardians of a forest and the humans of the Iron Town who consume its resources.

The Moorish idol (Zanclus cornutus) is a marine fish species that resembles [[butterflyfish|butterflyfish]] and [[angelfish|angelfish]]. The Moorish idol differs from butterflyfish in having a black triangular tail fin.

They have distinctively compressed and disk-like bodies, and stand out with contrasting bands of black, white and yellow. The fish have relatively small fins, except for the dorsal fin, whose six or seven spines are dramatically elongated to form a trailing, sickle-shaped crest.

A type of low-powered [[motorcycle|motorcycle]] that uses bicycle pedals to assist the engine with hill-climbing and pedaling away from a stationary position. The term *moped* originates from the Swedish words ***mo**tor* and ***ped**aler*. Some mopeds have a step-through design (post #1132037) while others use a conventional motorcycle frame (post #689998). At the lighter end of the scale, there is some overlap between mopeds and motorized [[bicycle|bicycles]].

Some regional governments classify motor scooters as mopeds based on factors such as engine displacement or speed. As these rules vary between jurisdictions and vehicle performance can not always be ascertained based on artwork, two-wheeled motor vehicles with a step-through design but without pedals should always be tagged [[scooter|scooter]] instead.

A common name for more than 1000 species of [[flower|flower]]ing plants in the *Convolvulaceae* family.

The [[plant|plant]] bears funnel-shaped flowers that close late in the day. They are known for their five symmetrical, finely overlapping petals and bright colors in shades of pink, red, blue, and purple; the center is often white. The flowers often have a distinctive star shape in the center, which is often emphasized by artists. Depending on the species, the leaves can be heart-shaped or ivy-shaped (three-lobed). Morning glory [[vines|vines]] are often trained to climb [[trellis|trellis]]es but will eagerly climb [[fence|fence]]s as well.

As morning glories are easy to grow, Japanese elementary schools often have their students grow them as part of their plant cultivation experience. It is typical summer homework for Japanese students to bring home the morning glories (that they have grown to a certain extent at school) and observe and record their growth (note that summer vacation is in the middle of the school year in Japan).

Its common Japanese name, アサガオ (朝顔 *asa-gao*), literally translates to "morning face". There is a night-blooming species, *Ipomoea alba*, commonly called [[moonflower (flower)|moonflower (flower)]]. Its common Japanese name is ヨルガオ (夜顔 *yoru-gao*), which literally translates to "night face".

Murata Himeko is one of the main characters in the [[honkai (series)|Honkai series]].

Himeko belongs to Saint Freya Houkai Fighting Strategy Unit, while also the Valkyrja Squad Fifth Platoon Commander-in-chief. Her rank is Lieutenant Commander. She is a good [[captain (honkai impact)|captain]] who is fully respected from her subordinates, able to perfectly carry out the strategy, deal calmly under any adverse circumstances.

The following year after her father’s death, she responded to call of the “Valkyrie Project” of the Houkai Fighting Strategy Unit Training Program. With her natural abilities and excellent understanding, she passed through many battles and became the existence called “Ishtar of the battlefield”. In addition with her calm deposit nature, precise judgment, superior leadership, she always emerges victorious in every one of her battles.

Due to not having the resistance against the Houkai energy at birth, Himeko was forced to have her body transplanted with artificial Stigmata developed by Shicksal, in their “Valkyrja” project,  a counter measure to fight against the Houkai. However, as the result of having her body remodeled, plus the side effects from the artificial Stigmata combined with the Houkai Energy taking a toll on her body, it has been declared that she only has one more year to live.

Current age as of Honkai Impact 3rd's start: 27.

A high performance and potent [[car|car]], usually American, sometimes Australian, British or South African. Distinctive characteristics include a large, heavy frame similar to a mid-size family sedan, a huge V8 engine with at least 4 liters (244 CID) of displacement, a gearbox with extremely tight ratios, an interior with enough room for 4 people, and a price that is much lower than an European simile. Due to their poor handling and their fabulous acceleration, they are best suited for straight-line drag racing.

Examples of muscle cars include the AMC Machine, the [[chevrolet chevelle|chevrolet chevelle]], the Ford Torino, and the 2010 [[dodge challenger|dodge challenger]].

Similar in concept is the pony car, which is basically a smaller, lighter muscle car, such as the [[ford mustang|ford mustang]], the 1970 [[dodge challenger|dodge challenger]], or the [[chevrolet camaro|chevrolet camaro]]. While not often considered muscle cars, many Japanese cars in the 70s (such as the [[nissan skyline c110|nissan skyline c110]], [[toyota celica a20|toyota celica a20]], and [[mitsubishi galant gto|mitsubishi galant gto]]) featured styling that made them resemble compact muscle cars.

For the actual muscle tissue under the skin (such as seen in [[anatomy|anatomy]] pictures), please use [[exposed muscle|exposed muscle]]. For unknown pink tissue that doesn’t have the lines seen in muscle tissue, use [[flesh|flesh]].

A Japanese corporation best known as a former [[video game|video game]] developer and publisher. Following a merger with [[bandai|bandai]] in September 2005, the two companies' game production assets were spun off into [[bandai namco|Bandai Namco Games]] on March 31, 2006. Namco was re-established to continue domestic operation of video arcades and amusement parks. Its headquarters are located in Oota, Tokyo. The company's English name is officially often written as **NAMCO** (in all capital letters).

Namco was a front-runner during the Golden age of [[arcade|arcade]] video games. [[pac-man|pac-man]], its arguably most famous title, went on to become the best-selling arcade game in history and an international popular culture icon. They went on to create other hit franchises such as [[splatterhouse|splatterhouse]], [[steel gunner|steel gunner]], [[tekken|tekken]], [[soulcalibur|soulcalibur]], [[ridge racer|ridge racer]], and [[ace combat|ace combat]].

**Nanatsu no Taizai** (七つの大罪, lit. *The Seven Deadly Sins*) is a Japanese manga series written and illustrated by [[suzuki nakaba|suzuki nakaba]]. It has been serialized in [[kodansha|kodansha]]'s Weekly Shounen Magazine since October 2012. The manga features a setting similar to the European Middle Ages, with its titular group of knights representing the seven deadly sins. The series was continued with the next-generation manga *[[mokushiroku no yonkishi|mokushiroku no yonkishi]]*.

Not to be confused with the [[the seven deadly sins|the seven deadly sins]], another series by the same name.

The logo of the [[nasa|United States' National Aeronautics and Space Administration]].  Images should depict one of NASA's three official logos, their insignia, logotype, or official seal.

###### Red, White, and Blue Insignia - 1959-1975 & 1992-present

Commonly known as the "meatball" logo, it depicts the name NASA written in white along with white stars representing space overlaid on a blue circle representing a planet.  A red v-shaped wing represents aeronautics and a white orbital around the name represents space travel.
Example: post #2959451

###### NASA logotype 1975-1992 & 2020-present

Commonly known as the "worm" logo, it is a simple logo only depicting the name NASA in a stylized red font.  It was retired in 1992, but was brought back as a secondary NASA logo in celebration of the return of manned spaceflights being launched from US soil.
Example: post #3336963

###### Official Seal

Sharing most of the same elements as the "meatball" logo the official seal is reserved for formal events.  It depicts a yellow sphere representing a planet with an orbital around it and a red v-shaped wing on it, these are on a blue fading to black background filled with stars and another sphere. The full title National Aeronautics and Space Administration circles the image with USA written on the bottom.

The **"Navy Cross":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navy_Cross]** is the highest award for valor in combat that can be bestowed by the United States Department of the Navy, and so is typically held by members of the U.S. Navy, U.S. Marine Corps, or U.S. Coast Guard (while operating under the Department of the Navy, as for instance during World War II).

Among U.S. military decorations, the Navy Cross follows only the "Medal of Honor":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medal_of_Honor] in precedence, although it has equivalents connected to the country's other armed forces.

A visual novel revolving around [[sayori (neko works)|sayori (neko works)]]'s original [[cat girl|cat girl]] characters. Localized to English by "Sekai Project":[http://www.sekaiproject.com/].

So far, there are five "episodes" in the series:

###### Episode 0

Episode 0, which is counter-intuitively the second novel released, is a short "fandisk" that takes place before the events of episode 1, and gives the player character's sister a much larger role. It's also somewhat of a showcase of new features not present in the first game, which include the ability to directly interact with the cast by clicking on them.

###### Episode 1

Episode 1, the first novel released, centers on the characters [[chocola (nekopara)|chocola (nekopara)]] and [[vanilla (nekopara)|vanilla (nekopara)]], whom the main character lives with, sleeps with and eventually has sex with. While Chocola and Vanilla are the main characters, the novel also includes a supporting cast of four other cat girls and the player character's sister.

###### Episode 2

Episode 2, the third novel released, adds [[coconut (nekopara)|coconut (nekopara)]] and [[azuki (nekopara)|azuki (nekopara)]] to the center character group. The two were formerly members of the supporting cast. 

###### Episode 3

Episode 3, the fourth novel released, focuses on [[cinnamon (nekopara)|cinnamon (nekopara)]] and [[maple (nekopara)|maple (nekopara)]]. As with [[coconut (nekopara)|coconut (nekopara)]] and [[azuki (nekopara)|azuki (nekopara)]] before them, they started as supporting characters.

###### Episode 4

The fifth novel released, Episode 4 focuses on the player character [[minazuki kashou|minazuki kashou]] and his family, exploring his past. It also introduces a new supporting character, [[fraise (nekopara)|fraise (nekopara)]].

An otome game spinoff titled [[nekopara - catboys paradise|nekopara - catboys paradise]] was released in 2021. The spinoff was originally presented simply as an April Fool's joke in 2019, but due to unexpected high demand, it would later be made into a full game.

An image relating to the first day of the new year on the Gregorian calendar.

It's a tradition for many Japanese artists to celebrate the new year by drawing girls clad in expensive [[kimono|kimono]], eating [[zouni soup|zouni soup]], carrying [[hamaya|hamaya]] (a [[shinto|shinto]] ward against evil and bad luck) and playing [[hanetsuki|hanetsuki]]. 

Many artists also pay tribute to the [[chinese zodiac|chinese zodiac]] by incorporating whatever animal corresponds to the year. It should be noted that the Chinese new year is not on January 1 of the Gregorian calendar, but instead varies from one year to the next (falling in either late January or early February). The year of the horse, for example, begins January 31, 2014. Despite this, images utilizing the animal of an upcoming Chinese New Year tend to begin appearing around January 1, as Japan uses the same zodiac but does not use the Chinese Lunar calendar. 

The typical way of telling if an image is celebrating the New Year is by the phrase 謹賀新年 (*kinga shinnen*, literally "happy new year") or by one or both of the more traditional greeting exchanges (shortened as [[akeome|akeome]] and [[kotoyoro|kotoyoro]]). It is also common for New Year images to include [[happy new year|happy new year]] in English text, and/or the number of the year. Text indicating a new year related image may also be absent from the image itself but present in Pixiv tags/artist commentary, website text, etc.

A city of southern New York State on New York Bay at the mouth of the Hudson River and capital of the State of New York. Founded by the Dutch as New Amsterdam, it was renamed by the English in honor of the Duke of York. It is the largest city in the [[united states|united states]] and a major commercial and cultural center. Originally consisting only of Manhattan Island, it was rechartered in 1898 to include the five present-day boroughs of Manhattan, the Bronx, Brooklyn, Queens, and Staten Island.

Site of the [[9/11|9/11]] terrorist attack.

New York is the central location for many of [[marvel|marvel]]'s comic series and superheroes, being home to Avengers Tower in the [[avengers (series)|avengers (series)]] comics and the Baxter Building; the [[fantastic four|Fantastic Four's]] headquarters, as well as being the home city and main setting for [[spider-man|spider-man]] and [[daredevil|daredevil]]'s stories.

During the start of the first episode of Ren she dyes her hair [[black hair|black]] which lacks a ponytail and a hairclip along with wearing a much [[long skirt|longer]] [[skirt|skirt]] in order to keep her identity a secret, but fails at the end of the first episode as she changes back into her old appearance, but during the finale she briefly wears her hair in [[twin braids|twin braids]], round [[glasses|glasses]] and [[white socks|white socks]].

She's a Class Representative (and originally a [[cheerleader|cheerleader]], but later joins the drama club as of Ren) from [[togashi yuuta|togashi yuuta]]'s class who, like him, used to be diagnosed with a chuunibyou in which she labeled herself as "[[mori summer|mori summer]]", but then moved to Icho Private Highschool in order to escape her horribly embarrassing past. She often tends to fight with [[dekomori sanae|dekomori sanae]] because of it in achieving the goal of erasing the traces of her own past as Mori Summer for good.

Shinka is generally described as a gorgeous and friendly girl in the anime, and is popular among her peers due to her good looks. However, she shows her blunt and edgy side when she's alone [[takanashi rikka|Rikka]], [[togashi yuuta|Yuuta]] and others, particularly whenever it comes to dealing with [[dekomori sanae|dekomori sanae]], who doesn't know is the real [[mori summer|mori summer]]. She usually takes her frustration out on her whenever she says "fake Mori Summer" and feeding her milk, which Sanae deems poisonous, but it's later revealed that they actually care for each other and vice-versa. 

Despite her flaws, she's a genuinely kindhearted girl who cares deeply about her friends/clubmates, and doesn't hesitate to help them whenever they need it. In Episode 7, it is revealed that she's enthusiastic when it comes to romance, but in Episode 9 Shinka makes it fairly clear that Rikka and Yuuta must be together, and often tends to help them on their relationship.

Niconico (ニコニコ) is a popular Japanese video sharing site. The site is sometimes still known by its old name, Niconico Douga (ニコニコ動画, *Niconico Video*), and similarly so still believed to require registration to watch any videos onsite, when access has been loosened up over the years.

Niconico has several sister sites:

- Niconico Seiga (ニコニコ静画, *Niconico Imageboard*), an imageboard.
- Niconico Nama Hosou (ニコニコ生放送, *Niconico Live Streaming*), a livestreaming service. Often abbreviated as ニコ生 or ニコなま.
- Nicopedia (ニコニコ大百科), a wiki system. Each article also has a [[2channel|2channel]]-like [[oekaki|oekaki]] board.

A unique feature of Nicovideo is that user comments are displayed as a scrolling feed over the video. See [[danmaku comments|danmaku comments]].

Niconico's mascot character is called [Niconico TV-chan (ニコニコテレビちゃん)](http://dic.nicovideo.jp/id/695104) (tagged here as [[terebi-chan|terebi-chan]]).

This tag is used for posts referencing the site itself, and locations associated with the site (such as the old [[niconico headquarters (harajuku)|Harajuku HQ]]), as well as for various Niconico(-adjacent) characters that have gained some fanart.

**Nijisanji** is a face-tracking app and [[virtual youtuber|virtual youtuber]] group, managed by Anycolor Inc. (formerly named Ichikara Inc.). The company began activities in early 2018, originally as an app developer with no intention of management (legend saying that at one time management had fewer people than their talent, before Mito exploded in popularity and necessitated more staff). The project was helmed by CEO [[tazumi riku|tazumi riku]] and then-COO Iwanaga Taiki, the latter having since departed from the company.

While the app has no release date, and early on wasn't even approved by Apple, it is actively used by *Nijisanji Project*, a group of official [[virtual youtuber|virtual youtuber]]s referred to as "Virtual Livers".

Their characters are notably in 2D, instead of the initially more popular and established trend of 3D. This strategy was to minimize upfront investment and allow themselves a broader range of personalities. While some of the more popular characters do also have 3D models, 2D is still used for most appearances.

Many of the characters have alternate variations, such as [[official alternate costume|alternate costume]]s, [[official alternate hairstyle|hairstyles]], accessories like [[kemonomimi mode|kemonomimi]], or even [[aged up|aged up]] forms. 

The official website offers a short profile for each character; however, the talent is given the freedom to develop their characters as they wish. As a result, few if any actually resemble their original profile.

Saki was the special attack unit captain of Dorami, a bosozoku gang during the 1990s led by [[kirishima reiko (zombie land saga)|kirishima reiko (zombie land saga)]]. Nikka Edvardine Katajainen (ニッカ・エドワーディン・カタヤイネン ?) is a witch of the [[502nd joint fighter wing|502nd joint fighter wing]], originating from [[suomus|suomus]]. She is referred to as "Nipa" by her friends. Her familiar is the Ermine.

Nikka is affiliated with No.24 Squadron, an elite unit of the Suomus Air Force. As [[eila ilmatar juutilainen|eila ilmatar juutilainen]] is also a member of this squadron, the two are fellow squadron members.

Nikka is something of a tomboy, bearing a boyish appearance and often unladylike manner. She was once something of a delinquent, which has since eased somewhat with the influence of her close friends such as Eila and [[hanna wind|hanna wind]]. She possesses a very exacting personality which usually splits any situation into right or wrong. While not stupid, she is relatively guileless and often distracted, making her a popular subject for Eila's pranks.

Nikka is based on the Finnish flying ace Nils Katajainen (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nils_Katajainen ). Like Nikka, Nils had a reputation for frequently crashing his craft, often surviving with only minor injuries. Her nickname, "Nipa," was also Nils' nickname during the war.

[[nintendo|Nintendo's]] seventh game console, released in the Eighth Generation of consoles and the successor to the [[wii u|wii u]]. Known as the NX during development. The first production model went on sale on March 3rd, 2017. 

The Nintendo Switch has two dedicated [[game controller|game controller]]s (one for each hand) called [[joy-con|joy-con]]s. These can be attached to and removed from the console at will, essentially making it a hybrid home/handheld platform.

A smaller version, the [[nintendo switch lite|Switch Lite]], was revealed July 10th, 2019, built strictly for handheld gaming. The Lite has no detachable Joy-Cons; the controllers are hard-built into the console. It also has no HDMI output so cannot be connected to a TV like the original model Switch can. 

The platform has enjoyed a positive reception and high sales numbers in the years since its release. In addition to carrying many popular flagship titles like [[the legend of zelda: breath of the wild|the legend of zelda: breath of the wild]] and [[super mario odyssey|super mario odyssey]], the Switch has also become a welcoming home for many older games from last-gen systems. This led the Switch to be the *de facto* portable way to play popular older titles like [[diablo 3|diablo 3]], [[dark souls i|dark souls i]] and [[castle crashers|castle crashers]] which had previously only been playable on non-portable platforms. As of early 2023, the combined Switch product line is one of the best-selling platforms in Nintendo's entire history, outselling both the [[wii|wii]] and the [[game boy|game boy]] and now second only to the [[nintendo ds|nintendo ds]].

For tagging purposes, if the Switch has its Joy-Cons detached (or is being controlled by other compatible controllers), tag it as a [[game console|game console]] (post #3259420, post #3528468). If the Switch has at least one Joy-Con connected or the console itself is the Lite, tag it as a [[handheld game console|handheld game console]] (post #3471232, post #3470179).

18-year-old [[sora (no game no life)|sora (no game no life)]] and his 11-year-old stepsister [[shiro (no game no life)|shiro (no game no life)]] are a pair of [[neet|shut]][[hikikomori|-ins]] and gamers under the collective account of "『  』" ("Kuuhaku"; lit., a blank space), legendary for winning every game they play, who are also disillusioned with society.

Their lives are changed when they are summoned to Disboard, a world where violence is banned and all disputes are settled with games, by its androgynous deity, [[teto (no game no life)|Teto]]. Deciding to settle in, the pair began representing humans, ranked last among the sixteen sentient races of Disboard, together with its former princess, [[stephanie dora|stephanie dora]], in order to reclaim lost lands as well as their power.

*Japanese theater masks.*

Masks used in *Noh* (能) performances, a classical Japanese form of dance drama. The same masks are also used in Kyōgen performances (the comedic counterpart to *Noh*) and sometimes also in other Japanese performing arts and ceremonies.

Noh masks are traditionally made from carved cypress wood, painted or lacquered. They are frequently affixed by means of a red silk tying cord. Noh mask designs tend to employ heavy emphasis of shadows in order to portray different emotions (which can be changed by angling the mask).

Masks depicting human beings tend to reflect traditional medieval Japanese aesthetics (resembling characters from woodcut prints), having pale 'chubby' faces with well defined brows and cheek lines, plus prominent eyebrows. Masks depicting older humans tend to have extensive wrinkles and beards.

Masks depicting supernatural entities tend to have large eyes and exaggerated expressions. They may also have horns, fangs and other nonhuman features. Gold paint is frequently used to (literally) highlight the otherworldly appearance of such entities.

Noh masks are used to portray different characters when on stage, similar to Western makeup. An actor may, however, rapidly switch between different masks to fulfill different roles.

Nora Valkyrie is a supporting character in [[rwby|rwby]], a 3DCG series produced by Rooster Teeth.

Nora is a member of Team JNPR, and is the "N" in the team's name. She is highly energetic and has a bouncy, cheerful personality. Her design and abilities are inspired by Thor.

#### Abilities

Nora wields [[magnhild|magnhild]], a weapon that can transform between a large two-handed hammer and a revolver-action grenade launcher. Her symbol is a hammer with a lightning bolt through it. Her semblance (special ability) allows her to absorb electrical energy and convert it to a temporary strength boost.

#### Physical characteristics

Nora is short (5' 1") and curvy, and has [[short hair|short]] [[orange hair|orange hair]] and greenish eyes.

||As of volume 8 episode 3, her arms and upper body are covered in [[lichtenberg figure|lichtenberg figure]]-shaped scars.||

#### Attire

Nora usually wears pink and white clothing accented with black and/or blue. In addition to her hammer and lightning symbol, her outfits often incorporate one or more heart-shaped designs. Most of her outfits include a short skirt.

E2 Stage boss of [[kantai collection|kantai collection]]'s Aleutian Islands / Midway Islands Summer 2014 Event. Also known as "Northern Princess", and based off "Dutch Harbor":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Dutch_Harbor].

The youngest by appearance of the [[abyssal ship|Abyssal]] "Princesses", she is often depicted as the child character of said fleet. Due to similar appearances, [[seaport princess|seaport princess]] is often seen as the parent-like figure, and [[airfield princess|airfield princess]] as her elder sister. She is also shown together with [[midway princess|midway princess]] and [[aircraft carrier princess|aircraft carrier princess]], whose first appearances are in the same Summer Event. She is also associated with [[ryuujou (kancolle)|ryuujou (kancolle)]], as the Akutan Zero (see below) originally belonged to her.

The nickname ほっぽちゃん ("Hoppo-chan") comes from the first two kanji of her name (pronounced "Hoppo"). あくたん ("Akutan") comes from the "Akutan Zero":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akutan_Zero], a [[a6m zero|Mitsubishi A6M Zero]] fighter plane which crashed on "Akutan Island":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akutan_Island] but was recovered largely intact by the US following the Dutch Harbor campaign.

Her sudden overwhelming popularity led the developers to turn her into a mainstay for 3-5. Because of this, she also has numerous seasonal CG:

- Christmas 2014 (and onwards): Based on her "yelling" portrait, she wears an "abysallized" santa hat while carrying a present box (with an abyssal mouth, of course). Part of her machinery has turned into a christmas tree and her airplanes have been turned into ornaments.
- Rainy Season 2015 (and onwards): Based on her "running" portrait, she replaces her Zero plane with an abyssalized teruterubouzu and umbrella. She also appears to be looking at her umbrella instead of looking "at the viewer".
- Fall 2015 (and onwards): Based on her yelling portrait, she makes sign that there's no [[saury|saury]] where she is (and indeed, you cannot gather saury from her) instead of yelling.
- New Year 2016: She happily holds some kagami mochi.
- Valentines 2016: She blushingly holds some fine chocolates in a box (with a mouth, of course).
- Sukiya Promotion: She is happily eating a serving of Sukiya's gyuudon while her hungry aircraft pleads for her to share some of her food.
- New Year 2017: She wears a furisode and haori set while her machinery has been replaced by abysallized versions of New Year paraphernalia.

Her catchphrase *kaere!* (カエレ！) is [officially translated](http://www.cospa.com/detail/id/00000065534) as "[[go back!|go back!]]", but a popular alternate translation has it as "Go home!".

A system where numbers are used to spell out Japanese words. It is similar to things like the use of 2 for *to* in English, but more complex.

Numbers may be read as native Japanese (kun'yomi), Sino-Japanese (on'yomi), or as English, and are usually shortened to the first kana. They can also be read as though they had dakuten (゛) or handakuten (゜) added to them if necessary. E.g. the number 8 can be *ya* (short for yattsu), *ha* (short for hachi), *ba* (ha with dakuten) or *pa* (ha with handakuten).

A lay woman who has taken special vows committing her to a religious life, otherwise known as a religious sister. They must adopt a celibate life, refraining from marriage and sexual relationships - a religious sister takes part in a religious institution, while a nun lives a cloistered monastic life. They are recognized by their distinctive set of garments, called a habit. Christian ones can be additionally recognized by the appearance of a [[cross|cross]] or [[crucifix|crucifix]].

The term "nun" is applicable to Catholics – both eastern and western traditions – Orthodox Christians, Anglicans, Lutherans, Jains, [[buddhist nun|Buddhists]], and Taoists. Nuns can vary in appearance not just across each tradition, but within traditions as well; common subtypes of nuns across traditions include military nuns (or battle/combat/warrior nuns).

See [[traditional nun|traditional nun]] for the traditional modest Christian nun outfit, as opposed to the sexualized nun outfits typically seen in anime.

Nunchaku, more commonly known as the "nunchucks", is a traditional East Asian [[weapon|weapon]] that consists of two sticks connected at their ends with a short chain or rope.

While often associated with Chinese and Okinawan martial arts, most long chained and small handle nunchaku were actually created in the Philippines, where they are called **Tabak-Toyok** and are commonly known as **Chako**.  The Chako is often used as a street weapon in brawls.  The smaller size of the Tabak-Toyok allows for easy concealment and everyday carry.  The weapon is best used at long-range.

This small handle type of nunchaku is more often used for quick and multiple strikes than grips or holds (like its Chinese and Japanese counterparts), and was popularized by [[bruce lee|bruce lee]] after he was introduced to them by his Flilipino fellow martial artist and friend, Dan Inosanto.

Not to be confused with [[three section staff|three section staff]].

When a character is wearing the attire of a nurse. A nurse is a health care professional who regularly assists [[doctor|doctors]] and other health care professionals in the [[syringe|treatment]], safety, and recovery of [[sick|ill]] and [[injury|injured people]]. Nursing is largely a female profession, but men can be nurses as well.

While most modern nurses wear [[medical scrubs|medical scrubs]] at their workplaces, the attire this tag most often applies to is the [[white dress|white dress]] and [[nurse cap|nurse cap]] combination that was popular during the 20th century. Obidome (帯留め, おびどめ) are small brooches worn threaded onto the obijime, making a charming decoration on the front of the obi. Can be made of wood, ceramic, resin, mother-of-pearl, or precious metals. Often in designs such as flowers, small objects, or animals.
The back surface will almost always be flat with two closely-spaced raised rectangular holes, used for sliding the obidome over the thin flat obijime cord.

When an obijime is made specifically to be worn with obidome, it will be thinner and flatter than average, and known as sanbu-himo.

These are generally the only jewelry that is acceptable to wear with kimono (other than a wedding band or tasteful watch). Typically an informal item, even when made with precious gems and are only acceptable with more casual or funky outfits. 

However, Maiko will wear a very large and elaborate form of obidome known as pocchiri with their hikizuri. These are often made of incredibly fine materials such as gold and diamonds or emeralds, as well as very detailed enamel workmanship. They are also much larger than normal obidome.

**Obijime** (帯締め, おびじめ) is a small decorative string tied around the [[obi|obi]], used only in women's [[kimono|kimono]].

It's about 150 cm (4.9 ft) long and is tied around the obi and through the knot, and which doubles as decoration. It can be a woven [[string|string]], or be constructed as a narrow sewn tube of fabric. There are both flat and round obijime. They often have [[tassel|tassels]] at both ends and are made from [[silk|silk]], [[satin|satin]], brocade or viscose. This tag is to be used when well-developed oblique muscles are noticeable, i.e. you should not use this tag to describe [[hip lines|hip lines]] or [[hip bones|hip bones]]. The external oblique muscle is one of the outermost abdominal muscles, extending from the lower half of the ribs around and down to the pelvis ending where the [[groin|groin]] begins. Common names to describe developed obliques are "fish gills" (upper) and the Adonis or Apollo's Belt (lower). While it is possible for females to develop this muscle, it is more visible and far more common in males due to the differences in bone structure and distribution of body fat.

A traditional Japanese courtesan in Edo (present-day Tokyo), the *Yoshiwara*. They were a much higher-class subtype of [[yuujo|yuujo]], the iconic feudal-era Japanese [[prostitution|prostitutes]]. 

Unlike [[yuujo|yuujo]], oiran were more educated and cultured, and had talents beyond those used in the bedroom. This gave them a social standing which put them well above any common prostitute, even outside the red-light districts. The companionship of an oiran did not come cheaply, so their clientele were primarily men of high political or social ranking. 

Oiran should not be confused with [[geisha|geisha]], who tend to dress far less luxuriously and who do not provide any sexual services. After World War II, the geisha eventually ended up replacing the role of "classic, respectable female entertainer" that oiran had filled in Japanese society.

A [[card game|card game]] for two or more players.

An extra card, usually a [[joker (playing card)|joker (playing card)]] or "old maid" card, is inserted into a regular deck of [[playing card|playing card]]s. The cards are then dealt to the players who then take turns selecting a card from another player's hand. If a pair is formed, it is discarded. This continues until one player is left holding the "old maid". This is the variation often seen in Japan; the original rules call for removal of three queens, while other rule sets dictate the removal of either one queen, three jacks, one jack, three cards of the same value, or any card whatsoever.

The popular name used for [[amulet|amulets]] sold in [[shinto|shinto]] [[shrine|shrines]] and Buddhist [[temples|temples]] in Japan. It is said that these amulets have the ability to grant special wishes such as "being successful in a college entrance examination" or "for certain love to come true." 

Although omamoris come in a variety of shapes, their most popular form is a little bag called an お守り袋 (*omamori bukuro*, omamori pouch) which is a flat pouch with sharp angles, made of vibrant colors containing items that attract good luck. The shape of this pouch was invented by a [*Nishijin* textile](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nishijin) manufacturer after [[world war ii|world war ii]]. (This company, [Akie Charms Co.,](http://www.akie-net.com/) is still nowadays the largest company in the omamori pouch manufacturing industry.) Nevertheless, omamoris of this type tend to appear frequently in works of fiction set in the Edo period, such as the [*jidaigeki*.](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jidaigeki)

Random fortunes written on strips of paper at [[shinto|shinto]] [[shrine|shrines]] in Japan.

The short messages that may be found on them follow below, ordered tentatively from worst to best:

- 大凶 (dai-kyou), Great Curse
- 末凶 (sue-kyou), Future Curse
- 半凶 (han-kyou), Half-Curse
- 小凶 (shou-kyou), Small Curse
- 凶 (kyou), Curse
- 末小吉 (sue-shou-kichi), Future small Blessing
- 末吉 (sue-kichi), Future Blessing
- 半吉 (han-kichi), Half-Blessing
- 吉 (kichi), Blessing
- 小吉 (shou-kichi), Small Blessing
- 中吉 (chuu-kichi), Middle Blessing
- 大吉 (dai-kichi), Great Blessing

The temples and shrines across Japan do not have a unified system for their omikuji. Some places do not offer the full range of fortunes, and a few offer an additional fortune rank:
- 平 (hira), Neutral

How the unmodified "Blessing" ranks compare to Small and Middle blessings also varies.

Tying these strips of paper to trees or wires is a common custom, especially when receiving a negative fortune.

A Western-inspired Japanese dish that features [[rice|rice]] cooked into an [[omelet|omelet]], forming a pouch, and usually topped with [[ketchup|ketchup]]. The ketchup is often poured to spell out words (such as the intended eater's name).

Typically, the rice is "chicken rice" [[fried rice|fried]] in a pan with chicken and ketchup, but the ingredients can vary. Other variations include *omusoba* substituting [[yakisoba|yakisoba]] for the rice and *omutako* in Okinawa consisting of an omelet over taco rice.

Stories about the origin of omurice vary, but two such stories attribute its origin to Western-style restaurants. The first says it originated around the turn of the 20th century at Renga-tei in Ginza, Tokyo after the restaurant got the idea for it from chakin [[sushi|sushi]], which features sushi rice wrapped in a thin omelet. The second says it originated in 1925 at Hokkyokusei in Minami, Osaka when a cook decided to enliven a regular customer's order of an omelet with rice.

The Onbashira are sacred logs that are used, after being cut using special ceremonial tools, in renewal of the Suwa Grand Shrine that occurs every six years, the ceremony which has gone uninterrupted for 1200 years. There are used in two festivals, Yamadashi and Satobiki. Yamadashi uses large trees that are covered in red and white regalia and covered in ropes. Part of this includes the ceremony on "Ki-Otoshi" which involves young men riding onbashira down steep slopes to prove their manhood.

Satobiki involves the ceremonial placement of onbashira in the foundations of the Suwa Grand Shrine, with a ceremonial group of log bearers that ride the log as its being raised and sing from the top of the log to signify that it has been raised.

The **Late Night Serious 60-Minute Drawing Game** (深夜の真剣お絵描き60分一本勝負, Shin'ya no Shinken Oekaki 60-bu Ipponshōbu), or **1draw** (ワンドロ, Wandoro), is a self-explanatory Twitter hashtag where artists are given a prompt and have an hour to exercise their skills.

The prompt is usually composed of three characters from a set copyright. Each copyright gets their own tag.

The challenge was originally started on May 13, 2013, by twitter user [[monyomoke|monyomoke]], establishing a prompt where participants were to draw [[touhou|touhou]] characters [[komeiji koishi|Koishi]], [[nazrin|nazrin]], and/or [[ibaraki kasen|Kasen]]. After a couple months, however, the organizer decided to quit, since he was tired. The role of organizer has since been passed over a couple of times.

The Touhou prompt is currently being hosted by "@1draw_night":[https://twitter.com/1draw_night]. They also have "a website":[http://1draw.aqn.jp] which hosts the artworks posted at the hashtag, with the artists' permission.

Other accounts dealing with different copyrights have been appearing. Some tags may be defunct.

A creature from Japanese folklore. Usually translated as "demon" or "[[ogre|ogre]]".

Traditionally depicted with [[red skin|red]] or [[blue skin|blue skin]], a [[tiger print|tiger print]] [[loincloth|loincloth]], and [[horns|horns]]. Oni horns can be depicted in various ways, whether it be as long, smooth, [[skin-covered horns|skin-covered]] or otherwise the same color as the skin, located on the forehead; or [[cone horns|cone-shaped]] in any number of colors, whether it be white, grey, yellow, etc. atop their head. Their weapon of choice is the [[spiked club|spiked club]], particularly the [[kanabou|kanabou]]. They are violent and favor brawn over brains.

Save for the horns, modern depictions tend to mute these characteristics considerably or entirely, especially in female characters, only keeping their iconic dual horns intact.

Oni are commonly associated with [[setsubun|setsubun]], a holiday taking place on February 3rd, the last day of winter in the traditional Japanese calendar. On this day it is tradition to throw roasted soybeans in order to drive away oni; this practice is known as [[mamemaki|mamemaki]].

Typical examples of oni are [[lum|lum]], [[gedomaru|gedomaru]], [[ibuki suika|ibuki suika]] and [[hoshiguma yuugi|hoshiguma yuugi]].

The "Sanzu Ferryman", penultimate boss of [[touhou|touhou]]'s [[phantasmagoria of flower view|phantasmagoria of flower view]] and later a recurring playable character.

A shinigami with the ability to manipulate distance. She ferries the souls of the dead across the Sanzu River to be judged by her boss, [[shiki eiki|shiki eiki]]. However, she is also notorious for being a carefree slacker who works at her own pace, much to the irritation of her employer, who sometimes beats her up with the [[rod of remorse|rod of remorse]]. Mostly depicted with a rather [[large breasts|large bust]], which sometimes angers her superior, who is usually depicted with a [[flat chest|flat chest]].

Because of her connection with the Sanzu River, she may appear along with [[spider lily|spider lilies]].

A *[[touken ranbu|touken ranbu]]* character. He is based on the sword of the same name that belonged to the Date clan. The sword initially belonged to the second shogun Hidetada before being bestowed to Date Tadamune. It is the work of the swordsmith Soushuu, though the sword itself does not carry his signature.

His name comes from the Kurikara dragon depicted on the sword, a common representation of the deity Fudou Myou'ou. The dragon appears as a [[tattoo|tattoo]] on Ookurikara's right arm in human form. He also wears a [[necklace|necklace]] with the Sanskrit character "Kan" (खनति), which is said to represent Fudou.

Ookurikara is curt to the Saniwa, and often acts aloof to the rest of the Citadel. He often makes comments about how he does not plan to get along with his master or the other swords. Fans have depicted a much gentler, nicer side to him in spite of his standoffish exterior; this variation is called "Kara-chan", similar to *[[kantai collection|kantai collection]]*'s "Nuinui" variation of [[shiranui (kancolle)|Shiranui]].

He is a [[dark-skinned male|dark skinned man]] with [[brown hair|brown hair]] and [[yellow eyes|yellow eyes]]. He wears a black [[jacket|jacket]] with a white [[t-shirt|t-shirt]].

Voiced by [[furukawa makoto|furukawa makoto]]. Designed by [[komo (sleepy)|komo (sleepy)]].

A type of Japanese [[sword|sword]]. The ootachi (also known as 野太刀, *"nodachi"*) is essentially a [[katana|katana]] with a very long blade, often longer than the wielder's height. The best-known examples are probably [[sephiroth|sephiroth]]'s Masamune in *[[final fantasy vii|final fantasy vii]]* and the various long sword-class weapons featured in the *[[monster hunter (series)|monster hunter (series)]]* series.

The ootachi was a rare weapon. In real life, it was used by men on foot to fight against mounted cavalry, however [[polearm|polearm]]s were much easier to produce and in most cases were more effective in that role. Due to it being an expensive weapon that was difficult to forge, it was seen as proof of a swordsmith's skill and a status symbol for a samurai who carried it.

One of the most recognizable [[transformers|transformers]] that first appeared in the original [[transformers: generation 1|transformers: generation 1]] TV cartoon from 1984. The heroic, wise and powerful Optimus Prime leads the [[autobot|autobot]]s against [[megatron|megatron]], the evil leader of the [[decepticon|decepticon]]s.

In the first series his alternate mode is a red, silver and blue Kenworth K100 cab over [[truck|truck]]. But since his [[transformers (live action)|appearance in the the live action movie]], he is also frequently depicted as a red and blue [[peterbilt 379|peterbilt 379]] [[semi truck|semi truck]] with distinctive flame paintjob.

Before becoming leader of the Autobots, Optimus ||used to be a smaller robot called [[orion pax|orion pax]]. He was mortally damaged by Megatron, but Alpha Trion reconstructed him into the ultimate powerful form of Optimus Prime.||

In [[japan|japan]] (except for the Japanese dubs of the live-action films and of [[transformers animated|transformers animated]]), Optimus Prime is known as **Convoy**.
 
His quote in the G1 series, "”I've got an idea.”":[http://dic.pixiv.net/a/%E7%A7%81%E3%81%AB%E3%81%84%E3%81%84%E8%80%83%E3%81%88%E3%81%8C%E3%81%82%E3%82%8B] is regarded as a type of [[meme|meme]] among Japanese Transformers fandom due to its low success rate.

Optimus Prime's original G1 design was created by [[mecha|mecha]] designers Obara Hiroyuki, [[kawamori shouji|kawamori shouji]] (famous for his work in [[macross|macross]]) and Ohno Kouhjin for the [[diaclone|diaclone]] Japanese transforming robot toy series in the early 1980s.

The **Orca** (*Orcinus orca*) is a black and white carnivorous marine mammal. Commonly known as the **killer whale** and also known as **orca whale**. The orca is the largest species of dolphin, being part of the family Delphinidae. (Delphinidae is within the Odontoceti or toothed whales, which is within the Cetacea or whales, so orcas are whales in the sense that all dolphins are whales.)

Usually growing around 5-8 meters long, orcas are known to be apex predators of the sea, as they have no natural predators.

In its Sensu Style, native to Poni Island, Oricorio's feathers are mainly purple. The tips of its wings broaden into a fan shape, and it has a fan-shaped crest on top of its head.

A person obsessed with any subject, whether anime, manga, [[comic|comic]]s, entertainment, [[video game|video game]]s, electronics, [[toy|toy]]s, trains, vehicles, weapons, [[history|history]], etc.

The term started as a derogatory term in [[japan|japan]] during the late 70s towards anti-social people who are highly fixated over a particular subject or person, but has since evolved (in the West mostly) to imply a cool, eccentric individual with particularly unique hobbies or interests. However, depictions of generic otaku as an "unhealthily obsessive fan" stock character remains in widespread uses in media (specially in Japan). In the West, otaku are often conflated with Western nerds, to the point of the term being used as a synonym, but each have their own specific differences socially and culturally. For the purposes of Danbooru though, they are one and the same.

A male character who looks or acts feminine, often passing as female.

The Japanese term "otoko no ko" is a pun on 男の子 (*otoko no ko*), meaning "boy", replacing 子 with the *ko* reading of 娘 (commonly *musume*, girl).

Otoko no ko characters are sometimes called "traps" or "femboys" in English-speaking communities. These terms have been deprecated in some areas (including this site, which aliases both tag names to this one) due to use as anti-LGBT slurs.

Some communities have mistakenly taken to using the term as a word for feminine boys no matter if they convincingly look like girls or not. If you can correctly tell the character is male with complete certainty from the thumbnail alone without looking at the genitalia, it's not this.

While many otoko no ko engage in [[crossdressing|crossdressing]], it is not a requirement. Sufficiently feminine characters can pass as girls even when near-nude or dressed in typically masculine clothing.

#### Background

**Details:**
The son of Nikolas Apocalypse and Sabrina Schariac, Otto was born in 1452 as a member of House Apocalypse. During his childhood, he met [[kallen kaslana|kallen kaslana]] and deemed her as his only friend, vowing together to save the world against the threat of the Honkai. When Kallen's father died for fighting the Honkai, Otto later discovered the 1st Divine Key, Void Archives into hopes of bringing back her late father, which he ended up reconsidering as her father's sacrifice will be in vain. This Divine Key would later assist him in his later goals.

Afterwards in his adulthood, Otto became the next Overseer of Schicksal (specifically the 227th), securing the position for the next 500 years in his own callous obsession of finding ways to revive Kallen. In one of his cloning attempts, he created [[theresa apocalypse|theresa apocalypse]] and would later adopt her as his granddaughter.

A sequel called [[pacific rim: uprising|pacific rim: uprising]] was released worldwide in March 2018. An animated series titled [[pacific rim: the black|pacific rim: the black]] was released in 2021.

#### Guidelines

Uploading paid rewards is against the rules. These are the rules for paid rewards:

- Public or free posts aren't paid rewards.
- If a post was free at the time of upload, then it's allowed.
- If an artist releases a paid reward for free later on, then it's allowed.
- Deliberately uploading paid rewards, even with this tag, will result in a warning then a ban.
- Paid rewards uploaded before 2020-07-06 are allowed.
- Paid rewards uploaded after 2020-07-06 should be reported in topic #10525 so they can be banned.
- **Be careful about uploading posts from Yande.re, E-Hentai, or other sites that host unmarked paid rewards. Also be careful when uploading unmarked paid rewards hosted by potential art thieves.**

A traditional Chinese greeting where the [[clenched hand|fist]] of one hand is pressed against the palm of the other.

There are two types: Gongshou Li and Baoquan Li. In Gongshou Li, the fingers cup the fist, and in Baoquan Li, the fingers are held straight out.

Gongshou Li (拱手礼), also know as *Fist and palm salute*, is a formal greeting etiquette in ancient China. It is commonly used in daily occasions (meeting and parting, when offering thanks or apologies). This greeting consists of a half-fist held in the palm of the other hand at stomach level, while [[bowing|bowing]] slightly to deeply depending on how much respect they want to convey.

Note that for males, the right-hand makes the fist and the left hand is on top. For females, it's the opposite. At a funeral, the greeting is done on the other way around: right-hand on top for men and left-hand on top for women.

Baoquan Li (抱拳礼) also know as *Kung Fu Salute*, *Hold palm salute* or *Hold fist salute*, is a common etiquette derived from (but not exclusive to) Chinese martial arts. It shows the humility and often widely used among the kung fu masters and students. This salute is generally characterized by an open left hand placed next to a closed right fist. The importance is that the fingers on the left hand should stay extended and not flexed to cover the right fist.

The **Panzerkampfwagen IV** (Pz.Kpfw. IV), commonly known as the **Panzer IV**, was a medium [[tank|tank]] developed in [[nazi|nazi]] Germany in the late 1930s and used extensively during [[world war ii|world war ii]]. Its ordnance inventory designation was Sd.Kfz. 161.

Designed as an infantry-support tank, the Panzer IV was not originally intended to engage enemy armor—that function was performed by the lighter [[panzer iii|panzer iii]]. However, with the flaws of pre-war doctrine becoming apparent and in the face of [[soviet|soviet]] [[t-34|t-34]] tanks, the Panzer IV soon assumed the tank-fighting role of its increasingly obsolete cousin. The most widely manufactured and deployed German tank of the Second World War, the Panzer IV was used as the base for many other fighting vehicles, including the [[sturmgeschutz iv|sturmgeschutz iv]] assault gun, [[jagdpanzer iv|jagdpanzer iv]] tank destroyer, the Wirbelwind self-propelled anti-aircraft weapon, and the Brummbär self-propelled gun.

A single shot, disposable, recoilless anti-tank weapon that was developed by Germany during World War II. Developed as a lighter, shorter range alternative to the [[panzerschreck|panzerschreck]] that could be used by a single person rather than a two-man team, the panzerfaust weighed 6.5kg (14 lbs) and fired a High Explosive Anti-Tank (HEAT) grenade. The effective range of the weapons were initially 30 meters (33 yards) and able to penetrate 200mm (7.9") of armor. Late WWII models had a effective range of 150 meters (164 yds) and could penetrate 280mm (11") or more of armor. They were often deployed to rifle squads or volksgrenadiers, giving a single squad unparalleled tank-killing ability. Several examples of the panzerfaust were captured by the Russians towards the end of World War Two, and the panzerfaust is often credited with having inspired their rocket-propelled grenade weapons. 

Despite being intended to replace the panzerschreck, itself a derivative of the American M1 Bazooka, it should be noted that the panzerfaust and its derivative, the RPG-2, were not rocket launchers, as the projectiles they fired did not use rocket motors and the charge that was detonated to launch the grenade burned entirely within the tube at launch.  The weapon was based on those of a recoilless gun.

A type of organism that is inhabiting a host (other organism)'s body, either by getting inside their body through some means or attached themselves to the host. Parasites often comes in a form of a [[worm|worm]], though many other types of parasitic creature exists, with different preference for hosts.

On Danbooru, parasite refers to when one creature has "attached" themselves to the host and is clearly visible within that image, not just the traditional concept of parasites. JP: 孔雀 *kujaku*

Peacock refers colloquially to peafowl in general, of which the peacock is the male and the [[peahen|peahen]] is the female. Indian peacocks famously feature an unmistakable elongated tail (known as a train) with an eye-spot pattern in iridescent green, blue and gold/bronze. Their head and neck are royal blue, with a spray of tuft-tipped feathers at the back of the head and white markings below and above the eye.

Peahens are brown for camouflage.

White peafowl are generally leucistic (rather than albinistic). Additionally, there are hundreds of domestically-bred color variations, including purple, bronze, opal, midnight, charcoal, jade, and taupe.

Besides the Indian peafowl "*Pavo cristatus*":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_peafowl], there are also the green or Java peafowl "*Pavo muticus*":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_peafowl] and the relatively dull-plumaged Congo or African peafowl "*Afropavo congensis*":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congo_peafowl].

The **People's Republic of China flag**, the Five Star Red Flag, often called simply the "Chinese flag" is the flag that has *de facto* represented Mainland China since the end of the Chinese Civil War. The design consists of a group of golden stars on a red background.

- !asset #20077398

Designed, developed and officially introduced in 1949. The red field is officially meant to symbolize [[communism|communism]], the big yellow star the Communist Party, and the four smaller stars meant the farmers, workers, intellectuals, and the bourgeoisie. Some people interpret the stars to be meant the five major ethnic groups of China, with the Han Chinese getting the large star and the four other stars meant to be Manchurians, Mongolians, Tibetans, and Uyghurs.

Not to be confused with the [[republic of china flag|Republic of China flag]] (a.k.a. Taiwanese flag).

A Playstation 2 RPG and part of the [[persona|persona]] series of the *[[shin megami tensei|shin megami tensei]]* franchise, released 10 July 2008 in Japan, 9 December 2008 in North America and 13 March 2009 in Europe.

The game follows a [[narukami yuu|high school junior]] who, due to his parents' work overseas, moves from the city to the rural town of Inaba to live for a year with his uncle and local policeman [[doujima ryoutarou|doujima ryoutarou]] and his six-year-old daughter Nanako. With his new friends from the local high school, he investigates a series of inexplicable murders and the truth about a TV channel that only appears during midnight, armed with Personas, materialized aspects of their personalities.

Received a enhanced port on the [[playstation vita|playstation vita]], and later [[microsoft windows|microsoft windows]], [[xbox one|xbox one]], [[xbox series x|xbox series x]] and S and [[nintendo switch|nintendo switch]], entitled *[[persona 4 the golden|persona 4 the golden]]*. It is set in the same universe as its predecessor, [[persona 3|persona 3]]. A fighting game, [[persona 4: the ultimate in mayonaka arena|persona 4: the ultimate in mayonaka arena]], also acts as a direct sequel to the game.

Another spinoff is the novel [[persona x detective|persona x detective]], taking place 1 year after the events of Persona 4.

Science fantasy and magic action role-playing games and sub-series of *[[phantasy star|phantasy star]]* made by [[sega|sega]]. It's well known as one of the first online multiplayer games for video game consoles. 

The series received several expansions after it's first release on the [[sega dreamcast|sega dreamcast]], starting with the updated edition Phantasy Star Online ver.2, followed by ports to both the [[gamecube|gamecube]] and [[xbox (original)|xbox (original)]] as *Phantasy Star Online Episode I & II*. The Gamecube also received a spin-off of the series, *Phantasy Star Online Episode III: C.A.R.D. Revolution*, with [[card|card]] based gameplay instead of the usual beat-em-up style. Finally, the series returned to form on the PC with release of *Phantasy Star Online: Blue Burst*, featuring Episode IV.

She is very happy most of the time and is determined to make everyone else happy, usually by planning parties and making sweets at the bakery where she is employed. A post that is completely identical to its parent, and was either uploaded afterwards or has no source while their parent does, and thus is inferior for Danbooru purposes.

Pixiv and Twitter posts are often identical, even if they have different filesizes. In 2019 Twitter stopped compressing as harshly as they used to, and in late 2020 Pixiv started losslessly recompressing their JPGs to strip metadata, so typically if there's only a few KBs of difference between two identical pictures from these two sites, it means they're the same exact image.

To check if two similar images are pixel-perfect duplicates, use https://duplicatebooru.zipfiled.info.

This tag is automatically populated and should not be removed by users.

**Do not flag posts just because they are under this tag if they come from a first-party source.**

Pixiv Red, or Fandom Red, is a depiction of [[red (pokemon)|Red]] that became very popular on Japanese art sharing websites like [[pixiv|pixiv]] during the late 2000s to early 2010s. He is a version of the Red that appears on Mt. Silver in *[[pokemon hgss|pokemon hgss]]*.

Departing from the game's design, this fandom version had [[short hair|short]], loose [[black hair|black hair]] and [[red eyes|red eyes]] (sometimes [[black eyes|black]], [[brown eyes|brown]], or [[grey eyes|grey]]). He was slim, if not [[toned male|toned]], with a stoic face and a cool persona. His feelings were usually kept very subtle.

 When depicted with a Pokemon, he usually favored [[charizard|charizard]] as his main, or was drawn with [[pikachu|pikachu]] as his companion.

**Take note:** not every Red depicted as stoic, with black hair, and/or with red eyes is a Pixiv Red. The hair on a typical depiction of Pixiv Red is more relaxed and glossy and does not [[flipped hair|fan out to the sides]], a la post #2278447. His eyes aren't very wide either, compared to his official counterpart.

A large spherical astronomical object that typically [[in orbit|orbit]]s a [[star (sky)|star (sky)]]. The tag should be used when at least one planet is seen from outer [[space|space]] or from the surface of another nearby planet. This includes real and fictional planets.  

Scientifically, there has always been some ambiguity as to what constitutes a planet, with some celestial bodies such as [[pluto (planet)|pluto (planet)]] and Ceres being considered at different times or by different people either as planets or as "dwarf planets". The International Astronomical Union (IAU) came up with a definition for a planet in 2006, meaning that the planets in our solar system are officially [[mercury (planet)|mercury (planet)]], [[venus (planet)|venus (planet)]], [[earth (planet)|earth (planet)]], [[mars (planet)|mars (planet)]], [[jupiter (planet)|jupiter (planet)]], [[saturn (planet)|saturn (planet)]], [[uranus (planet)|uranus (planet)]] and [[neptune (planet)|neptune (planet)]], but the definition remains contentious.

Plants vs. Zombies is a tower defense and strategy video game developed and originally published by PopCap Games for Windows and OS X in May 2009.

In Plants vs. Zombies, players take the role of a homeowner in the midst of a zombie apocalypse. To defend their home from zombies, some which have unique abilities, the player uses plants that can fire projectiles at, give "sun" to purchase other plants to help or block the advancing zombies. Players must plan defenses in multiple "lanes" across the home's lawn and should a zombie make it to the house on any lane, the game is over. Director George Fan was inspired to make the game after playing other tower defense titles and desiring to eliminate the typical strategies of sending advancing enemies through mazes of defenses, instead adapting the lane approach to remove this strategy.

A classical set of [[card|card]] consists 52 unique cards, categorized by suit and by rank. The ranks include Ace, the numbers two through ten, and the face cards Jack, Queen, and King. A [[joker (playing card)|joker (playing card)]] or two may or not be present. The **PlayStation 2** (officially abbreviated **PS2**) is a [[video game|video game]] home console manufactured by [[sony|sony]] Computer Entertainment and the successor to the [[playstation 1|playstation 1]] as part of the PlayStation series. 

It was first released on March 4, 2000, in [[japan|japan]], and then was released on October 26, 2000 in North America, and November 24, 2000 in Europe.

The second in Sony's line of PlayStation consoles, developed for the sixth generation market to compete against Microsoft's [[xbox (original)|xbox (original)]], Nintendo [[gamecube|gamecube]] and [[sega dreamcast|sega dreamcast]]. The PS2 is hailed as **the best selling console of all time**, having reached over 154.4 million units sold as of November 21, 2011. As of 2012, over 12 years after its initial release, new games continue to be developed and sold for it.

The **PlayStation 3** (プレイステーション3, Pureisutēshon Surī?, officially abbreviated as "PS3") is the third home [[video game|video game]] [[game console|console]] produced by [[sony|sony]] Computer Entertainment and the successor to the [[playstation 2|playstation 2]] as part of the PlayStation series. 

The PlayStation 3 competes with [[microsoft|microsoft]]'s [[xbox 360|xbox 360]] and [[nintendo|nintendo]]'s [[wii|wii]] as part of the seventh generation of video game consoles. Its big, heavy and low capacity first model was first released on November 11, 2006, in Japan, with international markets following shortly thereafter. A newer and more refined slim model with higher capacity was released in 2009.

Major features of the console include its free unified online gaming service, the PlayStation Network, its multimedia capabilities, connectivity with the [[playstation portable|playstation portable]], and its use of the Blu-ray Disc as its primary storage medium.

Like the [[super famicom|super famicom]]/[[super nintendo|super nintendo]]'s controller, which it was based on, the face of the controller features a [[d-pad|d-pad]] on the left, four action buttons on the right, and initially two buttons in the middle (originally a Start and  Select button). The **PlayStation Portable** (officially abbreviated PSP) is a [[handheld game console|handheld game console]] manufactured and marketed by [[sony|sony]]. 

The system was released in Japan on December 12, 2004, in North America on March 24, 2005 and in Europe and Australia on September 1, 2005.

The PlayStation Portable is the only handheld video game console to use an optical disc format, Universal Media Disc (UMD), as its primary storage medium. Other distinguishing features of the console include its large viewing screen, robust multi-media capabilities, and connectivity with the [[playstation 2|playstation 2]], [[playstation 3|playstation 3]], other PSPs and the Internet.

The XrossMediaBar (pronounced cross-media bar and officially abbreviated as XMB) is a graphical user interface developed by Sony Computer Entertainment that was first used in this handled system. 

A slimmer, lighter, remodeled version of the PlayStation Portable (the PSP-2000/"Slim & Lite") was released in early September 2007. 

This model was later replaced by another remodeling, the PSP-3000, which included a new screen and an inbuilt microphone. Since then, a complete redesign called the [[playstation portable go|PSP Go]] has been released, which was sold alongside the PSP-3000. 

In 2011 a budget model, the PSP-E1000, was released. The PSP line was succeeded by the [[playstation vita|playstation vita]] released in 2012.

The **PlayStation Vita** (プレイステーション・ヴィータ, officially abbreviated PS Vita) is a handheld game console manufactured and marketed by Sony Computer Entertainment. 

It is the successor to the [[playstation portable|playstation portable]] as part of the PlayStation series. 

The PS Vita was released in Japan and parts of Asia on December 17, 2011, in Europe, North America, South America and Singapore on February 22, 2012 and in Australia on February 23, 2012. 

It primarily competes with the [[nintendo 3ds|nintendo 3ds]] as part of the eighth generation of gaming.

Software for the PlayStation Vita is distributed on a proprietary flash memory card called "PlayStation Vita card" rather than on Universal Media Discs (UMDs) as used by the PlayStation Portable.

The handheld includes two analog sticks, an OLED multi-touch capacitive touchscreen, and supports Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and optional 3G. Internally, the Vita features a four-core ARM Cortex-A9 MPCore processor and a four-core SGX543MP4+ graphics processing unit, as well as LiveArea software as its main user interface, which succeeds the XrossMediaBar.

The blossoms of plum trees, especially of the genus *Prunus mume*. The petals are white, pink or red, and bloom in early spring. 

The aesthetic of the plum blossom has always been of major importance across East Asia, and while [[hanami|viewing them]] was initially a popular practice in Japan beginning in the Nara period, it was overshadowed by the popularity of [[cherry blossoms|cherry blossoms]] during the Heian period. This preference was only reinforced by subsequent generations of intellectuals, who in effect argued the *sakura* to be more quintessentially Japanese. 

Today, however, some older Japanese who find sakura *hanami* too crowded and noisy take to plum blossom viewing (or *umemi*) instead, enjoying the peace of its relative obscurity. 

Distinguished from cherry blossoms in that cherry petals have slits at the ends of the petals. Plum petal ends on the other hand are round ("see reference":/media_assets/7899985).

The plum blossom is the national flower of [[china|china]], and is an important cultural symbol in the country.

Pokémon (ポケットモンスター, *Pocket Monsters*) is a highly popular [[tag group:role-playing games|RPG series]] developed by Tajiri Satoshi, with art by [[sugimori ken|sugimori ken]], for [[nintendo|nintendo]] handheld video game devices since 1996, and has since spawned several spinoff games, [[pokemon adventures|manga]], and [[pokemon (anime)|an anime series]].

In the main games, the player character goes on a journey through various cities, towns and landscape (caves, forests, sea, etc.) and meets creatures known as [[pokemon (creature)|Pokémon]]. The player is able to collect Pokémon to form a personalized team, train them to make them stronger, choose their known skills and command them to fight against other Pokémon. People who do that are Pokémon Trainers. Many NPCs are Pokémon Trainers available to fight against the player.

The storyline advances as the player gains eight [[gym leader badge|badges]] for defeating different Gym Leaders and eventually challenges the Elite Four and the current Champion; defeating them all grants the player the title of Champion for himself/herself. Typical side quests, such as finding a specific item or person, are also required at certain points. Additionally, the player repeatedly fights against his or her personal rivals and routinely clashes with a criminal organization.

A mobile app created by Niantic, Inc. and the Pokemon Company. Players take their smartphones with them, walk around, and catch [[pokemon|pokemon]], just like in the main series. The game initially included Generation I Pokemon, but began adding Generation II Pokemon in early 2017 and Generation III during the same year's Halloween event.

The game is often set as an example of a "flavor of the month" fad. Its online popularity dropped drastically a few months after its release; many blame this on the lack of updates and content on launch, Niantic, Inc.'s poor management and playerbase communication, and its freemium pay-to-win system prevalent in many other mobile games. However, despite the decrease in internet activity, it's still a popular game, and some cite the game and the release of *[[pokemon sm|Pokemon Sun and Moon]]* as the causes of a resurgence in franchise popularity overall. More features being added over the course of 2017 have also drawn back some of the initial fans that dropped off for the above reasons.

Headlights for [[car|car]]s that are hidden and flip or rotate into position when engaged. While they were often seen in [[sports car|sports car]]s in the 90s and earlier for the aerodynamic benefit while disengaged, they ultimately fell out of use due to advancements in fixed headlight design and stricter pedestrian safety requirements in certain regions.

The last major production car to feature this design trait was the [[chevrolet corvette c5|C5]] [[chevrolet corvette|chevrolet corvette]]. Certain models with pop-ups (primarily Japanese cars from the 80s and 90s) are commonly modified so that the headlights only open a portion of the way. Pop-ups modified in this manner are often referred to as "sleepy eye" headlights.

This tag is only for posts that depict pop-up headlights in the engaged position.

A postage stamp is a small piece of paper that is purchased and displayed on an item of mail as evidence of payment of postage.
The stamp’s shape is usually that of a small rectangle of varying proportions, though triangles or other shapes are occasionally used.

Before the introduction of postage stamps, recipients were unable or unwilling to pay for delivered items, and senders had no incentive to restrict the number, size, or weight of items sent. The postage stamp resolved this issue in a simple and elegant manner, with the additional benefit of room for an element of beauty to be introduced.
