One of two symbols composed of a Zero (Circle) and One (vertical line) overlaid on top of each other.

Under the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) 60417 standard, Graphical symbols for use on equipment, 0 is the symbol for "off" and 1 is the symbol for "on." Combining these two symbols you get either the symbol for "on/off" (a circle with a vertical line inside of it) or "stand-by" (an incomplete circle with an opening at the top and a vertical line sticking out of the opening).  For electronics it is very common to see the "Standby" symbol used nowadays, as the electronic device does not completely turn off but instead goes into a low power state.

The symbol in [[purple heart (neptunia)|purple heart (neptunia)]]'s eyes in images like post #1151905 is an example of the "stand-by" symbol.

Pretty Rhythm is a Japanese Taito Type X2 arcade game by Takara Tomy. It has been adapted into a manga series by Mari Asabuki. An anime adaptation by Tatsunoko Production, titled [[pretty rhythm aurora dream|Pretty Rhythm: Aurora Dream]], aired in Japan between April 2011 and March 2012. This was followed by a sequel, [[pretty rhythm dear my future|Pretty Rhythm: Dear My Future]], which aired between April 2012 and March 2013. A third series, [[pretty rhythm rainbow live|Pretty Rhythm: Rainbow Live]], began airing from April 6, 2013.

The series focuses on the creation and management of idols that perform in Prism Shows, a form of entertainment that combines singing, performance art, and figure skating.

The series has an alternate continuity spinoff franchise known as [[pripara|pripara]], and another separate continuity called [[kiratto pri chan|kiratto pri chan]]. All three are collectively under the *[[pretty series|Pretty]]* metafranchise label.

A [[male focus|male-focused]] spinoff movie series called *[[king of prism|king of prism]]* launched in 2016. *[[king of prism by prettyrhythm|king of prism by prettyrhythm]]* premiered in January 2016, starring [[hayami hiro|hayami hiro]], [[mihama kouji|mihama kouji]], and [[nishina kazuki|nishina kazuki]] as the main characters, with sequel films following in 2017 and 2019.

The official name was originally just Athena, the title Princess was added over time and is maybe not official, but useful for a clearer distinction to her descendant [[asamiya athena|asamiya athena]].

Princess Athena has long purple hair held by a golden barrette. She wears a red bikini and purple sandals, wields a sword and a round brass shield with spikes.

Princess Athena made a second appearance in SNK vs. Capcom: SVC Chaos as a secret boss. Her costume was only slightly modified. She got a red fingerless glove on her shield hand, a heart-shaped shield with a lion's head, some additional ribbons, her sandals got wings and her barrette got decorations that look as if it was a tied ribbon. This version should be labeled [[svc chaos|svc chaos]], the older one not.

In nude pictures, Princess Athena and Asamiya Athena can be distinguished by the barrette, which for the latter is usually red or white with a golden star, or (in [[the king of fighters 2003|KoF 2003]]) gold with a red heart. However, sometimes artists use one of Asamiya Athena's barrettes when they obviously intend to draw Princess Athena.

Princess Connect! is a web browser game created by [[cygames|cygames]] which closed in late 2015. In August 2016, **Princess Connect! Re:Dive** was announced as a remake of the original game and advertised as an Anime RPG.

In February 2018, the game was officially released for Android and iOS. The remake is notable for using an anime-style format to tell its story complete with an "opening song":[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hq8uuBB7SoM], "cutscenes":[https://youtu.be/xCX1Qx40sUM?t=447], "ending credits":[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3XXC4TSTuxU], and even a next "episode preview":[https://youtu.be/xCX1Qx40sUM?t=739]. Wit Studio is credited for the anime portions of the game. A global version was released on January 19, 2021, and later "ended":[https://www.crunchyroll.com/news/latest/2023/3/30/an-important-update-regarding-princess-connect-re-dive] on April 30, 2023.

The gameplay in the remake is heavily reliant on team composition to progress through the more difficult portions of the game and encourages raising multiple characters to complete certain challenges. Despite differing initial rarities, all characters can be raised to the maximum rarity which unlocks their full stories and maximum potential.

In the original story, the game was set in "Legend of Astrum", an MMO where the player would meet various girls and recruit them. Because of the MMO setting, each girl had a fantasy version and a real-life version. The story in the remake plays out as a sequel, starting the narrative with a "Bad End" to the original series in which the characters remain in the MMO, unaware of there ever being a separate real world.

Prinnies contain the souls of humans or demons who lead a criminal life or committed a grave sin, and have to work in Celestia (Heaven) or the Netherworld (Hell) to pay off their debts and reincarnate as something else. It's stated somewhere that you also become a Prinny if you lead a meaningless life.

Prinnies slur the words at the end of their sentences as "~ッス", or in English localizations, say "dood" at the end of sentence, dood.

[[kazamatsuri fuuka|kazamatsuri fuuka]] is a notable "prinny" from Disgaea 4 who wasn't fully converted into a prinny, and instead looks and acts as a girl with a prinny hat on and doesn't explode, in spite of her technical prinny status.  Other characters who die in Disgaea frequently reappear as prinnies, including some bad endings, but they are [[spoilers|spoilers]]. 

There are some Prinnies who break the usual standards of being one, though those instances tend to be rare. [[big sis prinny (disgaea)|big sis prinny (disgaea)]] is the first to break tradition by having a woman's voice. Another is the giant yellow Prinny that [[usalia (disgaea)|usalia (disgaea)]] rides around on during battles, which doesn’t have a name and never speaks. Another is [[pii-chan (disgaea)|pii-chan (disgaea)]], a bright yellow cat-themed Prinny who serves as [[pirilika (disgaea)|pirilika (disgaea)]]’s secretary and speaks like a normal person.

A multimedia project developed by DynamisOne and Studio Alaya. The project had been given the nickname "[[blue archive|blue archive]] with Swords" or "Red Archive" due to not only sharing a similar theme of school girls with [[halo|halo]]s and weapons, but is made by several former Blue Archive developers.

It was initially teased on August 18th, 2024, before a promo video officially revealed it on September 1st, with a visual novel planned for [[comiket 105|comiket 105]], and a gacha game speculated to release in the future. The project has been "cancelled":[https://x.com/DynamisOne/status/1832722210160554111] as of September 8th, 2024, speculated to be due to both controversy surrounding accusations of plagiarism, and a suspected threat of a copyright infringement lawsuit from [[nexon|nexon]], Blue Archive's publisher.

Peculiarly, since the project's announcement, it has spawned a trend of [[futanari|futanari]] fanarts. This trend stemmed from the Korean community, where it was joked that the game would be more popular if it involved "cockfighting" rather than "sword fighting". The original jokes originated from joking KV stood for the Korean slang words "kochu" (sword) and "valgi" (sword drawing), which is used for penis and erection, respectively.

In-game they are made to be much harder for larger ships like battleships to hit unless they are armed with secondary guns, as they are meant to represent swarms of tiny coastal craft rather than individual ships. 

They were introduced in the Fall 2015 event, which notably involves battles in the [Solomon Islands Campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solomon_Islands_campaign) where the US tried on several occasions to sink Japanese convoys with PT boat torpedo attacks, usually with unsuccessful results. They were quite successful though at "barge busting", attacking the barges and transports in the littorals as they tried to ferry supplies and reinforcements under the cover of night to avoid Allied air superiority. **Post Traumatic Stress Disorder** (modern term: **PTSD**) is a [[crazy|mental disorder]] that can develop after a person is exposed to a very traumatic event, such as [[rape|sexual assault]], [[war|war]]fare, traffic collisions, or other threats on a person's life. Frequent among [[soldier|soldier]]s, it used to be called **Shell Shock** ([[world war i|world war i]]) and **Combat Fatigue** ([[world war ii|world war ii]]) in the past.  

Symptoms may include: paranoia, overvigilance, concealment of [[handgun|handgun]]s and other weapons for easy access, fear of unexisting treats, disturbing thoughts, feelings, or dreams related to the events (usually war flashbacks in most veterans); mental or physical distress to trauma-related cues; attempts to avoid trauma-related cues and alterations in how a person thinks and feels. 

The most severe cases may feature trauma-related visual and auditory [hallucinations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hallucination) with mental disturbances (such as severe [depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depression_(mood))) that could lead to [[suicide|suicide]] or full-on [psychosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychosis) and [[vegetative state|loss of contact with reality]].

**Puzzle & Dragons** (パズル&ドラゴンズ *Pazuru Ando Doragonzu*) is a Japanese mobile game developed by GungHo Online Entertainment. The Japanese title is often shortened to パズドラ (*Pazudora*), while the English title is often shortened to PAD.

The gameplay consists of the player going through dungeons (there are regular dungeons, special dungeons, and technical dungeons) and battling monsters and bosses via matching element tiles to attack and/or heal in order to earn various in-game currencies. Beating dungeons eventually gives enough experience points to allow the player to level up so their rank, stamina, team cost, and monster box capacity may increase. Another factor of gameplay is the player collecting, fusing, and evolving their monsters in order to make them stronger. Utilizing monster abilities and stats is vital to the gameplay, especially later on in the game.

There are approximately 1400 and counting unique monsters that can be collected by the player. These range from traditional [[dragon|dragons]], [[demon|demons]], [[ogre|ogres]], [[goblin|goblins]], and [[knight|knights]] to mythological figures from various real world cultures and religions, fictionalized versions of popular historical figures, and even third party fictional characters.

[[crossover|The game also does various collaborations with several anime and video game properties]] which are usually Japanese only. Many collaborations have been released to the international editions, however.

There have been a few anime adaptations of the game [Puzzle & Dragons x (Cross)](https://www.tv-tokyo.co.jp/anime/pad-x/) in 2016 and [PazuDora](https://anime-pad.com/index.html) in 2018.

||

#### Abilities

Pyrrha wields [[milo and akouo|Miló]] and [[milo and akouo|Akoúo̱]]. Miló is a weapon with three forms: a [[javelin (spear)|javelin (spear)]] [[spear|spear]], a [[xiphos (sword)|xiphos]] (small [[sword|sword]]), or a [[rifle|rifle]]. It is red with bronze trimming. Akoúo̱ is a bronze metal rounded [[shield|shield]] often worn as a [[buckler|buckler]].

*This term is properly spelt "QUALITY" (without the quotes), in ALL CAPS. This tag is written in lowercase due to limitations in Danbooru's tagging system.*

The term "QUALITY" indicates (with ironic intent) glaring yet humorous errors and flaws in commercial works of poor quality or works of otherwise good quality. This can be caused by poor budgeting (blowing most of the budget of an anime into the first episodes, per example), a small budget or outsourcing to cheaper studios, although it can also be as a result of a honest mistake.

The Japanese equivalent is "ヤシガニ" ("Coconut crab"), a reference to [[lost universe|lost universe]]'s 4th episode which, due to the show's notoriously bad animation, was turned into a byword for bad animation in general. A more descriptive term is "作画崩壊" ("Animation collapse").

This tag can be applied to any posts that *intentionally* recreates the disfigured art or animation frame for humorous purposes. Do *not* apply this tag to any other post with generally poor quality otherwise. For posts featuring an error unintentionally created by an artist, see [[artistic error|artistic error]].

A model usually present at auto racing events. They are typically seen wearing skimpy outfits bearing the logos of the racing team and/or its sponsors. Their official job is to hold a [[parasol|parasol]] over the driver to shield them from sunlight while their car is being worked on. Also known as a *grid girl* or *umbrella girl*.

The term *race queen* can be used interchangeably with the terms *campaign girl* and *[[booth babe|booth babe]]* as all refer to models in skimpy outfits. Campaign girls can be seen more in trade shows and the like, specially those that market [[motor vehicle|motor vehicle]]s, while booth babes are seen in smaller booths, especially acting as booth tenders or helpers.

Due to the increased presence of women in motorsports and safety concerns regarding their outfits in pit lanes, race queens have been phased out of almost all major motorsport series, with [[super gt|super gt]], [[moto gp|moto gp]], and [[deutsche tourenwagen masters|deutsche tourenwagen masters]] being notable holdouts - DTM even offering the option for male pit models to accompany female drivers.

The most recognizable form of race queen outfit is a revealing outfit usually consisting of a [[crop top|crop top]] or [[tube top|tube top]] with a [[skirt|skirt]] or [[shorts|shorts]], designed to highlight the model's [[midriff|midriff]] and legs, although [[highleg leotard|highleg leotard]]s and [[highleg one-piece swimsuit|swimsuits]] with or without additional accessories have also been common as outfits especially during the 1990s in Japan. Recently, race queens in less revealing outfits have also become more common, primarily in regions outside of Japan that still employ them - their outfits will usually consist of form-fitting [[dress|dress]]es or [[bodysuit|bodysuit]]s instead.

The 2009 derivative is the only version of the Racing Miku derivatives which did not have an official illustration as per her release, though it was featured in merchandise for that season and new official arts have been given later on. The unveiling of the Racing Miku derivatives only became a feature from the 2010 season onwards. All merchandise related to Good Smile Racing featuring Miku prior to the 2010 season, with the exception of the 2009 Racing Miku figurine, features Miku in her normal attire.

Raglan sleeves are sleeves attached to a garment via a diagonal seam from the armpit to the neckline (rather than a simple circular seam at the edge of the shoulder). They are often made in a different color than the torso of the garment and are constructed from one piece of material. Raglan sleeves are commonly used in sportswear, as they are designed to give greater freedom of movement for the arm and shoulder. 

T-shirts with this type of sleeve are sometimes called "baseball shirts" due to their popularity of use as undershirts for baseball uniforms. Raglan sleeves became very popular in fashion outside of sports in the start of the 1970's.

A **railgun** is an electro-magnetic projectile launcher typically consists of two or more metal rails flanking the launcher (hence the name) connected to an electrical power supply. When a conductive projectile is inserted between the rails (at the end connected to the power supply), it completes the circuit, launching a projectile with extreme force and speed.

As of current, real life railgun is still under development to reduce the power input needed to operate the system, and to reduce the wearing of the system for military uses. Railguns are often seen in [[science fiction|science fiction]] works due to their advanced design and extreme power.

Not to be confused with [[railway gun|railway gun]]. For a manga and anime spin-off of [[toaru majutsu no index|toaru majutsu no index]], see [[toaru kagaku no railgun|toaru kagaku no railgun]], or [[railgun (misaka mikoto)|railgun (misaka mikoto)]] for the specific attack done by the main character of the series.

**"Rainbow" Mika Nanakawa**, or **"Rainbow" Mika** (**レインボー・ミカ**) or **R. Mika** for short, is a video game character from the [[street fighter|street fighter]] fighting game series. Her first appearance is in [[street fighter zero (series)|Street Fighter Zero 3]], later re-appearing in [[street fighter v|street fighter v]].

Mika is a Japanese [[wrestling|professional wrestler]] trained by the big, domineering, shinai-sporting, golf cart-riding [[harmageddon yoko|harmageddon yoko]]. One of her favorite attacks (outside of grappling) is a flying [[hip attack|hip attack]]. She is usually seen with her tag-team partner [[yamato nadeshiko (street fighter)|yamato nadeshiko (street fighter)]]. She is considered the forefront representative of "joshipuro" (Japanese women's pro wrestling) in fighting games. [[zangief|zangief]], a fellow pro wrestler, is her hero.

Mika is most commonly seen wearing a white and sky blue [[wrestling outfit|wrestling outfit]] of some design, complete with a [[domino mask|domino mask]] serving as a [[wrestling mask|wrestling mask]] around her [[blue eyes|blue eyes]] and her [[long hair|long]], [[blonde hair|blonde hair]] done up as [[twintails|twintails]].

Mika's goal is to be "Star of the Ring." To try to accomplish this, Mika decided she would travel abroad and battle famous street fighters even before she made her official debut. During that time, she met Zangief, a wrestler she is a huge fan of. Zangief inspired her as a pro wrestler to train hard for the next time they meet.

There are different flavor distinctions for ramen, such as shio (salty), tonkotsu (pork bone), shoyuu (soy), hiyashi (chilled) and miso.

A style of [[backpack|backpack]] commonly used by elementary schoolchildren in Japan. Its name is derived from the Dutch "ransel". They're a firm leather pack with a single large flap that curves over the top.  The traditional colors are red for girls and black for boys, and are usually depicted this way.  Additional colors have been available since the 1960's, but culturally only took off after the 2000's. Black is still the preferred color for boys, but the preferred color for girls has shifted to lavender purple, peach pink, and light blue over red.

These bags are expensive, averaging around ¥60k, but are intended to last through the entirety of elementary school.

What you get when a country tries to use any language that's not their native language, and makes mistakes in the process. That country is usually Japan in Danbooru's case, but other international screwups are possible and encountered. These mistakes can include both misspellings (such as the very common error of mixing up "L" and "R") and grammatical errors. Sometimes the speaker also is too young to speak his or her native language properly.

To find images containing this, search for the language name with [[ranguage|ranguage]]. 

Examples:

- finnish ranguage
- french ranguage
- german ranguage
- greek ranguage
- latin ranguage

[[engrish text|Engrish]] is a well-defined and by far the most common form of ranguage and so gets its own tag.

A Rash Guard (sometimes called a *Rash Vest*, *Rashie* or *Swim Shirt*) is a type of athletic shirt worn for extra function and protection when surfing, snorkeling, jet skiing, or doing other watersports where you want more protection than a [[swimsuit|swimsuit]], but don't really need a full [[wetsuit|wetsuit]].  Most rash guards have long sleeves and while some women's tops show midriff, most are regular shirt length.  Of note, they are sometimes worn under a wetsuit or [[diving suit|diving suit]] for added comfort.

Because rash guards are made from [[tight clothes|tight clothes]]-fitting materials like spandex, nylon, polyester, or neoprene and are often sold as matching top/bottom sets, this can sometimes make them appear similar to a [[wetsuit|wetsuit]] or [[one-piece swimsuit|one-piece swimsuit]] at a glance when no midriff is visible.  A clue to watch for is the horizontal line where the top-piece and bottom-piece come together/overlap.  If there is no line clearly identifying top from bottom, assume the garment is a wetsuit instead.

Re:Stage! (Re:ステージ!) is a Japanese multimedia franchise by Pony Canyon and Comptiq. The story revolves around female junior high school idols who aim to become a top in Prism Stage, a nationwide tournament where many middle school idols compete and become top idols. These girls are divided into several units. Their stories are serialized in monthly Comptiq and short stories are released online via the official website.

A manga series and several unit singles has been released. A mobile rhythm game developed by Hotarubi titled "Re:Stage! Prism Step":[http://rst-project.com/ps/] (Re:ステージ！プリズムステップ) was released on July 31, 2017 for Android and August 5, 2017 for iOS. An anime television series titled "Re:Stage! A receding hairline refers to the thinning or loss of hair on the scalp, particularly at the front and top of the scalp, starting at the temple. It is a disorder that can be caused by many different factors and is more common in men than women.

It is typically caused by genetics, aging related to male pattern hair loss, stress and hormonal changes (aka testosterone).

A family of woodwind [[instrument|instrument]]s.  The most common type are soprano recorders, with low cost plastic versions frequently issued to school children since the 20th century.

It is played perpendicular to a person's lips through a mouthpiece called a *fipple* or *block*. It has a slightly tapering body with eight finger holes and can come in a variety of colors. The name comes from one of the meanings of the word *record*, which is "to practice a piece of music."

This tag is for images with an emmisive red light source. There must be a red light casting a red shade either on screen or offscreen. It's important that the red light is a significant portion of the image

#### When to use

- You can clearly see where the red light comes from, like a lamp, a bright neon sign, or sunlight coming through something red.
- The red light changes how the picture feels or looks a lot.
- The red light is visible and a key feature of the character (like with Olimar from Pikmin)

#### When not to use

- If there's only a little bit of red such as with sci-fi suit LEDs that doesn't change the picture much.
- If the surface is red (like they're painted red or a raspberry) and not emmisive
- If there is rainbow light
- More than two different colored light/light sources

#### Exceptions

- If the picture is heavily desaturated, but there's saturated red lights, you can use this tag regardless of the light size

Latin: *Grus japonensis*
JP: タンチョウヅル (*tanchou-dzuru*)

A rare, endangered East Asian [[crane (animal)|crane (animal)]] species, distinctive for the red patch on its head which is actually bare, brightly-colored skin. This plus the black neck, white streak leading from the red crown partially down the neck, and white body make them easy to identify. This crane is one of the largest crane species.

Overall, they are snow white with black secondary flight feathers (in flight, these are the row of largest feathers present on the "lower arm" of the wing). This can appear like a fluffy black tail when the birds are standing, but the real tail feathers as well as the primary flight feathers are actually white. The bill is olive green to greenish horn, the legs are slate to grayish black.

Males are black on the cheeks, throat, and neck, while females are pearly gray in these spots. 

Some artistic renditions may show a black tail or black primary flight feathers if the artist did not reference a photo or accurate illustration of the bird in flight. Regardless, if the crane has a red forehead or a line delineating this marking, it is almost certainly a red-crowned crane.

In Taoism this crane is a symbol of longevity and immortality. It also symbolizes luck and fidelity.

The ***Reichsadler*** ("Imperial Eagle") is a German [[heraldry|heraldic]] emblem used since the Holy Roman Empire as a symbol of the [[germany|German]] State, adopted by the German Empire as the national emblem. Its use as the National Emblem continued under the Weimar Republic. The Weimar version was re-adopted by the West Germany and modern-day Federal German Republic as the *Bundesadler*. 

Despite its medieval origin, the term *Reichsadler* in common English understanding and here refers to the **[[nazi|nazi]]-era** version that consists of a monochrome [[eagle|eagle]] facing to its side, with straight outstretched wings, and both talons clutching a circular wreath containing a [[swastika|swastika]]. This also includes the variants, such as the *Parteiadler* (NSDAP party emblem, left-facing) and the [[luftwaffe|luftwaffe]] one (curved wings with single talon clutching).

The **Reiwa era** (令和時代 *Reiwa jidai*, lit. "Age of Sacred Peace") is the official name of the present era of Japanese history, which began on May 1, 2019 following the abdication of [[emperor akihito|emperor akihito]] and the ascension of Crown Prince [[emperor naruhito|Naruhito]] to the Chrysanthemum Throne.

The Reiwa era follows the [[heisei|heisei]] era (1989-2019), the [[shouwa|shouwa]] era (1926-1989), the [[taishou|taishou]] era (1912-1926), and the [[meiji|meiji]] era (1868-1912). Since the Meiji era, each era has corresponded to the rule of one emperor.

The name of the new era was announced during a press conference in which Chief Cabinet Secretary [[suga yoshihide|suga yoshihide]] [[holding sign|held up a sign]] revealing the new name. This event has revived a minor [[meme|meme]], with many posts parodying the reveal of the new name in a fashion that had been done periodically with Suga's predecessor, [[obuchi keizou|obuchi keizou]].

The design consists of a white sun in a blue canton on a red field. In Chinese, the flag is commonly called the **Blue Sky, White Sun, and a Wholly Red Earth** flag.

Not to be confused with the [[people's republic of china flag|People's Republic of China flag]] (the flag of Mainland China, widely known simply as the *Chinese flag*).

A remake of the game was released on 2020.

***Resident Evil 4*** known in Japan as *Biohazard 4*, is a 2005 third-person shooter survival horror video game developed and published by [[capcom|capcom]].

The story of Resident Evil 4 follows the U.S. government special agent [[leon s. kennedy|Leon S. Kennedy]], who is sent on a mission to rescue [[ashley graham|ashley graham]], the U.S. President's daughter whom a sinister cult has kidnapped. Traveling to a rural area of Spain, Leon fights hordes of violent villagers and reunites with the mysterious spy [[ada wong|ada wong]].

The game is notable for redefining the third-person genre with its over-the-shoulder camera.

When the image resolution on Danbooru differs from the image resolution at the source. The following two tags can be used with this tag.

- [[source smaller|source smaller]]:
  - One or both dimensions must be larger than the source.
  - `height_source <= height_danbooru and width_source <= width_danbooru`
- [[source larger|source larger]]:
  - One or both dimensions must be smaller than the source.
  - `height_source >= height_danbooru and width_source >= width_danbooru`
- **Neither**:
  - One dimension is larger than the source, and the other dimension is smaller than the source.
  - `(height_source > height_danbooru and width_source < width_danbooru) or (height_source < height_danbooru and width_source > width_danbooru)`

Any [[ammunition|ammunition]] fired by [[rifle|rifle]]s. Larger and longer than a handgun cartridge, smaller than cannon shells. This tag applies to any calibers, ranging from [[assault rifle|intermediate cartridges]] like 5.56mm NATO, full-power rounds like 7.62mm NATO or larger ones fired by [[heavy machine gun|heavy machine gun]]s such as the .50 BMG.

A decent rule of thumb is that if the cartridge's length is more than 3.5 times the diameter of the case, it lacks a distinct rim, usually has bottlenecked [[shell casing|case]] and the [[bullet|bullet]] diameter is approximately a half inch or less, then it is most likely a rifle cartridge regardless of specific caliber.

A modern **[[shield|shield]]** used by [[police|police]] and some [[military|armed forces]] in riot control to protect the shield carrier from melee attacks and also thrown projectiles, or non-lethal weapons such as rubber bullets and water cannons.
Riot shields are typically made out of transparent polycarbonate and are designed to be shatter resistant, but are generally not ballistic resistant. See post #6195921 for example. 

Riot shields can either come in two main variants, one that is one-handed that affords less protection but allows the user to use the other arm, generally to wield a baton. It has two handles, the left-most of which is held on to while the other keeps the arm in place. And another that requires both arms and provides full protection.

**Not to be confused** with [[ballistic shield|ballistic shield]] (post #6308441) - which is identifiable by its opaque, often metallic appearance and with narrow viewing port.

A road is a route that has been [[pavement|paved]] or otherwise improved for travel by foot or vehicle. Possible road surfaces include dirt, gravel, concrete, and asphalt.

The North American adaptation/westernification of [[choujikuu yousai macross|Super Dimension Fortress Macross]], [[choujikuu kidan southern cross|Super Dimension Cavalry Southern Cross]], and [[kikou souseiki mospeada|Genesis Climber Mospeada]] -- actually an edited amalgamation of the three original (and unrelated) Japanese anime series, with their plots significantly altered to appear as though they comprise a single continuous storyline. 

The ROBOTECH adaptation also featured modified dialogue and different music (by "Ulpio Minucci":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulpio_Minucci]), which was developed by an American company called [[harmony gold|harmony gold]] and producer and story editor "Carl Macek":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Macek]. It was first syndicated to American TV stations in 1985 and a few years later in several other countries across the world. It was quite popular during its first time of release in the West, as many anime fans of that era thought it was made of original content (which it wasn't).

Historically, **ROBOTECH has been an extremely polarizing subject amongst [[otaku|anime fans]], and it remains controversial even to this day**.

Many critics look down upon the show for its extensive edits to the source material (Westernizing character names, editing for content, forging a connection between previously-unrelated series, and so on), to the extent that some of its most ardent detractors compare it to the Woody Allen film [*What's Up, Tiger Lily?*](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What%27s_Up,_Tiger_Lily%3F,) a Japanese spy thriller completely redubbed and re-edited to become a campy musical comedy.  

On the other hand, the series does have its staunch defenders as well, most of whom will cite the fact that the adaptation had a new original epic and memorable music soundtrack and that it served as an important "gateway" to anime (particularly the [[mecha|mecha]] genre) for many Americans (and other Westerners) who grew up in the [[1980s (style)|80s]]. 

After several legal disputes over the international rights of the original series ([[macross|macross]] mostly) a settlement was reached between the parties in 2021 and now both the original and adapted series will be freely available everywhere in the world, allowing western anime fans to know more about the original franchises and the Japanese to watch the adaptation and purchase their respective merchandise without any legal constrains for the first time.

This tag should be used sparingly, and *only* on pictures that are clearly intended to depict or reflect the ROBOTECH version of events. Otherwise, the tags for the original three series should instead be used:

- **The Macross Saga**: [[choujikuu yousai macross|choujikuu yousai macross]]
- **The Masters Saga**: [[choujikuu kidan southern cross|choujikuu kidan southern cross]]
- **The New Generation**: [[kikou souseiki mospeada|kikou souseiki mospeada]]

Also note that the American-produced anime film [[the shadow chronicles|the shadow chronicles]] is considered part of the ROBOTECH universe, but not that of any of the original Japanese series.

Romaji is Japanese words written in the Roman alphabet. It is seldom used in media, unless for the purpose of educating in the Japanese language or other special purposes. Sometimes used to explain, expound or guide in Kanji/Kana usage.

For Danbooru purposes, the tag refers to instances of Japanese text written in Latin alphabet where Japanese characters would normally be expected. Thus character names, trademarks etc. don't warrant the tag, even if technically they contain romanised Japanese text. Any piece of dialogue, however, as well as sound effects and similar elements which would normally be expected to be understood by Japanese speakers, but are for whatever reason rendered romanised, do qualify.

Do **not** use this tag for Japanese words that have been fully incorporated into English, such as "[[sushi|sushi]]", "tsunami", or "[[sumo|sumo]]"; "senpai" and "sensei" are borderline.

The **Roman Empire** (Latin: *Imperium Rōmānum*) was the post-Republican period of ancient Rome. 

As a polity, it included large territorial holdings around the Mediterranean Sea in Europe, North Africa, and Western Asia, ruled by emperors. 

From the accession of Caesar Augustus as the first Roman emperor to the military anarchy of the 3rd century, it was a principate with Italy as the metropole of its provinces and the city of Rome as its sole capital. 

Later, the Empire was ruled by multiple emperors who shared control over the Western Roman Empire and the Eastern Roman Empire. 

[[rome (city)|rome (city)]] remained the nominal capital of both parts until AD 476 when the imperial insignia were sent to Constantinople following the capture of the Western capital of Ravenna by the Germanic barbarians under Odoacer and the subsequent deposition of Romulus Augustulus. 

The adoption of Christianity as the state church of the Roman Empire in AD 380 and the fall of the Western Roman Empire to [[germany|Germanic]] kings conventionally marks the end of classical antiquity and the beginning of [[medieval|the Middle Ages]].

Refers to the ancient Roman way of writing numbers. Likely because of the elegant style, it is still usually recognized and understood by everyday people (at least from 1 to 10), as well as frequently used on clocks.

- 1 = I
- 2 = II
- 3 = III
- 4 = IV (one below 5)
- 5 = V
- 6 = VI (one above 5)
- 7 = VII (two above 5)
- 8 = VIII
- 9 = IX
- 10 = X (can be remembered by how 2 V's form an X; 5*2=10)
- 11 = XI
- 12 = XII

- 50 = L
- 100 = C
- 500 = D
- 1000 = M

A type of [[flower|flower]] associated with romance, and it is a traditional gift given to a loved one. Each color a rose can be in has specific symbolism as well.

[[red rose|red rose]]s: Red roses are the traditional symbol for love and romance. The red rose has long symbolized beauty and perfection. A bouquet of red roses is the perfect way to express your deep feelings for someone special.

[[pink rose|pink rose]]s: As a symbol of grace and elegance, the pink rose is often given as an expression of admiration. Pink roses can also convey appreciation as well as joyfulness. Pink rose bouquets often impart a gentler meaning than their red counterparts.

[[yellow rose|yellow rose]]s: Yellow roses evokes a feeling of warmth and happiness. The warm feelings associated with the yellow rose are often akin to those shared with a true friend.

[[orange rose|orange rose]]s: Orange roses are the embodiment of desire and enthusiasm. Orange roses often symbolize passion and excitement and are an expression of fervent romance. 

[[white rose|white rose]]s: Represents purity and innocence. Can also symbolize honor and reverence. Arrangements of White Roses are used to express remembrance.

[[purple rose|purple rose]]s: With their fantastical appearance, lavender roses are a perfect symbol of enchantment. The lavender rose is also traditionally used to express feelings of love at first sight.

[[black rose|black rose]]: Black roses do not naturally occur in nature. In fiction, they can represent a tragic romance and symbolizes death, hatred, and farewell. If one is about to embark on a long journey that are unlikely to return from, they might be given a black rose as a farewell.

Other roses not seen in nature but are tagged on Danbooru include [[blue rose|blue rose]]s, [[brown rose|brown rose]]s, [[golden rose|golden rose]]s, [[green rose|green rose]]s, [[grey rose|grey rose]]s, and [[multicolored rose|multicolored rose]]s. 

Note that the Pixiv tag "バラ" (read "[[bara|bara]]"), which is literally translated as "rose", is more often used to tag any [[yaoi|yaoi]] or [[bara|bara]] content, and as such only apply this tag with the actual flower is seen.

Rosenkreuzstilette is a doujin soft game created by the indie company [erka:es]. It's known for being similar in game mechanics to the [[mega man (series)|mega man (series)]] series and also borrows elements from the [[castlevania (series)|castlevania (series)]] series. It contains nods to the Order of the Rose-Cross and is a polar opposite of the Mega Man series, with female Magi as opposed to the male Robot Masters and magical, serene and beautiful settings with a comical German horror theme as opposed to Mega Man's futuristic setting with a comical robot theme.

The game revolves around people with the gift of magic. These people are known as "Magi". For years, the Magi were feared and persecuted by the Holy Empire and the Orthodox Church, until a man named Rosenkreuz stood up to them and led his eight disciples in a war against them, ultimately sacrificing his life to have the Empire accept the Magi as part of their military. From that point, the Magi became known as RKS: Rosenkreuzstilette, the Blades of the Rose-Cross. Years had passed since then and the persecution seemed like a thing of the past, but to RKS, it was not forgotten. Eventually, RKS believed they would be the target of persecution again and that the Empire was bringing them back down and disrespecting their former leader Rosenkreuz. They decided to use their power to claim dominance and end their "persecution" once and for all, so their leader [[graf michael zeppelin|graf michael zeppelin]] commanded [[freudia neuwahl|freudia neuwahl]] to lead a rebellion against the Empire in hopes to put it in its place. A few decades later, the heroine, [[spiritia rosenberg|spiritia rosenberg]], returns home to find her friends caught up in a holy war. Knowing that the battle is already over, Spiritia disagrees with their way of doing things and, aided by [[lilli|lilli]], takes it upon herself to stop the others at RKS, eventually fighting her way up to Count Zeppelin himself. Unbeknownst to her and the rest of RKS, however, someone else is indeed pulling the strings, having RKS fight against the Empire for their own amusement...

To determine the winning number and color, a croupier (dealer) spins a wheel in one direction, then spins a ball in the opposite direction around a tilted circular track running around the circumference of the wheel. The ball eventually loses momentum and falls onto the wheel and into one of 37 (in French/European roulette) or 38 (in American roulette) colored and numbered pockets on the wheel. Payouts range from 35:1 for a single number bet down to 1:1 for an odd/even or red/black bet.

A typically circular symbol. The term is used in heraldry, but also commonly used to refer to a type of national insignia used on [[military|military]] [[aircraft|aircraft]], generally circular in shape and usually comprising concentric rings of different colours.

Notable examples:

- United States has circle with a white star, with two white or white-and-red bars on the left and right side.
- Japan has a single red circle, mostly bordered with white stylized after the Japanese flag.
- Germany has a black [[iron cross|iron cross]] with white borders.
- Britain has a blue, white, and red circle.
  - Canada, Australia, and New Zealand replace the circle with a maple leaf, a kangaroo, and a kiwi bird respectively.
- France has a red, white, and blue circle.
- Italy has a red, white, and green circle. During World War II, it has white circle bordered in black with three black fasces in it.
- Soviet Union had a five-pointed [[red star|red star]] with white border. Belarus also uses this roundel after the collapse of the USSR, while Russia added blue border between the white and red section.
- China also has a red star, but with a Chinese text meaning "8.1" and bordered by two red yellow-bordered bars.
- Taiwan and the former Republic of China uses [[kuomintag|kuomintag]] "white sun" symbol" contained within blue circle.
- Sweden has a blue circle bordered in yellow with three gold crowns in it.
- Poland has a red and white checkerboard design.
- South Korea has a red and blue yin-yang bordered with three black bars on either side.
- Israel has a blue six-pointed star on a white circle.
- Indonesia has a white red-bordered pentagon design.
- The Philippines has a blue, white, and red diamond with wings.
- Finland has a white, blue, and white circle design. Formerly, they used a blue swastika on a white circle.

Ruqun (襦裙) is a set of attire in [[hanfu|hanfu]] which consists of a short [[jacket|jacket]] worn under a [[long skirt|long skirt]].

An [[aoqun|aoqun]] is the opposite; hanfu where the top is worn over the skirt (not tucked in). 

Ruqun is however a very broad term, an umbrella term for any kind of hanfu wherein the top is tucked into the skirt. Try to use one of the more specific terms below.  Use [[ruqun|ruqun]] when none of the below categories apply.

The original **Gundam** [[mobile suit|mobile suit]] from the series [[mobile suit gundam|mobile suit gundam]]. Together with the [[guntank|guntank]] and the [[guncannon|guncannon]], it is the final mobile suit of the [[earth federation|earth federation]]'s Project V. It also serves as the [[gundam|gundam]] franchise's mascot. It is piloted by the series' protagonist, [[amuro ray|amuro ray]]. 

Extremely powerful and resilient (thanks to its experimental *Luna Titanium Alloy* or *Gundarium*), it is equipped with an advanced A.I. system that improves the combat abilities of its [[pilot|pilot]]. The model was designed by [[tem ray|tem ray]] specifically to counter the treat of [[zeon|zeon]]'s standard mobile suits, most notably the [[zaku ii|zaku ii]].

Visually, the RX-78-2 has a white, red, blue, and yellow color scheme. It also has a white [[v-fin|v-fin]] on its head unit, and is often seen carrying a couple of [[beam saber|beam saber]]s, a [[shield|shield]] and a [[beam rifle|beam rifle]]. Not the be confused with the [[gundam mk ii|gundam mk ii]], [[strike gundam|strike gundam]], [[ground gundam|ground gundam]], or [[gundam gp-01 zephyranthes|gundam gp-01 zephyranthes]].

In [[real life|real life]] it was designed by [[ookawara kunio|ookawara kunio]] and refined by [[yasuhiko yoshikazu|yasuhiko yoshikazu]] in the late 70s. (Yasuhiko designed the Gundam's face mask and color scheme.)

The first Gundam was inspired by [[mazinger z (mecha)|mazinger z (mecha)]] and the [[power armor|power armor]]s from [[starship troopers|starship troopers]].

Prior to joining the bar, she kept her hair at [[long hair|waist length]]. Later on in the series, she stops dyeing her hair and starts to regrow it again.

Ryu's workplace attire consists of a [[long dress|long]] [[green dress|green dress]] with [[juliet sleeves|juliet sleeves]] and an [[orange ribbon|orange ribbon]], a [[maid apron|white maid apron]] with matching [[maid headdress|maid headdress]], and [[black thighhighs|black tights]] with [[ankle boots|brown ankle boots]]. An [[androgynous|androgynous]] [[nijisanji|nijisanji]] [[virtual youtuber|virtual youtuber]]. Character designed by [[asasumiboochan|asasumiboochan]].

They debuted in the first wave of Nijisanji SEEDs, before later being integrated into the main Nijisanji group in December 2018. Their real name is Sengawa Midori. Despite their looks, they're of Japanese descent. They love to sing and would like to make some friends through live streaming.

#### Appearance

*See post #5596948.*

They have [[green hair|green hair]] and [[red eyes|red]]-[[purple eyes|purple eyes]]. In most situations they're depicted as being [[androgynous|androgynous]].

Although their hair is always the same color, the style it's in changes often. Sometimes it's [[short hair|short]]. Other times it's [[long hair|longer]] and tied into a [[braid|braid]]. Regardless of the style, an [[ahoge|ahoge]] is always present.

Their [[ryuushen (3rd costume)|default costume]] is inspired by traditional [[chinese clothes|chinese clothes]]. They wear a [[sleeveless|sleeveless]] [[black shirt|black]] [[crop top|crop top]], a brown [[choker|choker]], and a [[white jacket|white jacket]] usually worn [[off shoulder|off shoulder]] with sleeves going [[sleeves past fingers|past their fingertips]]. They wear black [[pants|pants]] with a traditional garment around their waist, [[black footwear|black shoes]], and multiple [[ear piercing|ear piercing]]s on both of their ears.

###### Alternate Costumes

Their [[ryuushen (1st costume)|original]] default costume appears to be even more [[chinese clothes|Chinese]] inspired.

Their [[sleeveless shirt|sleeveless shirt]] is [[white shirt|white]] with a [[red trim|red trim]]. A traditional [[multicolored jacket|"jacket"]] is [[black jacket|black jacket]] with a [[red trim|red]], [[gold trim|gold]], and [[green trim|green]] trim. Their [[pants|pants]] are red at the top and bleed into orange at the bottom.

They wear [[black footwear|black]] [[boots|boots]] have a [[gold trim|gold trim]].

In August 2020, they were shown in two new costumes.

For one thing, their hair is [[hair down|down]]. They wear a [[panda|panda]] [[animal hood|hoodie]] with a [[black shirt|black]] [[undershirt|undershirt]]. A red [[choker|choker]] rests over a [[bandaid|bandaid]] on their neck.

Another [[bandaid|bandaid]] is on their [[bandaid on cheek|right cheek]]. An [[eyepatch|eyepatch]] is over their left eye.

Its main base of operations is the [[macross quarter|macross quarter]] space warship in the Macross Frontier fleet. 

Some of its tactical units include the *Skull* Team and the all-[[meltrandi|meltrandi]] *Pixie* Team. Most of its members are former N.U.N.S. ace pilots and/or experienced Human and [[zentradi|zentradi]] veterans and soldiers.

**Sagat** (*katakana*: **サガット**, *thai*: **สกัด**) is a character in the [[street fighter|street fighter]] series. He was originally a boss character in the early editions of series. He was later turned into a regular, playable character.

Sagat won the title of Emperor/God of [[muay thai|muay thai]] from Nuah Kahn as a teenager, and became a national hero in [[thailand|thailand]]. He defended his title from a fighter named Go Hibiki, in a match that cost Sagat the use of his right eye, and cost Go his life. Go's son, [[hibiki dan|Dan]], swore revenge on Sagat.

Sagat trained [[adon (street fighter)|Adon]], and held the first World Warrior tournament to prove that he was not only the strongest Muay Thai fighter, but the strongest fighter in the world. Only one fighter managed to reach Sagat: a young martial artist named [[ryu (street fighter)|Ryu]]. Initially, Sagat was able to pin Ryu, and was sure that he was the winner of the match, even going to help Ryu up. However, Ryu became desperate to win the fight and was consumed by the Satsui no Hadou and his "[[evil ryu|evil ryu]]" side and executed the Metsu Shoryuken, grievously wounding Sagat and leaving a massive scar across his chest. Because of this event, Sagat has sworn revenge on Ryu.

He is often paired with [[aisaka taiga|aisaka taiga]] of [[toradora!|toradora!]] due to the "Tiger" in his moves written and pronounced the same way as "Taiga", as well as Taiga parodying him.

**Saint Seiya**, also known as **Saint Seiya: Knights of the Zodiac**, is a 1986 Japanese [[fantasy|fantasy]] and [[martial arts|martial arts]] action manga series created, written and illustrated by [[kurumada masami (style)|kurumada masami (style)]].

It was serialized first in [[weekly shounen jump|Weekly Shōnen Jump]] from 1986 to 1990, with the chapters collected into 28 tankōbon volumes by Shueisha. 

The story follows five mystical warriors called the "Saints" (or "Knights" in some adaptations) who fight wearing sacred armors named "Cloths", the designs of which derive from the various constellations the characters have adopted as their destined guardian symbols, and empowered by a mystical energy called "Cosmo". The Saints have sworn to defend the reincarnation of the benevolent Greek goddess [[athena (saint seiya)|athena (saint seiya)]] in her battle against other evil Olympian and Norse mythology gods who want to dominate Earth.

The manga was adapted into an anime television series by [[toei animation|toei animation]] with character designs and art by [[araki shingo|araki shingo]] that ran from 1986 to 1989, before being continued in the form of three original video animation series between 2002 and 2008. 

Four animated feature films were shown in Japanese theaters from 1987 to 1989, with a fifth in 2004 and a sixth in 2014. 

Since 2006, creator Kurumada has been publishing a sequel manga titled [[saint seiya: next dimension|saint seiya: next dimension]]. Several spin-off manga by different authors have also been created, as well as a standalone anime and original net animation.

Saint Seiya has been very successful, with over 34 million copies sold in Japan alone. The series began to be known in the west after it became popular in France]in 1988, where it was given the French name of *Les Chevaliers du Zodiaque*; this was also the first foreign release of the series. Since the early 90s the series also became very popular in Spanish-speaking countries after it was released in Spain as "Los Caballeros del Zodiaco". 

Because of its popularity many RPG, action and fighting video games based on the series have been released in the last decades.

A video game series produced by [[sega|sega]] and Red Entertainment, beginning in 1996. It consists of five main games, which are hybrid tactical RPG/dating sims, and numerous spinoffs in various genres. There are also several anime adaptations, a manga adaptation of the first game, and even live-action performances by the [[voice actor|voice actor]]s. 

The [[sakura taisen v|fifth game]] was released in America in 2010 (five years after its Japanese release) under the title ***Sakura Wars: So Long, My Love***, and was the only game in the series that released outside of Japan until [[shin sakura taisen|the reboot]] was released overseas under the title ***Sakura Wars*** in 2020. Despite this, many of the series' anime adaptations were licensed and received English releases complete with dubs - though the OVA based on V was ironically never released overseas.

An [[idolmaster cinderella girls|idolmaster cinderella girls]] character in the Cute (Pink Flower) category. She appeared in the Idolm@ster Cinderella Girls anime.

Momoka is a very elegant young 12 y.o. lady with a princess-like disposition, who acts very mature for her age. Her clothes tend to be very frilly and covered in flower motifs. She's from a wealthy upbringing.

In the tie in Cinderella Girls Theater skits, Momoka is a mature girl who appears to have a lady-like aura about her. While she often tries to act older than she is, Momoka still is a young girl at heart and is susceptible to things girls her age enjoy. She was scouted by considering herself the prize in the Production Match Festival. She regularly holds tea parties with the younger idols, and takes them very seriously. Her favorite tea seems to be “Rose Hip Tea”, although she can occasionally be distracted from it via the antics of her guests.

Momoka found a friend in [[umeki otoha|umeki otoha]], as they both shared a similar demeanor. She appears to enjoy teasing [[kamiya nao|kamiya nao]], as she notes Nao chooses her clothes and costumes with the Producer in mind. Momoka also really likes the glasses [[kamijo haruna|kamijo haruna]] gave her, and enjoys selecting kimonos with friends. She holds the Producer in very high regard and shows that she will put herself on the line in order to show him that she cares about him.

Due to her popularity, she was selected for the 8th CINDERELLA MASTER CD series, alongside [[tachibana arisu|tachibana arisu]], [[ichinose shiki|ichinose shiki]], [[katagiri sanae|katagiri sanae]], and [[shiomi syuko|shiomi syuko]].

Voiced by [[terui haruka|terui haruka]].

The sakuramon (桜紋) is a stylized depiction of a five-petaled [[cherry blossoms|cherry blossom]]. The tips of the petals often feature an indent.

It is notably used on rank and cap badges of the [[imperial japanese navy|imperial japanese navy]] and all branches of the Japan Self-Defense Forces. It frequently shows up in copyrights with a naval theme. In [[azur lane|azur lane]] it's used as the emblem of the Sakura Empire and appears on many of that nation's characters. It's also seen on several [[kantai collection|kantai collection]] characters, where it is often mistaken for a [[kikumon|kikumon]].

A gesture of greeting and respect, typically a hand raised in the air.

###### Salute Tags

- [[straight-arm salute|straight-arm salute]]
- [[two-finger salute|two-finger salute]]
- [[vulcan salute|vulcan salute]]

###### Official national forms vary from country to country:

- American: forearm at 45° angle to the forehead, blade hand with palm towards face.
- British: similar to American, but with palm facing outward.
- Straight-arm salute (also called Roman, Hitler or Nazi salute and was used by fascist or Nazi movements and governments, most notably Nazi Germany): straight arm extended forward and upwards.

###### Stylized forms appear in many [[magical girl|magical girl]] titles:

- [[sailor moon|sailor moon]] in particular popularized the "V" hand held sideways, partially framing the eye. This was later inherited by [[asamiya athena|asamiya athena]] from [[the king of fighters '96|KOF 96]] onwards
- In [[final fantasy viii|final fantasy viii]], [[rinoa heartilly|rinoa heartilly]] gestures with an upward pointing index finger.

###### Other well-known forms:

- [[palm-fist greeting|Kung fu]]: a closed fist wrapped in an open palm, often with a slight bow
- Peace/Victory: outward palm with index and middle finger extended, arm extended forward
- Love: opposing thumbs and index fingers join at the fingertips in the shape of a heart; other fingers may suggest wings

Aleksandra "Sanya" Vladimirovna Litvyak is a Night Witch of the [[501st joint fighter wing|501st joint fighter wing]], originating from Orussia and affiliated with her home unit: the Imperial Army of Orussia’s 586th Fighter regiment. Her familiar is the domestic cat. Her mild personality and nocturnal lifestyle give her a "ghost like" impression. 

Her Magic Antenna (魔導針, Madō Shin, lit. "Magic Needles") allow her to interact with radio waves. It is a type of non-visual perception that can detect objects at extreme ranges. Also can use a spell to provide guidance cues to other witches and aircraft and is able to tune in and rebroadcast radio transmissions.

Sanya based on Russian flying ace Lydia V. Litvyak, one of only two female aces of [[world war ii|world war ii]] and the only female pilot out of the pilots the witches are based on. Both share the name "White Lily of Stalingrad"; a nickname that may have been influential on the color choice of Sanya's hair.

A long, winding strip of cloth, usually thick cotton, wrapped tightly around the midriff up to the chest. Historically, samurai wore them under their kimono to resist injury.

In anime series, particularly in classic older ones, a delinquent character will be seen wearing one under their coat or unbuttoned shirt. The wrapping was a visible cue as to their general level of bad-assery.  In this form the sarashi is wound mostly around the abdomen.

Alternatively, a tomboyish girl may wear one to bind and/or flatten her breasts, especially if she is trying to pass as male.  This gradually evolved into what is nowadays the more common way of wearing a sarashi, which is in the style of a [[tube top|tube top]]; in this case, it wraps around only the chest area in a very nontraditional way, leaving the [[midriff|midriff]] bare (e.g. post #4296298, post #4076845, post #3616420, post #2644312). This sarashi style is especially seen on kendo girls and other fighters.

An upbeat girl with [[short hair|short]] [[brown hair|brown hair]] who usually wears a [[green jacket|green]] [[track jacket|athletic jacket]] decorated with buttons. Her weapon is a pair of greaves. She has an obsession with Kung fu, and even uses them in battle, similar to Lisa Silverman of Persona 2. Most of the time, she is friendly, cheerful, and energetic, but she has a short temper, especially with Yousuke. Chie, Yukiko, and Rise are unskilled at cooking, often providing the main cast with unpalatable to terribly awful dishes through the course of the story. Yousuke refers to their horrible cooking as "Mystery Food X."

Her Persona is [[tomoe (persona 4)|tomoe (persona 4)]] of The Chariot Arcanum, a muscular female figure wearing a yellow outfit reminiscent of Bruce Lee's famous tracksuit, wielding a double bladed naginata. Tomoe is shown to use both physical and low-level ice spells. Tomoe evolves into [[suzuka gongen|suzuka gongen]] after maxing out her Social Link, the one for The Chariot Arcana.

She is also one of the female characters whom the protagonist can have a romantic relationship with.

Voiced by [[horie yui|horie yui]].

A sauna is a small room or house designed as a place to experience dry or wet heat sessions, or an establishment with one or more of these and auxiliary facilities.

A sauna session can be a social affair in which the participants disrobe and sit or recline in temperatures typically between 70°C (158 °F) and 100°C (212 °F). This induces relaxation and promotes sweating.

Saunas can be divided into two basic styles: conventional saunas that warm the air or infrared saunas that warm objects. Infrared saunas may use various materials in their heating area such as charcoal, active carbon fibers, and other materials.

A musical instrument that is popular in jazz, classical, and funk music. Comes in four popular sizes (listed from smallest to largest): soprano, alto, tenor, and baritone. (Smaller and larger variations of the soprano and baritone exist, but they are very rarely used.)

[[alto saxophone|Alto]]: Most commonly used and often in small jazz groups as well as large ensembles. Most distinct feature is that the neck is straight where the mouthpiece is attached. Convenient in size for generally all player heights, standing or sitting. 

 [[tenor saxophone|Tenor]]: Slightly larger with the physical distinction being the curved neck. Second most common and can be just as essential as the alto. 

 [[baritone saxophone|Baritone]]: Largest and with a deep bass-like sound, the neck has a complete loop. The size and the weight is considerably harder to maneuver than the rest. They are less common than the prior two, but can be still seen in large wind ensembles and medium to large jazz groups to provide bass depth.

[[soprano saxophone|Soprano]]: The look and posture it is held is almost exactly like a [[clarinet|clarinet]]. Mostly used as a solo instrument in classical or orchestral environments, or in a saxophone quartet.

Artifacts made due to poor [[scan|scanning]]:

- [[binding discoloration|binding discoloration]] - The Image gets blurry as the perspective warps to either side due to the page bending
- [[bleed through|bleed through]] - Visible contour of illustrations from the opposite side of the page
- [[color halftone|color halftone]] - Visible printing dots, usually in a high definition scan

- [[scan dust|scan dust]] - Debris opacating the original illustration

The traditional style, used by middle and high school students, looks like a [[briefcase|briefcase]] with a rigid flat front and back, and a single large flap that goes over the top with a handle on the top. It may also have a shoulder strap, but this is rarely depicted. Additionally, this style of bag can also have a strap fastened on the back and can be worn like a [[backpack|backpack]].

The modern style looks like a small blue sports bag or duffel bag, with a zipper on the top and a strap on each side. The straps are typically big enough to be worn over the shoulder like a [[shoulder bag|shoulder bag]], or sometimes on the back like a [[backpack|backpack]].

The original [[old school swimsuit|old school swimsuit]] has thicker shoulder straps, vertical seams over torso and a [[school swimsuit flap|flap]] over the groin.

The [[new school swimsuit|new school swimsuit]] is identical in style to the old school swimsuit except with no flap over the groin.

The [[competition school swimsuit|competition school swimsuit]] has thinner shoulder straps, is unseamed and has no flap over the groin. It is closer in style to the more modern [[competition swimsuit|competition swimsuit]], but still in the style of a school swimsuit.

A voluntary non-political movement for young people, consisting of three major age groups: the [[cub scout|cub scout]]s between 5 to 12, the [[boy scout|boy scout]]s, usually between 10 to 18, and the Rover Scouts for those over. Parallel groups would also be created for girls, the most noteworthy being the parallel to the Boy Scouts, the [[girl scout|girl scout]]s, for those between 10 and 14.

The Scout Association of Japan also includes Beaver Scouts, for those aged between 6 and 8, and Venture Scouts, for those aged 14 and 19. In Japan, Cub Scouts are between 8 to 11, regular Scouts are between 11 and 15, and Rover Scouts are between 18 and 25.

Scouts can be easily identified by the [[scout uniform|uniform]] that they were.

A descendant of this movement is the [[pioneer movement|pioneer movement]] found in (ex-)communist countries.

The **U.N. Spacy SDF-1 (Super Dimensional Fortress One) "Macross"** is the titular [[space|space]] fortress (and [[mecha|mecha]]) from the anime [[choujikuu yousai macross|choujikuu yousai macross]] released in the 80s. 

This massive [[alien|alien]] [[spacecraft|spacecraft]] was originally ||a [[supervision army|supervision army]] Gun Destroyer that crashlanded in [[south ataria|south ataria]] island on Earth in the year 1999 (codenamed [[ass-1|ass-1]] or **Alien Space Ship One** by U.N. Spacy scientists),|| but was later repaired and reconstructed, thus becoming humanity's main defense against the [[zentradi|zentradi]].

The SDF-1 is 1.2 km long and can transform from Cruiser into [[storm attacker|storm attacker]] mode. It is equipped with a "Fold" drive that enables the ship to travel through *Super Dimension* space (or *Hyperspace*), thus making it capable of traveling several light years between different star systems in a matter of hours.

The Macross is armed with a very powerful "Super-Dimension" (hyperspace) energy cannon with a beam polarizing converging system, as well as several energy cannons, electro-magnetic rail cannons and anti-ship [[missile|missile]] launchers. 

The ship also has several [[qf-3000e|qf-3000e]] [[ghost drone|ghost drone]] fighters, [[vf-1|vf-1]] variable fighters and many [[tomahawk (destroid)|Tomahawk]], [[defender (macross)|defender (macross)]], [[spartan (destroid)|Spartan]], [[phalanx (destroid)|Phalanx]] and [[monster destroid|Monster]] [[destroid|destroid]] [[mecha|mecha]] on its multiple hangar bays.

In [[real life|real life]] the SDF-1 was designed by [[miyatake kazutaka|miyatake kazutaka]] in the early 80s. The design was inspired by the [[yamato (uchuu senkan yamato)|Yamato]] from [[uchuu senkan yamato|uchuu senkan yamato]] and the [[white base|white base]] from [[mobile suit gundam|mobile suit gundam]].

**Sega Corporation** (株式会社セガ *Kabushiki gaisha Sega*), pronounced /ˈseɪɡə/ (US/Canada/UK/New Zealand/Australia) and usually styled as **SEGA**, is a Japanese multinational [[video game|video game]] developer, publisher and hardware development company headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, with various offices around the world. 

The company started as the merger of two different coin-operated game machine companies made by Americans: *Service Games* created in Hawaii in 1940 and *Rosen Enterprises* founded in Japan in 1954. The name SEGA comes from **SE**rvice **GA**mes.

Originally a maker of video [[game console|game console]]s, it later shifted into just creating and publishing video games for other game consoles. However, in 2019 the company published a miniature version of their popular Sega Mega Drive console with several built-in games included.

SEGA is the creator of the popular [[sonic (series)|sonic (series)]] franchise.

Since 2013, it is the parent company of fellow publisher [[atlus|atlus]].

SEGA was also a major [[arcade|arcade]] operator and owned several iconic arcades in Japan.  Due to declining income, especially caused by the COVID-19 Pandemic, in 2022 they completely sold off their arcade operations division to GENDA Inc.  All remaining SEGA branded arcades to be rebranded with the "GiGO" logo (short for "Get into the Gaming Oasis").

Sega ultimately had to withdraw from the console market when it couldn't compete against [[sony|sony]]'s [[playstation 2|playstation 2]] and [[nintendo|nintendo]]'s [[gamecube|gamecube]], instead sticking to producing games. **Seisenshi Dunbine** (*Sacred Warrior Dunbine*), also known as **Aura Battler Dunbine**, is a [[mecha|mecha]] anime television series created by  [[tomino yoshiyuki|tomino yoshiyuki]] and produced by Sunrise Studios in 1983. It also had mecha designs by [[miyatake kazutaka|miyatake kazutaka]]. 

The series is notable because it was one of the first anime mecha shows that combined medieval [[fantasy|fantasy]] with [[science fiction|science fiction]] [[super robot|super robot]] and real [[robot|robot]] concepts.

The series would later inspire several OVAs, listed below
- **[[seisenshi dunbine: new story of aura battler dunbine|seisenshi dunbine: new story of aura battler dunbine]]** - a sequel set in the distant future of the original series' world.
- **[[rean no tsubasa|rean no tsubasa]]** - a standalone ONA set in a separate continuity, but featuring similar setting elements. This ONA is an adaptation of Tomino's 80s novel series of the same name, which itself is an alternate Byston Well story to Dunbine.
- **Byston Well Monogatari: Garzey no Tsubasa** - a 3-episode non-mecha fantasy OVA released in 1996, notorious for it's comically bad English dub. Also known as **Garzey's Wing**.

One thousand years ago, this menace was sealed by the hero Creation, and peace returned to the world. However, a gigantic hole suddenly opened up in the world one day, and demons appeared. Hero No. 45 (Alba) and a sadistic palace warrior (Ros) team up, and their adventure begins.

A fanmade [[m.u.g.e.n|m.u.g.e.n]] character by MUGEN author Pre-to and [[touhou|touhou]] [[original|original]] Character.

Depicted as [[hakurei reimu|Reimu]]'s predecessor. She was apparently not created with a proper given(first) name, so her name may vary. Usually portrayed as a powerful physical fighter.

She wears a [[nontraditional miko|customized]] miko uniform consisting of a one-piece skintight [[leotard|leotard]] rather than a sarashi (frequently resulting in [[sideboob|sideboob]]), sturdy [[combat boots|combat boots]], and sometimes [[hakama pants|hakama pants]] rather than a skirt.

Also, unlike Reimu, she does not wear a ribbon on the back of her head, although in some depictions, she wears one to tie her long hair together near the end. Some artists depict her as muscular and/or covered in scars.

She is usually depicted as Reimu's mother, though as a fan character her relation to Reimu on the Hakurei family tree can change with each depiction.

A very popular fanwork featuring this character is [[osana reimu|osana reimu]] and its sequel [[reireimu|reireimu]], a story about Sendai Miko, a young Reimu, and an [[ex-rumia|adult]] [[rumia|rumia]]. This version looks almost identical to Reimu herself, only taller and more endowed, and oftentimes wearing a mask of some sort.

This is a story about 212cm military otaku with "Sensha Otoko" as his handle name, who despite his huge, imposing appearance, is actually very shy, and thus no girlfriends. One day, he saves a teenage girl from being harassed, and falls in love. The [[school uniform|school uniform]] with a [[sailor collar|sailor-style collar]] worn by Japanese schoolgirls in middle school and high school. The standard uniform consists of a white [[blouse|blouse]], a [[pleated skirt|pleated skirt]], and a red [[neckerchief|neckerchief]], but there are as many variations as there are stars in the sky. 
 
Serafukus are commonly worn with a [[ribbon|ribbon]] or [[bow|bow]] in lieu of the traditional neckerchief. The line between "neckerchief" and "bow" is blurry, as the bows worn with serafukus often aren't actually dedicated bows or [[bowtie|bowties]], but rather a neckerchief tied into a bow instead of its intended scarf-like shape.
 
A serafuku always includes a [[skirt|skirt]]. If a sailor-style top is paired with shorts or another bottom, [[sailor shirt|sailor shirt]] should be used instead. In fact, sailor suits with shorts are the older, original style: in the Victorian and Edwardian eras, they were used as boys' suits, from which then the girls' uniform with a skirt was derived.

For colored serafuku tags, both the [[shirt|shirt]] and [[skirt|skirt]] must match in color to apply, but not the neckwear or [[sailor collar|sailor collar]].

[[sailor dress|sailor dress]]es should not be tagged as serafuku.

A [[cyberpunk|cyberpunk]] [[horror (theme)|horror (theme)]] multimedia project including an anime series by Triangle Staff, a [[playstation 1|playstation 1]] game by Pioneer LCD, plus a number of soundtracks and artbooks.

By far the most widely known Lain product is the anime, released 1998. The game was released later the same year, although its scenario had been created first. [[abe yoshitoshi|abe yoshitoshi]] designed the characters for both, and mostly his art can be found in the art books, on the CD sleeves, etc. Various Lain products feature small amounts of [[4koma|4koma]] strips and manga pages by ABe, even one nine-page story that makes reference to both the anime and the game.

Due to Serial Experiments Lain's non-linear storytelling (even the anime is divided into "layers" instead of "episodes"), the plot is hard to summarize. Main themes include virtual world vs. reality, communication, loneliness, psychology, parapsychology, cyberculture and theology.

**Setsubun** (節分, lit. "seasonal division") is the last day of winter in the Japanese calendar. It usually corresponds to February 3rd in the Gregorian calendar.

A digital card battle game by [[cygames|cygames]]. The game is divided into a story campaign spread across multiple worlds sci-fi or fantasy alike and a PVP mode featuring various tournaments in addition to "tie-in" events (collaboration events) between different franchises.

To begin, one must choose one of eight classes to play with (whichever one you choose can be changed later) each with a different playstyle and mechanics. Each class has access to a personal selection of cards in addition to a general pool (which is counted as a ninth class not playable on its own). 

Each player can mulligan their starting hand to find better cards in case of a bad draw. The player who goes first gets 2 evolution points, and the player who goes second gets 3 evolution points. 

At the start of their turn, each player draws one card from their deck and places it in their hand. The player who goes second draws two cards on the first turn. Cards in the deck can't be seen during battle.

#### Media
Shadowverse was released in June 2016. An [[shadowverse (anime)|anime adaptation]] by Zexcs aired from April 2020 to March 2021. A second anime series titled [[shadowverse flame|Shadowverse Flame]] is currently being aired following the events of the first one after a three-year time skip.

The "Traditional Reporter of Fantasy". First appeared as an opponent (and later, playable character) in the ninth [[touhou|touhou]] game, *[[phantasmagoria of flower view|phantasmagoria of flower view]]*. She has since reappeared in other games as a playable character, and often appears in the various print works.

Aya is a crow tengu, and has the ability to manipulate the wind in addition to the exceptional sight and long-range hearing possessed by most tengu. She is also absurdly fast, perhaps even the fastest in Gensokyo. She runs, reports, and photographs for her own newspaper, the *[[bunbunmaru|bunbunmaru]] Shinbun*. However, the publication is notorious for being filled with rumors, gossip, and personal opinion. 

She is the rival of fellow journalist [[himekaidou hatate|himekaidou hatate]], who runs the *Kakashi Nenpo* ("Kakashi Spirit Times"). She was (and still is) also often depicted in fanworks as a friend to (or the superior of) the white wolf tengu [[inubashiri momiji|inubashiri momiji]], one of the guardians of Youkai Mountain. However, it was revealed in [[double spoiler|double spoiler]] that the two actually dislike one another. 

Her catchphrase is "[[ayaya~|ayaya~]]".

#### Appearance
Aya has [[red eyes|red eyes]] and [[black hair|black hair]] of varying lengths. Her outfits have changed somewhat throughout her various appearances, but by far her most common outfit is a small [[red hat|red]] [[tokin hat|tokin hat]] with two strings of [[pom pom (clothes)|pom poms]] attached, a [[white shirt|white]] [[collared shirt|collared shirt]] with a [[black ribbon|black ribbon]] tied around the collar, [[frilled skirt|frilled]] [[black skirt|black skirt]], [[black socks|black]] [[kneehighs|knee-high socks]], and [[red footwear|red]] [[tengu-geta|tengu-geta]]. She often carries around an old [[camera|camera]], a [[notebook|notebook]] and [[calligraphy brush|calligraphy brush]], and a [[hauchiwa|hauchiwa]] (a leaf-shaped fan).

Due to variations in depiction, she may also have [[pointy ears|pointy ears]] or long, [[black wings|black]] [[bird wings|feathered wings]]. Her outfit may also sport an [[armband|armband]] or a tan, [[leaf print|leaf-patterned stripe]] motif. Other times, she may be shown wearing a completely different outfit, such as the [[kourindou tengu costume|kourindou tengu costume]] from [[curiosities of lotus asia|CoLA]] or her combination of a [[cabbie hat|cabbie hat]], [[necktie|tie]], and [[suit jacket|suit jacket]] from [[forbidden scrollery|forbidden scrollery]] which should be tagged as [[shameimaru aya (newsboy)|shameimaru aya (newsboy)]].

Shana is the main heroine of the [[shakugan no shana|shakugan no shana]] media franchise.

She is the Flame Haze bound as contractor to the Crimson God [[alastor (shakugan no shana)|Alastor]]; their job is to stop other Crimson Denizens from running amok. The series begins when she gets involved with [[sakai yuuji|sakai yuuji]], an ordinary high schooler who's been imbued with a powerful artifact that can't fall into the wrong hands. Shana becomes his protector, and gradually more like a partner as he learns to fight; in turn, sharing daily life with Yuuji gradually brings Shana out of her shell (she's always lived in the world of Flame Haze, to the point of not even bothering with a *name* till Yuuji gives her one).

Shana is often seen wearing a [[pendant|pendant]], the vessel of Alastor, and wielding the [[sword|sword]] she's named after, the Nietono no Shana. She sports [[long hair|long hair]] ([[black hair|black]] normally, [[red hair|red]] with a flame effect when she's fighting), an [[ahoge|ahoge]], and [[zettai ryouiki|zettai ryouiki]]. Her closest connections are with Alastor (partner and advisor), Yuuji (love interest), [[yoshida kazumi|yoshida kazumi]] (friend/love rival), and [[wilhelmina carmel|wilhelmina carmel]] (mother figure). Her love for [[melon bread|melon bread]] is the stuff of legend.

While not the first [[tsundere|tsundere]] character, Shana is rivalled only by [[tohsaka rin|tohsaka rin]] for most famous one.

[[touhou|touhou]] character. The physical component for [[alice margatroid|alice margatroid]]'s spellcard "Eerily Luminous Shanghai Doll" in [[perfect cherry blossom|perfect cherry blossom]] / [[immaterial and missing power|immaterial and missing power]], as well as her familiar in [[imperishable night|imperishable night]].

Shanghai is a very popular supporting character (or artifact) in [[touhou|touhou]] fan art depicting Alice.

Some comic artists give the [[doll|doll]] a personality and feelings of its own, making it a "master doll" that helps control the lesser dolls. Others show it as Alice's primary magically-controlled "puppet". These points of view can be mixed, possibly to give an impression of Alice "debating with herself" through doll use, reminiscent of the way ventriloquists use puppets. Sometimes she/it is even depicted as lacking "doll" traits entirely, resembling a [[minigirl|minigirl]].

Another view is that Shanghai is a type or class of magical dolls rather than an individual doll. This is based on the fact that several Shanghai dolls are seen simultaneously in [[perfect cherry blossom|perfect cherry blossom]].

Canonically, Shanghai, like all the rest of Alice's dolls, is a mindless drone that requires direct supervision for all but the most basic of autonomous action, despite Alice's ongoing efforts to create a truly sapient construct. When a fanwork depicts Alice finally succeeding, Shanghai is usually the subject.
