A [[straight-on|forward-facing]] style of character sprite popular in visual novels. They are commonly (but not always) [[full body|full body]], [[standing|standing]], and feature a [[simple background|simple background]].

Tachi-e originated as character art in [[visual novel|visual novel]]s and adventure games. Often this is a [[looking at viewer|front-facing]] [[game cg|character sprite]] used during conversations with various prepared expressions and poses that can be switched as it flows. It does not strictly require your character to be standing, nor be [[full body|full body]] (e.g. from the [[cowboy shot|knee]] or [[upper body|waist]] up), as long as art is reusable enough - it should qualify.

Aside from the regular tachi-e used in story mode, many gacha games' skin illustration will also have a tachi-e aesthetic, thus they sometimes also come with a [[faux figurine|faux figurine]] counterpart, usually being its evolved form. A clean character art removed from a faux figurine will also likely become a tachi-e if the character is standing, if they're sitting it's [[invisible chair|invisible chair]] instead.

When tagging, use the following rule of thumb: if you can slap an image onto the random background, add a textbox and the result will look like [[fake screenshot|fake screenshot]] it should probably be considered a Tachi-e.

Tachi-e is **not** applicable if image:

- Has more than one instance of the character ([[turnaround|turnaround]]s, [[reference sheet|reference sheet]]s, [[multiple views|multiple views]], [[variations|variations]], [[expressions|expressions]], etc...): post #3490670, post #2195716, post #3213462, post #2538995, post #2288278
- Has non [[simple background|simple]] or non [[transparent background|transparent background]]s ([[zoom layer|zoom layer]]s, [[gradient background|gradient background]], etc..): post #2925837 (vs post #2951458), post #4133229 (vs post #4133230), post #4028183, post #4151481
- Is a [[character profile|character profile]] or featuring character [[stats|stats]]
- Is a [[faux figurine|faux figurine]] or a [[dakimakura (medium)|dakimakura (medium)]]
- Has a tachi-e within [[screenshot|screenshot]]s or [[fake screenshot|fake screenshot]]s: post #818170,  post #1713628
- Has an extra [[outline|outline]]: post #3589935 (vs post #3589913)

A country located on the titular island of Taiwan in East Asia. As a country, it was established by [[chiang kai-shek|chiang kai-shek]] and various [[kuomintang|kuomintang]]-affiliated Chinese after the Republic of China was [[chinese civil war|defeated]] by [[mao zedong|mao zedong]]'s [[china|Communist China]] and evacuated to the island. The state still serving as the continuity of the Republic of China and still using the same official name of "Republic of China" as when the state ruled mainland China.

The political status of Taiwan is complex, with the People's Republic of China claiming sovereignty over the island under the One-China Policy and refusing diplomatic relations with any country that officially recognizes Taiwan. Taiwan itself, meanwhile, is politically divided between the current ruling "Pan-Green Coalition" lead by the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP), which seeks to relinquish the claim on mainland China and officially become an independent country as Taiwan, and the "Pan-Blue Coalition" lead by the Kuomintang Party, which maintains its claim as the sole and legitimate government of the entirety of China.

This tag can be applied if the post features the [[republic of china flag|republic of china flag]], or features [[real world location|real world location]]s in Taiwan. The fifth main entry in the [[tales of (series)|Tales Series]], as well as the first 3D entry. Released [[2003|2003]] for the [[gamecube|Nintendo GameCube]] in Japan and then in America the subsquent year, and then ported to the [[playstation 2|playstation 2]] (in Japan only) with a small amount of extra content. Notable for being the series' first major hit in the west thanks to [[nintendo|nintendo]]'s involvement in the game's localization, as well as the dearth of RPGs on the GameCube at the time. In addition, a 12-episode OVA adaptation by [[ufotable|ufotable]] was released sporadically from [[2007|2007]] to [[2012|2012]].

Tales of Symphonia follows 17-year-old Lloyd Irving's quest to keep his childhood friend and Chosen of Mana, Colette Brunel, safe on her journey to save the world of Sylvarant. This quest becomes an adventure through multiple worlds in a struggle to stop an endless cycle.

Tales of Symphonia takes place 4000 years before [[tales of phantasia|tales of phantasia]]. The game received a sequel, [[tales of symphonia knight of ratatosk|tales of symphonia knight of ratatosk]], in [[2008|2008]].

[[pokemon|pokemon]] #663 in the National PokéDex, a dual-type Fire/Flying Pokémon. 

It evolves from [[fletchinder|fletchinder]] starting at level 35. It is the final form of [[fletchling|fletchling]]. 

Talonflame is an avian Pokémon that closely resembles a falcon. Its plumage is predominantly red-orange, with gray underparts and black tips on its long, pointed wings. Ovular orange spots dot its underside, and flame patterns mark the boundaries between colors on its body. Large yellow talons extend from the shaggy feathers on its legs. Talonflame has a pointed crest atop its head and a black and yellow mask-like pattern around its eyes. Its black beak is hooked with a yellow cere. It also has long black tail-feathers marked with three yellow "v"-shapes. The tail ends in two points and has another feather sticking out of the base on each side, giving the impression of the fletching on the end of an arrow. 

Japanese Name: **Fiarrow**

One observed custom during the festival is to write wishes on small slips of paper called [[tanzaku|tanzaku]] and hang them on [[bamboo|bamboo]]s. On Danbooru, the tanabata tag refers to this custom.

Tanabata originates from the [[qixi festival|qixi festival]], written the same way. When Qixi made its way to Japan, it quickly got localized and was fused with several other local traditions, notably another folklore about the Tanabata-tsume (棚機津女), hence the reading "Tanabata", and the practice of hanging tanzuku on bamboos. 

Therefore, although written the same way, the terms should not be used interchangeably, Qixi applies strictly to the traditional Chinese version and Tanabata strictly the traditional Japanese version.

A **tangzhuang** (Simplified Chinese: 唐装) is a kind of pseudo-traditional Chinese [[jacket|jacket]], typically with a [[mandarin collar|mandarin collar]] .

It originated at the end of the Qing Dynasty (1644-1911) as an evolution of the Manchurian *magua*, which had been adopted by the Han Chinese during the [[qing dynasty|qing dynasty]]. At that time, only noblemen, aristocracy and government officials wore it, however, in modern times it was eventually adopted by common people. This kind of clothing is often seen as a national costume for men, although women wear it as well.

A tank's cupola is a raised, armored structure on the roof of a [[tank|tank]]/armored vehicle or [[tank turret|tank turret]] that often carries observation devices and has a [[hatch|hatch]]. 

Tanks of WW2 often had large cupolas on their turrets to allow space for periscopes or windows to give a crew member, often the commander, a much better view outside the vehicle. Usually they were also the most logical place for the commander's hatch, as it would allow them to stand partially outside the vehicle for a better view or to operate a top-mounted [[machine gun|machine gun]]. As technology progressed and allowed for smaller periscopes and later cameras, cupolas became shorter and smaller, to the point that some modern vehicles don't have any at all.

The Japanese name for the Japanese raccoon dog. In Japanese folklore, a tanuki is a playful shape-shifting [[traditional youkai|traditional youkai]].

Not to be confused for the [[raccoon|raccoon]], which looks similar to the tanuki but is not the same animal. A key difference is their fur color: tanuki tend to have brown fur while raccoons have grey fur.

The words "tanuki" (狸), "mujina" (貉), and "mami" (猯) were historically confused in Japan. "Mujina" and "mami" used to mean [[badger|badger]]s in some areas, while on the other areas these terms used to mean raccoon dogs. There are some areas in which badgers were called tanuki.

In folklore, a type of tanuki called the *mamedanuki* (豆狸) sports comically [[huge testicles|huge testicles]]. "Shigaraki ware":[http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shigaraki_ware], a type of traditional Japanese pottery, often depicted these tanuki. The statues depicted a mamedanuki as he transforms (or fails to transform) into an errand boy going out to buy [[sake|sake]] at a liquor shop.

Tarot is a set of [[card|card]]s originally designed to be used as [[playing card|playing card]]s, but which was later adopted by occultists as a means of divination. A typical tarot deck consists of 78 cards, divided into two groups: the Minor Arcana and the Major Arcana.

The Minor Arcana consists of 56 cards divided into four suits: swords, wands (batons), cups, and pentacles (coins). Each suit has ten numbered cards and four court cards: Kings, Queens, Knights, and Pages.

The Major Arcana, or trump cards, consists of 22 cards without suits:

- 0. [[the fool (tarot)|the fool (tarot)]]†
- 1. [[the magician (tarot)|the magician (tarot)]]
- 2. [[the high priestess (tarot)|the high priestess (tarot)]]
- 3. [[the empress (tarot)|the empress (tarot)]]
- 4. [[the emperor (tarot)|the emperor (tarot)]]
- 5. [[the hierophant (tarot)|the hierophant (tarot)]]
- 6. [[the lovers (tarot)|the lovers (tarot)]]
- 7. [[the chariot (tarot)|the chariot (tarot)]]
- 8. [[justice (tarot)|justice (tarot)]] or [[strength (tarot)|strength (tarot)]]‡
- 9. [[the hermit (tarot)|the hermit (tarot)]]
- 10. [[wheel of fortune (tarot)|wheel of fortune (tarot)]]
- 11. [[justice (tarot)|justice (tarot)]] or [[strength (tarot)|strength (tarot)]]‡
- 12. [[the hanged man (tarot)|the hanged man (tarot)]]
- 13. [[death (tarot)|death (tarot)]]
- 14. [[temperance (tarot)|temperance (tarot)]]
- 15. [[the devil (tarot)|the devil (tarot)]]
- 16. [[the tower (tarot)|the tower (tarot)]]
- 17. [[the star (tarot)|the star (tarot)]]
- 18. [[the moon (tarot)|the moon (tarot)]]
- 19. [[the sun (tarot)|the sun (tarot)]]
- 20. [[judgement (tarot)|judgement (tarot)]]
- 21. [[the world (tarot)|the world (tarot)]]

† The Fool is unnumbered and not considered a trump card in traditional decks. It may be numbered 0 or 22 in decks designed for fortune-telling.
‡ In traditional decks, Justice is the 8th card and Strength is the 11th card. Starting in the early 20th century, they swapped positions in many fortune-telling decks.

A tate-eboshi (烏帽子, lit. "standing eboshi cap") is a tall, straight hat worn by Japanese male aristocrats since the "Heian Period":[http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heian_period]. Afterwards, various types of eboshi were born, e.g. *Kazaori eboshi (Samurai eboshi), Okina eboshi*, etc. *Tate eboshi* is the best-known one. This headdress came about in the [Heian period](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heian_period) based on headgear known as a *hashiha-kouburi* (圭冠).

Kanmuri are official hats worn in the imperial court and eboshi are casual headdresses worn by the nobility and it was also worn by the normal people. The Mikado never uses an eboshi. **Danbooru currently does not distinguish *eboshi* from ancient Japanese *kanmuri* (冠).**

Physically, the kanmuri stands out thanks to the "koji (巾子)", a cylindrical shape that stands upright from the top of the headwear, and the "ei (纓)", string-shaped cloth which hangs down from the rear of the headwear towards the wearer's back. The Japanese at the time when kanmuri were still simple sack-like shapes had a topknot on their head. They wore kanmuri by putting the topknot through a tube and binding the root of the topknot wearing this sack and letting the rest of the string hang down their backs. The terms "koji" and "ei", which were used even when the shape and quality of the kanmuri changed, serve as a reminder of this older form. 

Notably worn by [[mononobe no futo|mononobe no futo]] and [[soga no tojiko|soga no tojiko]] of the [[touhou|touhou]] series.

**Tate no Yuusha no Nariagari** (transl. *The Rising of the Shield Hero*) is a 2013 to present isekai light novel series by Yusagi Aneko that was originally published as a web novel series. The series has a 2014 to present manga adaptation and a winter 2019 anime.

The series follows the twenty-year-old college student [[iwatani naofumi|iwatani naofumi]] who was summoned to a fantasy world along with three other young men in their teens to early twenties. The four were summoned as heroes to save the country from periodic mass appearances of monsters, an event they refer to as a "wave." Each was equipped with one of four legendary weapons: Sword, Bow, Spear, and Shield.

From the onset Naofumi as the Hero of the Shield is treated differently from the other three, with people treating him coldly, spreading rumors about him, and refusing to group with him. His situation greatly worsens and he is shunned by nearly everyone when the only person who choose to group with him falsely accuses him of raping her. Outcasted, but unable to escape his situation, he eventually is convinced to purchase a slave to make up for his lack of offensive ability. Lacking proper funds he purchases a young demi-human girl named [[raphtalia|raphtalia]]. Together, Naofumi desperately tries to improve his combat ability in preparation for the next impending wave of monsters.

A comical depiction of crying or tears. Very similar to [[sweatdrop|sweatdrop]]. This tag is not meant to specify when there's one tear versus when there's more than one. Usually there is never more than one on a character's face.

Basically, teardrop is used when the tear is drawn on for comedic purposes, rather than to actually represent happiness/sadness/pain/pleasure/etc. They usually have a specific color, rather than being transparent like real tears, and are usually connected directly to the eyes. A teardrop may also accompany [[yawning|yawning]].

Rule of thumb: if the character appears to be actually crying, or the teardrop is transparent, it is usually *not* a teardrop. For all other instances of shedding tears that don't properly meet the requirements for teardrop, use [[tears|tears]] instead.

For non-comedic pictures with a single teardrop, use [[single tear|single tear]].

A phrase coined by the [[voice actor|voice actor]] [[hikasa youko|hikasa youko]], a combination of the onomatopoiea "tehe" for giggle and "pero" for sticking the [[tongue out|tongue out]].

It is often rendered with a star 「てへぺろ☆」; the full emoticon is 「てへぺろ☆(・ω<)」, from [her 2009 blog post](http://blog.livedoor.jp/hiyonikki/archives/844295.html) 

The archetypical facial expression and pose for *tehepero* incorporates a cheeky grin with [[tongue out|tongue out]], a [[one eye closed|wink]], and either one [[arm up|arm up]] behind the head (the [[k-on!|k-on!]] version, see post #784089) or a [[v|v]] hand sign raised to the face ([[hikasa youko|hikasa youko]] version, see post #838257 or [photo of her](https://twitter.com/_higetter_/status/253411516223721472) on Koyama Tsuyoshi's twitter)

The pose is usually used in the Japanese pop culture as a way for the character to cover their mistake and brush it off with a cute expression.

Since [[one eye closed|winking]] and sticking the [[tongue out|tongue out]] are both common facial expressions, an image should only be considered a reference to *tehepero* and tagged as such if the complete *tehepero* pose is emulated, or if a reference is made explicitly in text (i.e. 「てへぺろ」 in speech or sfx). If the character is tapping their head while winking and sticking their tongue out, use [[dojikko pose|dojikko pose]] instead; if they're touching their head with both hands with both eyes closed, use [[ah eto... bleh (meme)|ah eto... bleh (meme)]].

**Tekken Tag Tournament 2** (鉄拳タッグトーナメント2) is a fighting game in the Tekken series and the successor to [[1999|1999]]'s [[tekken tag tournament|tekken tag tournament]]. Developed and Published by [[bandai namco|bandai namco]], the game was released in Japanese arcades on September 14, 2011, with the console version being released on September 11, [[2012|2012]] for the [[play station 3|PS3]] & [[xbox 360|xbox 360]] and on November 18, 2012 for the [[wii u|wii u]]. 

Unlike the original Tekken Tag Tournament, Tekken Tag Tournament 2 features a storyline although it is still not the series canon. Just like last time, it is more of a "dream match", giving fans the opportunity to play as almost every character in the series up to that point, including some of those that had apparently been missing in the main Tekken storyline, in addition to the character roster of [[tekken 6|tekken 6]].

In "Fight Lab", Violet is working on a new version of Combot. As soon as Combot is complete, Violet begins its simulation test. After the simulation test, the Combot explodes and destroys the lab. Violet decides to use the other functioning Combot to complete the tests. After Combot completes five tests, Violet kidnaps Jin, Kazuya and Heihachi for Combot's final test. Combot apparently has the upper hand, but Jin transforms into his devil form and destroys it. Violet blows up the Combot, presumably taking the Mishima bloodline with it, and says, "Excellent!"

The Russian telnyashka is a [[white shirt|white]] [[undershirt|undershirt]] that is horizontally [[striped shirt|striped]] in various colors and which may be [[sleeveless shirt|sleeveless]] or not. It was originally adopted by the Imperial Russian Navy in the 19th century and spread to other Soviet units during and after the Second World War. This iconic uniform garment continues to be worn today, particularly by the Navy, the  Airborne Troops ([[vdv|vdv]]) and the  Naval Infantry. 

The color of the horizontal stripes traditionally signify different troops:
- Dark blue - Navy
- Black - Naval Infantry
- Light blue - VDV paratroopers
- Light green - Border Troops

A 2007 original [[super robot|super robot]] [[mecha|mecha]] anime series animated by [[gainax|gainax]] and co-produced by [[aniplex|aniplex]] and [[konami|konami]]. Best known for its over-the-top plot, action sequence, along with its ridiculously huge mecha.

#### Plot summary

In the distant future, people build their homes and raise domestic animals in subterranean caverns. As a result, they live in fear of the occasional earthquake and cave-in, and have been for hundreds of years. Jeeha is one such village.

One day, a boy named [[simon (ttgl)|simon (ttgl)]] happens to find a small, shiny drill while digging to expand the village. At the same time, [[kamina (ttgl)|kamina (ttgl)]], a guy who believes that there is another land above the village, persuades a gangster to break through the ceiling in order to leave the cavern. Suddenly, an earthquake occurs and the ceiling collapses, followed by a big [[robot|robot]] breaking through the ceiling.

Kamina is now sure that there is a world above them. Recklessly, he begins to fight against the robot. At that moment, another person appears from the land above. It is a girl by the name of [[yoko littner|Yoko]]. With a [[rifle|rifle]] in hand, she had been tracking the robot. However, all she could do was distract it. Then, Simon shows what he had found to Kamina and Yoko. It's a mysterious robot whose head is also its body.

A Japanese [[traditional youkai|traditional youkai]], generally seeing wearing the clothing of the "yamabushi":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamabushi] - practitioners of Shugendou ([[tokin hat|tokin hat]], yuigesa/[[pom pom (clothes)|pom-pommed]] sash, [[shakujou|shakujou]], etc). A sport usually played between two players (singles) or between two teams of two players each (doubles). Each player uses a racket that is strung to strike a hollow rubber ball covered with felt over a net into his opponent's court. The object of the game is to play the ball in such a way that the opponent is not able to play a good return. Tennis is an Olympic sport and is played at all levels of society at all ages. The sport can be played by anyone who can hold a racket, including people in wheelchairs.

The player gets 15 points each time his opponent either misses the ball, strikes the ball to the outside of the court or the net, or fails to serve the ball twice. The player can only get a maximum of 40 points. Upon winning a break point, the player wins the game and this continues after the player wins 6 games or 2 more games than his opponent, thus winning the set.

If the game system is best of 3, the player must win 2 sets to win the match. If it is best of 5, he must win 3 sets to do exactly the same.

Rin is a girl who was born with short malformed arms that were subsequently amputated. Her birth defect was due to the side effects of the drug [thalidomide](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thalidomide.) To make up for her lack of arms, she uses her feet to accomplish everyday tasks with surprising dexterity. She has short red hair and dark green eyes, and wears a boy's uniform to avoid awkward situations that would arise from using her feet while wearing a skirt. 

Rin is a painter and has a penchant for getting lost in her thoughts. 

She is [[ibarazaki emi|ibarazaki emi]]'s friend and roommate.

*The Iron of Yin and Yang: Buront's Entrance into Gensoukyou* (Japanese: 東方陰陽鉄 ～ブロントさんが幻想郷入り～) is a series of [[touhou|touhou]] videos made using [[rpg maker|rpg maker]] and uploaded to NicoNico Douga, featuring crossover elements from the MMORPG *[[final fantasy xi|final fantasy xi]]*. These videos became surprisingly popular, and gained enough of a following to spawn a significant amount of fanart based on its themes.

Short summary: After saving his linkshell from a King Behemoth, an [[elvaan|elvaan]] [[knight (final fantasy)|knight (final fantasy)]] named [[buront|buront]] is catapulted into [[gensokyo|gensokyo]], landing directly in [[hakurei reimu|Reimu]]'s donation box. From there, Buront becomes part of several new adventures, encounters old enemies, and generally annoys people with his knightly boasting.

This tag should apply wherever scenes or characters from the video series are depicted, or when the artist's comments and/or tags (on pixiv, for example) indicate the relation.

#### Characters of *The Iron of Yin and Yang*

- [[buront|buront]], an [[elvaan|elvaan]] [[knight (final fantasy)|knight (final fantasy)]] who frequently boasts, and who has an unusual manner of speech that must be read to be understood.
- [[kitanai ninja|kitanai ninja]], a.k.a. That Dirty Ninja, a [[hume|hume]] [[ninja (final fantasy)|ninja (final fantasy)]] who harbors a grudge against Buront. His eyes are usually obstructed from view or [[bar censor|black-bar]] censored.
- [[naitou|naitou]], a Hume [[paladin (final fantasy)|paladin (final fantasy)]] with blond hair, who laughs ("lololol") with exceptional frequency.
- [[final tatsuya|final tatsuya]], another Elvaan. Frequently seen in the company of [[izayoi sakuya|Sakuya]].
- [[sumitaru|sumitaru]], a [[tarutaru|tarutaru]] [[black mage (final fantasy)|black mage (final fantasy)]]
- Usuhime, a Hume [[white mage (final fantasy)|white mage (final fantasy)]]
- Nekokari, a [[mithra (ff11)|mithra (ff11)]] [[ranger (final fantasy)|ranger (final fantasy)]]
- Tsuufuu, a red-haired Elvaan [[thief (final fantasy)|thief (final fantasy)]]
- [[fu-ha jin|fu-ha jin]], Kitanai Ninja's musclehead lackey. (borrowed from [[ryuuko no ken|ryuuko no ken]])
- [[ryu-san|ryu-san]], a Hume [[dragoon (final fantasy)|dragoon (final fantasy)]] with a resemblance to [[kain highwind|kain highwind]], often seen with [[mystia lorelei|Mystia]]

**The Legend of Zelda** (ゼルダの伝説, *Zelda no Densetsu*) is a high fantasy action-adventure video game series developed and published by [[nintendo|nintendo]] and created by the famous game designer [[miyamoto shigeru|Shigeru Miyamoto]].

The gameplay consists of a mixture of action, adventure, puzzle solving, role-playing, and occasional platforming, stealth, and racing elements. The series centers around [[link|link]], the sole playable character and hero, and is usually set in the land of Hyrule. Link is often given the task of rescuing [[princess zelda|princess zelda]] from [[ganondorf|ganondorf]], the primary villain of the series.

The story commonly involves a relic known as the [[triforce|triforce]], a set of three golden triangles of omnipotence. The hero in each game is not always the same iteration of Link, although the same character sometimes appears across multiple games.

A game in [[the legend of zelda|the legend of zelda]] series, released on September 26, 2024.

Announced in the "June 18, 2024 Nintendo Direct (26:16 mark)":[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kX3BkD5PVUM&t=1576s], it is the first mainline *Zelda* title to feature [[princess zelda|princess zelda]] herself and not [[link|link]] as the main character. She previously was the protagonist in the Philips CD-i spin-offs *[[zelda: the wand of gamelon|zelda: the wand of gamelon]]* and *Zelda's Adventure*.

Her gameplay differs from that of Link's, per her association with the Triforce of Wisdom. The trailer shows her wielding a new staff, the [[tri rod|tri rod]], and making use of its powers, including making copies (Echoes) of objects and even enemies. She is accompanied on her journey by [[tri (zelda)|tri (zelda)]].

Sixteenth entry in the [[the legend of zelda|the legend of zelda]] series.

The game's storyline is the earliest in Zelda continuity, preceding The [[the legend of zelda: the minish cap|Minish Cap]]. Skyward Sword follows an incarnation of the series protagonist [[link|link]] who was raised in a society above the clouds known as Skyloft. After his closest childhood friend, [[princess zelda|Zelda]], is swept into the land below the clouds by demonic forces, Link does whatever it takes to save her, traveling between Skyloft and the surface below while battling the dark forces of the self-proclaimed "Demon Lord", [[ghirahim|ghirahim]].

**THE MOON STUDIO** was a creative studio established by [[virtual youtuber|virtual youtuber]] [[kaguya luna|kaguya luna]] and illustrator [[mika pikazo|mika pikazo]] in fall 2018.

The studio's name and image was built around its main talent, Kaguya Luna, whose name references the moon. She debuted in December 2017, and the small team behind her channel would later help found the studio.

After its founding, the first new talent would debut under the studio in early 2018, [[pinky pop hepburn|pinky pop hepburn]], with a familiar design by [[mika pikazo|mika pikazo]], the same artist behind Kaguya Luna's design. She, alongside Luna, were intended to be a part of a new group called the [[kotodama tribe|kotodama tribe]], consisting of six more VTubers who never ended up coming to fruition.

It announced the end of its activities in fall 2019, after which Kaguya Luna and Pinky Pop Hepburn reverted back to their original company, Vic inc. while each maintained their music contracts with Sony Music's [[sacra music|sacra music]] and the label Anarchic Record respectively. By the end of 2021, both talent had disappeared.

Has grossed over US$1.36 billion in the box office worldwide against a US$100 million budget and been setting records in the process (including the highest-grossing film based on a video game and the first film based on a video game to gross at least US$1 billion, the second highest-grossing film of 2023, and the fourth-highest-grossing animated film) despite mixed reviews from critics which are being offset by positive audience response. A [[honkai (series)|honkai (series)]] character, appearing in [[honkai impact 3rd|honkai impact 3rd]] and [[benghuai xueyuan|benghuai xueyuan]]. She is a clone of [[kallen kaslana|kallen kaslana]] made by [[otto apocalypse|otto apocalypse]], dubbed as A-310, in an attempt to bring Kallen back. As a test body, A-310 has excellent Houkai resistance and strong powers. She was born on March 28, 1972. In the world of [[honkai impact 3rd|honkai impact 3rd]], she was made using the genes of the Honkai Beast Vishnu alongside Kallen's DNA.

Being part of the A Series clones, A-310 did not know her identity and Otto told her that he would tell her anything she needed if she completed the tests. At the final test, A-310 was told by Otto to defeat and kill [[amber (honkai impact)|A-303]]. A-310 defeated A-303, but refused to kill the other clone. As a result, Otto believed that A-310 could potentially be Kallen's reincarnation due to the empathy she showed, along with her incredible combat capabilities. However, he stated that science is different from reincarnation. Otto would later adopt A-310 and call her Theresa.

Otto later gave the 11th Divine Key, [[oath of judah|oath of judah]] to Theresa.

In both [[honkai impact 3rd|honkai impact 3rd]] and [[benghuai xueyuan|benghuai xueyuan]], Theresa Apocalypse is the principal of St. Freya Academy and best friend of [[cecilia schariac|cecilia schariac]], and the World's Cutest Valkyrie (in her words).

A container or vessel designed to keep liquids hot or cold for long periods of time.  This is accomplished by the container being composed of two flasks, one within the other, and joined at the neck. The gap between the two flasks is partially evacuated of air to produce a near vacuum which helps to impede the transfer of heat between the contents and the outside.  These are also known as a vacuum flasks (or vacuum bottles), though these should not be confused with Büchner flasks (used in laboratory vacuum filtration), which are also known as vacuum flasks.

The **Thompson** is a .45 caliber American [[submachine gun|submachine gun]], invented by John Talifero Thompson in 1919. It was initially marketed to the law enforcement officers as "Thompson's anti-bandit gun", but eventually became widely associated with the [[mafia|mafia]]. The [[weapon|weapon]] earned various nicknames such as the "Tommy Gun," the "Trench Broom," the "Trench Sweeper," the "Chicago Piano," the "Chicago Typewriter," and the "Chopper." The [[gun|Thompson]] was adopted by the US Army during the [[world war ii|world war ii]], and remained in service until the Vietnam War.

This tag applies to all Thompson variants such as:
- _(post #3628555: The original **M1921** and **M1928 Thompson**. Features a finned barrel, a charging handle knob, [[vertical foregrip|vertical foregrip]] with finger grooves, adjustable iron sights, and accepts [[drum magazine|drum magazine]]s.)_
- _(post #5103708: Pre-WWII **M1928A1 Thompson** (with rectangular handguard).)_
- _(post #2362155: **M1/M1A1 Thompson**. WWII-era simplified design with rectangular handguard, lack of muzzle device, charging handle on the right, and accepts only stick [[magazine (weapon)|magazine (weapon)]].)_

A German heavy [[tank|tank]] developed in 1942 and used in [[world war ii|world war ii]]. The final official German designation was **Panzerkampfwagen VI Tiger Ausf.E**, often shortened to **Tiger**.

It was an answer to the unexpectedly formidable [[soviet|soviet]] armour encountered in the initial months of the Axis invasion of the Soviet Union, particularly the [[t-34|t-34]] and the [[kv-1|kv-1]]. The Tiger I design gave the Wehrmacht its first tank mounting the 88 mm gun, in its initial armored fighting vehicle-dedicated version, which in its [[88 flak|Flak version]] had previously demonstrated its effectiveness against both air and ground targets. During the course of the war, the Tiger I saw combat on all German battlefronts. It was usually deployed in independent tank battalions, which proved to be quite formidable. However, it was over-engineered and prone to mechanical breakdowns and faults, making it unreliable and causing many Tigers to be lost outside of combat. The overlapping wheel system in particular was extremely hard to perform field repairs on.

The tank was given its nickname "Tiger" by Ferdinand Porsche, and the Roman numeral was added after the later [[tiger ii|tiger ii]] entered production. The initial official German designation was Panzerkampfwagen VI Ausführung H (‘Panzer VI version H’, abbreviated PzKpfw VI Ausf. H), but the tank was redesignated as PzKpfw VI Ausf. E in March 1943. It also had the ordnance inventory designation SdKfz 181.

A [[germany|German]] heavy [[tank|tank]] of [[world war ii|world war ii]]. The final official German designation was **Panzerkampfwagen Tiger Ausf. B**. It is often referred to by the informal nickname "Royal Tiger" or "King Tiger", from the German "Königstiger". 

The Tiger II was the successor to the [[tiger i|tiger i]], combining the latter's thick armor with the armor sloping used on the [[panther (tank)|panther (tank)]]. The tank weighed almost 70 metric tons, and was protected by 100 to 180 mm (3.9 to 7.1 in) of armor to the front. It was armed with the long barreled 8.8 cm KwK 43 L/71 gun. The chassis was also the basis for the [[jagdtiger|jagdtiger]] turretless [[tank destroyer|tank destroyer]].

Main character of [[eiyuu densetsu|eiyuu densetsu]]'s [[zero no kiseki|Zero]]/[[ao no kiseki|ao no kiseki]] duology. [[mishy|mishy]] fangirl.

Has an in-game nickname ティオすけ (tiosuke) given her by [[randolph orlando|randolph orlando]] and adopted by fans. Translated as Tio Tot.

*ティオすけ is a pun on combining ティオ + ちび助. ちび助 (chibisuke, usually written using kana alone) literally means young child, pipsqueak. So meaning of this nickname can be understood as tiny/little Tio.*
***Tio Tot** translation was first introduced by Geofront fan-translation team in [[zero  no kiseki|zero  no kiseki]]. Later in [[sen no kiseki iii|sen no kiseki iii]] it was adopted as an official translation.*
*There is also exists **Petiote** variant of translating this nickname, it was found in Guren's fan-translation of [[zero no kiseki|Zero]] and [[ao no kiseki|ao no kiseki]]. Petiote is a french slang name for little girl, which is also works as a pun on petite + Tio.*

Tionishia, or "Tio" for short, is an [[ogre|ogre]] and a member of the M.O.N., where she serves as the team's hostage escort/guard, due to her immense size and [[strong|strength]].

One of her most noticeable physical features is a [[single horn|single]] large dark [[red horns|red horn]] in her forehead, which connects directly to her skull.

She is one of the tallest characters in the series, easily dwarfing any human and most other Liminals. When on missions she wears a bulky suit of [[armor|armor]], which covers everything except her horn. Because of her size, figure and horn, all of her clothes have to be custom-made.

Outside of her armour, when on duty, she wears the standard M.O.N. uniform, with a long yellow [[dress|dress]]-[[robe|robe]] under it.

Shorthand for trinitrotoluene, an [[explosive|explosive]] compound primarily used for [[weapon|military purposes]] due to its high stability.

Contrary to popular belief, TNT is **not** a general-purposes explosive that is widely used in the [[mining|mining]] industry, due to their relatively low explosive yield and high cost compared to [[dynamite|dynamite]]. The confusion stemmed from various American cartoons that often used the word "TNT" as a catchword for any type of explosives for the sake of simplicity.

For tagging purposes, the tag "TNT" should be used when the [[explosion|explosive]] material in question is clearly labelled as "TNT" or its alternate names. If not, tag it as [[dynamite|dynamite]] (stick explosive) or another identifiable [[bomb|explosive]] type.

May be used with boxes of TNT or bundles/single sticks of dynamite labelled as TNT.

A semi-automatic 7.62×25mm **[[handgun|handgun]]** of [[soviet|soviet]] origin, developed in 1930 by Fedor Tokarev for the Soviet [[military|military]] to replace the [[nagant m1895|nagant m1895]]. Initially designated as the TT-30, then slightly revised as the **TT-33**. It saw service during the [[world war ii|world war ii]].
The [[weapon|weapon]] uses short recoil operation with tilting barrel, akin to the [[m1911|m1911]]. Visually recognizable by its wide slide serrations, circular external hammer, and [[star (symbol)|star]] symbol on the standard grip panels. 

This tag can also apply to any similar Tokarev pistol variants such as the [[china|Chinese]] Type 54.

*Arya Sometimes Hides Her Feelings in Russian* (Hepburn: Tokidoki Bosotto Roshiago de Dereru Tonari no Ārya-san), abbreviated as *Roshidere*, is a Japanese light novel series written by SunSunSun and illustrated by [[momoko (momopoco)|momoko (momopoco)]]. It was originally published online as two short stories on the novel publishing website "Shōsetsuka ni Narō" from May 6 to May 27, 2020, respectively. It was then acquired by Kadokawa Shoten, who have published nine volumes and a short story volume since March 2021 under their Kadokawa Sneaker Bunko imprint.

A manga adaptation by [[tenacitysaho|Saho Tenamachi]] began serialization online on Kodansha's Magazine Pocket website and app in October 2022. An anime adaptation by DogaKobo has started airing on July 3, 2024.

#### Synopsis
[[alisa mikhailovna kujou|alisa mikhailovna kujou]] is a half-Russian, half-Japanese high school student who attends one of Japan's best institutions, Seiren Private Academy. With her unparalleled looks and silky silver hair, she can make anyone turn around if she walks past them. Her elegant persona, alongside intelligence, has made her the idol of her school.

On the other hand, Alisa's benchmate [[kuze masachika|kuze masachika]] is an unmotivated student who sleeps in classes and always plays gacha games. Unable to be honest, Alisa sometimes expresses her thoughts in Russian so that Masachika won't understand. However, unbeknownst to her, Masachika understands Russian as well at the native level.

A steel lattice communications and observation tower in [[tokyo (city)|Tokyo]]. Opened in 1958, it is painted white and international orange to comply with air safety regulations and has two circular observation decks, features which help distinguish it from its inspiration, the [[eiffel tower|eiffel tower]]. It is also surrounded by high rise buildings, the presence of which hampered plans to use the Tower for digital broadcasting in the region, and resulted in the building of the taller [[tokyo skytree|tokyo skytree]].

It is the setting of the tokusatsu series [[kamen rider kabuto (series)|Kamen Rider Kabuto]], as well as being an important location in [[ghostwire: tokyo|ghostwire: tokyo]].

Considered a [[vegetable|vegetable]], particularly for culinary purposes, the tomato is botanically a [[fruit|fruit]] produced by the plant *Solanum lycopersicum* of the nightshade family.

The word "tomato" comes from the ancient Nahuatl word *tomatl*.

In the US, the US Supreme Court ruled in the 1893 case Nix v. Hedden that the tomato is legally classified as a vegetable.  This was to resolve an issue with the Tariff Act of 1883 which required a tax be paid on imported vegetables, but not fruits.

A girl who displays boyish behaviors. Girls who are tomboys tend to be very athletic and sporty.

They almost always dress like boys and frequently have short and/or spiky hair and can often be seen wearing tight cycling shorts. Examples include [[kagura (azumanga daioh)|kagura (azumanga daioh)]], [[arisawa tatsuki|arisawa tatsuki]] and [[makoto (street fighter)|makoto (street fighter)]]. 

Not to be confused with [[reverse trap|reverse trap]], which refers to a girl with an androgynous or masculine *physical appearance* regardless of personality. An androgynous girl may not necessarily act like a tomboy and a tomboy isn't required to look androgynous. Though there is a recognizable overlap between the two. [[crossdressing|crossdressing]] does not automatically make a girl a "tomboy" either.

**Note**: Just having [[short hair|short hair]] is not enough to count as a tomboy. The girl in question has to act in a masculine manner.

A type of electric [[washing machine|washing machine]] where the opening to load it is on the top.

Inside the machine the clothes go into a vertical drum where an agitator or impeller inside will move the clothes around while in operation.  They tend to be less common in places where space is a premium as the opening at the top makes it difficult to stack with other washing machines or [[clothes dryer|clothes dryer]]s to save in floor space.  Some units do come in a stacked configuration with a dryer on top, but this is usually done through restricting the opening to the washing machine making it more difficult to put in and take out clothing.

As the opening is on the top, this type of washing machine does not need to have a locking mechanism on the door to prevent people from opening it while it operation like a front-load washing machine.

In nature, tornadoes are spawned from severe thunderstorms or tropical cyclones under specific, complex meteorological conditions. While tornadoes can spawn virtually anywhere in the world, they are most common in America, with the majority occurring in two principal areas: Tornado Alley, famously stretching across the plains of the central US, and Dixie Alley, comprising portions of the American southeast. In fiction, tornadoes can be deliberately spawned by individuals or devices capable of controlling the wind or weather.

"東方" (Japanese for "eastern") 

A series of "bullet hell" vertical shooter games created by [[zun (artist)|zun (artist)]], featuring a large cast of girls and almost no male characters.

Touhou first appeared on the NEC PC-9801 computers in its first five games between 1996 and 1998 before going into hiatus, during which time ZUN left his former team, Amusement Makers. These games make up the [[touhou (pc-98)|touhou (pc-98)]] era. In 2002 he returned as the one-man doujin group *Team Shanghai Alice* and released Touhou for Windows, thus exposing it to a larger audience. 

The games themselves, mostly in the [[danmaku|danmaku]] ("bullet hell") genre, are addictive and have acquired a large following. In particular, his original music is incredibly popular and is the subject of numerous doujin remix albums.

Currently Touhou has nineteen mainstream danmaku shooter games, six danmaku spinoffs, six fighting spinoffs and an action spinoff, with the fighting games and action game made in collaboration with Tasogare Frontier. The series also has a number of supplementary materials including manga, short stories, fanbooks, and music CDs.

The backgrounds and personalities of its characters (the majority of which come from the Windows generation) are often expanded upon in doujins and, occasionally, ZUN canonizes some concepts. 

Touhou is also notable for being a *de facto* open source franchise, in which ZUN allows various fan works such as doujinshi and video games to be published and sold with little to no licensing fees. This allowed the franchise to remain popular to this day.

**Touken Ranbu** (刀剣乱舞, lit. "Boisterous Sword Dance", often abbreviated *Tourabu*) is a Japanese free-to-play browser game developed by Kadokawa Games and [[nitroplus|nitroplus]] released in January 2015. A mobile version of the game called *Touken Ranbu Pocket* was released in March 2016.

The gameplay typically centers around controlling and managing *touken danshi* (刀剣男士, lit. "sword warriors"), male personifications of historical Japanese [[sword|sword]]s. Players assume the role of a [[saniwa (touken ranbu)|saniwa (touken ranbu)]] (審神者) that creates these characters in order to fight against [[jikan sokougun|monstrous]] [[kebiishi (touken ranbu)|enemies]] within different eras. Like in [[kantai collection|kantai collection]], battling is automated, but players can manually forge, repair, and team up their characters.

The game has two anime adaptations: one called [[touken ranbu: hanamaru|touken ranbu: hanamaru]] which is animated by Dogakobo and began airing in October 2016, and another, [[katsugeki/touken ranbu|katsugeki/touken ranbu]], animated by Ufotable which begain airing in July 2017. The game also has a series of musicals ([[musical touken ranbu|musical touken ranbu]]) and stage plays based on it.

The very first 3D fighting game for the Playstation 1 platform, released in 1995. Toushinden is a primitive version of [[soulcalibur|soulcalibur]], utilizing weapons combat in a 3D field, but with the addition of [[street fighter|street fighter]]-like special attacks that each character can use. The sidestep was also introduced in Toushinden, which Soulcalibur goes on to use.

In late 2009, a Toushinden game for the Wii was released, although its title uses slightly different kanji - 闘真伝.

Packaging used to display a [[toy|toy]] for sale in a [[shop|shop]].

This is often of the form of a plastic clam-shell inside a [[cardboard box|cardboard]] [[box|box]] (common for e.g. [[figure|figure]]s and [[doll|doll]]s) with (or without) a window in the front, a plastic [[blister pack|blister pack]] with a cardboard backing (common for e.g. smaller [[toy car|toy car]]s), or a thermally sealed [[plastic bag|plastic bag]].  In all cases, there will be the product name printed somewhere on the package, and possibly a UPC [[bar code|bar code]] or [[price tag|price tag]].

The contents may be an actual toy, a [[model kit|model kit]], an inanimate [[character doll|character doll]] or [[character charm|charm]], a miniaturized version of a living character ([[miniboy|miniboy]] or [[minigirl|minigirl]]), or possibly a scaled-up version of such a box with the actual living character inside.  In the latter two cases, the character might be described as [[encasement|encased]] or [[restrained|restrained]].

The Toyota Sprinter Trueno is a small, lightweight coupe introduced by Toyota in 1983 as part of the fifth generation Toyota Corolla lineup. The insider-chassis code of "AE86" depicts the 1600 cc rear-wheel drive model from the range. The Levin has fixed-headlights, and the Trueno has retractable headlights, both could be hatchback or coupe. The export model name Corolla covers both variations. 

The car is best known for its incredible handling characteristic, which leads into it being frequently used in various [[drifting|drift]] [[racing|racing]] tournaments.

This tag also covers the AE85 (sold as the Toyota Corolla Levin, Toyota Sprinter Trueno or Toyota Corolla DX), likewise a rear-wheel drive sports coupe, manufactured by Toyota from 1983-1987. While the AE85 shares its chassis and basic design with the famous AE86, the AE85 was designed for economy and differs mainly in its engine, compared to the AE86, which was designed for performance.

The white and black color variant (informally known as the "panda" Trueno) is most known as [[fujiwara takumi|fujiwara takumi]]'s [[fujiwara takumi's toyota trueno ae86|'Tofu Delivery' car]] from the [[initial d|initial d]] series, while [[takeuchi itsuki|takeuchi itsuki]] purchases an AE85 Levin, mistaken for an AE86. Later on, a young man by the name of [[inui shinji|inui shinji]] appears, driving a notchback late-model Trueno.

Since the creation of [[magic: the gathering|magic: the gathering]] in 1993, a derivative of trading card known as trading [[card game|card game]] has emerged, which involves using these cards as a game piece. These has since supplanted the traditional trading card market, albeit the non-game trading cards (such as [[soccer|footballer]] cards) were still being produced to this day.

This tag is applicable to the depiction of either trading cards or the trading card games, including the real and fan-made card face. If the cards were shown to be played, the tag [[card game|card game]] is applicable.

An image drawn with traditional tools without a computer. This is in contrast with "digital media" which dominate Danbooru.

Please use this tag only if you're 100% sure that the image is actually drawn by hand. Use [[faux traditional media|faux traditional media]]  for digital images that mimic a hand-drawn/non-CG style.

An image that is partly traditional, but also contains digital elements (e.g. digital [[spot color|spot color]]), should receive the additional tag [[mixed media|mixed media]]. Digital filtering, performed to improve the visibility of the traditional artwork (e.g. color adjustment), rather than as a creative effect or to remove flaws, does not make an image [[mixed media|mixed media]].

A good way to tell if a drawing is traditional is to look for "analog" or アナログ in kana. You'll find this tag on Pixiv and used on some Japanese artists' sites. (Beware however that some people will tag their image "アナログ" that don't qualify to our standards of the tag).

A traditional [[nun|nun]]'s habit, specifically a traditional Christian style (Catholic, Orthodox, etc), as opposed to the fetishized, non-traditional nun habits typically seen in anime and fanart.

It consists at most of a [[long dress|long dress]] (that's black) with [[long sleeves|long sleeves]] and a [[guimpe|guimpe]] (that's white), and typically stars the distinctive nun headdress (consisting of a [[wimple|wimple]]/[[coif|coif]] [that's white], headwear bandeau [that's white], and [[veil|veil]] [that's black], though it has become increasingly optional for some since the 20th century), and may also include a [[tabard|tabard]], underdress, and so on. The habit is typically white-on-black, with black the predominant color, but they can also be wholly white, or white-on-blue. Color can depend on the religious order which the nun is a part of. They can also be wholly black, which is the common choice for Orthodox nuns.

The traditional habit can be accentuated with minor additions, but not so much that it detracts from the basics (ex. [[sister claire|sister claire]] and [[double (skullgirls)|double (skullgirls)]] as opposed to [[specter (arknights)|specter (arknights)]] and [[index (toaru majutsu no index)|index (toaru majutsu no index)]]), and some degree of modesty must be adhered to (ex. not too tight-fitting, no shortened dresses, no cutouts, no openings where they wouldn't normally be, no side slits which reveal skin or undergarment, no overtly sexual depictions of certain undergarments, etc).

A barricade designed control the flow of vehicular or pedestrian traffic in a specified area.  Commonly used to keep vehicular traffic within the roadway or prevent them from hitting obstacles or running off steep slopes.  They're also used to bar entry, such as on blocking access to incomplete roads and bridges.  Such barriers are also used to protect pedestrians from vehicles, and may be placed to separate areas of high pedestrian traffic from vehicular traffic.

#### Types

- [[guard rail|guard rail]]: 
  - Flex-Beam/W-Beam: A long metal W-shaped beam of metal that runs alongside the road.
    - Example: post #5627306, post #6243008
  - Thrie Beam: A long metal VVV-shaped beam of metal that runs alongside the road.
    - Example: post #5519007, post #6483822
  - Cable barrier: A barrier composed of metal wires affixed to metal poles.
    - Example: post #2616332, 
  - Pipe railing: A barrier composed of metal pipes.
    - Example: post #6577813, post #4563235
- Type I, II, & III traffic barricade: Styles of traffic barriers that use 1-3 reflective warning planks/sheets, the type refers to the number used.
  - A-frame traffic barricade: A portable wood or plastic barricade made of two A-shaped end pieces and planks with reflective sheeting placed in-between.
    - Example: post #6164622, post #6405555, post #4171864 (Type II)
  - Basic Type I-III:  May be portable and kept on t-legs or permanent posts embedded in the ground.
    - Example: post #6034006 (on left: Portable Type II), post #5254303 (Portable Type III)
- Traffic cones and bar: A small rod that affixes between two traffic cones, used to regulate pedestrian traffic .
  - Example: post #6459980
- [[jersey barrier|jersey barrier]]: A modular concrete or plastic barrier.
  - Example: post #5498800
- Traffic barrel: A large barrel or barrel-shaped portable barrier used as a larger version of a traffic cone to direct traffic or warn of hazards.
  - Example: post #5288604, post #6089185
- [[bollard|Traffic bollard]] (barrier poles): Metal or concrete poles used to restrict vehicle access while allowing pedestrian access
  - Example: post #5656419, post #554460, post #636645

She reached one million subscribers on 12 December 2022, the fifth Nijisanji VTuber to reach this milestone.

Shizuka Tsuruki is the leading main character from the [[girls und panzer|girls und panzer]] spinoff, [[girls und panzer ribbon no musha|Girls und Panzer: Ribbon no Musha]]. 

Shizuka, [[matsukaze rin|matsukaze rin]], and [[endou haruka|endou haruka]] are students at Tatenashi High School. They represent the school in Tankathlon (a cousin of Tankery) under the banner of Team Centipede. Shizuka is not only the team's leader, but also serves as the commander, gunner, and loader of the team's sole vehicle, a red [[type 97 te-ke|Type 97 Te-Ke tankette]].

She has [[tsurime|upward-angled]] [[red eyes|red eyes]] and [[short hair|short]] [[brown hair|brown hair]] (or [[black hair|black]], depending on the artist). Her long bangs have been swept around in an unusual loop and kept in place with a [[large bow|large]] [[red ribbon|red]] [[hair ribbon|ribbon]] tied into [[red bow|a]] [[hair bow|bow]], from which the series derives its name. She also has a [[mole under eye|mole under her left eye]]. Shizuka is most often found wearing either a [[white shirt|white]] [[dress shirt|dress shirt]] or the full [[tatenashi high school uniform|tatenashi high school uniform]], along with [[loafers|loafers]] and [[brown legwear|brown]] [[pantyhose|pantyhose]]. However, she frequently slips off one of her shoes in battle "in order to non-verbally convey her directions to Rin":/posts/2227380.

On more than one occasion, she has gone into Tankathlon battles wearing a suit of classical [[japanese armor|japanese armor]] and wielding a [[bow (weapon)|bow]].

Shizuka makes frequent use of the [[emblem|emblem]] of [[takeda shingen|takeda shingen]]'s [[centipede|centipede]] force, even to the point of making it her own team's emblem and decorating the Type 97 with the symbol.

A [[tachi (weapon)|tachi]] forged by Gojou Kuninaga. He had gone through several owners (one of them being Oda Nobunaga, so he is often depicted in fanworks alongside other swords owned by him), and was stolen from his owners twice; once from the grave of Sadayasu of the Adachi clan, and also from a shrine by Koudeki of the Honami Clan. He is currently part of the Imperial Collection alongside [[ichigo hitofuri|ichigo hitofuri]], [[uguisumaru|uguisumaru]] and [[hirano toushirou|hirano toushirou]].

Because of how he tended to be stolen from his resting place, and because of his long life in general, Tsurumaru has a love of surprises and likes to sneak up on people to surprise them. This has naturally earned him a reputation of being a troll in fanworks who plays pranks on the other characters for his own amusement. 

He has [[white hair|white hair]] and [[yellow eyes|yellow eyes]], and wears [[japanese clothes|japanese clothes]] with a [[hood|hood]] and [[pom pom (clothes)|pom pom]]s. He has [[black gloves|black gloves]] that are [[partially fingerless gloves|partly fingerless]] and [[japanese armor|japanese armor]] at his waist.

His name is written with the kanji for "[[crane (animal)|crane]]", and he often references how he resembles one due to his white clothing. Ironically, despite cranes representing longevity and good fortune in Japanese culture, most of his masters did not live long.

This drink has a lot of similar products and other brand names. Tupet is the best known one (but not the first one). The other names include "Bou-juice (Stick-juice)" by Satou Seika, "[[chu chu ice|chu chu ice]]" by Alps Seika, "Pokkin Ice", "Pakkin Ice" and so on. Similar products outside of Japan include the Colombian "Bon-Ice". The manufacturer of tupets, MAEDA SANGYO Co.ltd, issued a voluntary recall of this product in 2009, saying, "We understand that there has been some concern for an outbreak of mold caused by a flaw in the manufacturing process." After that, the company stated that "In the end, we have identified that resolving this problem by improving our facilities/machines would cost too much time and money." and decided to discontinue the product. This drink has more than 30 years of history and many fans. The news of the discontinuation caused great sorrow among them. However, actually nobody was troubled because some similar products are still sold. #### Variations in other countries United States: Freeze pop, Freezer pop, Icee; Otter Pops ©, Fla-Vor-Ice ©, Pop-Ice © United Kingdom: Ice pole, Ice pop; Mr. Freeze © Australia: Zooper Dooper © Philippines: Ice candy Spain: Polo Flash India: Sip Up #### See also - [[tag group:food tags|tag group:food tags]] #### External links - "Wikipedia (JP): チューペット":[https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/チューペット] - [Q&A site 'Oshiete goo': What do you call this popsicle? In addition to images tagged with this tag, any image that matches either of the following queries are also treated as twitter samples, given that they are *visually identical*:

- source:*twitter.com/ md5 mismatch -upscaled status:active
- source:*pbs.twimg.com/ md5 mismatch -upscaled status:active

Make sure they are fairly identical to the original image, however. Sometimes the source might be incorrect. This doesn't factor in edits such as post #2440268.

#### Examples

- Sample: https://pbs.twimg.com/media/C2uQastUQAE5nyc.jpg (900x1200)
- Original: https://pbs.twimg.com/media/C2uQastUQAE5nyc.jpg:orig (1200x1600)

Following "the Experimental Tank Number 1":[http://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E8%A9%A6%E8%A3%BD1%E5%8F%B7%E6%88%A6%E8%BB%8A], which was the first [[tank|tank]] to be domestically produced in Japan, the Type 89 medium tank was Japan's first domestically mass-produced tank. 

Although the experimental model completed in 1929 (year 25**89** of the imperial dating system) was designated as a light tank, its classification soon changed to that of medium tank due to an increase in weight brought about by early modifications. 

The tank was divided into two subtypes, the Kou-gata (subtype-A), which was mounted with a water cooled gasoline engine, and the Otsu-gata (subtype-B), mounted with an air cooled diesel engine. The tank's chassis shape, undergoing repeated modifications, can broadly be divided into 4 different types. The majority types were equipped with an unditching tail (In actuality it was mostly used as a storing shelf.) 

Although the I-gou was a successful vehicle, its low horsepower and mobility prompted the development of the [[type 95 ha-gou|type 95 ha-gou]]. It was, moreover, widely inferior to both the Soviet BT-5 and T-26 *light* tanks used in [the battle of Khalkin Gol](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battles_of_Khalkhin_Gol) and the American [[m3 stuart|m3 stuart]] *light* tanks used during the invasion of the Philippines.

The **U.N. Spacy** (United Nations [[space|space]] Navy) is the fictional [[military|military]] arm of the Earth U.N. Government (地球統合政府 *"Chikyuu Tougou Seifu"*) in the [[macross|macross]] Japanese anime series.

The organization's name is derived from words **SPAC**E and NAV**Y**, therefore, combining them to make the word **SPACY**. 

In the Macross chronology it was established after 1999 by the successor to the modern [[united nations|united nations]] in order to defend Earth from a possible attack by hostile [[alien|alien]]s.

However, from 1999 to 2008 the U.N. Spacy was also involved in the [[macross zero|U.N. Wars]] conflict, fighting against a human [[anti-u.n.|anti-u.n.]] faction opposed to the formation of the worldwide U.N. government. 

A year later (2009) the U.N. Spacy was involved in the subsequent [[choujikuu yousai macross|Space War I]], defending our planet from an hostile extraterrestrial race called the [[zentradi|zentradi]]. Later operations of the U.N. Spacy expanded into interstellar colonization and general peacekeeping of off-world Earth settlements.

At the time of the Zentradi invasion, the U.N. Spacy's assets included military bases on Earth, the [[moon|moon]] and [[mars (planet)|mars (planet)]], squadrons of variable fighters and other [[mecha|mecha]], several capital [[spacecraft|spacecraft]] in orbit and the repaired SDF-1 *Macross* on South Ataria Island, the flagship of the United Nations Spacy.

The U.N. Spacy was succeeded by the **New U.N. Spacy** ([[n.u.n.s.|n.u.n.s.]]).  

In the [[robotech|robotech]] western adaptation the U.N. Spacy is reimagined as the actual space navy component of the **Robotech Defense Force (R.D.F.)**.

Uchi no Hime-sama ga Ichiban Kawaii (My Princess Is The Cutest) is a Japanese Card-based RPG for iOS.

In Uchihime, the princesses of the land had been imprisoned into crystals by the Demon King. The player takes the role of a prince who was cursed into an [[kaeru ouji|anthropomorphic frog]]. However, despite being cursed with a seemingly permanent and debilitating transmogrification, the prince can still battle the army of the Demon King. Together with the help of [[anna (uchi no hime-sama ga ichiban kawaii)|Anna]], a fairy who acts as a magical slingshot and a guide, the prince sets course to rescue the captured princesses and defeat the Demon King.

The main storyline revolves around four princesses: [[lina princella|Princess Lina]], [[akane garnet|Princess Akane]], [[marina sophia|Princess Sophia]], and [[clarice lapis|Princess Lapis]].

**Uchuu Senkan Yamato** (宇宙戦艦ヤマト, *Space Battleship Yamato*) is a legendary and classic [[japan|japan]]ese [[science fiction|science fiction]] anime series. It was created by [[matsumoto leiji|matsumoto leiji]] and Nishizaki Yoshinobu in the early [[1970s (style)|1970s]]. 

The first TV anime series aired on Yomiuri TV in October 6, 1974 and was followed by several animated movie sequels and two more TV series seasons (broadcast in 1978 and 1980 respectively). 

It is notable because it was one of the first military science fiction anime that depicted space battleships and cosmic [[battle|battle]]s among fleets of spaceships. Its creators were also inspired by [[star trek|star trek]] when the series was being developed. 

Uchuu Senkan Yamato influenced several later sci-fi anime like [[gundam|gundam]], [[macross|macross]], [[top wo nerae!|top wo nerae!]] (Gunbuster) and [[ginga eiyuu densetsu|ginga eiyuu densetsu]] (Legend of the Galactic Heroes) among others. It also influenced various productions in the west, like [[star wars|star wars]] and [[battlestar galactica|battlestar galactica]] (both the original and re-imagined versions).

It is known to English-speaking audiences as ***Space Battleship Yamato*** and also as ***[[star blazers|star blazers]]***. In Spanish and Latin American countries it was called ***Astronave Intrepido*** ("Starship Intrepid"). In European and Asian countries it was also called ***Estrellas Luminosas*** ("Luminous Stars"), ***Cosmoship Yamato***, ***Anti-Space Ship***, ***Journey to the Final Galaxy*** and ***Star Patrol***. 

Its last anime film sequel to the original series was released on December 2009 and a live action film adaptation of the first TV series was released on December 2010 in Japan. 

A new reboot series based on the first season called [[uchuu senkan yamato 2199|uchuu senkan yamato 2199]] was released in 2012. A  series sequel to 2199 called [[uchuu senkan yamato 2202: ai no senshi-tachi|uchuu senkan yamato 2202: ai no senshi-tachi]] was released in 2018. 

The latest animated film series (sequel to 2202) were released in 2021 with the name [[uchuu senkan yamato 2205: arata naru tabidachi|uchuu senkan yamato 2205: arata naru tabidachi]].

Ugoira is a custom [[animated|animation]] format used by Pixiv. A Ugoira is a Zip file of images, played back using a custom Javascript player.

To download a Ugoira, use the "Save as video (right click and save)" link beneath the image. This is a WebM conversion that can be played on regular video players, but is not lossless in quality.

To upload a Ugoira, paste the Pixiv URL into the source field on the upload page, or upload using the "bookmarklet":[/static/bookmarklet]. Uploading a Ugoira file from your computer will not work.

Technically, a Ugoira consists of Zip file containing each frame in JPEG or PNG format, and a separate JSON file containing the delay between each frame. Since each frame has a separate delay, it's possible for a Ugoira to have a variable frame rate. A "custom Javascript player":[https://github.com/pixiv/zip_player] is used to play animations back. Since the JSON file containing the frame delays is separate from the Zip file containing the images, saving raw Ugoiras and playing them outside of a browser is difficult.

Ugoira is a custom format exclusive to Pixiv. Animations from other sites cannot be Ugoira.

Ugoira is often considered inferior to animations found on other sites due to Pixiv's limitations on uploading GIFs or MP4 videos. As a result, artists may convert their animations to GIFs before uploading, introducing [[gif artifacts|dithering]] and/or [[color banding|color banding]], and Pixiv's recompression process can introduce additional [[jpeg artifacts|jpeg artifacts]], affecting the overall quality of Ugoira animations.

A Japanese computer program that provides mascot characters on the user's desktop. Also referred to as "偽ペルソナウェア with 偽春菜" (Fake personaware with Nise-Haruna), "あれ以外の何か with 任意" (Are Igai no Nanika with [[nin'i-tan|nin'i-tan]]), "何か" (Nanika), and "偽春菜" (Nise-Haruna).

When the user launches the program (called Baseware), cute (or weird) characters called Ghosts (usually a set of two) appear on the screen, have random conversations, do things at specific times and perform actions in response to events, such as being touched by the mouse. Additional trivial functions are available, such as having them check incoming email, synchronizing the clock and making online updates.

Ghosts can be made by users, and at its height of popularity around the year [[2002|2002]], a countless amount (in the thousands, according to one theory) of diverse Ghosts created by users were being distributed. Even simple graphic files of Ghost forms (called "Shells") were being circulated as freeware.

The most famous Ghosts are "[[sakura (ukagaka)|Sakura]] & [[unyuu|unyuu]]," which are installed by default by Baseware, along with the famous "[[emily (ukagaka)|Emily]] and Teddy" that were default Ghosts of SSP, a famous Ukagaka-compatible Baseware.

Known as *Migatte no Gokui* in the original Japanese, it is a state of being introduced in [[dragon ball super|dragon ball super]], where its user can react without the need of acknowledging and subsequently thinking about the threat at hand - an ability so notorious for being exceptionally difficult to master that even the gods struggle to achieve it at times.

[[son goku|son goku]] is shown accessing the ability - first in an incomplete state (-Sign- or -Omen-) and later in a perfected state - though not retaining it afterwards. In the former state, his body receives a blueish [[aura|aura]] around it, his hair becomes slightly spikier and his eyes become [[grey eyes|silver-colored]]; in the latter form, alongside the previous additions, his hair becomes fully [[white hair|white]] and his hair becomes slightly more wild. Later, it is revealed that perfected Ultra Instinct can manifest a ki-based [[perfected ultra instinct giant form|Giant form]].

A [[personification|personified]] [[ultra series|Ultra]] [[kaiju|kaiju]] project originally proposed by "Griffon Enterprises":[https://www.griffon.co.jp/], which was officially sanctioned by [[tsuburaya productions|tsuburaya productions]] after the success of the 2011 Ultra kaiju variety show Ultra Zone. The project would be split into various sub-projects (or versions) across multiple companies - the Griffon Enterprises mixed-media project designed by Pastel Design's [[pop (electromagneticwave)|pop (electromagneticwave)]], the Dengeki ([[kadokawa|kadokawa]]) mixed-media project developed by ASCII Media Works, the "Plex":[http://www.plex-web.com/index.html] figures, the [[kodansha|kodansha]] project, the [[tokyo otaku mode|tokyo otaku mode]] project, the *KAIJU MUSUME 6* restaurant operated by THINKR, and the [[akb48|akb48]] crossover *[[tanabe miku|Tana]][[miclas|miclas]]*. The transcorporate multimedia project would be formally announced in 2013 through [[haitai nanafa|haitai nanafa]], and by 2020, each project had officially ended.

Of the six projects' designs, the Dengeki designs would generally be the most popular in fanart, in part thanks to the light novel and anime series that ran from 2015 to 2018, with the Plex designs following behind it, and after it the POP designs (varying from kaiju to kaiju).

The titular hero of Tsuburaya Productions's [[ultraman (1st series)|1966-1967 tokusatsu TV series]]. His human host is [[hayata shin|hayata shin]]. Due to Ultraman becoming a title for those of the Land of Light who have protected Earth, he is often referred to with additional names to distinguish him from his Ultra Brothers, such as *Shodai [Ultra-]Man* ("The First [Ultra-]Man"), *[Ultra-]Man-niisan* ("Brother [Ultra-]Man"), or even just *Man*, with *Ultraman Hayata*, based on his host's name, becoming a popular choice for some younger Western fans.

In the original series, Ultraman went through three designs (referred to as Type A, Type B, and Type C), with Type C being the most common design used in appearances since, though with the first two being referenced from time to time. There was also a "Type D" design that existed briefly after the original series, used in stage shows, originating from converting [[zoffy (ultra series)|zoffy (ultra series)]]'s suit back into an Ultraman suit, as his suit was originally the Type A suit (previously also used by [[imit ultraman|imit ultraman]], and would go on to be used for [[ultraman jack|ultraman jack]]). This would all establish a trend of slight redesigns for Ultras during and after their original series, especially those who look similar to one another.

**Umamusume: Pretty Derby** is a mobile game developed and published by [[cygames|cygames]] featuring [[horse girl|girls]] based on famous [[horse|racehorses]]. The game was first announced in 2016 and was initially slated for a Fall 2018 release, only for development to start out from scratch; with the ultimate release date pushed back to Febuary 2021. A party game spinoff, [[umamusume: party dash|Uma Musume Pretty Derby: Party Dash]], was announced for a 2024 Worldwide.

The franchise received several anime adaptations, with the first season airing before the game's official release in Spring 2018, and a second season launching alongside the game in Winter 2021. A spinoff featuring [[narita top road (umamusume)|narita top road (umamusume)]] was aired for Spring 2023. The third season premiered in Fall 2023, followed by an anime film centered on [[jungle pocket (umamusume)|jungle pocket (umamusume)]] in May 2024.

There is also the *[[umayon|umayon]]* spinoff, which was a 4koma manga that was adapted in to a anime short in 2020, and the *[[umayuru|umayuru]]* spinoff which was released directly on *Umamusume*'s YouTube channel in Fall 2022. On June 21 2023.

A cover song from [[umamusume|umamusume]], which has been [[parody|parodied]] for various poses from the idol performance.

This tag is generally used for when characters are dancing or singing along to the song. Common identifiable poses including raising both arms with hands pointing forwards and slightly down as though imitating a horse's ears (or a horse rearing up), and blowing a kiss with both hands. The first pose is associated with the line "Uuuu (Umapyoi Umapyoi)" (parentheses exactly as written) and the second with "Today the Goddess of Victory grants a kiss only to me".

Avoid using this tag for when "umapyoi" is used as [[umapyoi (phrase)|a slang phrase]] within normal conversation (that is, the characters are neither singing nor dancing nor posing).

An image that has not been [[censored|censored]] by the artist. See [[decensored|decensored]] for images that have been decensored by a [[third-party edit|third-party edit]].

This tag applies only to genitalia, sex acts, body fluids, or other things that would normally be censored. It does not apply to [[nipples|nipples]], or to body parts that aren't fully visible. Note that this tag is mutually exclusive from [[censored|censored]], and that both tags can be applied if one of the chracter's genitalia is left uncensored.

In Japan, it is illegal to draw uncensored genitalia if they are to be published publicly for domestic distribution. Some artists skirt around this law by applying censorship that is easy to remove, or by applying [[pointless censoring|pointless censorship]] that barely hides the censored body part. Others maintain a non-Japanese presence to bypass Japanese laws altogether and distribute uncensored versions of their work. It is also noted that some censorship also doubles as a paywall or sample work of sorts, with the uncensored version available in an artists' donation page, such as Patreon, Fanbox and others.

A fictional manned giant robot from the [[gundam|gundam]] [[mecha|mecha]]verse. 

The titular [[mecha|mecha]] (and plot device) from [[gundam unicorn|gundam unicorn]] (2010). The **RX-0 Unicorn Gundam** is the "key" to Laplace's Box, a MacGuffin purported to contain a secret that could overthrow the Earth Federation government. Possession of the Unicorn Gundam is therefore hotly disputed, as it also acts as a map to the Box by way of a "La+ program" installed in its operating system.

Its physical design is a throwback to the [[rx-78-2|rx-78-2]], being a "white [[mobile suit|mobile suit]]" armed with a set of beam sabers mounted behind its head, a beam rifle with power equivalent to that of a battleship class beam weapon, and a shield with a viewport. It also incorporates concepts from its chronological predecessor, the [[nu gundam|nu gundam]], by adapting the Nu Gundam's cockpit-lined [[psycho frame|psycho frame]] throughout its entire body (visible in [[nt-d|nt-d]] mode) and having the ability to use [[funnels (gundam)|funnels (gundam)]] or bits (though it requires the NT-D to be active and the enemy to have said remote weapons so the Unicorn could hijack them).

|| Upon its awakening, the Unicorn Gundam also gains abilities similar to the Nu Gundam's: The Shield Funnels (Unicorn Gundam's shields with a beam gatling gun attached on each), which has both offensive and defensive capabilities not unlike the [[fin funnels|fin funnels]] and the ability to create a phenomena similar to the Axis Shock. ||

Piloted by [[banagher links|banagher links]]. Designed by [[katoki hajime|katoki hajime]].

The Unicorn Gundam's popularity led to a 1:1 statue of it, with partial Unicorn Mode to Destroy Mode transformation, to replace the original Gundam statue in Diver City, Odaiba, Tokyo.

Also known as the **Union Flag**, it is the name given to the national [[flag|flag]] of the [[united kingdom|united kingdom]]. It is a combination of three different flags: the red St. George's Cross of England, the white St. Andrew's Cross of Scotland, and the red St. Patrick's Cross of Ireland.

The design of the Union Jack consists of a blue field, known as the Union Flag, with a red diagonal cross (St. Patrick's Cross) that extends from corner to corner. This cross represents [[ireland|ireland]]. Superimposed on the diagonal cross are two intersecting crosses. The upright red diagonal cross (St. George's Cross) represents [[england|england]], and the white diagonal cross in the shape of an "X" (St. Andrew's Cross) represents [[scotland|scotland]].

The Union Jack's design was first created in 1606 when England and Scotland were separate kingdoms but shared the same monarch, King James VI of Scotland and I of England. The flag was officially adopted in 1801 after the Act of Union, which united the Kingdom of Great Britain (combining England and Scotland) with the Kingdom of Ireland.

Also appears in the national flags of [[australia|australia]], [[new zealand|new zealand]], [[fiji|fiji]], and [[tuvalu|tuvalu]], as well as those of British colonies and territories. It is also on the flag of the American state of [[hawaii|hawaii]].

This may be confused with a mecha from [[gundam 00|gundam 00]] called a [[union flag|union flag]] used by the world superpower Union in the series.

The United Kingdom is a unitary state governed under a constitutional monarchy and a parliamentary system, with its seat of government in the capital city of [[london|london]]. This tag could go hand-in-hand with [[alternate universe|alternate universe]] if it is a full-on scene of a fanmade character design interacting with canon characters, rather than a character just standing there showing off an outfit (post #1400262).

**Unsinkable Sam** (also known as **Oskar** or **Oscar**) was the name of an alleged black and white German [ship's cat](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship%27s_cat) whose original owner was unknown. He saw service in both the [[kriegsmarine|kriegsmarine]] and [[royal navy|royal navy]] during [[world war ii|world war ii]]. He served on board three vessels and miraculously survived the sinking of all three (*Bismarck*'s, then the HMS *Cossack*'s, and finally the HMS *Ark Royal*'s).

After the sinking of HMS *Ark Royal* he retired from his shipborne career and was first transferred to to the offices of the Governor General in Gibraltar as a mouse-catcher. He then was sent back to the United Kingdom where he lived the rest of his life in a seaman's home in Belfast, Northern Ireland until his natural death in 1955.

Some researchers are skeptical whether or not Sam actually existed.

He is often seen in fanart with [[kantai collection|kantai collection]]'s [[bismarck (kancolle)|bismarck (kancolle)]]. He also appeared in [[z1 leberecht maass (kancolle)|z1 leberecht maass (kancolle)]]'s holiday damage CG (post #2128215).
