A Japanese multimedia franchise about male idols by *Broccoli*, originally starting with an otome game published in 2010 and since then has spawned multiple sequels and rhythm game spin-offs, with the most notable being [[uta no prince-sama: shining live|uta no prince-sama: shining live]]. It has since received a manga and a 2011 anime with a second season in 2012, a third in 2014, a fourth in 2016, and a movie in 2019. 
It is considered one of the foremost franchises in the male [[idol|idol]] genre and has retained its fame both in Japan and worldwide for more than a decade. 

The original plot line followed the heroine [[nanami haruka|nanami haruka]]’s life in Saotome Academy, a prestigious performing arts school made up of students who are either vying to become an idol or a music producer, as she chases after her dream of becoming a composer and someday writing a song for her favorite idol HAYATO. Haruka becomes acquainted with six of her classmates, who are all competing to become idols. For her project, she must team up with another student as an idol-producer team, and if they are successful, they will join Shining Agency after graduation.  

The franchise features three idol groups: the main group [[starish|ST★RISH]], [[quartet night|quartet night]] - a band made up of the seniors of ST★RISH in the 2013 game *Uta no Prince-sama: All Star*, and HE★VENS - an anime-only idol group introduced in [[uta no prince-sama maji love 2000 percent|Uta no Prince-sama: Maji Love 2000%]] and not seen before in the games who become rivals to ST★RISH

UTAU is a free singing synthesizer program that was developed to use wave files that could be put together to simulate singing. UTAU is best known for letting people create their own voice banks by the use of their own voice. 

The UTAU voice banks are often personified into characters called UTAUloids. This became popular after [[kasane teto|kasane teto]], a former [[vocaloid|vocaloid]] joke character, became known as an UTAU. 

**UTAU isn't [[vocaloid|vocaloid]]** and shouldn't be confused with or tagged as such (and vice versa).

A **vernier thruster** is a rocket engine used on a [[spacecraft|spacecraft]] for fine adjustments to the direction, attitude or velocity of the vehicle. Depending on the design of a craft's maneuvering and stability systems, it may simply be a smaller thruster complementing the main propulsion system, it may complement larger attitude control thrusters or be a part of the main reaction control system. 

The name is derived from vernier calipers (named after mathematician [Pierre Vernier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Vernier)) which have a primary scale for gross measurements and a secondary scale for fine measurements.

A notable and popular mecha from the [[macross|macross]] series. 

The **VF-1 Valkyrie** is Earth's three-form [[variable fighter|transformable]] aerospace multi-role combat [[mecha|mecha]] developed from [[alien|alien]] *[[protoculture|Overtechnology]]* obtained from the [[sdf-1|sdf-1]] "Macross" [[spacecraft|spacecraft]]. Its armaments include a modular [[gunpod|gunpod]], [[laser|laser]] cannons and several different types of [[missile|missile]]s. It can be equipped with modular attachments such as [[reactive armor|reactive armor]] and external fuel/thruster packs.

Thanks to its FF-2001 thermonuclear engines it can fly in both an atmosphere and outer [[space|space]]. The VF-1 [[variable fighter|variable fighter]] can also transform into fighter, [[gerwalk|gerwalk]] and [[battroid|battroid]] (giant robot) modes.

There are several different variants of the fighter, called [[vf-1a|vf-1a]], [[vf-1j|vf-1j]], [[vf-1d|vf-1d]], [[vf-1s|vf-1s]], [[vf-1j armored|vf-1j armored]], [[sdp-1 stampede valkyrie|sdp-1 stampede valkyrie]], [[ve-1|ve-1]], [[vt-1|vt-1]], [[vt-1 super|vt-1 super]], [[vf-1 super|vf-1 super]] and [[vf-1 strike|vf-1 strike]].

It first appeared in [[choujikuu yousai macross|choujikuu yousai macross]] (1982) where it was created by the [[u.n. spacy|u.n. spacy]] to fight a race of humanoid alien [[giant|giant]]s called [[zentradi|zentradi]]. It was eventually succeeded by the far more advanced [[vf-4|vf-4]] *Lighting III*.

In [[real life|real life]] the VF-1 was designed by [[kawamori shouji|kawamori shouji]] in the early [[1980s (style)|80s]]. The design of the mecha's fighter mode is loosely based on the [[f-14 tomcat|F-14]] combat jet and its name is a tribute to the [[xb-70|xb-70]], Kawamori's favorite aircraft.

This mecha was called the **VF-1 Veritech** in the [[robotech|robotech]] American adaptation of Macross. In that continuity the mecha was developed from alien *[[zor|Robotechnology]]* and the term VERITECH is an acronym which stands for **V**ariable **E**ngineering and **R**obotics **I**ntegration **TECH**nology.

**Artworks that serve as thumbnails** for videos in external platforms (e.g. [[youtube|youtube]], NicoNico, bilibili), which means the entire post is a thumbnail.
 
This tag should only be used in one of the following cases:
**1.** The original artist themselves created a video using their own illustration (e.g. post #6849506 and post #5598651)
**2.** Someone directly commissioned an artist to create the picture for their video (so they were granted permission to use it as a thumbnail) (e.g. post #6766229)

There must be proof that the image is a thumbnail of a real video, namely:
A. The video is directly linked in the *source field* (e.g. post #6278828)
B. The artist linked the video URL in the *commentary field* (e.g. post #6582857)
C. By posting a *comment* (e.g. post #6813221)

This tag should not be used for [[parody|parodies]] of actual video thumbnails (which means things like post #6515886 and post #6467103 do not qualify for this tag). It should not be used either for redrawn thumbnails of actual videos (as seen in post #8204965)

For posts that depict the User Interface of video platforms or made-up videos, use [[fake video|fake video]] (e.g. post #7159298)

[[making-of|making-of]] videos in Youtube and bilibili always include the respective illustration as a thumbnail. However, these must not get this tag because it would dilute its utility and make it redundant.

**The Vietnam War** (Vietnamese: Chiến tranh Việt Nam), also known as the **Second Indochina War**, and known in [[vietnam|vietnam]] as the **Resistance War Against America** (Vietnamese: Kháng chiến chống Mỹ) or simply **The American War**, was a war that occurred in Vietnam, Laos, and Cambodia from 1 November 1955 to the fall of Saigon on 30 April 1975. 

It was the second of the Indochina Wars and was officially fought between North Vietnam and the government of South Vietnam. 

The North Vietnamese army was supported by the [[soviet|Soviet Union]], [[china|china]] and other communist allies and the South Vietnamese army was supported by the [[united states|United States]], [[south korea|south korea]], [[australia|australia]], [[thailand|thailand]] and other anti-communist allies. The war is therefore considered a [[cold war|cold war]]-era proxy war.

The [[viet cong|viet cong]] (also known as the National Liberation Front, or NLF), a South Vietnamese communist common front aided by the North, fought a [[guerrilla|guerrilla]] war against anti-communist forces in the region, while the People's Army of Vietnam, also known as the North Vietnamese Army (NVA), engaged in more conventional warfare, at times committing large units to battle. 

American involvement in the war peaked in 1968, the same year that the communist side launched the Tet Offensive. The Tet Offensive failed in its goal of overthrowing the South Vietnamese government, but became the turning point in the war, as it persuaded a large segment of the U.S. population that its government's claims of progress toward winning the war were illusory despite many years of massive U.S. military aid to South Vietnam.

Direct U.S. military involvement ended on 15 August 1973. 

The capture of Saigon by the North Vietnamese Army in April 1975 marked the end of the war, and North and South Vietnam were reunified the following year under a communist government. 

Estimates of the number of Vietnamese soldiers and civilians killed vary from 966,000 to 3.8 million. Some 240,000–300,000 Cambodians, 20,000–62,000 Laotians and 58,220 U.S. service members also died in the conflict, and a further 1,626 remain missing in action.

A musical [[instrument|instrument]] of the string family. Basically it consists of a formed, resonating box over which are suspended a fingerboard and four tightened strings. The player holds the larger end under the chin and the opposite end in the hand. Meanwhile, the other hand draws a [[bow (music)|bow (music)]] over the strings to make them vibrate; alternately, this strings can be plucked. Said vibrations are amplified in the resonator.

Despite the name, content is not limited to [[youtube|youtube]], and often, a VTuber is someone who declares themselves as such.

The term was first popularized by [[kizuna ai|kizuna ai]], who called herself "the world's first virtual YouTuber". Many others followed suit, and the explosion in popularity of the practice lead the term to be used even outside of [[youtube|youtube]], though variations on the term have been introduced as to diminish the use of the brand name, including "VTuber", "Virtual Singer"/"VSinger" (for those that exclusively do music, not be confused with [[vsinger (vocaloid)|Vocaloid China]]), and "Virtual Liver"/"VLiver" (specifically referring to virtual streamers) or "Virtual Streamer"/"VStreamer" (due to the former term reminding folks of the organ in English). In Chinese, the term "Virtual Uploader"/"VUP" is used more commonly alongside "VTuber", after being first coined by [[xiao xi|xiao xi]] on [[bilibili|bilibili]]. In English, terms such as "PNGTuber" and "GIFTuber" also exist to refer to VTubers whose models use those formats, now that they are no longer the norm among indies (that had no access to 3D models back in the day). In Japan, the term "VLiver" is also used to refer creators and companies in the 'walled garden app' niche, such as [[iriam|iriam]] and [[anilive|anilive]], apps which viewers use to watch VTubers who stream exclusively on them.

This tag should apply to not only virtual YouTubers themselves, but also to [[parody|parodies]] of virtual YouTubers, references to them, fictitious virtual YouTubers, fake virtual YouTubers, and concept art that ultimately isn't used (for the latter three, `original` should be used). While tagging mascots and staff with the tag is fine, family members and friends of VTubers don't apply, unless they too are VTubers, nor do things merely associated with VTubers.

Vladilena Milizé, nicknamed Lena, is a female main character from the light novel series [[86 -eightysix-|86 -eightysix-]]. Lena is one of the Alba, a race characterized by their silver hair (appearing [[light blue hair|light blue]], [[white hair|white]], or [[grey hair|grey]]), and silver eyes (appearing [[grey eyes|grey]]). Lena has [[long hair|long hair]] with [[bangs|bangs]] that is usually unadorned and loose, with two [[antenna hair|antenna-like ahoge]].  

At the start of the series she is 16 years old, but through a combination of talent and connections has already obtained the commissioned officer rank of Major in the Republic of San Magnolia's military. Lena usually wears a San Magnolia military uniform, which is a blue [[military uniform|military uniform]] composed of a [[blue jacket|blue]], [[high collar|high-collared]], [[long sleeves|long-sleeved]], [[cropped jacket|cropped jacket]] with an [[armband|armband]], a [[white shirt|white shirt]] with blue and gold trim, a [[blue skirt|blue]] [[high-waist skirt|high-waist skirt]], a [[white belt|white]] [[o-ring belt|o-ring]] [[belt|belt]] with one strap on one side and two straps on the other, a [[blue headwear|blue]] [[military hat|military]] [[peaked cap|peaked cap]], [[white thighhighs|white]] [[thighhighs|thighhighs]], and [[blue footwear|blue]] [[boots|boots]].  She wears her uniform along with [[white thighhighs|white thighhighs]] supported by [[garter straps|garter straps]] (the author admitted this was due to his own fetish for [[garter belt|garter belt]]s).

At the beginning of the series she is assigned as the handler of Spearhead Squadron and goes by the call sign Handler One.  After the events of the first cour of the anime/first volume of the light novel, Lena dyes a [[streaked hair|streak]] of her hair [[red hair|red]] and wears a black variant of her uniform, changing the color of her [[black jacket|jacket]], [[black skirt|skirt]], [[black headwear|hat]], [[black thighhighs|thighhighs]], and [[black footwear|boots]], thus including all five colors of the San Magnolia Republic's flag in her appearance.  She later obtains the nicknames "Bloody Reina" and "The Bloodstained Queen".

VOCALOID is a DTM (Desktop Music) singing synthesizer engine developed by [[yamaha|yamaha]] Corporation in collaboration with Pompeu Fabra University. 

VOCALOID products are created by various individual studios that develop voicebanks using the most current engine tools. The first set of synthesizer vocals was released in January 2004.

On August 31st, 2007, [[hatsune miku|hatsune miku]] was released for the VOCALOID2 engine. As the first product in [[crypton future media|crypton future media]]'s Character Vocal Series, she was the first voicebank designed with an anime-styled avatar representing the singer of the voicebank. Her immediate and immense popularity led to nearly all future voicebanks following the same trend of having an anime-styled avatar, a trend that still continues to this day.

The popularity of VOCALOID has inspired the creation of [[list of vocal synthesizers|similar products]].

A Japanese war fan is a fan designed for use in warfare. Several types of war fans were used by the samurai class of feudal Japan and each had a different look and purpose.

There are three kinds of war fan:

Gunsen (軍扇) were folding fans used by the average warriors to cool themselves off. They were made of wood, bronze, brass or a similar metal for the inner spokes, and often used thin iron or other metals for the outer spokes or cover, making them lightweight but strong. Warriors would hang their fans from a variety of places, most typically from the belt or the breastplate, though the latter often impeded the use of a sword or a bow. Example: post #2540638

[[tessen|tessen]] (鉄扇) were folding fans with outer spokes made of heavy plates of iron which were designed to look like normal, harmless folding fans or solid clubs shaped to look like a closed fan. Samurai could take these to places where swords or other overt weapons were not allowed, and some swordsmanship schools included training in the use of the tessen as a weapon. The tessen was also used for fending off knives and darts, as a throwing weapon, and as an aid in swimming. Example: post #1904493

[[gunbai|gunbai]] (Gumbai), Gunpai (Gumpai) or dansen uchiwa (軍配) were large solid open fans that could be solid iron, metal with wooden core, or solid wood, which were carried by high-ranking officers. They were used to ward off arrows, as a sunshade, and to signal to troops. Also used by scoring referees in sumo wrestling matches. Example: post #1990137

A late [[medieval|medieval]] weapon of war originally intended for close combat action. It was designed to deliver heavy damage against well-armored opponents through sheer blunt force. Though some adapted it as a versatile [[polearm|polearm]] weapon instead by giving it a longer handle.

Real life war hammers are comparable in size with a regular carpentry [[hammer|hammer]], though with a longer handle and often a spike opposite the blunt head to pierce armor. This tag can also be applied to [[huge weapon|huge]] fantasy weapons depicted simply as an oversized [[hammer|hammer]]/[[sledgehammer|sledgehammer]].

**Warship Girls R** (战舰少女 *Zhan Jian Shao Nyu*) is a shipgirl-themed Chinese smartphone game.

Gameplay is similar to [[kantai collection|kantai collection]]. However, unlike [[kantai collection|kantai collection]], where most of the ships originally came from the [[imperial japanese navy|imperial japanese navy]], Warship Girls R from the start featured ships from various Navy forces around the world. 

#### History

The game was initially released by "Suzhou Paiqu Network Technology":[http://www.p7game.com/], as Warship Girls, for Android and iOS devices in September, 2014.

In July 2015 there was a split between the publisher of the game and its developer, MoeFantasy (幻萌), and from then on each company developed and released its own version of the game, which differed in available characters, interface design, etc.

On August 29th 2015 at ComiCon16, Shanghai, MoeFantasy revealed via trailer the development of *Project R*, a major overhaul of the game including new features, updated UI and a new animated combat system. This version was released in November the same year as client version 2.0 and was dubbed 战舰少女R (Warship Girls R). The MoeFantasy version would become the main focus of all community efforts, from wikis to drop data libraries and fan works.

On June 23rd 2016, it was announced on the community's Baidu forum and later as official statements that a settlement had been reached between the two companies. SPNT shut down its servers on September in the same year.

On October 24th 2017, a Japanese translated version and server released under the name 戦艦少女R, or Senkan Shoujo R.

On December 18th 2018, a Global server and Korean server were officially released.

Also in 2018, on September 8th, a spinoff was released that was made by MoeFantasy's Japanese branch, entitled 蒼青のミラージュ or [[steelblue mirage|MiST: The mirage of steelblue]]. Due to various reasons, it became unavailable on March 15th, 2020, with refunds beginning at the same time, ending on June 15th.

The Global server and Korean server were shut down on the 31st of August, 2021.

Water tanks are usually made of plastic, glass, or steel.

An elevated structure supporting a [[water|water]] tank constructed at a height sufficient to pressurize a water supply system for the distribution of potable (drinking) water, and to provide emergency storage for fire protection.

A machine used to convert the energy of running [[water|water]] into useful mechanical power. It consists of a [[wheel|wheel]] with fixed blades that intercept the flow of water. Water wheels were used in the pre-modern era for grinding grain in gristmills or powering industrial machinery, but they have since been replaced with other forms of power.

#### Personality

Despite being called "the most normal-looking" and "oddball" out of the other [[holomyth|holomyth]] debut (due to her not being a monster girl), she is actually the most chaotic of the bunch. She also likes to make jokes and banter, giving rise to her connection with the [[ground pound|ground pound]] meme.

Her mascot and pet dog [[bubba (watson amelia)|Bubba]] can occasionally be heard during her streams. She also has a pet cat named [[wellington (watson amelia)|wellington (watson amelia)]].

Due to their frequent collaborations and chemistry both in videos and on Twitter, it is common to see her coupled with [[gawr gura|gawr gura]], a ship known as "AmeSame". Fans were quick to also compare her to [[akai haato|akai haato]] due to their similar chaotic nature, which extends to collabs.

Watson Amelia reached one million subscribers on February 11 (JST) / 10 (PST) 2021.

Weiss Schnee is one of the main characters of [[rwby|rwby]], a 3DCG series produced by Rooster Teeth. 

Weiss is the "W" in RWBY, and is associated with the color white. Her character design is inspired by [[snow white (grimm)|snow white (grimm)]].
[[winter schnee|winter schnee]] is her sister. As heiress to the Schnee Dust Company, her life has been marked by pressure. Her arrogant and prickly exterior hides a softer heart. 

#### Abilities
She wields a sword/revolver hybrid weapon named [[myrtenaster|myrtenaster]], a "Multi-Action Dust [[rapier|rapier]]" (MADR). Her symbol is a snowflake, and [[magic circle|magic circles]] ("glyphs") appear when she uses her semblance (special ability).  

#### Physical characteristics
Weiss has [[blue eyes|blue eyes]] and [[long hair|long]] [[white hair|white hair]] tied into a [[ponytail|ponytail]] off to one [[side ponytail|side]]. She has a [[scar|scar]] [[scar across eye|over]] her left eye.  

She stands 5' 3" tall (including [[high heels|high heels]]). 

#### Attire

She usually wears a [[tiara|tiara]] in her hair, around her ponytail, and often wears a bit of jewelry: [[earrings|earrings]] and a [[necklace|necklace]] with [[pendant|pendant]]. Her default outfit includes a white [[cropped jacket|cropped jacket]] with a [[high collar|high collar]] (revealing the red interior lining) and [[long sleeves|long]] [[wide sleeves|wide sleeves]], a blueish-[[white dress|white]] [[strapless dress|strapless dress]] with [[lace-trimmed skirt|lace-trimmed skirt]] over a [[petticoat|petticoat]], and blueish-[[white footwear|white]] [[boots|boots]] with [[high heel boots|high heels]]. Her [[belt|belt]] is a [[ribbon|ribbon]] tied with a [[bow|bow]] in front, holding a [[belt pouch|belt pouch]] with Dust supplies on her back.  

Her Beacon [[school uniform|school uniform]] consists of a [[white shirt|white]] [[blouse|blouse]] with [[neck ribbon|neck ribbon]], brown [[blazer|blazer]], and [[plaid skirt|plaid skirt]].

[[nintendo|nintendo]]'s fifth home video [[game console|game console]]. Formerly known as the "Revolution". The original model was released in 2006 and a reconfigured version was released in 2011.

The **Wii** competes with [[sony|sony]]'s [[playstation 3|playstation 3]] and [[microsoft|microsoft]]'s [[xbox 360|xbox 360]] as part of the seventh generation of video game consoles. 

The Wii has many advanced features compared to the previous Nintendo consoles. For example, the primary wireless controller, the [[wii remote|wii remote]], can be used as a handheld pointing device and detects movement in three dimensions. Another notable feature of the console is WiiConnect24, which enables it to receive messages and updates over the Internet while in standby mode.

The Wii is Nintendo's fifth home console, and the successor of the Nintendo [[gamecube|gamecube]], with most models being fully backwardly compatible with all GameCube games and most accessories.

It was succeeded by the [[wii u|wii u]].

The [[wild arms|wild arms]] series as a whole. See [[wild arms 1|wild arms 1]] for the first title in the series.

The original *Wild Arms* game was released by Media Vision in 1997 on the [[playstation 1|playstation 1]], one of the first RPGs for the console. It would become overlooked in favor of Squaresoft's [[final fantasy vii|final fantasy vii]], which was released around the same time. Despite this setback, the series still remains popular in Japan, and its tenth anniversary was celebrated in 2007 with a large number of cameos in [[wild arms 5|wild arms 5]] and a limited edition artbook.

The setting for the games is consistently a combination of Western and science-fiction tropes, and each story takes place on a (usually dying and/or war-ravaged) world known as Filgaia.

There are six Wild Arms games, an anime series, and a manga associated with the series:

- [[wild arms 1|wild arms 1]] - *Wild Arms Alter Code F* (re-release title)
- [[wild arms 2|wild arms 2]] - *Wild Arms 2nd Ignition*
- [[wild arms 3|wild arms 3]] - *Wild Arms Advanced 3rd*
- [[wild arms 4|wild arms 4]] - *Wild Arms the 4th Detonator*
- [[wild arms 5|wild arms 5]] - *Wild Arms the Vth Vanguard* 
- [[wild arms xf|wild arms xf]] - *Wild Arms Crossfire*
- [[wild arms twilight venom|wild arms twilight venom]] anime
- [[wild arms flower thieves|wild arms flower thieves]] manga

#### See also

The first game in the [[wild arms|wild arms]] series, encompassing both the original PS1 release and its remake Wild Arms: Alter Code F.

Taking place in the fantasy world of Filgaia, Wild Arms follows the adventures of a band of miscreants and adventurers called Dream Chasers who scour the world in search of excitement and fortune. The player assumes control of a young boy named Rudy who has the ability to operate powerful weapons called Ancient Relic Machines (ARMs), forbidden remnants of a lost age that resemble guns. Along with his companions Jack and Cecilia, the group must use their respective skills to navigate through the vast wastelands and dungeons of Filgaia and prevent an otherworldly threat from reviving their lost leader and destroying the world. -- Wikipedia

The PS1 Wild Arms started the series' recurring idea of steampunk, spaghetti western-styled worlds and characters blended together with typical fantasy world ideas like magic and summonable deities. In addition, both Wild Arms games are lauded for their storylines and characterization.

The PS1 version only has three playable characters:

- [[rody roughnight|rody roughnight]]
- [[jack van burace|jack van burace]]
- [[cecilia lynne adelhyde|cecilia lynne adelhyde]]

The PS2 version adds four new PCs who were all present in the original as NPCs.

- [[jane maxwell|jane maxwell]], aka Calamity Jane
- [[magdalen harts|magdalen harts]]
- [[emma hetfield|emma hetfield]]
- [[zed (wild arms)|zed (wild arms)]]

The sequel to the original PS1 Wild Arms game (a.k.a. [[wild arms 1|wild arms 1]]), produced in 2000 by Media Vision. It is available on the PlayStation Network for the Playstation 3 and Playstation Portable. While several elements from the original are borrowed for the sequel, the story is entirely different.

Wild Arms 2 starts off similar to Wild Arms, assuming control of three separate characters who eventually meet up and undertake missions against the terrorist organization Odessa. The overall story encompasses sacrifice and what it means to be a hero. The original members of the Agile Remote Missions Squad (ARMS) are:

- [[ashley winchester|ashley winchester]]
- [[lilka eleniak|lilka eleniak]]
- [[brad evans|brad evans]]

Later, two more characters join during the story:

- [[tim rhymeless|tim rhymeless]]
- [[kanon (wild arms 2)|kanon (wild arms 2)]]

In addition, [[marivel armitage|marivel armitage]] can be recruited as an optional character to unlock various extras.

The third game in the [[wild arms|wild arms]] franchise, also known as Wild Arms: Advanced 3rd. It all begins when the four main characters [[virginia maxwell|virginia maxwell]], [[jet enduro|jet enduro]], [[clive winslett|clive winslett]], and [[gallows carradine|gallows carradine]] meet each other on a train while after the same artifact. They suddenly need to team up to fend off a group of thieves led by [[janus cascade|janus cascade]], after which they travel together to learn about the mysteries surrounding the dying world Filgaia.

Of any of the games, this particular Wild Arms is well-known for its complexity and numerous plot twists. It is also the first game to transition into full 3-D environments. The only four playable characters are:

- [[virginia maxwell|virginia maxwell]]
- [[clive winslett|clive winslett]]
- [[jet enduro|jet enduro]]
- [[gallows carradine|gallows carradine]]

The fourth game in the [[wild arms|wild arms]] series, also known as Wild Arms: The 4th Detonator. Young [[jude maverick|jude maverick]] lives in Ciel, isolated from the rest of Filgaia, when intruders happen upon his home and he meets [[yulie ahtreide|yulie ahtreide]]. When the invaders attack and destroy Ciel, Jude and Yulie partner with two other Drifters, [[arnaud g. vasquez|arnaud g. vasquez]] and [[raquel applegate|raquel applegate]], to find the truth while discovering their paths to adulthood. Opposing them are the forces of Brionac who want to use Yulie's power to activate the Divine Weapon, a powerful and forbidden ARM.

The fifth installment in the [[wild arms|wild arms]] gaming franchise, also known as Wild Arms: The Vth Vanguard. It celebrates the series' 10th anniversary with an artbook featuring characters from the five games, plus cameos of the previous games' characters in WA5.

The setting is on Filgaia, as always, but an alien race called the Veruni took over 100 years ago and dominated the human race. The main hero [[dean stark|dean stark]] and his friend [[rebecca streisand|rebecca streisand]] live secluded from this life and have big dreams, but come across a golem's arm (from [[asgard (wild arms)|asgard (wild arms)]]) falling from the sky. Their adventure begins when they meet an amnesiac girl inside the arm; she only knows her name, [[avril vent fleur|avril vent fleur]], and the words 'Johnny Appleseed'.

The sixth installment of the [[wild arms|wild arms]] franchise exclusively for the Playstation Portable. The 'XF' in the title is pronounced as 'Crossfire'. This is the only title to utilize a tactical RPG format, rather than traditional combat used in the earlier games. It blends in the HEX system introduced in the fourth and fifth games by allowing characters to move in any one of six spaces around them, rather than in a square. The Flame Haze bound to the Crimson Lord Tiamat. Wilhelmina is [[shana|shana]]'s adoptive mother (though neither of them uses the word), having rescued her as an infant and raised her. She has the appearance of a woman in her 20s, but is clearly much older; she seems to have a past with every new character who turns up. She's also one of the most skilled and powerful fighters in the series -- bad news for anyone who gets close to Shana, of whom she's *very* protective.

Wilhelmina is something of an oddball. As the servant of a Crimson God (Alastor, the one bound to Shana), she's highly aristocratic, ending her sentences with *de arimasu* (an old-fashioned, formal variant of *desu*) and wearing a [[maid|maid]] outfit at all times. She speaks in monotone and has facial expressions to match; it takes a lot to make her smile. Nonetheless, her emotions run deep and she forms strong bonds with those who fight beside her. 

Almost all pictures of Wilhelmina include Tiamat, who's housed in her [[maid headdress|frilly maid thing]], and therefore has no separate tag.

A story-focused game with horror and light action elements created in RPG Maker 2000 by [[bluestar iz|IZ (BLUE STAR Entertainment)]].  

It follows [[claire elford|claire elford]], a cheerful young woman that gets trapped in a cursed mansion along with four other men - the traveler/witch researcher [[ashe bradley|ashe bradley]], the mysterious individual [[wilardo adler|wilardo adler]], a gentle young man named [[noel levine|noel levine]], and the lord of the mansion [[sirius gibson|sirius gibson]]. Throughout the course of five days, the group has to find a way to escape the mansion, all while uncovering the secrets within it, and learning the truth about the legendary wish-granting treasure: the *Witch's Heart*. 

The game is split into four scenarios, each based on the different main characters trapped with Claire, and they’re all mandatory in order to complete the base game. There are mild combat elements through the monsters and bosses the player encounters, as well as a wide variety of mini games and interactions with other characters. 

The game has a sequel named the "Bonus Stage", along with four endings of the routes in the form of separate games called "Conclusion" - though at the time only Sirius’ Conclusion is released.

A second season aired Fall 2011 and was titled *Working'!!*, with an apostrophe in the name.  The third and final season airing July, Summer 2015 and is titled *Working!!!*, with three exclamation marks in the name. The alternative "export" name of the series is **Wagnaria!!** which is the name of the restaurant chain of the restaurant where most of the series takes place. 

It is a work-life comedy series with a quirky cast mostly consisting out of teens and young adults. Multiple characters in the series have feelings toward each other. However, this anime is for the most part not romance driven, so your mileage might vary.

They also created a World of Tanks introductory comic series featuring various Girls und Panzer characters, and included GuP tanks in World of Tanks Blitz. Wargaming also produced a Girls und Panzer der Film Mod Pack with new voices, a garage theme and tank skins.

**World War I** (WWI), which was predominantly called the World War or **The Great War** from its occurrence until 1939 ([[world war ii|world war ii]]), and the **First World War** or World War I thereafter, was a major war centred in Europe. It began on 28 July 1914 when [[austria|austria]]-[[hungary|hungary]] declared war against [[serbia|serbia]] and lasted until 11 November 1918 after **[[germany|germany]] and the Allies signed an armistice**.

The geopolitical changes it generated in most of the world after its eventual outcome were a direct cause for [[world war ii|world war ii]] more than 20 years later.

World War I is notable for stalemate [[trench|trench]] warfare on the western front, and the development and application of new technology in warfare such as [[tank|tanks]], [[airplane|airplanes]] and [[submarine|submarines]].

**The Second World War** (abbreviated "WWII" or "WW2") was a major worldwide [[war|war]] that was first set off by the [[second sino-japanese war|Japanese invasion of Manchuria]] and then officially began when [[nazi|nazi]] [[germany|germany]] attacked [[poland|poland]] on September 1st of 1939 and ended after [[japan|japan]] surrendered on August 15th of 1945. It is considered a result of the outcome of [[world war i|world war i]].

The belligerents formed two major factions, the Allied Powers (or "Allies") and the Axis Powers (or "Axis").

World War II is considered the deadliest military conflict in human history. Over 60 million people died as a result of the fighting and/or resulting resource shortages, as well as deliberate mass killings throughout the war, and hundreds of millions were displaced or left destitute in the aftermath. WW2 can also be considered the deathblow to the old European empires which had dominated history up to that point; the war left them financially, militarily, and culturally even more exhausted than they had been after WW1 and saw the rise of two new super-powers with a rather anti-colonial bent to them: the [[soviet|USSR]] and the [[united states|USA]], thus kickstarting the [[cold war|cold war]].

Technologically, WW2 saw the first usage of the many trends that still dominate warfare to this day: the first modern [[missile|missile]]s and [[rocket|rocket]]s were used during WW2, [[aircraft carrier|aircraft carrier]]s replaced [[battleship|battleship]]s as the dominant surface warfare vessels, unmanned radio controlled vehicles saw limited use during the war, and [[stg 44|stg 44]], the world's first assault rifle, entered service during the later half of the war. The most important and influential technology used, however, is the first (and only) usage of a [[nuclear weapon|nuclear weapon]] in the history of warfare: [[atomic bombings of hiroshima and nagasaki|when the Japanese cities of Hiroshima and Nagasaki were destroyed by the atomic bombs dropped by the USA]].

This tag can be applied if the image is related to World War 2, such as featuring technology (tanks, aircraft, warships or weapons) of the era, uniforms & troops, or battle scenes.

**Xenogears** is a videogame developed and published by Square (now Square Enix) for the Sony [[playstation 1|playstation 1]].

In this Japanese RPG, you can either fight on foot, or in large robots called gears. It is the predecessor of the [[xenosaga|xenosaga]] franchise, and the creators had considered it would become the 5th game in a 6 part Xenosaga chronology. It was also spiritually succeeded by the [[xenoblade chronicles (series)|xenoblade chronicles (series)]] franchise.

It was released on February 11, 1998 in Japan and on October 21, 1998 in North America.

Xenogears never saw a PAL release. It is currently available for digital purchase only on the Japan PSN store, the English digital download version has not yet been offered in other regions.

A fictional [[mecha|mecha]] from the [[gundam|gundam]] series. It is the lead Gundam of [[gundam hathaway's flash|gundam hathaway's flash]].

The **RX-105 Xi Gundam** and the [[penelope (hathaway's flash)|RX-104FF Penelope]] were classified as fifth-generation MS and are said to have been developed and constructed by [[anaheim electronics|anaheim electronics]]. It was a unique [[mobile suit|MS]] with a built-in Minovsky Flight Unit and was equipped with the latest Beam Barrier system. Since the Penelope relied on optional units to obtain similar functions, it can be said that the Xi Gundam was a truly completed fifth-generation MS that could function independently.

Its armaments include a [[beam rifle|beam rifle]], a pair of [[energy sword|beam sabers]] (with a [[double-blade|double-blade]] function similar to the [[nu gundam|nu gundam]]'s large beam saber), a [[shield|shield]] with a [[beam cannon|beam cannon]] on its tip, forearm-mounted triple missiles, and its signature *Funnel Missiles*. True to its name, these [[funnels (gundam)|funnels (gundam)]] functions like remote controlled [[missile|missiles]], guided by the pilot's Newtype abilities and exploding upon impact. A [[fashion|fashion]] style based on the style trends of the late '90s and early 2000s, the cusp of the new millennium - as well as 2000s retrofuturism. The modern Y2K fashion revival has been spearheaded by musical acts such as [[pinkpantheress|pinkpantheress]] and certain [[k-pop|k-pop]] girl groups - most notably [[newjeans|newjeans]].

Clothing often uses shiny materials, [[fur|fur]], and [[denim|denim]], and may be decorated with sequins or [[rhinestone|rhinestone]]s. [[leopard print|leopard print]] and [[camouflage|camouflage]] are common, as well as imagery of butterflies, stars, and hearts.

Common garments include [[tube top|tube top]]s and cropped [[tank top|tank top]]s and big [[jacket|jacket]]s on the upper body, and oversized pants such as [[cargo pants|cargo pants]] or [[bell-bottoms|bell-bottoms]], denim shorts and skirts, or [[miniskirt|miniskirt]]s in bright colors on the lower body. Bottomwear often has a low-rise waistline. Common accessories include [[sunglasses|sunglasses]], [[belt|belt]]s with heart-shaped or jeweled buckles, [[leg warmers|leg]] and [[arm warmers|arm warmers]], fluffy [[hat|hat]]s, and [[handbag|handbag]]s. Footwear commonly worn includes [[fur-trimmed boots|fur-trimmed boots]], and [[platform footwear|platform footwear]].

It may sometimes overlap with [[cyber fashion|cyber fashion]], [[gyaru|gyaru]], [[streetwear|streetwear]] and [[heisei retro|heisei retro]].

**Yahari Ore no Seishun LoveCome wa Machigatteiru.** (やはり俺の青春ラブコメはまちがっている。, abbrev. *OreGairu* or *Hamachi*) is a Japanese light novel series written by Watari Wataru and illustrated by [[ponkan 8|ponkan 8]]. It is published by Shogakukan under the Gagaga Bunko imprint and spans 10 volumes, released between March 2011 and November 2014 and three short story collection volumes.

Additionally, the series has received three manga series adaptations and two manga anthology volumes. The artists of the manga series are:
- [[kazuki rechi|kazuki rechi]] - *Yahari Ore no Seishun Lovecome wa machigatteiru. -Monologue-* (やはり俺の青春ラブコメはまちがっている。-妄言録-),
- [[io naomichi|io naomichi]] - *Yahari Ore no Seishun Lovecome wa machigatteiru. @comic * (やはり俺の青春ラブコメはまちがっている。@comic),
- [[taneda yuuta|taneda yuuta]] - *Yahari 4koma demo Ore no Seishun Lovecome wa machigatteiru.* (やはり4コマでも俺の青春ラブコメはまちがっている。).

An anime television series, produced by Brain's Base, aired between April 5 and June 28, 2013, a second and third season, produced by feel. titled *Yahari Ore no Seishun Lovecome wa machigatteiru. Zoku* (やはり俺の青春ラブコメはまちがっている。続), premiered on April 2, 2015, and *Yahari Ore no Seishun Love Comedy wa Machigatteiru. Kan* ( やはり俺の青春ラブコメはまちがっている。完), premiered on Jul 10, 2020. All seasons were licensed in North America by Sentai Filmworks under the titles *My Teen Romantic Comedy SNAFU*, *My Teen Romantic Comedy SNAFU TOO!*, and *My Teen Romantic Comedy SNAFU Climax!*.

A video game, titled *Yahari Game demo Ore no Seishun Rabu Kome wa Machigatteiru.* and published by 5pb., for the PlayStation Vita was released on September 19, 2013.

The "Nine-Tailed Strategist". Extra Stage boss and Phantasm stage midboss of [[touhou|touhou]]'s [[perfect cherry blossom|perfect cherry blossom]].

[[yakumo yukari|yakumo yukari]]'s 800+-year-old [[kyuubi|kyuubi]] [[kitsune|kitsune]] shikigami who specializes in black magic. She is also powerful enough to have her own shikigami, a [[nekomata|nekomata]] named [[chen|chen]], to whom she is portrayed to act motherly towards prominently in fanworks.

In volume two of [[strange creators of outer world|strange creators of outer world]], it has been revealed that Ran is actually a shikigami parasitically taking host of a nine-tailed fox youkai so strongly that the host's personality never shows on the surface; leading people to not have any difficulty seeing her as a kitsune. However, this seemed to be subtlely hinted at in Yukari's [[bohemian archive in japanese red|bohemian archive in japanese red]] article where Yukari constantly repeats to [[shameimaru aya|Aya]] that Ran is a shikigami and not an animal.

In [[unfinished dream of all living ghost|unfinished dream of all living ghost]], Ran (or maybe just her host body) is revealed to have once been an inhabitant of the Animal Realm, and to have been friends with [[toutetsu yuuma|toutetsu yuuma]].

Ran has been described to have a gentle personality and to share her host's species-wide love of [[aburaage|fried tofu]]. She excels at mathematics and is able to solve nigh impossible equations instantly; simply seeing it as a hobby to kill time. She is rather robotic in nature when it comes to following Yukari's orders whereas Ran herself describes them as "Yukari's programming". Due to her master's prominent sleeping habits, Ran is usually doing her bidding at a constant. However, Yukari herself has stated that she would like to see Ran do something other than simply follow her orders.

Ran is simply seen as a tool that's loved in Yukari's eyes. If she is to ever stray away from her duties as a shikigami or to forget that she is one, she is to be violently disciplined, such as being beaten on the head by her parasol.

She is notorious in many fanworks as a streaker, earning her the nickname "Suppa Tenko":/pools/1733 ("Naked Heavenly Fox"), and for bursting into an [[excessive nosebleed|excessive nosebleed]] if Chen does anything exceptionally cute.

The "Youkai of Boundaries". Phantasm Stage boss of [[touhou|touhou]]'s [[perfect cherry blossom|perfect cherry blossom]] and later a recurring playable character.

A powerful youkai of at least 1200 years of age, reputedly older than [[gensokyo|gensokyo]] itself. Nominally responsible for guarding the border between Gensokyo and the outside world, but is frequently sleeping or slacking around, leaving her work to her shikigami [[yakumo ran|yakumo ran]] and Ran's own shikigami [[chen|chen]].

Yukari has the power to manipulate boundaries, as well as create [[gap (touhou)|gap (touhou)]]s, leading to her nickname "Sukima". However, she frequently holds back her powers and most of the time she only goes as far as playfully dragging any unsuspecting human from the outside world into Gensoukyou.

in [[silent sinner in blue|silent sinner in blue]] she has two pet crows - [[zenki (touhou)|zenki (touhou)]] and [[goki (touhou)|goki (touhou)]].

Besides her servants, she is friends with [[ibuki suika|ibuki suika]], [[saigyouji yuyuko|saigyouji yuyuko]] (whom she knew from as early as the latter's days as a human) and [[hakurei reimu|hakurei reimu]] (the other barrier guardian, whom she sometimes pesters). Also hinted to be [[morichika rinnosuke|morichika rinnosuke]]'s business partner and supplier of items from the outside world. Yukari has an as-yet undefined connection to [[maribel hearn|maribel hearn]].

"**Yandere Simulator** is a stealth game about stalking a boy and secretly eliminating any girl who seems interested in him, while maintaining the image of an innocent schoolgirl. ... The gameplay is similar to the [[hitman (game)|Hitman series]]; you are put into a large environment filled with many NPCs, and you must track down a specific target and eliminate them. You can use stealth to kill your target without any witnesses, stage an accident that leaves no evidence, or just slaughter anyone who gets in your way. If you don't dispose of corpses, clean up blood, and destroy evidence, then the police might be able to link you to a murder and arrest you." [1]

The game is notorious and often meme'd on for its long development cycle, primarily due to the fact that the developer YandereDev (Alex Mahan) often sidetracked his work to other things, such as streaming and [[virtual youtuber|vtubing]], as well as several controversies surrounding it. As such, the game is still under development as of date.

Upon her arrival on Earth, Tohka wore an Astral Dress with a black, cream, and pink color scheme and a set of purple-and-cream plated armor which adorned her shoulders and waist. The dress is open at the back and made up into a black corset (which exposes a part of her cleavage) and a two-layered, knee-length skirt which has a pink-to-white gradient. Her hair is tied back using a butterfly-shaped hair accessory. She also wears a pair of gauntlets which have petal-like cuffs, both sharing the same color scheme as her attire, as well as a pair of armored boots. While using Halvanhelev, her ribbon grows longer and sharper, and her underlying dress of light becomes more ragged.

Upon her admission to Raizen High School, Tohka adopts the female uniform of said school. This apparel consists of a black, long-sleeved top (winter version), or a white, short-sleeved top (summer version), together with a blue skirt, and a pair of long, black stockings that reach up to half of her thigh.

The **Year of the Dog** is not any particular year in history, but a recurring position in the 12-year zodiac cycle. Years of the Dog include 1934, 1946, 1958, 1970, [[1982|1982]], [[1994|1994]], [[2006|2006]], [[2018|2018]], and 2030.

The Dog occupies the eleventh position in the Chinese zodiac, after [[year of the rooster|the Rooster]], and before [[year of the pig|the Pig]].

The Dragon is the fifth of the 12 Chinese zodiac animals. Years of the Dragon include 1928, 1940, 1952, 1964, 1976, [[1988|1988]], [[2000|2000]], [[2012|2012]], and [[2024|2024]].

A **Year of the Dragon** always occurs after a [[year of the rabbit|Rabbit year]] and before a [[year of the snake|Snake year]].

#### See also

- [[chinese zodiac|chinese zodiac]]

The Goat is the eighth animal in the Chinese zodiac.  Years of the Goat include: 1931, 1943, 1955, 1967, 1979, [[1991|1991]], [[2003|2003]], [[2015|2015]], 2027.

A **Year of the Goat** always occurs after a [[year of the horse|Horse year]] and before a [[year of the monkey|Monkey year]].

The Chinese word (kanji) 羊 refers to both goats and [[sheep|sheep]], and is interpreted in Japan only as sheep.

#### See also

- [[chinese zodiac|chinese zodiac]]

The Monkey is the ninth of 12 animals in the recurring 12-year Chinese zodiac cycle. Monkey years include: 1932, 1944, 1956,  1968, 1980, [[1992|1992]], [[2004|2004]], [[2016|2016]], 2028.

The **Year of the Monkey** always occurs after a [[year of the goat|Goat year]] and before a [[year of the rooster|Rooster year]].

The Ox occupies the second position in the Chinese Zodiac. Years of birth include 1913, 1925, 1937, 1949, 1961, 1973, [[1985|1985]], [[1997|1997]], [[2009|2009]], [[2021|2021]], 2033.

An **Year of the Ox** always occurs after a [[year of the rat|Rat year]] and before a [[year of the tiger|Tiger year]]. Artists often portray female characters dressed up as or resembling a [[cow|cow]] since cows are simply female oxen.

The Pig is the last of 12 animals representing the Chinese zodiac. The following are years of the Pig: 1935, 1947, 1959, 1971, [[1983|1983]], [[1995|1995]], [[2007|2007]], [[2019|2019]], 2031.

A [[year of the dog|Dog year]] always comes before the **Year of the Pig**, and a [[year of the rat|Rat year]] always comes afterwards in the next 12-year Chinese zodiac animal cycle.

In Japan, the wild [[boar|boar]] is used instead of the (domesticated) pig.

The program presenter never told how to use it, though it is probably used for the declaration of sexual intention.

An *[[idolmaster cinderella girls|iDOLM@STER Cinderella Girls]]* character in the Passion (Yellow Sun) category. She is a mysterious girl who goes out of her way to help strangers, speaking and acting as if she's more than just an ordinary person. Her manner of speech, in addition to being very slow and soft, is highly elaborate and old-fashioned, making her sound more like a historical priestess than a modern-day girl: in particular she is known for ending her sentences with でして (deshite), which is regarded as a formal or old-fashioned form of です (desu).

Yoshino has an interest in shrines and temples, which suggests that before becoming an idol she was a miko - however it is heavily implied (due to her ability to resolve people's wishes and find lost items) that she is some form of supernatural entity, possibly the goddess Benzaiten (one of the Seven Lucky Gods or shichifukuji), as several of Yoshino's illustrations show her having a connection to water; in addition to fortune, music and words, Benzaiten is the goddess of water. If that is the case, then the Producer successfully talked a goddess into becoming an idol - although it's possible that she does it just because she enjoys being worshipped.

She is voiced by [[takada yuuki|takada yuuki]].

[[mcdonald's|mcdonald's]] Japan's post-5pm menu line-up, known as Yoru Mac (literally "Night Mac", with the alternate name of "McDonald's in the Night"), introduced in June 2017 first in Aichi, Gifu and Mie Prefecture, before being expanded nation-wide in March 2018. Several different products have come and gone as part of the line-up, and in turn, so too have several advertising campaigns.

In Autumn 2023, one such advertisement campaign launched, running from late September to early November, focused on depicting characters (ex. a family, a group of friends, etc. hanging out together) happily enjoying items from the line-up, in commercials animated by [[uraura ura-chan|uraura ura-chan]]. The main mascots of the campaign are a set of Halloween characters, originally first appearing in a Spring 2023 Yoru Mac advertising campaign called "Yoru Mac Manager", even receiving their own dedicated commercial (post #6713997). The six commercials that released would collectively be entitled the "Yoru Mac Anime Series" by McDonald's.

One of the commercials, depicting a [[mother (yoru mac)|mother (yoru mac)]], [[father (yoru mac)|father (yoru mac)]] and [[daughter (yoru mac)|daughter (yoru mac)]] (post #6702154), unexpectedly went viral on western Twitter, resulting in tons of fanart. Later, another commercial featuring a [[boyfriend (yoru mac)|boyfriend (yoru mac)]] and [[girlfriend (yoru mac)|girlfriend (yoru mac)]] (post #6834868) received similar amounts of attention.

A year later, in Autumn 2024, coinciding with the "McDonald's Favorite Character Grand Prix":[https://twitter.com/McDonaldsJapan/status/1834766516807475527], another commercial featuring the family from the first commercial was made (post #8169424), with the Halloween character keychains being swapped out for a Grimace keychain.

- **Silver Creator Award** - *100,000 subscribers*
  - - Nickel alloy
- **[[gold creator award|gold creator award]]** - *one million subscribers*
  - - Gold-plated brass. This is the award most commonly depicted.
- **Diamond Creator Award** - *ten million subscribers*
  - - Silver-plated metal inset with colorless crystal glass in the shape of a play button triangle.
- **Custom** (a.k.a. **Ruby**) **Creator Award** - *50 million subscribers*
  - - Design varies according to receipient.
  - - 35 recipients as of October 2022
- **Red Diamond Creator Award** - *100 million subscribers*
  - - Dark glass or metal with red Baccarat crystal (made of gold, barium oxide, and sand) in the shape of a play button triangle.
  - - Only 10 recipients as of March 2024: [[pewdiepie|pewdiepie]], [T-Series](https://www.youtube.com/user/tseries,) [Cocomelon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocomelon,) [Sony Entertainment Television India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Entertainment_Television,) [[mrbeast|mrbeast]], "Kids Diana Show":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kids_Diana_Show], "Like Nastya":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Like_Nastya], "Vlad and Niki":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vlad_and_Niki], "Zee Music Company":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zee_Music_Company], and [[wwe|wwe]].

**Yowane Haku** is an [[original|original]] [[vocaloid|vocaloid]] character originated from a thread in [[2channel|2channel]] where a user commented: *"I bought [[hatsune miku|hatsune miku]] for her cute looks but no matter how hard I try, I can't get anything better than mechanical sounding songs out of her."*

An artist ([[caffein|caffein]]) took this idea and ran with it to create Yowane Haku, an alter ego of all unskilled users of Hatsune Miku. Haku is a sad Vocaloid who just can't sing as well as Miku. She is always crying because of this and vents her frustration by drinking. Her image colors are silver and purple. Her character item is a sake bottle. She's also noted for her [[large breasts|curvier figure]] compared to Miku and has a decent following. Haku's name means "speaking weak words" ('speaking' here has connotation of a pent-up sigh or muttering.)

This created a trend of users labeling badly-made Vocaloid songs with voyakiloid, or "shouting vocaloid." It is implied that it was Haku who sung those songs, and not Miku. Later on, she received several fan-made [[mikumikudance|MMD]] models and being treated as a "genuine" character rather than a byword for bad Vocaloid songs.

Her usual attire consists of a [[crop top|cropped]] [[sleeveless shirt|sleeveless]] [[grey shirt|grey shirt]] with a [[purple necktie|purple necktie]], [[black pants|black pants]] with a [[purple belt|purple belt]] tied around them, [[detached sleeves|detached sleeves]], and a [[striped bow|striped bow]].

A manga series written and drawn by Togashi Yoshihiro, later adapted into an anime series. The manga ran from 1990 to 1994 from [[weekly shounen jump|weekly shounen jump]] and the anime from 1992 to 1995.

Teenage delinquent [[urameshi yusuke|urameshi yusuke]] surprised the Underworld when, in an uncharacteristic act of altruism, he was killed saving a boy from a speeding car. With no place prepared for him in either Heaven or Hell, Yuusuke was returned to the living world, but not before he was recruited by [[koenma|koenma]], son of the ruler of the Underworld, to become Spirit Detective, charged with investigating supernatural activity in the human world.

The original [[yu-gi-oh!|yu-gi-oh!]] series. Known in Japan as Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Monsters and is an anime based on the Yu-Gi-Oh! manga ([[yu-gi-oh! (toei)|minus the early parts]]). Produced by Studio Gallop and Nihon Ad Systems. Written by [[takahashi kazuki|takahashi kazuki]].

The series began its 224-episode run in Japan on April 18, 2000 and ended on September 29, 2004. In the United States, it began airing on September 29, 2001 and ended on June 10, 2006.

After the positive reception following the release of the official card game by [[konami|konami]] in 1999, the series marked the point where it transitioned from a dark fantasy to almost exclusively revolving around the "Duel Monsters" card game. The series' "Duelist Kingdom" arc is also (in)famously known within the community for retaining the RPG-like elements from the early part of the manga, resulting in several unconventional uses of the cards (such as the notorious "attack the moon" scene and fusing a zombie monster to an opponent's monster and causing it to rot).

In the second season of the series (subtitled *Kagayaki no Jewel*), fans noticed an unexpected change in Aine's 3D model, which was altered to show a more developed bust. Interestingly, this change is not noticable in the 2D animated parts of the show (she still appears flat even in bikini), and no similar adjustments were made to the body types of other characters (see 3D model comparison [here](https://i.imgur.com/13rS3pk.jpeg).) When fans online discovered this, it quickly became a meme, with many fan artists exaggerating Aine's bust size in their illustrations. Literally, "dream cute". Not necessarily cute as in [[tag group:subjective|subjective]] cuteness, but rather a specific aesthetic theme meant to give off the feeling of a floaty, dream-like environment that is conducive to emphasizing cuteness. Bright [[pastel colors|pastels]] and nostalgic appropriation of visual elements from [[retro artstyle|retro]] shoujo manga and anime are common motifs of the aesthetic. A surreal exploration [[horror (theme)|horror (theme)]] game created in [[rpg maker|RPG Maker 2003]] by *Kikiyama*. 

The player wanders around a variety of dream worlds as a little girl, dubbed [[madotsuki|madotsuki]] by the game menu. The only objective is to search for new "effects", such as a kitchen [[knife|knife]] which one can stab others with, a [[witch hat|witch hat]] and [[broom|broom]] which can be used to fly, the ability to grow [[cat ears|cat ears]], etc. The game has no dialogue or story, though it does have an ending which can be viewed when all the effects have been gathered.

On February 23, 2018, a 3D remake/reboot titled was [[yume nikki dream diary|yume nikki dream diary]] released on Steam.

A character from [[snk|SNK's]] [[ryuuko no ken|Art of Fighting]] and [[the king of fighters|the king of fighters]] series. She wears a red [[headband|headband]] and a training outfit - typically the upper half of a [[dougi|dougi]] - over a blue [[leotard|leotard]] and [[sports bra|sports bra]]. She has [[brown hair|brown hair]] most commonly done up as a [[braided ponytail|braided ponytail]].

She is the second child and only daughter of [[karate|Kyokugen-ryuu Karate]] founder [[takuma sakazaki|takuma sakazaki]]. She has an older brother named [[ryou sakazaki|Ryo]]. She is the love interest of fellow Kyokugen disciple and friend of the family [[robert garcia|robert garcia]].

She practices the Swallow discipline of Kyokugen-ryuu Karate, having learned the family style within a year (against her father's wishes, initially). She is also the first female to be able to perform the [[haou shoukou ken|Haoh Shoko Ken]]. She is often described as a genius, able to learn moves very quickly. For this reason, Yuri has a habit of parodying moves from other characters, most infamously [[ryu (street fighter)|Ryu]] and [[akuma (street fighter)|Akuma]] from [[street fighter|street fighter]] (a way for [[snk|snk]] to lightly poke fun back at [[capcom|capcom]] after the latter made [[hibiki dan|Dan Hibiki]]).

She first appeared as a damsel in distress, kidnapped by [[mr big (snk)|Mr. Big]] in Art of Fighting 1 and rescued by Ryo and Robert. She made her playable debut in Art of Fighting 2.

Her original fighting stage was a fitness gym, and her signature theme song is named "Diet". As of [[fatal fury: city of the wolves|fatal fury: city of the wolves]], which takes place long after the events of Art of Fighting, Yuri owns her own gym.

In the King of Fighters continuity, Yuri is a founding member of the Women Fighters Team alongside [[shiranui mai|Mai Shiranui]] and [[king (snk)|king (snk)]].

Japanese term for a category of [[mascot|mascot]] characters; usually created to promote a place or region, event, organisation or business. They are characterized by their kawaii (cute) and unsophisticated designs, often incorporating motifs that represent local culture, history or produce. They may be created by local government or other organizations to stimulate tourism and economic development, or created by a company to build on their corporate identity. They may appear as costumed characters (or [[kigurumi|kigurumi]]) at promotional events and festivals. Yuru-chara has become a popular and lucrative business, with character-driven sales reaching nearly $16 billion in Japan in 2012.

Popular yuru-chara include [[kumamon|kumamon]], [[funasshii|funasshii]], and [[chiitan|chiitan]], who have gained international recognition and have reached celebrity status in Japan.

Yuujo (遊女, lit. "women of pleasure"), were the [[prostitution|prostitutes]] of feudal era Japan. 

Yuujo are usually shown wearing a [[open kimono|kimono loosely hanging open]] or [[off shoulder|off their shoulders]] in order to expose their chest. Their hair tends toward extremes: either carefully sculpted shapes with the [[bangs pinned back|bangs pulled back]], or [[hair up|pinned up]] in an [[messy hair|artful mess]] (both of which are achieved through the use of several [[hair stick|hair sticks]] and [[kanzashi|kanzashi]]). Some form of makeup may be present, often [[eyeshadow|eyeshadow]] or [[lipstick|lipstick]]. Oftentimes, they are shown holding a [[kiseru|kiseru]], an [[oil-paper umbrella|oil-paper umbrella]], or a rolled-up mat. Sometimes the [[obi|obi]] will be tied in a bow on the front of their kimono, allegedly for "easy access". 

The most common depictions of yuujo are [[indoors|indoors]], [[on side|lying on their side]] in a state of seductive, carefully-arranged disarray, or waiting for clients at night on a [[bridge|bridge]] that crosses over a stream or a river.

There is a certain sub-type of yuujo, the [[oiran|oiran]], who despite also providing sexual services, were famed for being more cultured, educated, respectable, and skilled in providing classical entertainment and intelligent discourse.

One of the international maritime [[signal flag|signal flags]]. It is a square divided diagonally into four triangles, colored yellow, blue, red, and black. Also referred in NATO alphabet as "Zulu flag" (not the actual flag of the Zulu kingdom).

It represents the letter Z when communicating by individual letters. Combined with four number flags, it represents the time in UTC. On its own, it may mean "I require a tug" or "I am shooting nets".

The Z flag is of special significance in the context of Japanese naval history due to its role in the Battle of Tsushima where it was raised on the flagship [[mikasa (battleship)|Mikasa]]. In this battle, the Z flag was understood to mean, "The fate of the Empire rests on the outcome of this battle. Let each man do his utmost". However, the flag has gradually gained more notoriety after it was used as a signal flag of the Attack on [[pearl harbor|pearl harbor]] on board the flagship [[akagi (aircraft carrier)|akagi (aircraft carrier)]], along with being a battle flag in several major engagements in [[world war ii|world war ii]] (including the last voyage of the battleship [[yamato (battleship)|yamato (battleship)]] during [[operation ten-gou|operation ten-gou]]). As a result, much like the [[imperial war flag|Imperial German war flag]], it has turned into a symbol for far-right Japanese ultranationalism.

Zegapain is a 2006 ||post-apocalyptic|| sci-fi mecha anime series by [[sunrise (company)|sunrise (company)]] with manga and video game adaptations.  A sequel for the series was announced August of 2023.

The anime series follows Sogoru Kyou, a high school boy living a normal day to day life in the city Maihama.  A member of the school's swim club, he one day meets the girl Misaki Shizuno at the school's pool and is startled to find initially he's the only person who can see her.  As his clubs is at the risk of being closed, Kyou decides to recruit Shizuno to make a promo video for the club to draw in new members with the help of his childhood friend, Kaminagi Ryouko.  Shizuno agrees, but on the condition that Kyou pilots a mecha from what appears to be a video game.  Kyou agrees, but finds himself seemingly pulled into the video-game-like world where the the organization Celebrum is fighting a war against enemies called Gards-orm.

Franchise premise: ||The franchise as a whole revolves around the ongoing war between the organization Celebrum and the invaders called the Gards-orm.  The Gards-orm are part of a plan developed by the iAL Company, who developed a means of digitizing the human mind and uploading them to exist within a quantum server.  The CEO of iAL Company envisioned this as a means of advancing humanity to the next stage of evolution and to force his vision developed a virus that lead to the extinction of organic humans.  While most of humanity was wiped out, many still survived by being digitized onto quantum servers independent of iAL Company's control.  Some of the survivors from these servers became able to leave upon realizing the world they lived in on the servers were simulations, these "awakened" survivors created the organization of Celebrum. Using stolen technology they were able to produce weapons to both defend their servers and to stop the Gards-orm from re-terraforming the Earth's surface.||

A fetish in which [[public nudity|public nudity]] and sexual acts is treated as a normal everyday activity.

"Zenra" is a Japanese word, literally translated as "[[completely nude|completely nude]]". Zenra fetish features people (usually women) participating in everyday tasks that they might otherwise perform clothed, such as casual scenes with participants playing in an all-nude orchestra in a seemingly oblivious state of mind towards their nudity. Others incorporate the nudity on a more conscious level by doing such things as playing "[[strip game|strip volleyball]]", where the participants must remove clothing each time the other team scores a point.

While very similar to [[exhibitionism|exhibitionism]] and [[nudist|nudism]] in concept and often overlaps with each other, zenra fetish can be distinguished by how the setting treated nudity and sexual activity, as zenra fetish treats nudity either as a social norm at best and a minor inconvenience at worst. In addition, some zenra works also further emphasize sexual elements of the character (such as character exposing their private parts) as another form of beauty standard.

Please note that [[bathing|bathing]] or tanning on the beach are not zenra as that is normally done naked.

Usually the main antagonists in the [[macross|macross]] [[mecha|mecha]] anime franchise. An ancient [[space|space]]faring race of [[giant|giant]] humanoid [[alien|alien]] [[soldier|soldier]]s. 

They were created as proxy warriors by the first humanoid civilization in the galaxy, the [[protoculture|protoculture]], 500,000 years ago. They have been at war with the [[supervision army|supervision army]] since then.

Physically, most of them resemble humans, though some have [[pointy ears|pointy ears]] and many diverse and unique skin, eye and hair colors. Prior to their first encounter with the human race, all members of the **Zentradi** race were only reproduced and artificially fabricated through cloning.

The Zentradi army is a fearsomely powerful force of millions of space warships and mecha produced in thousands of huge and massive automated space factories scattered across the [[galaxy|galaxy]] and legions of expendable giant clone troops created in mass production facilities.

Zentradi in giant form are called [[maclone|maclone]]s, while their human sized variants are known as [[miclone|miclone]]s. Female Zentradi are called [[meltrandi|meltrandi]].

***Zeta Gundam*** is the [[mecha|mecha]] anime 1985 TV sequel to [[mobile suit gundam|mobile suit gundam]]. It was created by largely the same creative staff as is predecessor, but veteran designer [[ookawara kunio|ookawara kunio]] was assisted in mechanical designs by newcomers [[nagano mamoru|nagano mamoru]] and [[fujita kazumi|fujita kazumi]]. It also had character designs by [[kitazume hiroyuki|kitazume hiroyuki]] and [[yasuhiko yoshikazu|yasuhiko yoshikazu]]. 

*Zeta Gundam* followed in the footsteps of [[choujikuu yousai macross|choujikuu yousai macross]] (1982) by including a large number of transforming [[mobile suit|MS]] [[robot|robot]]s, a first for a [[gundam|gundam]] show.

It is set in the year **Universal Century 0087**, eight years after the original series. It follows the story of [[kamille bidan|kamille bidan]], designer and pilot of the [[zeta gundam (mobile suit)|MSZ-006 Zeta Gundam]], in a conflict known as The Gryps War, between the oppresive and brutal [[titans (gundam)|Earth Federation Titans]] against the alliance of the valiant [[aeug|aeug]] and the Karaba resistance organization.

The story of the series continues directly into [[gundam zz|gundam zz]].

To this day is considered by many anime critics as the most influential and best Universal Century Gundam series ever made.[(1)](https://www.fandomspot.com/best-gundam-anime/) [(2)](https://screenrant.com/best-gundam-anime-of-all-time/)

The **zodiac** is the "band" of the night sky roughly corresponding to the solar system's ecliptic plane. Western astrologers divide it into twelve signs, named for the constellation that is nearest the position of the Sun for one-twelfth of the year. Reanimated human or animal [[corpse|corpse]]. Stereotypical zombies are characterized by animalistic behavior, indifference to pain, and an insatiable hunger for human flesh (particularly [[brain|brain]]s). Some zombies walk with a stiff gait and outstretched arms due to rigor mortis. They are a common monster in [[horror (theme)|horror (theme)]] fiction and video games due to their predatory nature and tendency to shrug off debilitating injury.

Only characters with visible evidence of [[death|death]] or decomposition should be tagged zombie. Unnatural grayish-blue or green skin, [[blank eyes|blank eyes]], and festering [[injury|wounds]] are good indicators of when this tag should be used. Whether or not a character is canonically a zombie is irrelevant.

An additional layer that magnifies part of the illustration. It's a common technique used for backgrounds in character art. 

There are sometimes small, primarily 2D variations, such as:

- The layer being reversed.
- The layer being rotated.
- The layer being partially transparent, in greyscale, or having other changes in color.
- A character having a different expression.

If the layer is from a different 3D perspective, or there are larger 3D differences such as costumes, poses, or characters, it's a [[projected inset|projected inset]] instead.

For the "zoom layer" effect used on [[stage|stage]]s by projecting the performance on background [[screen|screen]]s, use [[screen zoom|screen zoom]] instead.

The Zweihänder (pronounced "tsvay-haen-dar", literally "two-handed") is a massive late medieval/early Renaissance Germanic [[sword|sword]] with a long hilt and two parrying hooks located above the ricasso (the unsharpened lower length of a blade), allowing it to be wielded similarly to a [[polearm|polearm]]. Due to its large size it required two hands to wield, hence the name. It was used in place of a [[halberd|halberd]] against cavalry and pike formations.

Commonly associated with the historical [[landsknecht|landsknecht]], and in modern times is a fantastic weapon in [[dark souls i|dark souls i]].
